route_step_status.reason: The modulus decay temperature T_chi(m_chi) is a simple analytic gravitational-decay estimate given explicitly in the paper, so a null tool_or_code is not a barrier.

The nonthermal abundance expression Omega_LSP h^2 proportional to (100 MeV/T_chi)(m_LSP/100 GeV)^3 is pen-and-paper math once T_chi, m_LSP, and <sigma v> are supplied, and <sigma v> can come from standard public SUSY tools (micrOMEGAs/DarkSUSY) for a chosen spectrum.
The check needs model-dependent Q-ball yields, gravitino branching fractions, and dilution factors that exist only as narrow scan regions in the paper, with no reusable calculator or table.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-yield code tracks LSP production from late modulus decay together with post-decay annihilation, gravitino branching, and entropy injection; the card's route relies on the paper's instantaneous-decay analytic expression, and standard relic-density codes (micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY) assume thermal freeze-out in a radiation-dominated history rather than a modulus-dominated one.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs or DarkSUSY with a nonstandard-cosmology module that solves the coupled modulus/radiation/LSP Boltzmann system (modulus decay width, branching to superpartners, LSP annihilation at T_chi), parameterized by (m_chi, T_chi, m_LSP, <sigma v>, Br(chi -> superpartners)), validating against the paper's analytic scaling.

gaps.description: No reusable parameterization exists for the Affleck-Dine Q-ball charge, formation efficiency, and decay yield of LSPs as a function of (M, v, chi_0, phi_0); the paper only reports narrow viable regions from its own scan, so the overproduction/dilution check cannot be re-evaluated for new parameter points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive (or fit from existing Affleck-Dine lattice results) an analytic Q-ball charge and decay-temperature parameterization on the (M, v, chi_0, phi_0) space and publish it as a lookup table or module feeding the nonthermal yield calculator of gap_1.

route_step_status.reason: The entropy-conservation abundance relation Omega_J h^2(m_J, beta, N_D) is a simple analytic formula given in the primary paper, so a null tool_or_code is not a barrier.

The paper used a modified CAMB/CosmoMC decaying-dark-matter solver that was never publicly released; public CLASS decaying-CDM-to-dark-radiation modules exist but must be adapted to the all-DM majoron-to-neutrino case.
Public CMB likelihoods (Planck 2018, and legacy WMAP) exist and plug into standard MCMC samplers once the Boltzmann step provides spectra.

Lyman-alpha/WDM recast pipelines exist publicly for thermal-relic WDM, but the card states no thermal-WDM transfer-function mapping and no phase-space distribution is available for the beta-parameterized majoron, so existing pipelines cannot be applied directly.

gaps.description: The paper's modified CAMB/CosmoMC solver for a flat cosmology in which all dark matter is a majoron decaying nonradiatively to neutrinos is private/unreleased, so the CMB constraint cannot be reproduced or updated to Planck data without rebuilding the solver.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt the public CLASS decaying-CDM-to-dark-radiation (dcdm->dr) module to the majoron case (decay products as free-streaming neutrino-like radiation, no stable CDM component), couple it to the Planck 2018 likelihood in Cobaya/MontePython, and validate by recovering the WMAP-era limits Gamma_J < 1.3e-19 s^-1 and tau_J > 250 Gyr.

gaps.description: No majoron phase-space distribution or transfer-function mapping exists for the beta-parameterized (thermal plus out-of-equilibrium) production, so the keV majoron's roughly 1 Mpc free streaming cannot be recast onto thermal-WDM Lyman-alpha limits.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) for the majoron as a function of beta and the decoupling degrees of freedom N_D, feed it through CLASS as a non-cold relic to compute T(k), and map the resulting half-mode scale onto existing thermal-WDM Lyman-alpha emulator/likelihood bounds.

gaps.description: The radiative branching ratio Br(J -> photons) is left uncomputed by the paper, so the predicted far-ultraviolet photon line from subdominant radiative decay cannot be quantified or compared to diffuse-background data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the loop-induced J -> gamma gamma rate from the seesaw model's charged-fermion couplings for the quoted keV mass window and publish it as an analytic branching-ratio formula usable in decaying-DM photon-flux estimates.

route_step_status.reason: The BEC condition and critical temperature are closed-form formulas in the primary paper (thermal de Broglie wavelength versus interparticle spacing), evaluable by hand.
The Jeans wave number and preferred collapse mass follow from the paper's analytic instability scalings (k_J branches in m^2/M_Pl and (m^2 rho)^(1/3)), which are pen-and-paper math.

Public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson/fuzzy-DM solvers (e.g. PyUltraLight, AxioNyx-class codes) and Thomas-Fermi halo models cover parts of the regime, but no named code implements this model's phenomenological condensation/collapse rates or its self-interacting relativistic BEC halo profiles end to end.

Public Lyman-alpha/LSS and rotation-curve likelihoods exist for generic fuzzy/warm DM, but they require a model-specific transfer function and halo-profile prediction that the upstream steps do not yet provide, and none has been run for this model.

gaps.description: The condensation and collapse rates (Gamma, Gamma') coupling the uniform boson gas, BEC, and localized dark-matter components are fixed purely phenomenologically; without a derivation from the scalar Lagrangian and gravitational-condensation microphysics, the three-component background history and the epoch of first collapse cannot be predicted, only parameterized.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the condensation rate from gravitational-relaxation/kinetic theory of the self-interacting scalar (condensation timescale as a function of m, lambda, and density) and the collapse rate from the paper's own instability analysis, replacing the free rates with functions of (m, lambda) that close the background equations.

gaps.description: No linear Boltzmann/perturbation solver exists for this three-component relativistic BEC cosmology (uniform gas, condensate, collapsed component with quartic self-interaction), so no transfer function can be produced for LSS or Lyman-alpha comparison.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing scalar-field-dark-matter CLASS branch (e.g. an SFDM/axionCAMB-style implementation) with the quartic self-interaction sound speed and phenomenological condensation source terms, outputting T(k) over the m = 1e-24 eV to 1 eV range discussed in the card.

gaps.description: No nonlinear simulation calibration exists for the collapse of self-interacting BEC condensates into halos in this model (simulation_calibrated: no), so halo density profiles, rotation curves, and the subhalo/halo mass function cannot be predicted beyond Thomas-Fermi analytic estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt a public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson solver (e.g. PyUltraLight or an AxioNyx-class cosmological code) to include the quartic self-interaction term, run collapse simulations across the (m, a_s) plane, and calibrate a core-halo relation usable in rotation-curve and minimum-halo fits.

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline connects the BEC particle parameters (m, a_s, lambda) to rotation-curve, minimum-halo, or Lyman-alpha data for this model; existing constraints in the card are analytic recasts from related papers with likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the gap_2 transfer function into an existing Lyman-alpha/WDM-style likelihood and build a SPARC-based rotation-curve likelihood over the Thomas-Fermi (m, a_s) halo model, validating against the quoted m ~ 2.92e-22 eV noninteracting and a_s-bounded repulsive regions.

route_step_status.reason: The two-photon and e+e- lifetimes follow from the paper's analytic large-volume coupling formulas (tau values quoted for m_phi = 2 MeV), which are pen-and-paper math.

Decaying-dark-matter line/diffuse flux integrals are standard semi-analytic calculations, and public D-factor/halo-template tools (e.g. CLUMPY-style integrators with standard Milky Way profiles) cover them.
The initial coherent modulus energy density from a given displacement is a textbook analytic misalignment estimate stated in the paper.

Only analytic e-fold estimates exist; no code in the card tracks modulus domination, heavy-modulus reheating, and thermal-inflation entropy injection to a residual Omega_phi, and the thermal-inflation implementation is model-dependent.

gaps.description: No modern MeV gamma-ray likelihood (COMPTEL, INTEGRAL/SPI, including the 511 keV positron channel) is packaged for decaying-dark-matter recasting of this model; the card's constraint is only the paper's analytic comparison to a COMPTEL diffuse-background fit, with likelihood_available: partial.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a reusable decaying-DM likelihood over COMPTEL diffuse and INTEGRAL/SPI line data (photon line at m_phi/2 plus 511 keV injection), parameterized by (m_phi, tau, Omega_phi/Omega_DM) with standard Milky Way halo decay D-factors, and validate against the paper's COMPTEL density-fraction bound.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann history solver exists for the coherent-modulus cosmology of this model — scalar domination, heavy-modulus reheating, a late thermal-inflation/trapping epoch, and entropy injection — so the residual fraction Omega_phi/Omega_DM (the dominant nuisance for all observables) can only be estimated by hand.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a coupled background solver (modulus field, heavy-modulus decay products, radiation, thermal-inflation flaton) parameterized by (m_phi, m_heavy, initial displacement, N_TI, T_R) that outputs residual Omega_phi and the BBN-era reheating temperature, validating against the paper's overclosure and dilution estimates.

route_step_status.reason: The pure kinetic Lagrangian L(X) and the exact affine background solution rho_X(a) are closed-form analytic results from the primary paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the pure kinetic k-essence field in CLASS or CAMB as a unified dark fluid (generalized-dark-matter module with c_s^2 from the k-essence L(X), or a dedicated k-essence perturbation module), verify recovery of the CDM transfer function in the alpha -> 0 limit, and compute P(k) and CMB spectra across the small-alpha regime.

gaps.proposed_resolution: After the Boltzmann implementation of gap_1, run an MCMC with Planck, BAO, and galaxy power-spectrum likelihoods over (p_0, alpha) to derive the first quantitative upper bound on the affine sound-speed parameter for this k-essence realization.

route_step_status.reason: The affine EoS to scalar potential mapping and rho_X(a) solution are exact closed-form results in the primary paper, evaluable by hand or with a trivial background ODE integration.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-code implementation exists for the canonical affine-quintessence unified dark fluid: linear perturbations of the scalar with the hyperbolic potential (including its effective sound speed and Compton scale) have never been evolved through a CMB/matter-power pipeline, so the alpha ~ 1e-6 bound rests on a scaling argument rather than a computation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the affine unified dark fluid in CLASS as either the derived scalar field (quintessence module with the hyperbolic potential and full perturbations) or a generalized-dark-matter fluid with c_s^2 set by the affine slope alpha, then compute P(k) and CMB spectra to turn the kpc-clustering and ISW arguments into quantitative constraints against Planck and galaxy-clustering data.

gaps.description: No likelihood analysis exists for the affine parameters (p_0, alpha): background viability and the sound-speed bound are stated qualitatively (likelihood_available: no/unknown) with no parameter posterior from expansion-history or perturbation data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the CLASS implementation of gap_1 exists, run an MCMC (MontePython/Cobaya) with Planck CMB, BAO, and supernova likelihoods over (p_0, alpha, initial scalar trajectory) to produce the first quantitative affine-quintessence constraint.

route_step_status.reason: The complete SM gauge-group thermal-production collision term is given as closed-form leading-order rates in the primary thesis, evaluable analytically from (gauge couplings, M_i, T_R, m_3/2), with gaugino inputs obtainable from public MSSM spectrum calculators (SoftSUSY/SPheno).
Converting the gravitino yield to Omega_3/2^TP under a standard entropy history is a one-line analytic step compared directly to the observed dark-matter density.

gaps.description: No public, reusable BBN late-decay constraint tool covers hadronic plus electromagnetic cascades from NLSP decays in gravitino-LSP scenarios; existing public codes (e.g. ACROPOLIS) treat photodisintegration but not full hadronic showers, so the (NLSP abundance, tau, branching fractions) plane can only be checked against fixed literature grids rather than recomputed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend ACROPOLIS (or wrap the published Kawasaki-Moroi-style hadronic-injection exclusion grids into an interpolated likelihood) to accept per-NLSP decay spectra from a spectrum calculator plus micrOMEGAs, outputting light-element constraints as a function of (NLSP identity, abundance, tau, branching fractions).

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level Z'-exchange effective nucleon coupling is a standard analytic formula computable by hand from B-L charges, m_Zprime, and g_B-L.
Public direct-detection likelihood tools (e.g. DDCalc with LZ/XENONnT limits) accept generic (sigma_SI, m_N) inputs, which is exactly what this step needs.
DarkSUSY's public solar-capture module, named in the card, computes capture rates from m_N and sigma_p for spin-independent scattering.

Public neutrino-yield/propagation tools (WimpSim-style) and released IceCube effective areas exist, but a model-specific pipeline for the leptonic B-L annihilation channels must be assembled and the card notes only a partial likelihood.

micrOMEGAs is a public Boltzmann solver, but no machine-readable B-L MSSM + RH sneutrino model implementation (spectrum plus annihilation matrix elements) is indicated by the card, so the model files must first be built.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the U(1)_B-L extended MSSM in SARAH (or FeynRules), generate SPheno spectrum code and micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP model files including Z', Z'-gaugino, and Higgs-sector superpartner exchange, and validate against the paper's benchmark relic-density regions including the Z'-pole.

gaps.description: No assembled IceCube solar-capture likelihood exists for this model's mostly-leptonic B-L annihilation final states; only event-rate comparisons in related papers are available, and the neutrino-transport plus effective-area recast has not been packaged.

route_step_status.reason: The superWIMP abundance relation Omega_G = (m_G/m_chi) Omega_chi is simple analytic algebra, and the input neutralino freeze-out density is computable with public SoftSUSY plus micrOMEGAs already used in the paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) analytically for monochromatic two-body decay with exponential decay-time distribution during radiation domination, tabulate it as a CLASS ncdm distribution over the (m_chi, m_gravitino, tau_chi) plane, and compute transfer functions to replace the lambda_FS proxy.

gaps.description: No BBN likelihood exists for late electromagnetic and hadronic energy injection from neutralino-to-gravitino decays in this scenario; the card records only pass/fail comparisons against 2007-era decay-constraint plots, with hadronic branching fractions the dominant untreated uncertainty.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast with ACROPOLIS for electromagnetic injection and extend to hadronic injection using published Kawasaki-Moroi constraint grids, wrapping the result as a likelihood in (tau_chi, zeta_EM, zeta_had) with modern light-element abundance measurements.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the nonthermal transfer functions from gap_1 onto Ly-alpha flux-power constraints via the area-criterion/half-mode matching validated against thermal-WDM emulators, or retrain an existing Ly-alpha emulator on the decay-produced suppression shape family.

route_step_status.reason: The step is a trivial data transform reading the completed model card, but it is a recovery placeholder and encodes no physics forward model from parameters to an observable.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the full enrichment on the primary paper to construct real routes: a freeze-out relic-density route (Boltzmann solver step using the gap_1 implementation), a Higgs-portal direct-detection route feeding public likelihoods (DDCalc), and a Higgs-mixing collider-constraint route (HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals).

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the modified Einstein equations from the locally scale-invariant action under an FRW ansatz with the S_0=0 gauge is a closed-form analytic derivation already performed in the primary paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the linearized field equations for perturbations of phi, S_mu, and the metric about the oscillating background, time-average them to obtain an effective-fluid description (sound speed c_s^2(k,a) and anisotropic stress, analogous to the ultra-light axion / coherent-field treatments), and implement that effective fluid as a new species in CLASS or hi_class alongside a background ODE solver for H(a) with subleading oscillation corrections.

gaps.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum has been computed for the first-order dark phase transition; only a broad transition-temperature range is quoted, with the first-order character itself estimated from a simplified finite-temperature potential.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the dark Higgs/singlet finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions to obtain alpha, beta/H, and T_*, then map through standard sound-wave/bubble-collision spectral templates to LISA and other detector sensitivity curves.

route_step_status.reason: Omega_d/Omega_b = (m_Y + m_Phi)/m_p from n_Y = n_Phi = n_B is a one-line analytic relation requiring only the measured density ratio.
Applying the kinematic inequality |m_Y - m_Phi| < m_p + m_e to the mass sum is trivial pen-and-paper validation.
Matching the dimension-six neutron-portal operator and X_a Y Phi coupling onto the effective IND amplitude is a standard EFT calculation performed in the paper.

The paper estimates the nucleon-to-meson matrix element only by analogy with nucleon decay; lattice-QCD nucleon-decay matrix elements exist publicly but have not been matched to the specific portal flavor/spin contractions and IND kinematics.
No IND event generator or detector recast exists; the card notes no public likelihood or efficiency was extracted and IND kinematics differ from standard nucleon-decay searches.
Compact-star capture rates follow from standard semi-analytic capture approximations given stellar parameters, local DM density, and the scattering cross section.
The steady-state capture-limited heating luminosity is a simple analytic formula from the capture rate and energy per IND event.

gaps.description: The nucleon-to-meson hadronic matrix elements for the induced-nucleon-decay process are only estimated by analogy with standard nucleon decay; the specific neutron-portal flavor/spin contractions at IND momentum transfer have no calibrated values, leaving sigma_IND uncertain at the rate level.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Match the model's X U^c D^c D^c contractions onto the lattice-QCD nucleon-decay matrix-element basis (chiral-perturbation-theory extrapolated) and evaluate them at the IND kinematics, propagating the lattice uncertainties into the sigma_IND prediction.

gaps.description: No event generator or detector recast exists for induced nucleon decay (p Y -> Phi* K+ and variants): the meson spectrum differs from standard nucleon-decay searches, and no efficiency map or likelihood from water-Cherenkov nucleon-decay analyses has been applied to these kinematics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a simple IND event generator producing the meson momentum spectrum from DM-nucleon scattering kinematics, then recast Super-Kamiokande p -> K+ nu (and analogous pion-channel) selections with published efficiency and background information to produce limits on sigma_IND versus the portal scale M.

gaps.description: No likelihood connects the predicted IND heating luminosity to compact-star observations: the card lists compact-star thermal observations as the target but no dataset of old neutron-star or white-dwarf temperatures with a capture-heating comparison framework is packaged.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble published temperature/luminosity measurements of old, cold neutron stars and white dwarfs in high-DM-density environments and wrap them in a likelihood comparing observed cooling against the capture-limited IND heating prediction with astrophysical nuisance parameters.

route_step_status.reason: ISAJET 7.80 is named in associated_code as the 2-loop RGE spectrum generator with 4-2-2 boundary conditions (m0, m_Hu, m_Hd, M2, M3, A0, tan beta, sign(mu)) exactly as this step requires, and public SUSY spectrum generators of this class exist.

IsaTools is named in associated_code for neutralino relic-density calculation from the ISAJET spectrum, and public codes (IsaReD, micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY) cover neutralino freeze-out including coannihilation and A-funnel regimes.

Public recast machinery for flavor, g-2, direct-detection, and collider limits exists in principle, but the card marks every constraint recasting_needed=yes with likelihood_available=no and states the recasts must be updated for post-2010 data, so no ready-to-use modern recast covers these benchmarks.

gaps.description: No modern likelihood or recast exists for the mu<0 4-2-2 Yukawa-unified benchmark spectra: the WMAP-era relic/flavor/g-2 cut flow, the post-Higgs (m_h ~ 125 GeV) LHC sparticle limits, and current direct-detection limits have not been applied to this branch (all three constraints have likelihood_available=no and recasting_needed=yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the 4-2-2 scan branch with a modern spectrum generator (ISAJET or SoftSUSY with non-universal gaugino boundary conditions), then chain micrOMEGAs (relic, sigma_SI/SD against LZ/XENONnT limits), FlavBit/SuperIso (B-physics, g-2 with the current Delta a_mu value), HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals (125 GeV Higgs), and SModelS/CheckMATE (LHC gluino/stau/electroweakino limits) into a composite likelihood.

gaps.description: No machine-readable scan table or benchmark-point file for the paper's allowed regions was extracted (constraint caveat: 'No machine-readable scan table was extracted'), so the quoted benchmark classes and the ~43 GeV lightest-neutralino point cannot be reproduced or recast without regenerating the scan from scratch.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the paper's benchmark tables and allowed-region plots into a machine-readable point list (input parameters m_16, m_10, M_2, M_3, A_0, tan_beta, sign(mu) plus spectra), or regenerate the scan with the documented ISAJET 7.80 setup and archive the accepted points.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level spin-independent scattering through a kinetically mixed vector is a standard closed-form analytic formula in (m_L, m_X, epsilon, g_X), so the null tool_or_code is trivially covered by pen-and-paper computation.

Public low-mass limit curves and tools like DDCalc exist for the ~7 GeV region, but the card provides no likelihood (likelihood_available=no, recasting_needed=yes) and the historical DAMA/CoGeNT-era comparison must be replaced by a modern low-threshold recast.
The annihilation/decay source rate with Sommerfeld enhancement from the sub-GeV mediator is a semi-analytic calculation the paper itself performs at framework level, requiring no dedicated code.

Cosmic-ray propagation and gamma-ray constraint codes (GALPROP/DRAGON-class tools, Fermi-LAT limits) exist publicly, but the card supplies no likelihood or recast configured for this TeV heavy sector with sub-GeV dark-boson cascades (likelihood_available=no).

Generic freeze-out solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) could compute LDM annihilation into dark gauge bosons and H_R, but no model implementation of the GMSB NMSSM plus U(1)_X sector exists (has_associated_code=no) so the step is currently done by rough estimate.
Transferring the frozen-out ONLSP number density to LDM through a branching fraction and lifetime is a simple semi-analytic sudden-decay calculation done by hand in the paper.

The approximate timing check (decay before BBN) is analytic, but a quantitative pass/fail on visible energy injection needs a BBN energy-injection code applied to the ONLSP decay channels, which the card does not provide (constraint caveat: no full BBN likelihood).

gaps.description: No numerical implementation of the GMSB NMSSM plus U(1)_X dark sector exists: LDM freeze-out into dark gauge bosons and the CP-even dark Higgs, the ONLSP relic abundance, and the coupled visible/dark-sector thermal history are only estimated analytically (has_associated_code=no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model Lagrangian (superpotentials W_1 and W_dark with kinetic mixing) in FeynRules/SARAH and export to micrOMEGAs or MadDM to compute LDM freeze-out with a possibly decoupled dark-sector temperature, plus the ONLSP (neutralino or right-handed sneutrino) abundance feeding the late-decay transfer.

gaps.description: No modern direct-detection likelihood is available for the ~7 GeV Dirac LDM scattering through a 0.2 GeV kinetically mixed mediator; the card's target region is the now-historical 2010 DAMA/CoGeNT window and current low-threshold limits have not been applied (likelihood_available=no, recasting_needed=yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the (m_L, m_X, epsilon, g_X) parameter space against current low-mass results (XENONnT, LZ, PandaX, DarkSide-50, SuperCDMS) using DDCalc or the experiments' published likelihoods, keeping the light-mediator form factor in the cross section.

gaps.description: No cosmic-ray propagation or gamma-ray constraint pipeline is configured for the Sommerfeld-enhanced TeV heavy dark sector annihilating/decaying through the sub-GeV dark boson; the paper only flags the gamma-ray issue qualitatively and provides no likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the e+/e- and gamma spectra of the dark-boson cascade (dark-photon spectra plus Pythia showering), propagate charged cosmic rays with GALPROP or DRAGON2, and confront Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal and Galactic-center likelihoods plus CMB energy-injection limits for the Sommerfeld-enhanced cross section.

gaps.description: The BBN safety of the late ONLSP decay is only an approximate timing estimate; no energy-injection likelihood evaluates the hadronic/electromagnetic decay products of the neutralino or right-handed sneutrino ONLSP against light-element abundances (constraint caveat: no full BBN energy-injection likelihood).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a public BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS with the ONLSP lifetime, abundance, and visible branching fractions to produce a tau_ONLSP versus injected-energy exclusion contour for both ONLSP options.

gaps.description: The phase-space distribution of the nonthermally produced LDM from late ONLSP decay has not been derived (distribution_function_available=no, all structure_formation entries unknown), so whether the light component free-streams enough to suppress small-scale power cannot be assessed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) for the decay-produced LDM from the ONLSP lifetime and two-body kinematics (including redshifting after decay), and feed it to CLASS as a non-cold relic to compute the transfer function and check against Lyman-alpha warm-dark-matter bounds.

route_step_status.reason: Chemical-potential equilibrium relations for given charge assignments are a standard pen-and-paper calculation carried out in the primary paper, so no tool is needed.
The Boltzmann-suppressed X number density as a function of m_X/T_D is an analytic formula given in the paper, evaluable without dedicated code.

Generic tools (micrOMEGAs/MadDM-class codes, collider recast frameworks) exist for annihilation and search signatures, but the card provides no concrete UV completion or operator normalization to implement, leaving only model-dependent qualitative expectations.

gaps.description: The XXudd transfer operator and the pseudoscalar/vector symmetric-annihilation sector are given only at framework level; no benchmark Lagrangian with normalized couplings exists from which direct, indirect, or collider signatures of the symmetric-component removal can actually be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write down one or two explicit UV completions (squark-mediated XXudd with a specified pseudoscalar or Z' annihilation sector), fix operator normalizations, and implement them as FeynRules/micrOMEGAs model files so annihilation cross sections and collider signatures become computable.

gaps.description: No public asymmetric-dark-matter transfer code couples the chemical-equilibrium network, the decoupling of the B-violating operator at T_D, and symmetric-component freeze-out; the route's required chemical-potential solver and asymmetric-abundance Boltzmann calculator exist only as the paper's instantaneous-decoupling analytic approximations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs' asymmetric-abundance machinery (or write a standalone solver) to integrate coupled Boltzmann equations for X, anti-X, and baryon chemical potentials through operator decoupling, replacing the instantaneous m_X/T_D approximation with a full numerical Omega_DM/Omega_B prediction.

route_step_status.reason: Chemical-potential relations for the XXLH_u operator plus electroweak sphalerons are a standard analytic equilibrium calculation done in the primary paper.
Thermal suppression of the X density via m_X/T_D is an analytic formula from the paper, including the bleed-off regime estimate, and needs no dedicated tool.

Standard phenomenology tools could compute signatures, but the card specifies no concrete UV completion (intermediate doublet, singlet Higgs, or dark gauge annihilation sector), so only model-dependent qualitative expectations exist.

gaps.description: The XXLH_u transfer operator and symmetric-component annihilation sector are defined only at framework level; without a normalized benchmark Lagrangian (doublet, singlet Higgs, or dark gauge completion) the direct, indirect, and collider signatures cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Fix an explicit UV completion of the XXLH_u operator with a specified annihilation mediator, and implement it as a FeynRules/micrOMEGAs model file so annihilation rates and search signatures become quantitative.

gaps.description: No public code tracks the coupled X-lepton-baryon chemical-potential evolution through sphaleron decoupling, including the lepton-number bleed-off regime where continued X-L transfer below sphaleron freeze-out depletes X number; the route's required chemical-potential solver and asymmetric-abundance calculator exist only as the paper's analytic approximations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build (or extend micrOMEGAs' asymmetric-abundance module into) a coupled Boltzmann/chemical-potential solver spanning sphaleron decoupling and operator decoupling, so the bleed-off Omega_DM/Omega_B prediction is numerical rather than an instantaneous-decoupling estimate.

route_step_status.reason: Chemical-potential relations under the new-gauge sphaleron interaction follow from charge counting, a pen-and-paper equilibrium calculation performed in the primary paper.
The thermally suppressed X density as a function of m_X/T_D is an analytic formula from the paper and requires no dedicated code.

Collider recast and annihilation tools exist generically, but the card fixes no concrete new gauge sector (W' mass, g_R, generation charges, singlet-doublet mixing), so signatures remain model-dependent qualitative statements.

gaps.description: The new non-Abelian gauge sector is specified only at framework level: no benchmark with fixed M_W', g_R, generation charge assignments, and singlet-doublet mixing exists from which annihilation rates, collider signatures, and the recast of W' mass bounds onto T_D can be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Define an explicit chiral gauge extension (e.g. a left-right variant with specified charges and the X1,X2,X3 mixing structure), normalize its couplings, and implement it in FeynRules plus micrOMEGAs and a collider recast framework so W' bounds and dark matter signatures become quantitative.

gaps.description: The rate and decoupling temperature of the exotic sphaleron of the new gauge group, which sets T_D and hence the predicted m_X, is not computed beyond electroweak-sphaleron analogy; no calculation of the new-gauge sphaleron rate as a function of gauge coupling and breaking scale exists in the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the exotic sphaleron energy and transition rate for the chosen gauge group and breaking pattern (adapting standard electroweak sphaleron rate calculations/lattice results to the new gauge coupling and scalar sector), yielding T_D(M_W', g_R) for use in the chemical-equilibrium step.

gaps.description: No public asymmetric-abundance code couples the chemical-potential network to the freeze-out of the new-gauge sphaleron transfer and to symmetric-component annihilation; the route's required chemical-potential solver and Boltzmann calculator exist only as instantaneous-decoupling analytic approximations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs' asymmetric-dark-matter machinery or write a standalone solver integrating coupled Boltzmann equations for X and Standard Model chemical potentials through sphaleron decoupling, producing numerical Omega_DM/Omega_B predictions.

route_step_status.reason: Sphaleron chemical-potential relations are standard pen-and-paper equilibrium algebra fully specified by the charge assignments in the card, so no tool is needed.
The Boltzmann-suppressed X number density is an analytic formula in m_X/T_D and degrees of freedom, reproduced directly from the primary paper.

Generic tools (micrOMEGAs/MadDM plus direct-detection recasts) can compute the signatures, but only after a concrete UV completion and symmetric-component annihilation channel are implemented as a model file, which the card says does not exist.

gaps.description: No machine-readable model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP model file) exists for the SU(2)_L doublet Xogenesis Lagrangian with its anomaly-cancelling partner and singlets X_S^0/X_S^-, so the symmetric-component annihilation, direct-detection cross sections, and collider expectations cannot be computed with standard pipelines.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the doublet-plus-singlet Xogenesis Lagrangian in FeynRules, export to micrOMEGAs (which supports asymmetric dark matter relic evolution) and MadDM, and use micrOMEGAs' built-in direct-detection module to recast the su2l_direct_detection constraint against modern xenon limits.

route_step_status.reason: Semi-analytic radial-infall UCMH profile prescriptions exist in the literature the card cites, but there is no public, simulation-calibrated code for PBH-seeded profiles including tidal survival (simulation_calibrated: no, tool_or_code null).
Converting a J factor and annihilation channel into gamma-ray and lepton source terms is an analytic formula using public spectra tables such as PPPC4DMID.

Public Galactic propagation codes (GALPROP/DRAGON) and Fermi-LAT data exist, but no public likelihood treats a UCMH point-source population plus diffuse emission for this scenario (card: no public likelihood included).
The redshift-dependent annihilation luminosity density is an analytic integral over the UCMH profile and abundance, doable by hand once the profile is chosen.

Energy-deposition machinery (f_eff transfer functions in DarkHistory/ExoCLASS-class codes) exists for homogeneous injection but must be extended with a UCMH-population boost history before it applies here.
CMB optical-depth and IGM thermal-history likelihoods exist publicly, but the card records no UCMH-specific likelihood implementation and the mapping to this source population is a required recast.

gaps.description: No simulation-calibrated model of WIMP density profiles around sub-Earth-mass PBH seeds, including tidal disruption and survival in the Galactic halo, exists; the boost factor of up to 1e5 rests on uncalibrated semi-analytic radial-infall profiles.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run high-resolution N-body/zoom simulations of WIMP accretion onto sub-Earth-mass PBHs through kinetic decoupling and free streaming, plus tidal-stripping evolution in a Milky Way potential, and release fitted profile and survival-fraction parameterizations as a public module.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for a PBH-seeded UCMH source population against Fermi-LAT point-source and isotropic diffuse gamma-ray data or against charged-lepton spectra; existing constraints assume smooth halos or standard subhalo populations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a population-synthesis likelihood that draws UCMH positions from the Galactic DM distribution, computes fluxes from the calibrated profile model, and compares to the Fermi-LAT point-source catalog and isotropic diffuse measurement, with GALPROP/DRAGON propagation for the leptonic channel.

gaps.description: Energy-injection codes for CMB/IGM constraints implement homogeneous annihilation only; the redshift-dependent UCMH boost to the annihilation luminosity after matter-radiation equality is not implemented in any public deposition/thermal-history pipeline.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend DarkHistory or ExoCLASS with a boost-factor module B(z) computed from the UCMH abundance and profile model, then propagate to ionization and temperature histories and constrain with Planck optical-depth and IGM temperature data.

route_step_status.reason: The four abundance contributions have analytic formulae quoted in the paper and IsaReD (Isajet/Isatools) covers the neutralino freeze-out, but no public coupled solver combines misalignment, thermal axino, NLSP-decay, and gravitino-cascade production with saxion/entropy effects, so the step works only in the paper's factorized approximation.

Public BBN energy-injection machinery exists (Jedamzik/Kawasaki-style bounds, ACROPOLIS-class codes), but the card records the step only as a recast target using literature limit curves, not an implemented pipeline for this neutralino NLSP lifetime, abundance, and hadronic branching.

No axino momentum distribution or transfer function is available (distribution_function_available is no, thermal_wdm_mapping unavailable), so the matter transfer function for the mixed cold-axion plus warm/hot-axino spectrum cannot currently be computed.

gaps.description: The axino phase-space distribution f(q) combining thermal production with nonthermal neutralino-NLSP-decay and gravitino-cascade components has not been derived, so the mixed cold/warm/hot transfer function cannot be computed and only crude m_axino and fraction flags stand in for structure-formation predictions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) for each axino production channel (thermal scattering/decay spectrum, decay kinematics of the neutralino NLSP and gravitino cascades with redshifting), sum weighted by the channel abundances, and feed it to CLASS/CAMB as one or more non-cold (ncdm) species to compute the mixed transfer function and half-mode scale.

gaps.description: Lyman-alpha and small-scale-structure limits exist only for thermal-relic WDM or sterile-neutrino mappings; no likelihood applies to a subdominant warm/hot axino admixture on a cold axion background, so the paper's 20 percent warm and 1 percent hot fraction flags cannot be replaced by a statistical constraint.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints for mixed cold-plus-noncold models, e.g. extend an existing Lyman-alpha emulator/likelihood to a two-parameter (fraction, free-streaming scale) mixed-dark-matter grid and interpolate limits applicable to the axino transfer functions from gap_1.

gaps.description: The BBN energy-injection constraint on the long-lived neutralino NLSP (lifetime, hadronic branching, abundance) is applied only by comparison to literature limit curves; no implemented pipeline computes light-element yields for the scanned PQMSSM points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the neutralino NLSP lifetime, abundance, and branching fractions from the spectrum calculation into an existing BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS to produce point-by-point light-element pass/fail and the allowed T_R window.

gaps.description: No public coupled relic-density solver combines axion misalignment, thermal axino production, and the two nonthermal channels with possible saxion decay and entropy production, which the route lists as required and the paper explicitly omits.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a PQMSSM relic pipeline coupling IsaReD (or micrOMEGAs) neutralino output with the axion misalignment and thermal/nonthermal axino production rates in one Boltzmann code, adding an optional saxion entropy-dilution branch.

route_step_status.reason: Standard SUSY spectrum generators (SuSpect-class tools) exist, but the No-Scale F-SU(5) boundary conditions at the elevated M_F scale with TeV-scale vector-like flippon RGE contributions are a customized private implementation the card says must be reproduced.
Given a sparticle spectrum, micrOMEGAs-class public codes compute the Bino relic density (with coannihilation) and sigma_SI for this MSSM-like neutralino sector.

Public recast frameworks (CheckMATE/MadAnalysis-class) cover generic SUSY cascades, but no validated implementation of the vector-like flippon production and high-jet-multiplicity signatures against modern LHC searches exists per the card.

gaps.description: No public spectrum generator implements the No-Scale F-SU(5) construction: M0=A=B_mu=0 boundary conditions imposed at the secondary unification scale M_F with flipped SU(5)xU(1)_X running modified by TeV-scale vector-like flippon multiplets; the paper relied on a customized private codebase.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the F-SU(5) model with vector-like multiplets in SARAH/SPheno (or patch SuSpect/SoftSUSY) with two-loop RGEs and the No-Scale boundary conditions at M_F, validating against the published golden-strip spectra, then chain the output SLHA files into micrOMEGAs.

gaps.description: The collider test of the golden strip rests on pre-Run-2 statements of LHC testability; no recast of the vector-like flippon production and high-multiplicity-jet SUSY cascade signatures against current LHC Run 2/3 search likelihoods has been implemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build the model in MadGraph via a UFO from the gap_1 SARAH implementation, generate flippon and gluino/squark cascade events, and recast against current multijet plus missing-energy and vector-like-quark searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 recast databases.

route_step_status.reason: The dark-atom spectrum with fine/hyperfine and SUSY-breaking splittings is standard nonrelativistic Coulombic bound-state math done analytically in the primary paper, so a null tool_or_code does not block it.

The dark recombination history requires a Boltzmann/recombination network for the supersymmetric atomic sector (including gaugino channels, molecules, and residual ionization); the card flags it as future work with no tool, and no public code covers this regime.

Inelastic recoil-rate formulas from epsilon and delta are analytic, but quantitative limits need atomic form factors and detector-specific recasting for which no likelihood or recast code is identified on the card.

Velocity-dependent Coulombic transfer cross sections can be computed semi-analytically, but comparison to halo-shape and Bullet Cluster bounds is a manual recast with no SIDM likelihood or atomic-scattering solver identified.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann/recombination code exists for the supersymmetric dark-atom sector: the dark recombination history, residual ionized fraction, and molecule/macroscopic bound-state formation (with photino as well as photon emission channels) are uncomputed, leaving the cosmological abundance of atoms versus ions undetermined.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a RECFAST/HyRec-style recombination network to a dark sector parameterized by (alpha_D, m_eD, m_pD, dark-sector temperature ratio), adding the supersymmetric bound-state multiplets and gaugino emission channels derived from the paper's spectrum, and couple its output ionized fraction to the perturbation step.

gaps.description: No linear transfer function exists for this model: the dark plasma undergoes dark acoustic oscillations and Coulomb-coupled damping before dark recombination, but the card records transfer_function_shape and all structure-formation entries as unknown, with no phase-space distribution or Boltzmann-hierarchy implementation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the tight-coupling dark-photon/dark-baryon perturbation equations for this sector and implement them in CLASS via an ETHOS-like parameterization (dark-radiation interaction rates from alpha_D and constituent masses), producing P(k) with the dark-acoustic-oscillation scale and Silk-like damping.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood or recast exists for inelastic dark-atom scattering with atomic form factors: the card's kinetic-mixing observable relies on order-of-magnitude benchmark cross sections from related papers rather than detector-level limits on (epsilon, delta, m_atom).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-atom charge-radius and inelastic form factors from the bound-state wavefunctions and implement the inelastic recoil spectrum in a standard direct-detection recast framework (e.g. DDCalc-style xenon likelihoods) to set limits in the (epsilon, delta, mass) plane.

gaps.description: Self-interaction constraints are applied only as rough recast targets: atom-atom scattering cross sections (including hyperfine-state dependence, recombination-enhanced channels, and molecular aggregation) are not computed for this model, and the quoted Bullet Cluster and halo-shape bounds predate calibrated SIDM simulations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute velocity-dependent atom-atom transfer cross sections by solving the multi-channel Schrodinger problem for dark hydrogen scattering (as done for atomic dark matter in the non-SUSY case), then compare against modern simulation-calibrated SIDM constraints at dwarf and cluster velocities.

route_step_status.reason: Mapping (Lambda, M_S) to the induced bilinear matter-parity breaking is a model-specific analytic scaling given in the source papers and needs no code.

Approximate NLSP and gravitino lifetime formulae are analytic, but precision values require a full superpartner spectrum with bilinear RPV, which public spectrum codes (e.g. SPheno) support but which is not wired up for this model.
The combined BBN/gamma-line/hidden-relic constraint is only a paper-level graphical overlay with likelihood_available approximate-or-no and no reusable likelihood file.

gaps.description: No reusable combined likelihood exists for the three constraints that define the allowed Lambda window: the catalytic-BBN NLSP lifetime bound, the Fermi-LAT gamma-line bound on the gravitino lifetime, and the hidden pseudo-NG overclosure check; the card only records paper-era approximate bounds needing recasting.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast module that combines an updated late-decay BBN injection code (AlterBBN or ACROPOLIS with catalytic Li-6 for charged NLSPs) with current Fermi-LAT gamma-ray line likelihoods, taking (tau_NLSP, tau_3/2, Omega_PNG h^2) as inputs and returning a joint likelihood over (Lambda, M_S, m_3/2).

gaps.description: The hidden pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone relic abundance Omega_PNG h^2 from SU(2) condensation is only estimated at paper level; no calculation of the hidden-sector thermal history and pseudo-NG freeze-out exists that could feed the overclosure check.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the hidden-sector temperature evolution and pseudo-NG annihilation cross sections after SU(2) condensation, then solve the hidden-sector Boltzmann equation (e.g. with micrOMEGAs' hidden-sector/two-temperature machinery or a custom integrator) parameterized by Lambda and the visible-hidden temperature ratio.

gaps.description: No pipeline computes precision tau_NLSP and tau_3/2 from a full supersymmetric spectrum with the induced bilinear matter-parity violation; the card relies on approximate analytic lifetime formulae tied to a reference spectrum.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model point in a public RPV-capable spectrum and decay calculator (SPheno/SARAH with bilinear RPV) to compute NLSP decay widths, and add the supergravity gravitino RPV decay widths as a small post-processing module.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level LOSP decay widths and branching ratios for the renormalizable stau-tau-X coupling are simple pen-and-paper formulae valid in the simplified setup.

Thermal gravitino yield formulae and the component sum are semi-analytic and reproducible, but the warm-fraction and momentum-distribution part of the output has no distribution function available and only a paper-level treatment.
The comparison uses paper-era BBN and Lyman-alpha/WMAP5 mixed cold/warm bounds with only approximate likelihoods and no public reusable likelihood.

gaps.description: No modern BBN energy-injection likelihood is wired up for late stau LOSP decays in this scenario; the card carries only the approximate paper-era BBN bound, and neutralino LOSP variants would additionally need a hadronic/electromagnetic injection recast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the LOSP abundance and lifetime through a current BBN injection code (ACROPOLIS or AlterBBN with electromagnetic/hadronic cascades and stau bound-state catalysis) to produce a pass/fail or chi-square surface over (tau_LOSP, LOSP yield).

gaps.description: The nonthermal momentum distribution of gravitinos from late stau or hidden-fermion X decays is not available (distribution_function_available is no), so the warm fraction f_WDM and free-streaming scale lambda_FS cannot be propagated to a linear transfer function.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-produced gravitino phase-space distribution f(q) from two-body decay kinematics redshifted from the decay epoch, and feed it to CLASS or CAMB as a tabulated non-cold dark matter species to compute mixed cold/warm transfer functions.

gaps.description: The mixed cold/warm small-scale constraint is inherited from a WMAP5-era Lyman-alpha analysis; no current mixed CDM+WDM Lyman-alpha likelihood or emulator is connected to bound f_WDM versus lambda_FS for this model.

micrOMEGAs is a named public Boltzmann solver adequate for coannihilating freeze-out, but the paper's model file for this Ma-model N1/N2 sector was not released (associated_code lists no repository), so the setup cannot be rerun as-is.
All three constraints have likelihood_available no/partial with recasting_needed yes; the XENON, LFV, and relic comparisons use 2012-era data and no likelihood implementation exists.

gaps.description: No public micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP model file exists for this radiative-neutrino-mass model with nearly degenerate N1/N2 and inert-doublet coannihilations; the paper's micrOMEGAs setup was private, so the relic-density colored regions cannot be reproduced or rescanned.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Ma-model Lagrangian (three N_i, inert doublet eta, Z2, complex Yukawa texture) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and rebuild the micrOMEGAs model file, validating against the paper's WMAP-era relic contours before updating to the Planck value.

gaps.description: No event-rate plus likelihood pipeline exists for the loop-induced inelastic photon-mediated scattering: the charge-charge/dipole-charge/dipole-dipole recoil spectra with inelastic N1-to-N2 kinematics and detector response have not been implemented, and no modern xenon likelihood (XENON1T actual data, XENONnT, LZ) has been recast onto (M_1, M_2 - M_1, M_eta, Im(h_2^* h_1)).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the paper's loop form factors into an inelastic-DM rate calculator (extend DDCalc or a WimPyDD-style package with delta-splitting kinematics and dipole/charge nuclear responses) and evaluate against published LZ/XENONnT likelihoods.

gaps.description: The charged-LFV constraint uses pre-MEG bounds with no likelihood; the analytic mu -> e gamma branching ratios have not been confronted with current MEG II limits or a proper likelihood over the Yukawa texture.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the model's radiative-decay branching-ratio formulas against the MEG II mu -> e gamma limit (and mu -> 3e / mu-e conversion projections) as a simple likelihood module joined to the relic/direct-detection scan.

route_step_status.reason: Partial widths and lifetime for the flavor-off-diagonal charged-lepton decays are closed-form expressions from the paper's ingredients, and PYTHIA 6.4 (named in associated_code) generates the resulting e+/e- injection spectra.

Public propagation codes of the class the card names exist (GALPROP/DRAGON-style), but the card lists only an approximate likelihood tied to 2012-era PAMELA/Fermi/H.E.S.S. fits, with recasting_needed yes and no model-specific public fit.
The phi phi -> h h cross section through s-channel S exchange is the paper's analytic benchmark formula, a pen-and-paper step.
The standard semi-analytic freeze-out estimate (x_f about 28, Omega_D h^2 about 0.1) is textbook math the paper already carries out for the benchmark.

gaps.description: The decaying-DM cosmic-ray comparison rests on 2012-era PAMELA/Fermi-LAT/H.E.S.S. excess fits with only an approximate borrowed likelihood; no pipeline propagates the model's e-tau/mu-tau decay spectra and confronts them with modern AMS-02 positron-fraction and CALET/DAMPE e+e- data over (m_phi, tau_phi, branching fractions).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate e+/e- spectra for the e-tau and mu-tau final states with PYTHIA 8 (replacing PYTHIA 6.4), propagate with GALPROP or DRAGON2 with a marginalized diffusion setup, and build a likelihood against AMS-02 positron fraction and DAMPE/CALET total e+e- flux, including a pulsar background component.

gaps.description: The relic density exists only as a single analytic benchmark that neglects scalar mixing (computational_representation is null and no model code is released), so the viable (m_phi, m_S, m_2, lambda) region cannot be mapped and the quoted Omega_D h^2 about 0.1 carries uncontrolled precision.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the pseudo-familon plus singlet-scalar potential (including S-h mixing) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and scan the relic density with micrOMEGAs, validating against the paper's x_f = 28 benchmark and updating the target to the Planck abundance.

route_step_status.reason: The higgsino-to-baryon asymmetry relation follows from the paper's chemical-potential equilibrium relations, a pen-and-paper calculation valid for the assumed heavy-sfermion spectrum.

The 'density-matrix evolution' named as tool_or_code is a method done by analytic estimate in the paper, not a public code; the route itself lists a density-matrix solver for higgsino oscillations as a required, unbuilt resource.
Both the direct-detection and indirect-detection likelihoods are recorded as unavailable and the step is explicitly a planned recast requiring current experimental likelihood tables.

gaps.description: No public numerical solver exists for the higgsino-antihiggsino density-matrix evolution through the low-temperature electroweak transition (oscillations driven by the m0 splitting, thermal damping, WW/ZZ annihilation, and expansion); the paper's analytic estimates cannot deliver the surviving asymmetric and regenerated symmetric densities that both detection observables depend on.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the quantum kinetic (density-matrix) equations for oscillating asymmetric dark matter — following the formalism of the oscillating-ADM literature — as a dedicated ODE solver over (mu, m0, T_EWPT, Y_h), outputting the symmetric fraction versus time and validating against the paper's analytic limits.

gaps.description: The inelastic direct-detection threshold statement (splitting below about 400 keV excluded by Z-mediated scattering) has never been recast onto modern xenon likelihoods; no implementation of the inelastic recoil spectrum for (mu, m0, sigma_n) against XENONnT/LZ/PandaX data exists.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the inelastic (delta = m0) Z-mediated recoil spectrum with standard halo kinematics in an inelastic-capable rate code (extend DDCalc/WimPyDD with splitting kinematics) and evaluate against published LZ and XENONnT likelihoods to obtain the modern minimum-splitting contour over mu = 200-1000 GeV.

gaps.description: No indirect-detection likelihood has been connected to the regenerated symmetric higgsino component: the sigma_ann v ~ 1e-26 (1 TeV/mu)^2 cm^3/s WW/ZZ rate weighted by the symmetric fraction has not been evaluated against Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal or CTA-class likelihoods.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the symmetric-fraction output of the gap_1 solver into the public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihood (WW/ZZ spectra from PPPC4DMID) to bound the (mu, m0) plane, rescaling the annihilation signal by the square of the symmetric fraction.

gaps.description: The required electroweak phase transition at T_EWPT ~ 1-10 GeV has no concrete, computable realization: the paper notes it may need degrees of freedom beyond the MSSM, so the abundance prediction is conditional on an unspecified scalar sector whose transition dynamics cannot currently be calculated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct an explicit extended-Higgs/singlet sector that delays the electroweak transition to 1-10 GeV and compute its finite-temperature effective potential and transition temperature with CosmoTransitions, recording the viable parameter map as a registry input.

route_step_status.reason: The scalaron-to-scalar decay width is a closed-form analytic formula in (m_phi, xi, mu) given explicitly in the primary paper, so a null tool_or_code is fine.

The yield/relic-abundance integration through Starobinsky reheating exists only as the paper's semi-analytic estimate; no reusable Boltzmann or reheating solver is cited, and the card lists such a solver under required_code_resources.

Public Boltzmann codes (CLASS/CAMB with a non-thermal ncdm distribution) can compute the transfer function, but the decay-produced f(q) for this model has not been implemented and the paper instead uses a rough v_eq velocity criterion, as the validity note ('needs a WDM/free-streaming recast') states.

gaps.description: No reusable code integrates scalaron-decay production of the nonminimally coupled scalar through R^2 reheating to a relic abundance; the yield step exists only as the paper's semi-analytic estimate, so Omega_phi h^2 (m_phi, xi, mu, T_rh) cannot be scanned reproducibly.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a small semi-analytic reheating module (Friedmann plus scalaron and scalar number-density Boltzmann equations with the coupling-dependent decay width) and validate it by reproducing the paper's 1.1 MeV viability threshold and the conformal suppression near xi = 1/6.

gaps.description: The warm/cold classification rests on an average-velocity-at-equality criterion; the decay-produced momentum distribution has not been propagated to a linear transfer function or confronted with a small-scale-structure (Lyman-alpha/subhalo) likelihood, and the card notes no dedicated Lyman-alpha likelihood was read.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-produced f(q) from the scalaron-decay kinematics, feed it to CLASS as a custom ncdm species to get the transfer-function cutoff, and map it to existing thermal-WDM Lyman-alpha and satellite-count bounds via a half-mode-mass matching.

route_step_status.reason: Writing the time-dependent mode frequency in the Starobinsky background from the R^2 parameters and the scalar effective mass is standard analytic/simple-ODE work given in the primary paper.

The nonadiabatic occupation-number calculation is done by analytic estimate only; no mode-function/Bogoliubov solver is cited, and the card explicitly lists one as a required-but-absent code resource with route_status planned.

Redshifting the number density to a present relic density is simple scaling arithmetic, but it requires an entropy/reheating normalization that the card marks as unresolved (depends_on_reheating_temperature unknown), so it is only partially specified.

gaps.description: No mode-function/Bogoliubov solver exists for gravitational particle production of a scalar with a scalaron-dependent effective mass at the end of R^2 inflation, so the occupation number, number density, and velocity dispersion of the superheavy relic cannot be computed beyond the paper's analytic estimate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a numerical mode-equation solver on the Starobinsky R^2 background (evolve the scalaron and scale factor, solve the scalar mode functions through the nonadiabatic mass transition, extract Bogoliubov beta_k), following the standard gravitational-production framework of Chung-Kolb-Riotto/Ema et al., and validate against the paper's 1e16 GeV viable-abundance benchmark.

gaps.description: The entropy/reheating normalization needed to convert the produced comoving number density into today's relic density is unspecified (the card marks reheating-temperature dependence unknown), leaving Omega_X h^2 undetermined even once the production spectrum is known.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the entropy injection history from scalaron decay in the same R^2 background (the reheating temperature follows from the scalaron width to Standard Model fields) and fold it into the redshift step so the relic density is a closed function of m_X and the fixed scalaron mass.

route_step_status.reason: Mapping the two-singlet potential parameters to tree-level couplings and annihilation/scattering amplitudes is standard pen-and-paper Higgs-portal algebra given in the primary equations.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Add a dark-recombination module (dark Saha/Peebles equations in alpha_prime and the degenerate constituent masses) plus millicharge and atomic-Compton momentum-exchange rates to CLASS's interacting-DM/ETHOS machinery, and evaluate the model against Planck rather than rescaled historical millicharged-DM bounds.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood is available for the doublet candidate's gauge-mediated spin-independent scattering: the card relies on a rescaled 2011 XENON100 limit (likelihood_available: no) and modern xenon limits were never applied.

route_step_status.reason: The scalar amplitude and tilt follow from standard slow-roll formulae applied to the explicit NH_uL flat-direction potential given in the card, a pen-and-paper calculation despite the null tool_or_code.

gaps.description: The perturbative reheating and thermalization history after NH_uL flat-direction inflation has not been computed with any identified tool; the quoted T_R ~ 1e6 GeV for m_phi ~ 1 TeV and the claim of efficient B-L thermalization of the sneutrino remain unverified, and T_R feeds both the relic calculation and the inflation consistency.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the inflaton decay rate from the h N H_u L superpotential coupling and solve the coupled inflaton-radiation Boltzmann equations (a small dedicated ODE code) to obtain T_R(h, m_phi) and verify B-L thermalization of the sneutrino.

gaps.description: The CMB constraint on the flat-direction inflaton uses only the amplitude and tilt normalization quoted in the 2012 primary paper; no Planck-era likelihood evaluation of (h, m_phi, A) exists (likelihood_available: no for cmb_flat_direction_inflation_target).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the NH_uL flat-direction potential in a slow-roll inflation pipeline (e.g. an ASPIC-style module) and confront the predicted (A_s, n_s, r) with the Planck 2018 likelihood to map the allowed (h, m_phi, A) region.

gaps.description: No direct-detection or collider recast exists for the right-handed sneutrino LSP: the card supplies no sneutrino-nucleon cross-section table (sigma_N status unknown), the search_recast step is only planned, and the cited SUSY-search context is generic rather than a model-specific likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Using the B-L/MSSM spectrum from the gap_1 implementation, compute the Z'-and-Higgs-mediated sneutrino-nucleon cross section with micrOMEGAs, evaluate against current LZ/XENONnT limits via DDCalc, and recast LHC Z' and superpartner searches with SModelS/CheckMATE.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Recreate the singlet-doublet model in FeynRules and publish the UFO/CalcHEP files, validating 2-to-2 static-limit rates and the three-body W f f-prime and t b W channels against the primary paper's benchmarks.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the event-record injection in the public WimpSim (or a modern equivalent such as the charon/HDMSpectra-based solar pipelines), reproducing the primary paper's Super-K and DeepCore detector comparisons, and release the patch.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs (named in required_code_resources and associated_code, with a public stock inert-doublet model) covers the relic-density, coannihilation, and sigma_SI outputs, but the paper's adaptation is private and the inflationary xi_i inputs and stability conditions are outside any tool the card identifies.

gaps.description: No public pipeline connects the multi-field Higgs-inflation sector (nonminimal couplings xi_1, xi_2, stability/perturbativity at the unitarity scale, pseudo-scalar direction effects on n_s, r, and non-Gaussianity) to the low-energy inert-doublet quartics; micrOMEGAs handles only the low-energy freeze-out side of the route.

gaps.description: The relic-density and light-H0 exclusion constraints carry only 'approximate' likelihoods with no likelihood_reference, so the WMAP-era allowed/excluded regions cannot be recast against modern data without a dedicated likelihood layer.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the micrOMEGAs inert-doublet output in a Planck-2018 Gaussian relic-density likelihood and a modern spin-independent direct-detection likelihood via DDCalc (LZ/XENONnT), replacing the paper's WMAP-era band and XENON100-era limits.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs (required_code_resources, and named in associated_code with a public stock inert-doublet model) covers Omega_H0 h^2 and sigma_SI, but the paper's specific adaptation is private and the card notes a precision recast requires dedicated implementation.

gaps.description: The loop-level wino-nucleon scattering prediction (sigma_SI ~ 1e-46-1e-48 cm^2 including two-loop gluon contributions) exists only as published formulas, with no public code producing Wilson coefficients for the heavy-Higgsino/scalar decoupling limit.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the Hisano et al. electroweak-loop matching (including two-loop gluon operators) into a small public module feeding DirectDM/DDCalc, parameterized by m_wino and M_SUSY with nucleon matrix-element inputs.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt the ATLAS/CMS HEPData tracklet efficiency maps for disappearing-track analyses inside a recast framework (CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 long-lived module) and validate against the published pure-wino exclusion curves before applying to the PGM gaugino spectrum.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the Z3 scalar potential via FeynRules/CalcHEP model files for micrOMEGAs, which supports semi-annihilation natively, and validate against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.105 benchmark with 54 percent semi-annihilation fraction.

gaps.description: Direct-detection and Higgs-invisible constraints on the mixed singlet-doublet Z3 scalar exist only as XENON100-era context recast from the minimal Z3 singlet model, with no likelihood implemented for the primary model's singlet-doublet-mixed sigma_SI and invisible width.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the micrOMEGAs sigma_SI for the mixed x1 state into DDCalc with LZ/XENONnT likelihoods and evaluate the invisible Higgs width against current LHC fits via HiggsTools, replacing the recast minimal-Z3 XENON100/40-percent-branching context.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the Z4 potential as CalcHEP/FeynRules model files in micrOMEGAs 5+, which handles two dark matter components with semi-annihilation and inter-sector conversion, validating against the paper's total h^2 about 0.1 benchmark with comparable sector abundances.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a DDCalc-based pipeline to sum component-weighted recoil spectra (xi_1 sigma_1 + xi_2 sigma_2 at their respective masses) and evaluate against LZ/XENONnT likelihoods, replacing the source's single-component XENON100-era normalized-cross-section comparison.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the relevant ATLAS/CMS SUSY analyses (7 TeV originals or, preferably, modern 13 TeV multilepton/ditau+MET successors) in a public recast framework such as MadAnalysis5-PAD or CheckMATE, generate cNMSSM singlino-cascade event samples with the NMSSMTools+MadGraph+Pythia+Delphes chain, and validate against the efficiency-ratio pattern reported in the paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the jets+MET analyses (7 TeV originals or modern 13 TeV successors) in MadAnalysis5-PAD or CheckMATE, run the NMSSMTools+MadGraph+Pythia+Delphes chain over the three benchmark lines, and validate the recast against the paper's 1/3-1/7 efficiency-drop envelope and 0.9-0.75 M_1/2 bound reductions.

gaps.description: Standard Boltzmann solvers compute the singlino relic density only in standard Big-Bang cosmology, where generic sNMSSM points overclose; there is no card-consistent tool for evaluating the relic abundance under the modified expansion or entropy histories the model invokes as viability escapes, so the relic flag cannot distinguish which nonstandard history rescues a given point.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a micrOMEGAs-based NMSSM relic calculation with a parameterized nonstandard pre-BBN history (modified Hubble rate and late entropy injection, as in low-reheating-temperature freeze-out treatments) so the overclosure flag can be evaluated as a function of the cosmological-history parameters alongside the resonance-annihilation option.

route_step_status.reason: The Sommerfeld factor S(v) for scalar-mediated Yukawa potentials is a standard analytic/Hulthen-approximation calculation in the nonrelativistic light-mediator regime and needs no dedicated tool.

The paper used a custom private integrator, and while a public coupled number-density/temperature Boltzmann solver of this class exists (DRAKE), its default moment-based treatment relies on the same Maxwellian approximation the card flags as unreliable in resonant Sommerfeld regions.

ETHOS-style transfer-function mappings from the decoupling temperature to M_cut exist, but the card states they are approximate without the full Boltzmann hierarchy and that no exact relation has been established for strongly resonant cases decoupling near or after matter-radiation equality.

gaps.description: No public coupled chemical/kinetic-decoupling solver validated for this model's resonant Sommerfeld regime evolves the full phase-space distribution: the Maxwellian second-moment approximation used by the paper (and by moment-based modes of DRAKE-class solvers) can fail in resonant and Ramsauer-Townsend-like regions where the reannihilation-driven relic shift reaches orders of magnitude.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public coupled Boltzmann solver (DRAKE) with its full f(p) phase-space evolution mode configured for scalar/pseudoscalar leptophilic mediators, including velocity-dependent Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation and self-scattering kernels, and validate against the paper's Y-y benchmark trajectories and the standard freeze-out limit.

gaps.description: The exact relation between the effective decoupling temperature and the smallest-protohalo cutoff mass M_cut has not been derived for strongly resonant cases where asymptotic free streaming is reached near or after matter-radiation equality, so the quoted O(10^-10) to O(10) M_sun cutoffs are only approximate in exactly the most extreme regions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the linear matter power cutoff for late (post-equality) effective decoupling by solving the full perturbed Boltzmann hierarchy with the model's velocity-dependent annihilation and self-scattering terms in an ETHOS-parameterized modified CLASS, replacing the standard T_kd-to-M_cut fitting formulae in this regime.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists that confronts the model's predicted sub-Earth-to-stellar-mass protohalo cutoff and its velocity-dependent scalar/pseudoscalar self-interaction with data: existing MW-satellite, stream, and lensing likelihoods probe halo masses far above the predicted M_cut range, and SIDM halo-structure bounds require a mediator-specific transfer-cross-section recast not packaged anywhere.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast layer that maps (m_chi, m_s, m_p, couplings) to sigma_T/m over dwarf-to-cluster velocities for spin-0 mediator exchange and evaluates it against published SIDM constraint surfaces, and couple the predicted M_cut to minihalo-sensitive probes (pulsar timing, photometric microlensing, and annihilation-boost limits from Fermi dwarf likelihoods) in one composite likelihood.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public photodisintegration code (ACROPOLIS) or AlterBBN to accept a parameterized photon-cooling factor modifying the eta(t) and photon-temperature history between BBN and recombination, run it over the zeta_X-tau_X plane with JINA REACLIB rates, and validate by reproducing the paper's allowed island and its photon-cooling-only deuterium overproduction.
