gaps.description: No public quantum-kinetic solver evolves the N2,3 density-matrix equations from sphaleron freeze-out down to T about 100 MeV with the required near-degeneracy (Delta M below 1e-6 eV at M about 2 GeV), so the lepton asymmetry that drives resonant N1 production and links it to the BAU cannot be computed end to end.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing public leptogenesis-via-oscillations density-matrix code to the low-temperature regime, adding hadronic-plasma susceptibilities and rates below the QCD transition and stiff-degeneracy-safe integration, validated against the published |mu_alpha| about 8e-6 benchmark.

gaps.description: There is no end-to-end structure-formation likelihood for the resonantly produced N1: the colder nonthermal momentum distribution must be propagated into a transfer function and compared to Lyman-alpha data, but the card provides no pipeline connecting f(p) to a Ly-alpha likelihood, so the structure verdict rests on qualitative WDM-bound arguments.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed sterile-dm-style resonant distribution functions into CLASS/CAMB as a non-cold relic (ncdm with tabulated f(p)), and evaluate the resulting flux-power suppression against a public Lyman-alpha likelihood or WDM emulator over the (M1, sin^2(2 theta_1), asymmetry) grid.

gaps.description: X-ray line constraints (NuSTAR Galactic Center, M31, cluster and diffuse fields) exist only as published exclusion curves, not as reusable target-specific likelihoods with halo-profile and background systematics, preventing consistent statistical combination over the 1-50 keV window.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Package the NuSTAR GC/M31 line-search likelihoods (flux versus line energy with J-factor and background nuisance parameters) as a reusable module keyed to (M1, sin^2(2 theta_1)) with an explicit dark-matter-fraction rescaling.

route_step_status.reason: The freeze-out estimates are analytic limiting-regime formulas that the card itself flags as approximate in the intermediate (semi-relativistic) GeVin freeze-out region, where a numerical Boltzmann treatment is needed.
The GeVin decay width, required entropy factor S_req, and reheating temperature T_r follow from standard analytic decay/entropy-injection formulas that are simple pen-and-paper math.

The Z-width bound is a clean analytic estimate, but the Lyman-alpha limit is obtained by rescaling a nonresonant WDM mass bound by S_req^(1/3) rather than from a dedicated transfer-function calculation, which the card notes a CLASS/CAMB recast would improve.

gaps.description: No numerical Boltzmann solver covers the intermediate GeVin freeze-out regime between the relativistic and nonrelativistic analytic limits, leaving the GeVin abundance (and hence the entropy dilution S_req that sets the keVin relic density) approximate exactly where the M_2 of a few GeV benchmarks sit.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the freeze-out Boltzmann equation with full relativistic Fermi-Dirac statistics and the suppressed Z-mediated cross sections (e.g. via micrOMEGAs with the epsilon-suppressed Z couplings implemented, or a small standalone solver), mapping S_req over the (M_2, epsilon_2, eta) plane.

gaps.description: The structure-formation bound on M_1 is a rescaled nonresonant-WDM mass limit (S_req^(1/3) scaling) rather than a transfer function computed from the diluted keVin momentum distribution, so the quoted lowest M_1 around 1.5 keV carries an uncontrolled mapping uncertainty.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the post-dilution keVin phase-space distribution, insert it as a tabulated ncdm f(p) in CLASS/CAMB to compute the linear transfer function, and evaluate it against a Lyman-alpha WDM likelihood or emulator to replace the rescaled bound over the (M_1, S_req) plane.

route_step_status.reason: The background energy-transfer equations with Gamma = alpha H are simple coupled ODEs solvable analytically or with trivial numerics; no dedicated tool is needed.

The paper's modified CAMB implementation is private and unreleased; public CLASS/CAMB include decaying-CDM-to-dark-radiation modules only for constant Gamma, so the Gamma = alpha H law and its perturbation equations must be re-implemented.
WMAP7, ACT, and SPT likelihood packages are public (and Planck-era successors exist), so the likelihood step is served once model spectra can be produced.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-solver implementation exists for CDM decaying to dark radiation with the time-dependent rate Gamma = alpha H; the paper's modified CAMB patch was never released, and the stock CLASS/CAMB decaying-CDM modules assume a constant decay rate, so neither the late-growing Delta N_eff(a) background nor the coupled perturbation hierarchy for the massless daughter can currently be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the existing dcdm/dark-radiation sector in CLASS to accept Gamma = alpha H (background energy transfer plus the paper's perturbation equations for the massive parent and massless daughter), validate against the published alpha < 0.027-0.028 WMAP7+ACT/SPT limits, then rerun with Planck/ACT-DR6/SPT-3G likelihoods.

gaps.description: The scalar-oscillation timing condition (oscillation onset T_osc ~ 100 eV before matter-radiation equality) is only checked against Lyman-alpha/SDSS matter-power bounds by rough analytic recasting; no quantitative matter-power or Lyman-alpha likelihood evaluation exists for the late-oscillating scalar CDM realization.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the linear matter power spectrum for the late-oscillating scalar (axion-like suppression scale set by m_phi and T_osc, e.g. with axionCAMB-style fluid equations added to the modified CLASS) and confront it with a public Lyman-alpha flux-power compressed likelihood or emulator to turn the timing condition into a quantitative bound on m_phi and T_osc.

route_step_status.reason: Mapping operator dimensions and m_d to the mixing angle theta_d and scale M is straightforward EFT power-counting done by hand in the paper.

Public resonant-production solvers (e.g. sterile-dm for Shi-Fuller production) cover the standard lepton-asymmetry case, but the low-reheating-temperature and inflaton-decay production histories of this model are outside their assumed thermal history and would need modification.

CLASS/CAMB ncdm sectors can take a tabulated momentum distribution to a transfer function, but the card only has an approximate T/m rescaling for the diluted thermal case and no Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood to evaluate the resulting cutoff.

The Delta N_eff and entropy-dilution bookkeeping is analytic, but the required dilution factor of order 1e4 depends on supercooling of a strongly coupled confinement transition that the paper only treats with approximate hidden-sector thermodynamics.

gaps.description: No production solver covers this model's non-standard sterile-neutrino production histories: resonant production with a large lepton asymmetry at low reheating temperature and direct inflaton-decay production; existing public codes for resonant Shi-Fuller production assume a standard high-temperature radiation-dominated history.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public resonant-production code (e.g. sterile-dm) with a low-reheat background evolution and an inflaton-decay source term to output full momentum distributions f(p) over the (m_d, theta_d, lepton asymmetry, T_R) space.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator evaluation exists for this model's non-thermal momentum distributions; the card translates bounds only through an approximate thermal T/m free-streaming rescaling, which cannot capture resonant or inflaton-decay spectra.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the model momentum distributions through CLASS ncdm to obtain transfer functions and evaluate them with a public Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator/compressed likelihood (area-criterion or MIKE/HIRES+XQ-100 style), replacing the m_nrp > 10 keV proxy translation.

gaps.description: The entropy dilution factor Delta ~ 1e4 required by the thermal variant depends on the degree of supercooling of the hidden-sector confining first-order phase transition, which is strongly coupled and was only estimated analytically; no nonperturbative calculation of the transition (latent heat, nucleation temperature, entropy release) exists for this composite sector.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the confinement-transition thermodynamics nonperturbatively (lattice study of the hidden gauge group's deconfinement transition, or a calibrated holographic/PNJL effective model) and couple the resulting entropy injection to the freeze-out calculation, e.g. via a CosmoTransitions-style nucleation analysis where an effective potential is available.

gaps.description: X-ray decay-line constraints on (m_d, sin^2 2theta_d) are applied only by quoting literature exclusion curves; no reusable X-ray line likelihood rescaled to this model's production-dependent sterile abundance is available.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble the published X-ray flux limits (Chandra/XMM/NuSTAR blank-sky and M31/dwarf compilations) into a digitized likelihood in the (m_d, theta_d, f_sterile) plane that scales with the abundance fraction output by the production solver.

route_step_status.reason: SOFTSUSY (spectra, m_h, NLSP identity) and micrOMEGAs (neutralino freeze-out abundance) are public, maintained, and cover the mGMSB parameter space used by the paper.
The superWIMP abundance Omega_G = (m_G/m_NLSP) Omega_NLSP is a one-line analytic rescaling of the micrOMEGAs output.
The bino-to-gravitino-plus-photon lifetime is a standard closed-form supergravity formula, and the tau < 1 s BBN criterion is a simple analytic check.
The comoving free-streaming length is a standard analytic integral of the decay-produced gravitino velocity to matter-radiation equality.

gaps.description: The warm-gravitino structure-formation test is reduced to a single analytic lambda_FS ~ 0.1 Mpc estimate; no transfer function computed from the actual decay-produced (non-thermal, delta-like injection) gravitino phase-space distribution exists, and no matter-power or Lyman-alpha likelihood is attached, so constr_warm_fs cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the gravitino momentum distribution from the exponential NLSP decay (monochromatic injection redshifted through the decay epoch), feed it to CLASS as a tabulated ncdm distribution to obtain T(k), and evaluate against a public Lyman-alpha/Milky-Way-satellite half-mode-mass constraint instead of the lambda_FS rule of thumb.

gaps.description: The BBN safety of the late-decaying TeV neutralino is enforced only through the tau_NLSP < 1 s lifetime criterion; the electromagnetic (and any subdominant hadronic) energy injection from the photon+gravitino decay is not propagated through an actual BBN network, so the constraint boundary near tau ~ 0.1-1 s is uncalibrated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the benchmark (m_NLSP, m_G, tau, abundance) grid through a public late-decay BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS to replace the 1-second criterion with element-abundance-based exclusion contours.

route_step_status.reason: The parity bookkeeping that identifies the stable states is analytic, but it needs an actual low-energy E6SSM-with-inert-sector spectrum, and no spectrum-generator implementation (e.g. a SARAH/FlexibleSUSY model file) is identified in the card.

No multi-component relic Boltzmann calculation exists for this model: micrOMEGAs supports two-component dark matter in principle, but no E6SSM inert-sector model implementation is available and the computation was not performed in the source or the batch.

Once the eV inert-neutralino abundance and decoupling temperature are known, hot-DM/N_eff limits follow from standard CLASS ncdm plus CMB likelihood machinery, but the required hidden-sector decoupling calculation through the heavy Z-prime has not been done.

gaps.description: No spectrum-generator or relic-density model implementation exists for this E6-inspired model with custodial Z_H2, matter parity, and the inert Higgs/singlino sector; consequently neither the stable-state spectrum (s1) nor the two-component (ordinary neutralino plus lightest inert state) relic abundance (s2) can be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model (superpotential W_IH with lambda_alpha, f_alpha, f_tilde_alpha couplings, U(1)_N gauge sector, and discrete-symmetry assignments) in SARAH to generate FlexibleSUSY/SPheno spectrum code and CalcHEP model files, then use micrOMEGAs' two-component dark-matter mode to solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the exotic-parity and R-parity relics.

gaps.description: For the eV-scale inert-neutralino variant there is no derivation of the hidden-state thermal decoupling history through the heavy Z-prime (decoupling temperature, temperature ratio, resulting Delta N_eff and hot-DM fraction), so the hot-dark-matter recast in step s3 cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the Z-prime-mediated interaction rates and decoupling temperature of the light inert neutralinos as a function of M_Z' and the singlet VEV, compute their temperature ratio and Delta N_eff, and evaluate the hot fraction with CLASS ncdm against Planck CMB plus BAO likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: Every ingredient of this monolithic step is served by public tools or closed-form formulas (SOFTSUSY/SPheno-class spectra and m_h, micrOMEGAs freeze-out, analytic superWIMP rescaling, lifetime, lambda_FS, and standard EDM expressions), but no integrated implementation exists and the card names only micrOMEGAs, so the combined pipeline must be assembled and no likelihoods are attached.

gaps.description: The route is a single unimplemented 'compute' step: no assembled pipeline links mGMSB inputs (Lambda, tan beta, m_chi, m_G, T_R) through spectrum generation, neutralino freeze-out, and the analytic superWIMP post-processing (Omega_G h^2, tau_chi, lambda_FS, d_e, m_h), so none of the paper's allowed-region contours can currently be reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire together SOFTSUSY (or SPheno) for the mGMSB spectrum and Higgs mass, micrOMEGAs for the neutralino freeze-out abundance, and a short post-processing module implementing the superWIMP rescaling, the neutralino-to-gravitino lifetime, the free-streaming integral, and one-loop EDM formulas; validate against the paper's quoted allowed/excluded regions.

gaps.description: The small-scale-structure and BBN tests are only threshold criteria (lambda_FS < 0.5 Mpc, tau_chi < 0.1-1 s) with 'approximate' likelihoods; no transfer-function-based matter-power/Lyman-alpha likelihood for the decay-produced gravitino spectrum and no element-abundance BBN injection calculation exist for this scenario.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the non-thermal gravitino momentum distribution from late neutralino decay, obtain T(k) via CLASS ncdm and evaluate a public Lyman-alpha or satellite-count likelihood in place of the 0.5 Mpc cut, and run the decay injection through a public BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS to replace the lifetime cut.

route_step_status.reason: The hylogenesis reheating/asymmetry Boltzmann system exists only as main-text equations with no public solver; the route itself lists a custom Boltzmann solver as a required resource.
Symmetric-depletion cross sections are given as closed-form appendix annihilation formulae and are simple analytic evaluations.
The BBN check is a pen-and-paper comparison of the pseudoscalar lifetime from Higgs-sector mixing against the quoted tau_a < 1 s criterion.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements the low-temperature-reheating hylogenesis system (modulus/X decays, CP-asymmetric baryon-number generation, and Higgs-portal symmetric depletion into light pseudoscalars) needed to compute the asymmetric relic yield for this variant.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the main-text hylogenesis Boltzmann equations (reheating, X decay asymmetry, hidden-sector annihilation) as a standalone numerical solver, e.g. a Python/ODE code or an extension of micrOMEGAs' asymmetric freeze-out machinery, with the appendix aa annihilation channel swapped in for the U(1)' depletion term.

gaps.description: The BBN constraint on the light pseudoscalar is only a crude lifetime cut (tau_a < 1 s) rather than a proper light-element abundance calculation for GeV-scale electromagnetic/hadronic injection, so the exclusion boundary in (m_a, theta_aA) is approximate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the pseudoscalar decay spectrum through a public BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS or AlterBBN to replace the one-second lifetime criterion with an actual light-element likelihood over (m_a, tau_a).

route_step_status.reason: Low-temperature-reheating asymmetry generation exists only as primary-paper equations; no public code solves the modulus/X-decay Boltzmann system and the route lists a custom Boltzmann solver as required.
Hidden-sector annihilation/transfer depletion between psi and phi states is only paper-level equations; no public solver covers this multi-state hidden U(1)' freeze-out during nonstandard reheating.
Applying the quoted WMAP7 energy-injection bound to the residual annihilation rate is a simple analytic comparison.
The IND cross section from the baryon-transfer operator scale and masses is an analytic-formula computation supplied by the primary paper.
No IND event generator or Super-K detector-level recast exists; nuclear effects, meson kinematics, and detector selections are explicitly outside the primary paper.
The elastic recoil rate through Z' kinetic mixing is a standard analytic dark-photon-mediated cross-section calculation.

Public collider recast frameworks (MadGraph plus CheckMATE/MadAnalysis-style tools) cover monojet and vector-like-quark searches, but no model implementation of the baryon-transfer mediators exists and the operator mapping depends on SUSY-breaking insertions.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements the three-stage hylogenesis cosmology: low-temperature modulus reheating, CP-asymmetric X decays generating equal and opposite baryon numbers, and hidden U(1)' annihilation/transfer reactions among psi and phi states.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the primary-paper reheating and hidden-sector Boltzmann equations as a dedicated numerical solver (coupled ODEs for modulus, X, visible and hidden asymmetries, and symmetric fractions), validated against the paper's benchmark scans and baryon-number-conservation test.

gaps.description: No induced-nucleon-decay event generator or Super-Kamiokande detector-level recast exists to convert the baryon-transfer operator into meson spectra with nuclear effects and detector acceptances, which blocks the model's most distinctive observable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build an IND event generator producing kaon/pion momentum spectra for the hyperon and neutron portals including Fermi motion and nuclear absorption, and recast published Super-K nucleon-decay selections onto the shifted kinematic windows to obtain acceptance-corrected limits.

gaps.description: No model implementation (e.g. UFO) of the vector-like color-triplet and X baryon-transfer mediators exists for collider recasting, and the mapping from monojet/dijet limits to the hylogenesis operator depends on unmodeled SUSY-breaking insertions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the mediator sector in FeynRules/UFO, generate signals in MadGraph, and recast modern ATLAS/CMS monojet and vector-like-quark searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis, including the SUSY-breaking operator-generation dependence as an explicit parameter.

route_step_status.reason: pMSSM spectrum generation is covered by the public SOFTSUSY and Suspect codes named in the card.

micrOMEGAs publicly covers the NLSP freeze-out density, but the NLSP-to-gravitino decay widths and branching fractions rely on a privately modified SUSY-HIT, and thermal gravitino production needs an explicit reheating assumption.

The ATLAS MET/non-MET/HSCP coverage was obtained with a private MadGraph/PGS-style fast-simulation recast; public frameworks exist for MET searches but the long-lived and non-MET analysis implementations are not publicly reproducible.

gaps.description: The NLSP-to-gravitino decay module (lifetimes and hadronic/electromagnetic branching fractions for varying NLSP identity and gravitino mass from eV to TeV) exists only as a private modification of SUSY-HIT, so tau_NLSP and injection spectra cannot be recomputed publicly.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the goldstino-coupling NLSP decay widths (suppressed by the SUSY-breaking scale F) as a public extension of SUSY-HIT or a micrOMEGAs add-on module, covering neutralino, slepton, stop, and gluino NLSP cases.

gaps.description: The BBN/CMB/diffuse-background late-decay constraint is applied via approximate digitized hadronic and electromagnetic injection curves with approximate decay-product mapping (notably for colored NLSP hadronization and neutrino limits), not a public likelihood in (tau_NLSP, abundance, branching fractions).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a public likelihood interpolating modern BBN injection bounds (Kawasaki-Kohri-Moroi-type curves, or ACROPOLIS extended to hadronic injection and long lifetimes) over NLSP lifetime, yield, and hadronic/electromagnetic branching fractions, including a colored-NLSP hadronization treatment.

gaps.description: Collider coverage of the gravitino model set rests on private fast-simulation recasts of 7/8 TeV ATLAS analyses; the HSCP, displaced/late-decay, and other non-MET searches that dominate gravitino-LSP sensitivity lack public, up-to-date recast implementations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the search set in public recast frameworks (CheckMATE/MadAnalysis with Delphes, plus dedicated long-lived-particle recast tools such as SModelS LLP or HSCP efficiency maps) and update from 7/8 TeV to current LHC analyses.

route_step_status.reason: pMSSM spectrum and neutralino-composition generation is covered by the public SOFTSUSY and Suspect codes named in the card.
Thermal neutralino relic abundance and elastic scattering cross sections for arbitrary pMSSM points are fully covered by public micrOMEGAs, including coannihilation.

The ATLAS coverage estimate uses a private reproduced/rescaled fast-simulation recast of 7/8 TeV analyses; public recast frameworks exist but this analysis suite is not publicly packaged and is outdated.

gaps.description: The collider filter on the neutralino pMSSM model set is a private fast-simulation recast of early 7/8 TeV ATLAS MET and non-MET analyses with no per-point public likelihood, so present-day exclusion statements over the model set cannot be reproduced or updated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rebuild the collider stage on public recast tooling (MadGraph plus Delphes with CheckMATE/MadAnalysis analysis implementations, complemented by SModelS simplified-model limits) using current LHC analyses, and publish per-point coverage likelihoods for the model set.

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the four-axion see-saw mass/decay-constant matrix from the Lambda_i hierarchy is pen-and-paper linear algebra given in the primary paper.
The QCD-axion misalignment relic abundance from (f_a, m_a, theta_i) follows standard analytic misalignment formulas, though the result inherits the model's unspecified initial-condition assumptions.
Public CLASS/CAMB and the axionCAMB extension cover CMB and matter-power computation for CDM-like QCD axions and ultralight-axion fractions including isocurvature modes.

Public Planck isocurvature and LSS likelihood pipelines (Cobaya/MontePython) exist and cover the generic axion case, but no likelihood was run and the model-specific isocurvature amplitude is not yet derivable from the card's parameters.

gaps.description: The axionic see-saw specifies the Lambda_1-Lambda_4 potential hierarchy but not the cosmological initial conditions (inflationary scale H_infl, initial misalignment angles, PQ-breaking epoch relative to inflation, topological-defect content) needed to turn the four-axion system into a unique prediction for Omega_a h^2 and the isocurvature fraction.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the coupled evolution of the four mass-eigenstate axions during and after inflation for the see-saw potential, parameterized by H_infl and the initial angle vector, producing the misalignment abundance and isocurvature amplitude as explicit functions of the Lambda_i hierarchy that can be fed to axionCAMB and a Planck isocurvature likelihood run.

route_step_status.reason: The one-loop Higgs diphoton amplitude is a standard closed-form analytic expression given in the primary paper and needs no dedicated tool.
micrOMEGAs handles this standard freeze-out/coannihilation calculation, but the card states no public model files exist, so the implementation must be rebuilt before the step can be run.

Direct-detection comparison is feasible with standard SI/SD machinery, but no likelihood is available (likelihood_available: no), the quoted XENON100/COUPP limits are outdated, and the CMS mono-photon bound needs a dedicated collider recast.

gaps.description: No public micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP model files exist for the vector-like lepton sector; the original relic-density implementation is private, so the freeze-out, resonance, and E_1 coannihilation calculation cannot be reproduced or scanned.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the vector-like lepton Lagrangian in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and rerun micrOMEGAs for relic density and SI/SD cross sections, validating against the paper's Z/Higgs resonance dips at 45 and 62 GeV.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for any of the model's constraints: the Higgs diphoton fit uses 2012-era data, direct-detection comparisons rely on superseded XENON100/COUPP limits, and the CMS mono-photon spin-dependent bound is not applicable without a dedicated simulation-based recast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a combined likelihood using a modern Higgs signal-strength fit (e.g. Lilith or HiggsSignals) for R_gamma_gamma, DDCalc with current LZ/XENONnT and PICO likelihoods for SI/SD scattering, and a MadGraph+recast (CheckMATE/MadAnalysis) implementation of compressed-spectrum LEP/LHC charged-lepton searches.

route_step_status.reason: Analytic expressions for thermal axino/saxion production and dissipation exist in the paper, but the card flags the thermally produced saxion yield as only approximated from axino production logic.

No public code solves the coupled saxion-axino-axion-neutralino-radiation Boltzmann system with coherent oscillation, thermal dissipation, and decays; the card lists no tool and identifies only a related private calculation as a template.

Comparing Delta N_eff and decay times to CMB/BBN limits is standard once abundances exist, but the card states no public likelihood was identified (likelihood_available: no/partial) and a data-release-specific recast is required.

gaps.description: The thermally produced saxion abundance is only approximated by analogy with axino production; an exact thermal saxion production/dissipation rate in the SUSY PQ plasma (including the thermal-log potential regime) has not been derived for this setup.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the saxion thermal production rate from the colored PQ-sector couplings using hard-thermal-loop resummed finite-temperature field theory, following the methods used for axino thermal production, and tabulate it as a function of T_R, F_a, and the PQ Yukawas.

gaps.description: No public coupled Boltzmann solver evolves the axion supermultiplet cosmology of this model: saxion coherent oscillation with thermal deformation and dissipation, thermal axino/saxion yields, saxion decays to axions/gluons, entropy injection, and the resulting axion cold component and Delta N_eff.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a dedicated coupled Boltzmann code (e.g. extending public mixed axion-neutralino freeze-out codes such as the Bae-Baer-Lessa-type setup) with inputs (F_a, T_R, m_sigma, initial saxion amplitude, branching fractions) and outputs (Y_sigma, Y_axino, Omega_a, Delta N_eff, dilution factor), validated against the paper's dissipation on/off limits.

gaps.description: No likelihood module exists to confront the model's Delta N_eff, entropy injection, and late saxion decays with current CMB and BBN data; the card records likelihood_available no/partial and recasting_needed for both constraints.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a constraint module combining the Planck Delta N_eff posterior, AlterBBN/PArthENoPE light-element yields with energy injection from saxion decays, and relic-density consistency, callable on the Boltzmann-solver outputs.

route_step_status.reason: The flippon-enhanced RGE spectrum generator is a proprietary modification of SuSpect 2.34 that the card explicitly flags as unavailable, so the spectrum cannot be reproduced with public code.
micrOMEGAs handles bino-stau coannihilation freeze-out from an MSSM-like weak-scale spectrum, which is exactly this step's task once the spectrum is supplied.

Public recast frameworks exist for SUSY multijet/stop searches, but the card notes only 2012-era LHC7/8 context and states a modern analysis requires current detector simulations, so a dedicated recast is still needed.
The p -> e+ pi0 lifetime estimate from M_32 is a standard analytic GUT formula given in the primary paper.

Neutralino gamma/Z line energies and internal-bremsstrahlung spectra for compressed stau-neutralino spectra are covered by standard public SUSY annihilation-spectrum machinery (DarkSUSY/micrOMEGAs class), given the spectrum.

Fermi-LAT line-search results and analysis tools are public, but the card states no current likelihood for this model's 130-145 GeV line/IB prediction was built, so a model-specific recast is required.

gaps.description: The F-SU(5) spectrum calculation requires flippon-enhanced RGEs implemented only in a proprietary modification of SuSpect 2.34; no public spectrum generator reproduces the No-Scale Flipped SU(5) strip, which every downstream observable (relic density, Higgs mass, collider signatures, gamma line, proton decay) depends on.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the flipped SU(5) x U(1)_X boundary conditions and TeV vector-like flippon RGE contributions in a public framework (SARAH/SPheno or FlexibleSUSY), and validate against the paper's benchmark (m_chi10 = 145 GeV, WMAP7 strip with M_1/2 = 400-900 GeV).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a modern constraint pipeline: Planck 2018 Omega_CDM h^2 interval, SModelS/CheckMATE recasts of Run-2 multijet and stop searches on the F-SU(5) spectrum, and DDCalc with LZ/XENONnT likelihoods for neutralino-nucleon scattering.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the current Fermi-LAT Galactic-center line-search likelihood (published line-search results with Fermi ScienceTools/fermipy) against the model's predicted line energies and IB spectrum for benchmark halo profiles.

route_step_status.reason: Mapping (m_s, tau_s, Y_s, branching fraction, m_axino) to Delta N_eff, Omega_axino h^2, and the redshifting decay-produced momentum is the closed-form analytic calculation given in the source paper.

Comparison to N_eff and Lyman-alpha data relies on an approximate thermal-WDM mapping and pre-Planck constraints; the card records likelihood_available no/partial and recasting_needed for all three constraints, with no recast rerun.

gaps.description: The small-scale cutoff of decay-produced axinos is only estimated via an approximate free-streaming-length mapping to a 1-4 keV thermal WDM mass; no exact linear transfer function has been computed from the actual nonthermal two-body-decay momentum distribution for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-produced axino phase-space distribution f(q) (two-body saxion decay with lifetime tau_s), feed it to the CLASS ncdm module as a tabulated distribution, and compute the exact transfer function and half-mode mass across the m_s, tau_s, m_axino/m_s parameter space.

gaps.description: No current likelihood confronts the model's joint Delta N_eff and small-scale-suppression predictions with data: the N_eff constraint predates final Planck results and the Lyman-alpha bound is applied only through the thermal-WDM equivalence rather than a likelihood evaluated on the nonthermal spectrum.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a joint likelihood combining the Planck 2018 (+BAO) N_eff posterior with a Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator (e.g. the MIKE/HIRES+XQ-100 based WDM likelihood generalized to nonthermal transfer functions), taking the CLASS outputs of the resolved transfer-function calculation as input.

route_step_status.reason: Public NMSSMTools covers the generic NMSSM, but the paper's analysis used a modified NMSSMTools 3.1.0 for the minimal PQ-NMSSM singlet sector (mu_S^2 S term, no cubic self-coupling) and no public release of that modification is described.
The Higgs invisible width and Higgs-mediated spin-independent recoil rate follow from mixing matrices via standard analytic formulas given in the paper.

The thermal freeze-out branch is standard micrOMEGAs/NMSSMTools territory, but the saxion entropy-dilution and nonthermal LSP/axion branch has no named tool and requires a nonstandard-cosmology Boltzmann treatment the card does not identify.

gaps.description: The minimal PQ-NMSSM singlet sector (tadpole/mass terms from PQ breaking instead of the Z3 kappa S^3 term) is implemented only in a private modification of NMSSMTools 3.1.0; the spectrum, mixings, and benchmark contours cannot be reproduced with public code.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the PQ-NMSSM superpotential (lambda S H_u H_d + mu_S^2 S, no singlet self-couplings) in a public spectrum chain — either the general-NMSSM mode of NMSSMTools or SARAH-generated SPheno — and validate against the paper's benchmark invisible-width and sigma_SI contours.

gaps.description: No code evolves the model's nonstandard cosmological history: late saxion decay with entropy production diluting the thermal singlino abundance, nonthermal LSP production, and the residual axion misalignment fraction that together set the final multi-component relic density.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple a saxion decay/entropy-injection Boltzmann module (of the mixed axion-neutralino type developed for PQ-augmented SUSY, e.g. Bae-Baer-Lessa style codes) to the micrOMEGAs freeze-out output, with inputs (v_PQ, saxion mass/lifetime, initial amplitude, misalignment angle) and output the diluted LSP plus axion abundance.

gaps.description: All constraints on the card are 2012-era statements without likelihoods: XENON100 SI limits, LHC Higgs-era invisible-width bounds, and an approximate overclosure screening; no modern combined likelihood exists for the light-singlino region.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a modern likelihood from the ATLAS/CMS Run-2 Higgs invisible-branching combination (via Lilith/HiggsTools), DDCalc with LZ/XENONnT SI likelihoods including the sub-m_h/2 mass range, and the Planck 2018 relic-density interval.

route_step_status.reason: The thermal yield of a relativistically decoupling keV fermion is a standard analytic freeze-out/decoupling estimate (Y ~ 0.278/g_*), which the paper itself uses.
Entropy dilution from an out-of-equilibrium N_2 decay follows standard semi-analytic dilution-factor formulas that are pen-and-paper given M_2, m0, and the N_2 lifetime.

Public non-cold-relic transfer-function machinery (CLASS/CAMB with a supplied f(p)) exists, but the card states the post-dilution N_1 momentum distribution is not provided and the paper only uses a sterile-neutrino Lyman-alpha mass analogy.
Radiative-seesaw charged-lepton-flavor-violation branching ratios are standard analytic one-loop formulas, as the card notes.

gaps.description: The post-dilution N_1 momentum distribution f(p) is not derived (card: distribution_function_available = no), so the free-streaming cutoff and transfer function for this diluted thermal relic cannot be computed beyond a sterile-neutrino mass analogy.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p) by evolving the decoupled thermal N_1 spectrum through the N_2 entropy-injection epoch (redshifting plus dilution in a momentum-resolved Boltzmann calculation), then feed the resulting f(p) into CLASS/CAMB as a non-cold dark matter species to obtain model-specific transfer functions.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha forest likelihood exists for this model's diluted-thermal distribution (card: likelihood_available = no for lyman_alpha_wdm_mass_bound); the quoted 5.6 keV sterile-neutrino bound is only an approximate proxy.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the model through an existing WDM Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator/likelihood by mapping the model-specific transfer function onto thermal-WDM equivalents (e.g. via the half-mode or area criterion) once gap_1 supplies f(p).

gaps.description: No reusable scan pipeline couples the thermal yield, N_2 entropy injection, BBN reheating bound (0.7-4 MeV), relic density, and LFV constraints; the paper provides only analytic estimates for benchmark points (agent_notes: no reusable global scan).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled yield/dilution ODE system with a BBN reheating-temperature check as a small standalone solver (or a micrOMEGAs non-standard-cosmology module) and combine it with the analytic LFV formulas into a parameter-scan driver.

route_step_status.reason: Modulus decay widths, the axion branching fraction B_a = 1/(2z^2+1), and T_d follow directly from the analytic formulas quoted in the primary paper.
Delta N_eff from the axion branching fraction and g_star at reheating is a standard pen-and-paper formula given the decay-width outputs.

Standard misalignment formulas exist, but the QCD-axion abundance in this modulus-dominated cosmology (dilution depending on whether modulus decay occurs before or after the QCD transition) is not implemented as a worked calculation in the card.

gaps.description: No implemented calculation of the QCD-axion misalignment abundance in the non-sequestered LVS modulus cosmology, where early matter domination and entropy injection from the O(10) TeV volume modulus modify the standard Omega_a(f_a, theta) relation depending on the decay timing relative to the QCD transition.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public axion relic solver (e.g. a MiMeS-style misalignment code that already handles non-standard expansion histories) with the modulus-dominated background H(T) and entropy-dilution factor derived from the decay_widths step, scanning f_a, theta_i, and T_d.

route_step_status.reason: Volume-modulus decay widths, axion branching fraction, and reheating temperature T_d follow from the analytic formulas quoted in the primary paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the modulus-radiation-LSP Boltzmann system (e.g. in micrOMEGAs' non-standard cosmology interface or a standalone ODE code) taking m_modulus and z_GM as inputs, using micrOMEGAs/DarkSUSY Wino cross sections, and jointly outputting Omega h^2 and Delta N_eff against modern Planck constraints.

route_step_status.reason: Minimizing the chameleon effective potential in a given ambient density to get phi_min and the effective scalar mass is standard pen-and-paper chameleon analysis, assuming the adiabatic tracking stated in the validity domain.

gaps.description: No structure-formation simulations or halo-shape/core likelihood exist for a self-interaction cross section that depends on both velocity and ambient density through the chameleon field; constant-cross-section SIDM bounds (sigma/m < 0.1 cm^2/g at 10 km/s) are only proxies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement sigma(v, rho) scattering in an existing SIDM N-body code (e.g. the GIZMO or Arepo SIDM modules), run dwarf-to-cluster zoom simulations over the chameleon parameter space, and calibrate a halo-shape/core-size likelihood against cluster lensing and X-ray shape data.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify a minimal visible portal (e.g. kinetic mixing of the dark U(1) with hypercharge), derive the environment-dependent nuclear/electron recoil rate with the terrestrial chameleon field value from step s1, and check the induced fifth-force/screening constraints.

gaps.description: No public calculator exists for W-mediated exoergic bound-state capture with nuclear transmutation in the MeV mass-gap regime: case B has no positron line, its rate depends on nuclear transmutation matrix elements, and the semiclassical approximation is valid only when many bound levels contribute.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a numerical capture-rate code solving for the charged-scalar bound levels in realistic nuclear Coulomb potentials and combining them with W-exchange transmutation matrix elements for the relevant Xe, C, and O targets, output as capture cross section times velocity over (Delta m, m_X, g_eff).

gaps.description: No reusable likelihood exists for the MeV gamma de-excitation signature in EXO-200, KamLAND-Zen, SNO, and Borexino: only published high-energy spectra with conservative background subtraction were used, and gamma-escape and acceptance effects can shift limits by a factor of about two.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published high-energy event spectra, model each detector's response (resolution, gamma-escape probability, fiducial acceptance) with a lightweight Monte Carlo, and package a binned Poisson likelihood over (Delta m, tau, capture rate), extendable to KamLAND-Zen 800 and nEXO-class data.

gaps.description: The collider constraint rests on the CMS 7 TeV 5 fb^-1 heavy-stable-charged-particle search only; no implemented recast covers electroweak scalar-doublet charged-state production with lifetime dependence, and Run 2/3 HSCP and long-lived-track searches are not applied.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement Drell-Yan production of the charged scalar doublet member in MadGraph and recast current ATLAS/CMS 13 TeV HSCP and disappearing-track searches (via existing long-lived-particle recast frameworks) as a function of (m_X, tau), updating the m_X > 210 GeV bound.

gaps.description: The catalyzed-BBN constraint on the long-lived charged scalar is only an approximate lifetime label (tau above about 1e3 s); no BBN network calculation with charged-relic catalysis and the actual coannihilation-set primordial X- abundance has been run for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the electroweak-doublet coannihilation freeze-out abundance of X- to a BBN network code extended with catalyzed reactions on charged relics (extending AlterBBN or PRIMAT with the CBBN reaction set), producing a quantitative excluded region in the (tau, Delta m) plane.

route_step_status.reason: E_gamma = m_phi / 2 is exact two-body kinematics, trivially analytic with no tool needed.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build an XSPEC/HEAsoft-based line-flux likelihood over archival Suzaku XIS (Draco, Ursa Minor) and complementary XMM/Chandra dwarf and blank-sky spectra, parameterized by (E_gamma, decay width, f_phi) with target D-factor priors, and include a derivation layer converting published sterile-neutrino sin^2(2theta) line limits into generic two-photon decay-rate limits across the 0.7-10 keV band.

route_step_status.reason: The gravitino two-body and cascade injection spectrum is a standard pen-and-paper calculation from m_3/2 and the gaugino spectrum, so a null tool_or_code does not block this analytic step.

Public direct-detection likelihood frameworks exist, but no assembled recast combines the loop-level and portal spin-independent cross sections for these specific multiplet choices with current experiment likelihoods (tool_or_code is null and the constraint is marked recasting_needed).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs or DarkSUSY with Sommerfeld and bound-state factors parameterized by SU(2)_L representation dimension n and hypercharge Y, validated against the published 4.60/9.17 TeV scalar quintuplet/septuplet benchmarks.

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the neutralino/chargino mass matrices from M_1, M_2, mu, tan_beta is standard analytic work also covered by public MSSM spectrum calculators.

The bino-to-gravitino/axino lifetime as a function of F, f_a, and M_1 is a simple analytic decay-rate formula.
The chargino lifetime and soft-pion spectrum from the 155-175 MeV charged-neutral splitting follow from known analytic formulas.
MadGraph/Pythia event generation exists, but the disappearing-track/soft-pion detector recast needs experiment-specific efficiency maps that are only partially available in public recast frameworks.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-extract the F and f_a inequalities from the source PDF of arXiv:1210.0555 and encode the pre-BBN bino decay condition as an explicit analytic bound in the card.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the gaugino/scalar spectrum and long-lived-particle lifetimes from F_X, M_*, and anomaly-mediated formulas is analytic work within the spread-SUSY effective description.

gaps.description: No public code computes the total wino abundance in Spread SUSY: Sommerfeld-corrected thermal freeze-out combined with gravitino freeze-in from heavy-scalar decays and UV gravitino production at reheating, as a function of (M_2, m_3/2, m_scalar, M_*, T_R).

route_step_status.reason: KK masses and tunneling rates follow from the paper's analytic warped-throat formulae given warp factors, local string scales, and curvatures; the step is analytic within the stated throat-geometry approximations.

The primary paper explicitly left collider signatures for future work and no model implementation or mono-X recast for the anapole operator is indicated by the card.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/UFO implementation of the anapole operator, generate mono-photon and mono-jet missing-energy samples in MadGraph, and recast current LHC/LEP mono-X searches with per-event EFT-validity cuts that disable the limit when the momentum transfer exceeds Lambda.

The T_RH < T_fo comparison is a trivial validation check requiring no tool.

route_step_status.reason: The initial nonthermal yield is an analytic paper formula in the bubble parameters, M_V, and lambda_V, computable by hand.

The spin-independent cross section follows from standard tree-level Higgs-portal matching, a well-known analytic result.

Public machinery for SI direct-detection limits (micrOMEGAs/DDCalc-type) covers Higgs-portal vectors, but the card records no wired-up likelihood and the collider comparison requires a dedicated recast not implemented here.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or a lightweight custom solver using its Higgs-portal-vector annihilation cross sections) to accept an injected comoving yield at a user-specified T_EW and evolve the number density through post-transition annihilation to today, validated against the paper's analytic washout estimate.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the analytic SI cross section to DDCalc (or micrOMEGAs' direct-detection module) with current LZ/XENONnT likelihoods, and recast LHC Higgs-portal/monojet limits for a multi-TeV vector using existing simplified-model recast frameworks.

route_step_status.reason: Standard relic-density codes (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) can compute the t-channel freeze-out, but the card records no public model implementation (has_associated_code unknown, tool_or_code null), so a model file must first be built.
Gamma-ray spectra for b bbar and tau+ tau- final states plus halo J-factor integration are covered by standard public tools (e.g. PPPC4DMID-style spectra used in GC-excess fits).

Public recast frameworks exist for heavy vector-like fermion searches and Higgs-invisible/electroweak fits, but the card notes no modern LHC recast was run and no model implementation exists to drive one.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/UFO/CalcHEP files) of the hidden-U(1) vector dark matter with vector-like fermion portal exists, so relic density, annihilation cross sections, and collider rates cannot be computed with standard pipelines.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the U(1)_dm Lagrangian (X_mu, vector-like tprime/bprime/tauprime, mixed scalar S) in FeynRules and export to micrOMEGAs for relic/indirect rates and to MadGraph (UFO) for collider production.

gaps.description: No runnable Galactic Center excess likelihood is bundled (likelihood_available: partial); the 20-40 GeV preferred window rests on source-era fits that cannot be re-evaluated for this model's b bbar/tau tau admixture.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Using the UFO model from gap_1, recast Run-2 LHC searches for third-generation partners plus missing energy with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5, and update Higgs-invisible and oblique-parameter constraints with current fits.

route_step_status.reason: The background density evolution and stationary-massive-daughter equation of state are simple analytic ODEs given (tau, epsilon), fully specified in the primary paper.

Public decaying-DM CLASS branches cover DM-to-dark-radiation and two-body massive-daughter kinematics, but the many-body limit (stationary massive daughter, epsilon up to 1) has no direct implementation and only an approximate mapping.
SNIa and CMB likelihoods are public (Union/Pantheon, Planck in MontePython/Cobaya), but the Lyman-alpha and weak-lensing recasts require emulators calibrated outside this model's decay phenomenology.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-solver implementation exists for the many-body decay kinematics (many massless daughters plus a stationary massive daughter with radiation fraction epsilon up to 1); existing public decaying-DM CLASS/CAMB branches implement either pure DM-to-dark-radiation decay or two-body kinematics, so the many-body perturbation equations are only approximately mapped.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the public two-body decaying-DM CLASS branch (Franco Abellan et al. lineage) with the many-body source terms: a zero-velocity massive-daughter fluid plus dark-radiation injection, with the epsilon range widened to (0,1) and the corresponding perturbation equations derived and implemented.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha or weak-lensing likelihood covers the many-body decay's late-time scale-dependent suppression; existing Ly-alpha emulators are calibrated on LCDM/WDM-like power spectra and the related-work constraints (arXiv:2210.06117-style) apply to two-body kinematics only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Validate an effective-parameter compression (amplitude and redshift of power suppression) of the many-body model against an existing Ly-alpha flux-power emulator, or retrain the emulator on hydro/N-body runs with the many-body linear input spectra.

route_step_status.reason: The background densities and the massive-daughter velocity/equation of state follow from the analytic two-body kinematics given in the primary paper.

Public modified-CLASS implementations of two-body decaying dark matter with a massive warm daughter exist (the codes behind the card's cited arXiv:2102.12498-class analyses) and cover this model's (tau, epsilon) space.

SNIa and CMB likelihoods are public (Union/Pantheon, Planck in MontePython/Cobaya), but the Lyman-alpha recast relies on emulators calibrated on non-decaying cosmologies and the weak-lensing constraint needs a nonlinear prescription.

gaps.description: No dedicated Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood exists for two-body decaying dark matter; current constraints rely on effective mappings of the decay-induced suppression onto emulators trained on LCDM/WDM grids, which is only approximate at the S8-favored (tau, epsilon) values.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Ly-alpha flux-power emulator with hydrodynamical runs using two-body DDM linear spectra from the modified CLASS branch, or validate the existing effective-model compression (arXiv:2210.06117 approach) across the full (tau, epsilon) plane.

gaps.description: The weak-lensing/S8 constraint at k ~ 0.1-1 h/Mpc needs a nonlinear matter-power prescription for two-body decaying dark matter; the card records simulation_calibrated: no, so the route currently stops at linear power.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt and validate an existing N-body-calibrated nonlinear suppression emulator for two-body DDM (the DMemu-style boost-factor approach) coupled to the modified CLASS output, and wire it into a weak-lensing likelihood in Cobaya/MontePython.

route_step_status.reason: Public phase-transition codes (CosmoTransitions-class bounce solvers) exist, but the high-scale nMSSM plus vector-like-multiplet thermal potential has no public implementation and the paper used a simplified bounce calculation.

Higgs-resonant freeze-out through the low-energy lambda_eff h s s coupling is a standard resonant thermal-average calculation handled analytically or by micrOMEGAs-class solvers for a Higgs-portal fermion.
The singlino lifetime is an analytic dimension-six effective-operator estimate given (lambda_N, mixings, M_SUSY, m_s), which is pen-and-paper math from the primary paper.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the high-scale nMSSM plus vector-like-multiplet finite-temperature effective potential exists, so the strongly first-order phase transition (phi/T > 0.9 benchmark region, bounce action, bubble-wall width) cannot be recomputed or scanned beyond the paper's simplified treatment.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the one-loop plus daisy-resummed thermal potential of the Higgs-singlet-vector-like sector into CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce solver), scan (M_SUSY, lambda, k, charged-Higgs mass), and recover the phi/T > 0.9 benchmark region.

gaps.description: The baryon-asymmetry calculation is incomplete: the CP-violating sources are deferred by the paper and the washout/BAU-survival estimate depends on an unquantified hierarchy between nucleation and roll temperatures, so no quantitative BAU prediction can be attached to a parameter point.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the CP-violating sources for the vector-like sector across the bubble wall and solve the standard electroweak-baryogenesis transport equations (VEV-insertion or WKB formalism) for the benchmark wall width L_w T ~ 30, packaging the result as a reusable BAU calculator for this model class.

gaps.description: The Higgs-resonant singlino region is only checked against paper-era direct-detection prospects (XENON1T testability); no current-generation (LZ/XENONnT) direct-detection recast or likelihood is attached, although the SI cross section itself is analytic.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute sigma_SI from the lambda_eff h s s coupling with standard nuclear form factors and compare the (m_s ~ 60 GeV, lambda_eff ~ 0.01) region against published LZ/XENONnT limit curves, optionally via a public direct-detection likelihood package.

route_step_status.reason: The loop-induced phi -> gamma_H gamma_H width is a closed-form analytic formula displayed in the primary paper, so a null tool_or_code is not limiting.

A Gaussian approximation to the public Planck N_eff posterior (or the official Planck likelihood) is a standard, readily applied comparison.
Gamma(h -> phi phi) from the Higgs portal is a textbook analytic formula given in the primary paper.

Published ATLAS/CMS Higgs invisible branching-fraction limits exist and comparing a single BR_inv value against them is straightforward, though the card's quoted numbers are paper-era and should be updated.

gaps.description: No implemented numerical pipeline evolves the subdominant hidden scalar's abundance and late decay into hidden photons to produce Delta N_eff at BBN and recombination for this model; the card's dark-radiation evolution step has no tool and the paper's exclusion contours are not reproducible from local text.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the model onto the existing decaying-cold-species-to-dark-radiation sector of CLASS (dcdm->dr) or write a small ODE code evolving rho_phi and rho_gamma_H through phi decay, parameterized by (m_phi, tau_phi, initial phi yield), and validate against the paper's Fig. 2 exclusion region.

gaps.description: The specific nonthermal WIMPZILLA production channel setting the 1e12-1e14 GeV relic abundance is not calculated in the paper or represented on the card, so the superheavy relic abundance cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the relic abundance for a concrete production mechanism (gravitational production at the end of inflation or preheating, following Chung-Kolb-Riotto-style calculations) as a function of m_DM and the reheating temperature, and add it as an explicit route step.

route_step_status.reason: Axion couplings and anomaly coefficients follow from the primary paper's analytic formulae once a 3HFPQ charge assignment and mixing matrices are specified, so no code is needed.

The N_DW classification is simple analytic bookkeeping, but the card notes the relic abundance and PQ-breaking-history dependence remain unresolved with no cosmology module identified.

gaps.description: No assembled likelihood or recasting tables map this model's flavored axion couplings (off-diagonal quark/lepton couplings, g_a_gamma, g_ae, g_aN) onto rare-decay, stellar-cooling, and helioscope/haloscope limits, so constraint comparison is limited to rough screening.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compile digitized public bounds (K -> pi + invisible from E787/E949/NA62, mu -> e a, globular-cluster and white-dwarf cooling, CAST and ADMX exclusions, e.g. from the AxionLimits compilation) into a coupling-space constraint module keyed to the model's coupling calculator output.

gaps.description: No relic-abundance calculation exists for the 3HFPQ axion class: the misalignment/domain-wall contribution as a function of v_PQ, N_DW, and the PQ-breaking epoch is not implemented, so whether a given charge assignment yields the full dark matter density cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the standard misalignment relic-density formulae (e.g. with a MiMeS-style axion cosmology code) parameterized by (m_a, v_PQ, N_DW, pre- vs post-inflationary PQ breaking), applying published string-wall simulation calibrations for the post-inflationary N_DW = 1 variants.

route_step_status.reason: Interacting DM-dark-radiation Boltzmann machinery exists publicly (ETHOS-type modified CLASS, nu-DM scattering branches), but no implementation covers this model's secluded-neutrino recoupling with sterile-active mixing, which the card says must be taken from the paper.
Semi-analytic cutoff-mass and SIDM core estimates can be made, but the card notes the mapping to dwarf cores and satellite counts needs simulation calibration that does not exist for this model.

The optical-depth calculation on the relic secluded-neutrino background is set up phenomenologically in the paper, but no public transport code (e.g. a nuSQuIDS extension) implements this secluded-sector absorption with regeneration and source-distribution modeling.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann implementation computes the secluded-sector thermal history, DM-neutrino kinetic decoupling (T_KD ~ 0.1 keV), the resulting smooth-cutoff transfer function, and the delayed neutrino free-streaming CMB effect for this U(1)_X neutrino-portal model with sterile-active mixing.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an ETHOS-parameterized modified CLASS (or an existing nu-DM interacting branch of CLASS) with the model's g_X, g_nu, theta_s scattering rates to compute T_KD, the linear power-spectrum cutoff, and CMB anisotropy shifts from delayed neutrino free streaming.

gaps.description: The combined effect of a damped initial power spectrum plus velocity-dependent self-interactions (1-10 cm^2/g at dwarf velocities) on satellite counts, subhalo mass functions, and dwarf central densities is uncalibrated by simulations for this model class.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run ETHOS-style N-body simulations with the model's truncated transfer function and a velocity-dependent SIDM cross section to calibrate the subhalo mass function and core-size relations, then fit a semi-analytic halo-response model for parameter scans.

gaps.description: No transport code computes TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrino attenuation and regeneration on the relic secluded-neutrino population as a function of m_phi, g_nu, theta_s, and source redshift distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend nuSQuIDS (or a comparable neutrino propagation code) with the secluded-sector nu-nu_s scattering cross sections and a relic-background target density to output absorbed spectra for standard source populations.

gaps.description: Only an approximate IceCube constraint exists on the card; there is no spectral/anisotropy likelihood for recasting the predicted absorption features against IceCube diffuse-flux data with source-distribution uncertainties marginalized.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast likelihood from public IceCube HESE/diffuse-flux data releases that compares absorbed versus unabsorbed spectra, marginalizing over spectral index and source redshift distribution.

route_step_status.reason: E_gamma = M_N^R/2 is trivial two-body decay kinematics needing no tool.

Transfer-function solvers for sterile-neutrino distributions exist (CLASS ncdm sector, sterile-dm for DW/Shi-Fuller production), but the model's production distribution is unspecified, so the cutoff cannot yet be computed for this card.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the dominant production channel in the U(1)_R setup (non-resonant Dodelson-Widrow oscillation production at the quoted mixing, checked with the public sterile-dm code, plus any freeze-in through the Higgs/neutralino sector), output the abundance and f(p), and feed the distribution to CLASS's ncdm sector for the transfer function.

gaps.description: No X-ray line likelihood exists for the 3.5 keV target: the card records likelihood_available = no, and comparing the (M_N^R, sin^2(2 theta_14)) plane against XMM-Newton M31/Perseus/stacked-cluster fluxes requires a recast with halo mass-profile and instrumental-response modeling.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a decay-flux calculator (standard radiative decay rate times line-of-sight DM column densities for M31, Perseus, and stacked clusters) and wrap published XMM-Newton flux measurements and upper limits into a Gaussian/profile likelihood over mass and mixing.

gaps.description: Structure-formation constraints beyond the analytic phase-space floor are not applicable yet: Lyman-alpha limits were not applied, and existing Lyman-alpha emulators are calibrated for thermal-relic WDM, not for this model's (currently unknown) nonthermal sterile-neutrino distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once f(p) is derived (gap_1), map the resulting transfer function to an equivalent thermal-WDM mass via half-mode matching and apply published Lyman-alpha thermal-WDM likelihoods/emulators, validating the mapping for the nonthermal shape.

route_step_status.reason: Mapping Planck n_s, A_s, r values to M_DUT through the Coleman-Weinberg slow-roll formulae is closed-form analytic work given in the source.

No SIDM scattering calculation exists for the confining SU(4)_DM sector — the source paper's self-interaction claim is qualitative and no tool or derivation maps mu_DM to a halo-scale cross section.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the lightest SU(4)_DM dark-hadron spectrum and low-energy self-scattering using lattice results and chiral-EFT methods developed for SU(N) dark-baryon models, parameterized by Lambda_4, and output sigma(v)/m for comparison with the 0.1-10 cm^2/g halo-scale window.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Write down and solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for inflaton decay, dark-to-luminous conversion via the scalar 15 fields, and dark-photon-mediated annihilation of the symmetric component, verifying Omega_DM/Omega_b against the observed ratio as a function of M_DUT and mu_DM.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the Coleman-Weinberg slow-roll predictions in a small module that evaluates them against current public Planck+BICEP/Keck (n_s, r) posteriors, propagating the updated allowed region to M_DUT and mu_DM.

route_step_status.reason: The pion-decay sterile source term is a closed-form analytic formula given in the paper, needing only literature finite-temperature pion mass and decay-constant inputs.

Omega_s, lambda_fs, and the phase-space density are simple integrals over f_s(q) (and CLASS-style ncdm runs can take a tabulated f(q)), but the X-ray line flux and dwarf phase-space comparisons need external target data and likelihoods the card says are unavailable.

gaps.description: No public production code computes the pion-decay sterile-neutrino distribution: existing sterile-neutrino transport codes implement Dodelson-Widrow/Shi-Fuller production and do not include the post-QCD charged-pion source term with finite-temperature pion mass and decay-constant tables.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a sterile-neutrino production code (e.g. the sterile-dm/Dodelson-Widrow class of solvers) with the paper's pion-decay collision term, packaging chiral-perturbation-theory finite-temperature f_pi(T) and m_pi(T) tables, and output tabulated f_s(q) suitable for a CLASS ncdm phase-space file.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for either constraint on the card: the CMB-abundance/dwarf-spheroidal phase-space bound and the X-ray decay-line bound are both quoted as exclusion statements with likelihood_available: no, so mass-mixing scans cannot be evaluated statistically.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a public likelihood layer: recast existing X-ray line search limits (XMM/Chandra M31 and cluster stacks) into a decay-rate likelihood in (m_s, |U_ls|^2), and implement the dwarf-spheroidal primordial phase-space-density bound as a likelihood over the computed f_s(q).

gaps.description: The small-scale-structure prediction stops at a few-kpc free-streaming estimate: no nonlinear N-body calibration exists for halo/subhalo statistics of this low-momentum-enhanced nonthermal distribution, and no thermal-WDM mapping is provided.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute linear transfer functions from the tabulated f_s(q) with CLASS ncdm, fit a half-mode mass and effective thermal-WDM mapping, and validate against a small suite of nonthermal-WDM N-body simulations to calibrate the subhalo mass function used by satellite-count and lensing likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: OHe stopping and radiative-capture rates depend on OHe-nucleus nuclear physics that the paper itself states is still under development, and no public code or validated semi-analytic model exists for this step.

Public cosmic-ray propagation codes (GALPROP/DRAGON class) cover positron propagation, but no ready multicomponent decaying-DM fit or AMS-02/Fermi likelihood pipeline exists for this benchmark, so viability rests on the source paper's quoted fit.

gaps.description: The OHe-nucleus interaction is not solved: no validated calculation of OHe slowing in matter, the shallow bound state with sodium, or the temperature-dependent radiative-capture rate exists (the paper flags this nuclear physics as under development), so the DAMA modulation and null-result evasion claims cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the OHe-nucleus potential and bound-state spectrum by solving the coupled Coulomb-plus-nuclear few-body problem (e.g. with standard nuclear few-body machinery) for sodium and cryogenic-detector targets, then publish temperature-dependent capture-rate tables usable in a detector-response model.

gaps.description: No cosmic-ray likelihood pipeline exists for the subdominant UU++ decay fit: the AMS-02 positron and Fermi diffuse-gamma comparison (f_UU ~ 1e-6, m_UU ~ 1 TeV, tau_UU ~ 1e20 s) was never rerun and likelihood_available is no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build the same-sign dilepton injection spectra from HDMSpectra/PPPC tables, propagate with DRAGON or GALPROP, and wrap AMS-02 positron-flux and Fermi diffuse-gamma data in a likelihood over (f_UU, m_UU, tau_UU, branching fractions).

gaps.description: No DAMA/LIBRA annual-modulation likelihood exists for the OHe radiative-capture signal (few-keV sodium capture), nor a recast framework mapping OHe capture rates onto CDMS/XENON/LUX null results for slowed composite atoms.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once capture-rate tables exist (gap_1), implement a detector-level modulation likelihood for DAMA NaI and a temperature-dependent capture recast for cryogenic and xenon experiments, extending an existing direct-detection framework such as DDCalc with a capture-signal channel.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the coupled background and linear perturbation equations from the Lagrangian with m(phi)=M-beta*phi is pen-and-paper work fully presented in the source paper.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann code implements this Yukawa-coupled quintessence-fermion model (field-dependent fermion mass m(phi)=M-beta*phi with exponential potential): the source's modified CAMB is private, so neither CMB nor matter-power spectra can be computed for new parameter points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled background and perturbation equations in CLASS or CAMB, following existing public coupled-quintessence/interacting-dark-energy patches, parameterized by (beta/M, alpha) and validated against the acoustic-peak and low-l responses reported in the paper.

gaps.description: The published constraints rest on Planck-2013 TT + WMAP polarization, Union 2.1 SNIa, and the HST H0 prior; no analysis pipeline with current-generation likelihoods (Planck 2018/ACT, modern BAO and SNIa compilations) exists for this model, so the reported negative-interaction preference cannot be re-evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the CLASS/CAMB module exists, wire it into Cobaya or MontePython with Planck 2018, DESI/BOSS BAO, and Pantheon+ likelihoods and rerun the (beta/M, alpha) posterior, including the fixed-alpha case.

route_step_status.reason: The p-wave XX->phiphi thermal-relic target is standard analytic freeze-out arithmetic given in the paper, and generic relic codes (micrOMEGAs-class) cover this simplified model if numerical precision is wanted.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood from isothermal-Jeans SIDM halo modeling calibrated on existing SIDM N-body simulations, covering dwarf spheroidal kinematics, Milky Way satellite densities, and cluster shape/merger constraints as a function of sigma_T/m(v).

gaps.description: Direct-detection exclusion of the light-mediator scenario is only partially available: existing LUX/SuperCDMS-style limits assume contact interactions, and no recast with the q^2-dependent light-scalar propagator plus detector efficiency and threshold curves exists for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend DDCalc (or an NREFT framework such as DirectDM+DMFormFactor) with the light-mediator momentum-dependent cross section and published efficiency/threshold curves for current xenon and low-threshold experiments, producing likelihoods in (m_X, m_phi, portal mixing).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public BBN code (AlterBBN or PRIMAT) with energy injection from late phi decays to neutrinos, mapping the allowed (m_phi, tau_phi, branching) region into a light-element likelihood replacing the 1 s rule of thumb.

route_step_status.reason: The BBDN aggregation network is handled only by the paper's analytic scaling-law and bottleneck limiting cases; no public reaction-network/coagulation solver exists to compute the final A distribution for general fusion parameters.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a Smoluchowski-type coagulation network solver with the paper's geometric fusion cross-section scaling laws, dissociation freeze-out, and optional small-A bottlenecks, validated by recovering the logarithmically peaked distribution in the efficient-fusion regime and the bottleneck-controlled large-A tail.

gaps.description: The self-interaction constraint on dark nuclei is not computable: the geometric elastic, fusion, and fission cross sections at late times have not been mapped onto a sigma/m(v) that halo-scale SIDM bounds can be applied to, and the linear transfer function of the composite population is unknown.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the effective sigma/m for the final A distribution from the geometric scaling laws (including inelastic fusion channels) and compare against dwarf and cluster SIDM bounds; check the pre-aggregation dark-sector coupling era for acoustic damping of the linear power spectrum with a CLASS-style interacting-dark-matter run.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs is public and handles coannihilating Majorana dark matter, but the card identifies no public model implementation for the k-degenerate chi_i plus charged-scalar setup, so the model files must be rebuilt before the step can be run.
The internal-bremsstrahlung cross section for a Majorana fermion with a charged scalar mediator is a known closed-form analytic result, so the null tool_or_code is not an obstacle.

Public FDM Boltzmann modules (axionCAMB, AxiCLASS) compute the linear-power suppression for m_a near 1e-22 eV, but they assume a standard thermal history and are not wired to this model's temperature-dependent mass onset or its extra dark-radiation component, and no small-scale-structure likelihood is connected.
Delta N_eff from N' and T'/T is analytic, and public BBN and Planck CMB N_eff likelihoods exist and directly constrain an extra free-streaming dark-radiation component.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run axionCAMB or AxiCLASS at the model's m_a and dark-radiation content to produce transfer functions, then recast through an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator (e.g. the WDM/FDM emulators used for m_a > 2e-20 eV bounds) and Milky Way satellite-count likelihoods, mapping the constraint into the f_a-m_a plane of this model.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Perform a lattice calculation of the topological susceptibility of the SU(3)_theta sector with the model's light dark-quark content across the confinement transition (analogous to QCD chi(T) lattice studies), and feed the resulting m_a(T) into the misalignment calculation.

micrOMEGAs (reported in associated_code) covers the thermal wino freeze-out piece, but the coupled axion/axino/saxion Boltzmann evolution with decays and entropy injection that fixes the mixed relic is only cited from prior literature and no public solver for it is identified.

The h_w^2/0.11 fraction rescaling itself is trivial arithmetic, but the comparison is to a superseded LUX bound with no likelihood run (likelihood_available: no, recasting_needed: yes), so current-generation direct-detection viability is not actually evaluated.
