gaps.description: The L_mu-L_tau mediator parameter space (g_LmuLtau, m_Zprime) needed for the depletion annihilation to neutrinos is not confronted with existing bounds (neutrino trident production, Borexino, Delta N_eff from a light Z' coupled to neutrinos) in a form usable by the route; the mediator-specific constraint recast is missing.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Collect the published L_mu-L_tau exclusion curves (CCFR trident, Borexino, BBN/N_eff) as machine-readable bounds and overlay them on the (g_LmuLtau, m_Zprime) region that achieves f_DM ~ 0.3-2 percent via chi chi -> nu nu annihilation computed with a micrOMEGAs model file.

gaps.description: No reusable statistical likelihood exists for the global 21-cm absorption depth (EDGES-based) applicable to millicharged baryon-cooling models; the card records no combined likelihood for the route.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct a global 21-cm likelihood from the EDGES (and SARAS 3) published band with an explicit foreground/systematics marginalization, exposed as a module consuming the predicted T_21(z) curve.

route_step_status.reason: The primary analysis used a modified CAMB implementing DM-to-dark-radiation conversion, but the card identifies no public release of that modification, so the capability exists only as private code.
Planck, BAO, and DES-Y1 likelihoods are public and usable through CosmoMC/Cobaya once the modified spectra are supplied.
Sommerfeld enhancement and Yukawa transfer cross sections follow from standard analytic (Hulthen-approximation) formulae, a pen-and-paper calculation with known unitarity caveats.
Comparing sigma_T/m_chi at the 30 km/s benchmark to the 10 cm^2/g bound is trivial, but a proper velocity-averaged dwarf-halo recast or likelihood does not exist per the step's own validity note.

gaps.description: The Boltzmann-solver modification implementing late DM-to-dark-radiation conversion (background density transfer parameterized by zeta and a_t plus the compensating dark-radiation perturbations) is a private modified CAMB; no public solver reproduces the CMB/LSS predictions for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the (zeta, a_t, transition-rapidity) conversion background and perturbation equations in public CLASS (or obtain and release the original modified CAMB), validated by recovering LambdaCDM at zeta=0 and the published Planck-era limits.

gaps.description: The perturbation treatment is only a generic parameterization: the card notes perturbations are model dependent beyond the background, and the conversion source term has not been derived from the actual Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation rate of the Dirac-fermion/light-vector model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the conversion rate Gamma(z) and its perturbation from the velocity-averaged Sommerfeld-enhanced cross section of the specific model, mapping (m_chi, m_med, alpha, T_kd) onto the phenomenological (zeta, a_t) parameters, and encode the mapping in the Boltzmann implementation.

gaps.description: No dwarf-galaxy self-interaction likelihood exists for the velocity-dependent sigma_T/m_chi(v) prediction; the route only supports an approximate threshold comparison at a single 30 km/s benchmark rather than a proper halo-population recast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood over published dwarf and low-surface-brightness halo fits (e.g. Jeans/isothermal SIDM halo-model inferences of sigma/m at measured velocity dispersions) that consumes sigma_T/m_chi(v) curves, replacing the single-velocity threshold cut.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level matching of Z' exchange onto the C9_NP=-C10_NP operator is a standard pen-and-paper calculation, and public Wilson-coefficient tools (flavio/wilson-style calculators) cover this weak-scale matching.

micrOMEGAs covers thermal freeze-out for Z'-portal WIMPs, but the card records no public model implementation (associated_code unknown, computational_representation null) for this U(1)' plus fourth vector-like family model, so model files must first be built.

Published xenon and Planck/Fermi exclusion curves exist, but the card marks likelihood_available: no for both constraints and flags that RG-induced light-quark couplings and nuclear matrix elements are needed before the limits can be recast onto this model.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP model files for micrOMEGAs or an equivalent Boltzmann code) exists for the non-universal U(1)' model with a fourth vector-like family, including the mixing-induced b and muon couplings, so the joint relic-density scan cannot be run out of the box.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model Lagrangian (Z', vector-like fourth family, mixing matrices) in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and validate a micrOMEGAs relic-density scan against the primary paper's viable band in M_Zprime and m_chi.

gaps.description: The loop/RG-induced effective couplings of the fermiophobic Z' to light quarks, and the corresponding nucleon-level matrix elements needed to compute sigma_SI for xenon targets, have not been derived for this model (the card explicitly flags them as needed for recasting).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the Z' couplings from the matching scale to the nuclear scale with an EFT running/matching package (e.g. DirectDM plus wilson) to obtain nucleon-level Wilson coefficients, then feed them to a rate calculator such as DDCalc.

gaps.description: No machine-readable likelihoods are available for the direct-detection (LUX/PandaX/XENON1T) and indirect-detection (Planck CMB energy injection, Fermi-LAT dwarf) constraints as they apply to this model's mu+mu-/b bbar/t tbar/Z'Z' final-state mix; the card records likelihood_available: no for both.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a composite likelihood by wiring DDCalc-style xenon likelihoods and public Fermi-LAT dwarf plus Planck f_eff annihilation likelihoods to the model's branching-fraction-weighted spectra (e.g. via MadDM/PPPC tables), and validate against the exclusion statements quoted in the primary paper.

route_step_status.reason: Expanding the S S annihilation cross section into a_eff and b_eff in the massless-final-state, suppressed-Z' limit is the analytic formula printed in the paper and is simple pen-and-paper work.
The standard approximate freeze-out expression mapping b_eff, x_f, and g_star to Omega_S h^2 is textbook semi-analytics requiring no dedicated code.

The relic-density window is an approximate analytic likelihood, but the LUX-like recoil bound (likelihood_available unknown, recasting_needed yes) and LEP/LHC Z' bounds (likelihood_available no) have no machine-readable likelihoods, so the overlay can only reproduce the paper-level scan.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the flavor-dependent U(1)_{B-L_1} x U(1)_{B-L_2-L_3} model with inert scalar S and vector-like fermions exists for a Boltzmann/recoil code, so precision relic scans covering Z'-resonance and coannihilation regimes (excluded from the paper's simple analytic expression) cannot be run; the card itself lists micrOMEGAs-or-equivalent as a required but absent resource.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Lagrangian (inert scalar S, vector-like Q'/L', two flavor-dependent Z' bosons, Higgs-portal coupling lambda_HS) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and run micrOMEGAs for relic density and sigma_SI, validating against the paper's a_eff=0, b_eff-dominated relic curve.

gaps.description: The constraint overlay lacks machine-readable likelihoods: the LUX-like spin-independent bound and the LEP/LHC Z' and flavor-coupling bounds are quoted only as formula-level statements in the source, so a modern recast of the allowed scan points cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct likelihoods from current public data products: xenon direct-detection likelihoods via DDCalc, LHC dilepton Z' limits via a recast framework, and flavor observables (C_9, Delta a_mu, meson mixing) via flavio, then combine them into one scan-level likelihood for the model parameters.

route_step_status.reason: Converting (m_J, tau_J) into a decay rate and the thermal-majoron abundance relation is the analytic relation quoted from the source and needs no dedicated tool.

CLASS/CAMB-style solvers exist and CLASS has a decaying-CDM-to-dark-radiation branch, but no public configuration combines a keV thermal warm phase-space distribution with late decay to neutrinos as this model requires.
The Ly-alpha bound exists only as a thermal-relic-WDM limit needing recast (likelihood_available no) and the CMB lifetime constraint is only partially available with no full Planck likelihood rerun.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-solver setup treats a keV-scale warm majoron with its thermal free-streaming distribution that also decays to relativistic neutrinos with tau_J of order 50 Gyr; the CLASS decaying-CDM module assumes cold parents, so the combined warm-plus-decaying linear evolution (T(k) and CMB spectra) cannot currently be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS by combining its non-cold-dark-matter (ncdm) sector with the decaying-dark-matter module: give the ncdm species a decay term sourcing massless neutrino dark radiation, parameterized by (m_J, tau_J, initial phase-space distribution), and validate against the paper's N-body initial conditions and the tau_J > 50 Gyr CMB benchmark.

gaps.description: The Ly-alpha forest constraint is available only as a 5.3 keV thermal-relic-WDM lower bound (XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE); no public flux-power likelihood or emulator accepts the decaying-warm-majoron transfer function directly, so applying the bound requires an ad hoc thermal-equivalent mapping that the card flags as approximate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast via a general small-scale-suppression Ly-alpha emulator: evaluate the majoron T(k) from the extended Boltzmann code and pass it through an existing Ly-alpha flux-power emulator framework trained on generalized cutoff shapes (alpha-beta-gamma parameterization), calibrating any decay-induced late-time suppression with a small set of dedicated hydrodynamic or N-body runs.

gaps.description: The nonthermal majoron phase-space distribution (from misalignment-like production or entropy-diluted scenarios mentioned in the paper) has not been derived, so all structure-formation predictions rest on the thermal-distribution assumption that the card marks as high extrapolation risk.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) for the paper's cited nonthermal production channels (freeze-in-like decoupling and entropy-dilution histories) analytically or with a momentum-dependent Boltzmann calculation, and feed the resulting distributions into the extended CLASS ncdm sector in place of the thermal ansatz.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs is public and the paper implemented the model in it, but the card records no released repository or model files (associated_code partial, reproducibility partial), so the implementation must be rebuilt to reproduce the relic contours.
Tree-level spin-independent scattering through the mixed Z/Z' couplings is an analytic formula with standard nuclear inputs, appropriate for a null tool_or_code.

Trident, B_s-mixing, and LHC dilepton bounds exist only as summarized exclusion statements (likelihood_available partial, recast code not released), so the overlay is a phenomenological recast rather than a reproducible computation.

gaps.description: The paper's micrOMEGAs implementation of the kinetically mixed U(1)_{L_mu-L_tau} Dirac-fermion model was not released, so the relic-density contours (including Z' resonance and Z'Z' pair regimes) cannot be reproduced without rebuilding the model files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the model (Z' with L_mu-L_tau charges, kinetic mixing epsilon with hypercharge, Dirac chi with charge q_chi) in FeynRules, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and validate against the paper's Omega_DM h^2 = 0.12 curves in the resonance and Z'-pair regimes.

gaps.description: Xenon direct-detection limits are published assuming equal proton/neutron couplings, while the kinetic-mixing-induced Z/Z' couplings here are isospin-violating; the card flags this normalization issue and records likelihood_available: no, so no likelihood correctly maps the model's sigma_SI onto XENON1T/XENONnT/DARWIN curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Use DDCalc (or an equivalent xenon likelihood package) with the model's per-nucleon couplings f_p and f_n computed from the mixed Z/Z' vertices, rather than rescaled published sigma_SI curves, and package this as a reusable likelihood for the scan.

gaps.description: No reproducible likelihood or recast code exists for the combined flavor/collider constraint set (neutrino trident, B_s mixing, b -> s mu mu band, and epsilon-dependent LHC dilepton limits); the primary's overlay is a hand-combined summary the card marks as only partially available.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build the flavor side with flavio/smelli (trident, B_s mixing, b -> s mu mu global fit for the L_mu-L_tau Wilson coefficients) and recast LHC dilepton searches with a public recast tool as a function of (m_Zprime, g_l, epsilon), then combine into one likelihood module for the joint scan.

route_step_status.reason: The a -> A'A' decay rate and injection spectrum follow analytically from the dimension-five operator normalization given in the paper.
The resonant A'-to-photon conversion probability is the small-probability Landau-Zener-style analytic expression from the paper, needing only a standard ionization/plasma-mass history table as input.

The brightness-temperature shift from an enhanced Rayleigh-Jeans background can be estimated semi-analytically, but the card states a likelihood-level comparison needs an astrophysical 21 cm model and no EDGES/global-21cm likelihood is provided.

gaps.description: No global 21 cm likelihood exists that accepts an excess Rayleigh-Jeans radio background of the model's redshift- and frequency-dependent shape: the EDGES-motivated absorption-depth comparison cannot be evaluated beyond order-of-magnitude statements without jointly modeling astrophysical spin-temperature evolution and the injected photon occupation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public global-signal code (ARES or 21cmFAST global-signal mode, which already support excess-radio-background terms) to take the model's converted-photon occupation dn/domega(z) as input, and wrap it with an EDGES-like data likelihood marginalizing over astrophysical spin-temperature parameters.

gaps.description: The FIRAS and low-frequency radio-background constraint on the distorted CMB Rayleigh-Jeans tail is applied only qualitatively: the card records no numerical FIRAS likelihood and notes that absolute low-frequency measurements (ARCADE-2-class data) have large uncertainties, so the viable (m_A', epsilon) window cannot be delimited quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a spectral-distortion likelihood from the public FIRAS monopole residuals plus low-frequency absolute radiometry (ARCADE-2 and long-wavelength surveys), evaluated on the model's converted-photon intensity as a function of x, and use it to map the excluded versus viable (m_A', epsilon, abundance) region.

gaps.description: The initial nonthermal scalar relic abundance and its momentum distribution are unspecified (production via misalignment or cosmic strings is only sketched, distribution_function_available unknown), so the normalization of the dark-photon injection rate that feeds every downstream observable is undetermined within the model itself.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the milli-eV scalar's relic abundance for the misalignment and cosmic-string production channels as a function of (m_a, f_a) using standard axion-like-particle abundance formulae, and record the resulting Omega_a(m_a, f_a) relation as a card-level input to the decay-rate step.

route_step_status.reason: No public code simulates or models clockwork-suppressed defect networks; the step relies on the paper's analytic estimates, which are explicitly caveated as breaking down at high f.
Splitting emitted axions into relativistic and nonrelativistic populations by emission epoch is a simple analytic calculation given in the primary text.
Converting the axion energy densities to Delta N_eff and Omega_a h^2 is standard pen-and-paper cosmology once a thermal history is chosen.

gaps.description: No field-theory or Nambu-Goto simulation of the clockwork defect network (strings and gear-mode domain walls with clockwork-suppressed tension) exists to calibrate the network scaling density, axion emission efficiency, and emission spectrum; the route currently rests on analytic estimates whose validity breaks down in the high-f regime where Delta N_eff > 0.1 is claimed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run lattice field-theory simulations of the N+1 clockwork scalar system through the PQ phase transition (extending existing axion-string simulation frameworks to nearest-neighbor clockwork potentials), extract the network scaling parameters and the emitted-axion spectrum as functions of N, q, and the gear mass spectrum, and fit a calibrated emission model to replace the analytic estimate.

gaps.description: No implemented likelihood connects the clockwork parameters (f, f_g, N, q, gear masses, reheating history) to the N_eff and relic-abundance data; the card records only approximate thresholds from the primary paper, with partial recasting needed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the route's analytic chain as a small parameter-scan module and evaluate it against the Planck Delta N_eff posterior and the observed Omega_DM h^2 (e.g., as an external likelihood in Cobaya or MontePython), replacing the paper's threshold statements with a proper likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The cannibal background history T_can(a) and rho_can(a) follows analytically from comoving-entropy conservation in the decoupled minimal model and needs no dedicated tool.
The modified linear perturbation equations exist in the primary paper, but no public Boltzmann code (CLASS/CAMB) implements the cannibal fluid, so an existing solver must be extended.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-code implementation of the cannibal fluid exists: the logarithmic temperature history, w_can(a), sound speed, and fluid perturbation equations for a percent-level cannibal subcomponent coexisting with cold dark matter are written in the paper but not available in CLASS or CAMB, so R(k) cannot be computed with public tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with a cannibal-fluid species implementing the paper's background scaling (parameterized by m, S_can, lambda, f_can,0) and its fluid perturbation equations with the self-scattering-supported sound speed, and validate against the paper's published R(k) suppression curves.

gaps.description: No survey likelihood is encoded for the model: the percent-level cannibal fraction and phase-timing targets are paper-level regions, not posteriors, and there is no pipeline comparing the predicted matter-power suppression to CMB, BAO, and weak-lensing S8 data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the CLASS cannibal module exists, wire it into Cobaya or MontePython with the standard Planck 2018, BAO, and KiDS/DES S8 likelihoods to turn the paper's target regions into real posterior constraints on (m, S_can, lambda, f_can,0).

route_step_status.reason: The early-matter-dominated Hubble history and entropy dilution with an instantaneous end are standard analytic cosmology parameterized by H_EW/m_h and T_end.
Higgs-portal production and annihilation rates for the singlet scalar are standard analytic results, and public tools such as micrOMEGAs already tabulate these cross sections.

Public relic-abundance solvers (micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY) handle standard freeze-out/freeze-in but do not combine an early-matter-dominated expansion and entropy injection with 4-to-2 cannibal number-changing terms, so extension is required.

Direct-detection and collider recasts for the singlet scalar are well served by public tools (DDCalc, micrOMEGAs, GAMBIT), but SIDM halo/cluster comparisons exist only as literature-level bounds, not quantitative likelihoods.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver computes the singlet-scalar yield combining Higgs-portal freeze-out or freeze-in with 4-to-2 cannibal self-annihilations in an early matter-dominated background with entropy dilution; the paper's numerical solution is not released, so the relic-density map over (m_s, lambda_hs, lambda_s, H_EW/m_h, T_end) cannot be reproduced with existing tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or a DRAKE-style dedicated solver) with a user-defined H(T) and entropy history for early matter domination and add the 4-to-2 collision term for the quartic singlet self-interaction, validating against the paper's freeze-out, freeze-in, and cannibal parameter-space bands.

gaps.description: No quantitative likelihood exists for the self-interaction observable sigma_self/m_s: halo-shape and cluster SIDM constraints are cited as literature bounds, and the card records detector and halo likelihoods as not reconstructed, so the recast step cannot produce statistically meaningful limits in the nonstandard cosmology.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble an interpolated likelihood module from published SIDM posteriors on sigma/m (dwarf, LSB, and cluster halo fits) and combine it with DDCalc-based direct-detection likelihoods inside a GAMBIT-style scan of the singlet parameters with the early-matter-domination relic calculation.

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the flat-FRW background equations for the non-canonical scalar with the coth potential is a simple ODE problem fully specified by the paper's Lagrangian and solvable with a custom integrator.

CLASS/CAMB support generalized dark fluids but have no native module for a single non-canonical UDM scalar acting as both dark matter and dark energy, so the perturbation sector must be added or approximated.
Public CMB+BAO+SN+LSS likelihoods exist in Cobaya/MontePython, but the card notes the connection to this model is unimplemented and no primary likelihood table exists.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-code implementation exists for the non-canonical UDM scalar with L=X(X/M^4)^(alpha-1)-V(phi) and the asymptotically-flat coth potential: neither CLASS nor CAMB evolves the perturbations of a single field whose kinetic energy clusters as dark matter with c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1 while its potential drives acceleration, so the transfer function and Jeans-scale viability test cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with a k-essence/UDM module that takes the background solution for this potential and evolves the exact scalar perturbation equations (or, as a first pass, map the model onto CLASS's generalized-dark-matter fluid with w(a) from the background solve and constant c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1), validating the pressureless large-alpha limit against the paper.

gaps.description: No data-comparison pipeline exists for this potential: the paper is a background demonstration with no likelihood table, and no implemented analysis confronts H(z), distances, and P(k) of the coth-potential UDM with CMB, BAO, SN, and LSS data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the perturbation module exists, wrap the model as a Cobaya theory class and run it against Planck 2018, BAO, and Pantheon+ likelihoods plus a linear P(k)/S8 probe to obtain posteriors on (alpha, M, V0, initial conditions).

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the flat-FRW background equations for the non-canonical scalar with the cascading step potential is a simple ODE problem fully specified by the paper's Lagrangian and solvable with a custom integrator.

CLASS/CAMB support generalized dark fluids but have no native module for a single non-canonical UDM scalar acting as both dark matter and dark energy, so the perturbation sector must be added or approximated.
Public CMB+BAO+SN+LSS likelihoods exist in Cobaya/MontePython, but the card notes the connection to this model is unimplemented and no primary likelihood table exists.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-code implementation exists for the non-canonical UDM scalar with L=X(X/M^4)^(alpha-1)-V(phi) and the cascading step potential: neither CLASS nor CAMB evolves the perturbations of a single field whose kinetic energy clusters as dark matter with c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1 while the staircase potential drives (possibly transient) acceleration, so the transfer function and Jeans-scale viability test cannot be computed, and the potential's step transitions need careful numerical treatment.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with a k-essence/UDM module that takes the background solution for this potential (with a smoothed parameterization of the vacuum-energy steps) and evolves the exact scalar perturbation equations, or as a first pass map the model onto CLASS's generalized-dark-matter fluid with w(a) from the background solve and constant c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1, validating the pressureless large-alpha limit against the paper.

gaps.description: No data-comparison pipeline exists for this potential: the paper is a background demonstration with no likelihood table, and no implemented analysis confronts H(z), distances, and P(k) of the cascading-step-potential UDM with CMB, BAO, SN, and LSS data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the perturbation module exists, wrap the model as a Cobaya theory class and run it against Planck 2018, BAO, and Pantheon+ likelihoods plus a linear P(k)/S8 probe to obtain posteriors on (alpha, M, V0, step parameters, initial conditions).

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the flat-FRW background equations for L=X(X/M^4)^(alpha-1)-V(phi) is a standard ODE solve that any custom scalar-background integrator handles with small effort, as the paper itself demonstrates analytically.

Public Boltzmann solvers (CLASS/CAMB) support fluids with a fixed sound speed and canonical quintessence but have no released module for the perturbations of this non-canonical UDM scalar with c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1, so a modified solver must be written.
Public CMB+BAO+SN+LSS likelihoods exist in Cobaya/MontePython, but the card notes the comparison 'requires implementation' because the model has no Boltzmann-code interface to feed them.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements linear perturbations for the non-canonical unified dark sector L=X(X/M^4)^(alpha-1)-V(phi), whose effective sound speed c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1 and Jeans scale set the clustering viability; CLASS/CAMB only offer constant-c_s fluids or canonical scalar fields.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the CLASS scalar-field (scf) or fluid module to a general k-essence Lagrangian L(X,phi), passing the background-dependent c_s^2 and adiabatic/non-adiabatic pressure terms into the perturbation equations, and validate against the large-alpha analytic limit c_s^2=(2 alpha-1)^-1.

gaps.description: No end-to-end likelihood pipeline exists that confronts this potential's background split (H(z), Omega_kinetic, Omega_potential) and matter power spectrum with CMB/BAO/SN/LSS data; both card constraints have likelihood_available no/unknown and recasting_needed yes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the modified CLASS module exists, wrap it in Cobaya with the standard Planck, BAO (BOSS/eBOSS/DESI), Pantheon+ and matter-power likelihoods, sampling alpha, M, V0, potential-shape parameters, and initial phi/phidot.

route_step_status.reason: Public recombination codes (HyRec, CosmoRec, RECFAST inside CLASS/CAMB) exist but none implement the modified charge-neutrality condition x_p = x_e + epsilon_X r_X from a sequestered negative charge, so the x_e(z) and T_g(z) history requires a model-specific modification.

The CMB, stellar/supernova, and laboratory exclusion curves exist in the literature but only as published figures with recasting_needed yes and no likelihood, so overlaying them on (m_X, epsilon_X, f_X) requires digitizing and recasting rather than an existing tool.

gaps.description: No public recombination/thermal-history code includes a stable sequestered negative charge epsilon_X r_X in the charge-neutrality condition, so the suppressed free-electron fraction x_e(z), earlier baryon cooling T_g(z), and resulting global 21 cm brightness temperature T_21 cannot be computed with released tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend HyRec or the RECFAST module in CLASS to solve the recombination network with x_p = x_e + epsilon_X r_X and the modified Compton/adiabatic cooling of the gas, then feed x_e(z), T_g(z) into a global 21 cm calculator (e.g. ARES) to produce T_21(z) at cosmic dawn; validate against the epsilon_X r_X ~ 1e-4 benchmark of the paper.

gaps.description: No machine-readable, recast compilation of the CMB millicharge limits, stellar/supernova cooling bounds, and collider/beam-dump/direct-detection exclusions exists in the (m_X, epsilon_X, f_X) parameterization needed to delimit the sub-eV, MeV, and heavy multicharged windows for the charge-sequestration scenario.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published Planck millicharge, stellar/SN cooling, and laboratory exclusion curves cited by the paper, recast them to (m_X, epsilon_X) at fixed dark-matter fraction f_X, and package the overlay as a reusable constraint module for the route.

gaps.description: The paper explicitly defers a complete realistic production model: no derivation ties the charge asymmetry, dark-photon annihilation, or parent X' decay history to the required abundance r_X and fraction f_X, so route inputs epsilon_X r_X and f_X are unanchored free parameters rather than outputs of a defined cosmology.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct explicit production histories for each viable window (asymmetric production with dark-photon annihilation for the MeV window; late X' parent decay for the sub-eV window), deriving r_X(m_X, epsilon_X, couplings) so relic-density and structure-formation consistency can be checked alongside the 21 cm signal.

route_step_status.reason: The BLSSM is a renormalizable, UV-complete model with public SARAH model files and SPheno spectrum generation, so identifying right-handed-sneutrino-LSP benchmarks in the double-focus-point soft-term space is covered by existing public tools.

Solving the Yukawa-potential self-scattering beyond the Born limit is possible with published semi-analytic results and public codes such as CLASSICS, but no released pipeline connects the BLSSM sneutrino/bilepton spectrum to sigma_V/m(v) across the classical/resonant regimes.

The overlay itself is a simple comparison, but its relic-density input requires Sommerfeld-enhanced hidden-sector annihilation not provided by stock tools, and the dwarf/cluster SIDM bounds are quoted ranges with likelihood_available no and recasting_needed yes.

gaps.description: No public tool computes the velocity-dependent sneutrino self-scattering cross section sigma_V/m(v) from the BLSSM spectrum: the light bilepton mediator (1-4 MeV against a 1-10 GeV sneutrino) puts the Yukawa scattering deep beyond the Born regime, and existing beyond-Born treatments (partial-wave solvers, the CLASSICS approximations) are standalone and not interfaced to SARAH/SPheno output.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the public CLASSICS semi-analytic Yukawa cross sections (or a numerical partial-wave Schroedinger solver) in a module that reads the SPheno/SARAH BLSSM spectrum (m_snu, m_eta1, effective coupling from T_eta/Y_eta) and returns sigma_V/m at v = 30, 900, 2000 km/s, validated against the paper's benchmarks.

gaps.description: Stock relic-density codes (micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY with standard model files) do not include the Sommerfeld enhancement of sneutrino annihilation into light bilepton pairs that the paper relies on to reach the Planck abundance in the MeV-mediator regime, so Omega h^2 cannot be computed with released tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a micrOMEGAs BLSSM implementation with Sommerfeld factors for the attractive Yukawa potential of eta_1 exchange (Hulthen-potential approximation) applied to the annihilation into bilepton pairs, and rerun the freeze-out integration to reproduce Omega h^2 = 0.1199 +/- 0.0027 benchmarks.

gaps.description: The dwarf and cluster self-interaction constraints used by the card exist only as quoted target ranges (0.1-10 cm^2/g at 30 km/s, 0.1-1.25 at 2000 km/s, 0.1-0.47 at 900 km/s) with no public likelihood, so the allowed region can only be delimited by hard cuts rather than a statistical fit.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood for sigma_V/m(v) from published SIDM halo inferences (dwarf/LSB rotation curves and merging/relaxed cluster analyses, e.g. the Kaplinghat-Tulin-Yu data points), parameterized in (m_snu, m_phi, effective coupling), and release it as a reusable SIDM constraint module.

gaps.description: The CMB/BBN safety of the scenario hinges on the retarded decay of right-handed neutrinos in the bilepton decay chain, but no released energy-injection calculation exists for this specific decay chain, so the bbn_cmb_decay condition is only checked qualitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the electromagnetic/hadronic injection spectra of the eta_1 -> nu_R nu_R -> SM decay chain as a function of Y_nu and mediator lifetime, and run them through DarkHistory (CMB) and standard BBN injection codes to map the allowed lifetime window.

route_step_status.reason: The graviton-to-dark-photon conversion probability in a dark magnetic background is a Gertsenshtein-type mixing calculation that the paper carries out analytically, so the step is pen-and-paper given B_D, the GW frequency, and the dark plasma frequency.

The Delta N_eff mapping from the temperature ratio xi is simple entropy bookkeeping, but the dark-acoustic response requires a Boltzmann code with tightly coupled dark baryons and dark photons through dark recombination, for which only ETHOS-style DM-DR implementations exist without an atomic-DM dark-recombination module.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements the full atomic-dark-matter perturbation history — dark Coulomb-coupled dark baryons and dark photons with a dark recombination transition set by (alpha_D, E_B, m_H, xi) and an interacting fraction f_int — so the dark-acoustic-oscillation signature and the precise f_int <~ 5% CMB bound cannot be recomputed; ETHOS-type CLASS versions cover generic DM-DR scattering but not hydrogenic dark recombination.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an ETHOS-enabled CLASS with a dark-recombination module (a rescaled RECFAST/HyRec solving the hidden-sector Saha/Peebles equations in alpha_D, E_B, m_H, xi) that switches the dark radiation from tightly coupled to free-streaming, then constrain (f_int, E_B, xi) with the standard Planck likelihood.

gaps.description: The conversion observable takes the cosmological dark magnetic field B_D as a free input: no derivation or simulation predicts the dark magnetogenesis mechanism, field strength, coherence length, or its evolution in the dark plasma, so P(g->gamma_D) cannot be turned into a prediction rather than a parameter scan.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run dark-sector magnetohydrodynamics simulations (adapting existing primordial-magnetic-field MHD codes to the U(1)_D plasma with dark recombination) for candidate magnetogenesis mechanisms, delivering B_D spectra and dark plasma frequencies as functions of (alpha_D, xi, E_B) to feed the conversion formula.

gaps.description: No ultrahigh-frequency gravitational-wave measurement or upper limit exists at the frequencies where graviton-to-dark-photon conversion would deplete the signal, so the gw_conversion observable has no dataset or likelihood to be evaluated against, only proposed detector concepts.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt published sensitivity projections of ultrahigh-frequency GW detector concepts (e.g. cavity/Gertsenshtein-based proposals) as forecast likelihoods for the depletion signature, and update to real limits as instruments are built.

route_step_status.reason: Enumerating gauge-invariant symmetry-breaking operators and the clockwork axion profile for a specified abelian quiver is straightforward symbolic algebra done analytically in the paper, requiring at most a small custom script for scans.

The gravitationally induced ALP mass follows from an analytic formula in the operator dimension, cutoff M_c, and decay constant f; the unresolved order-one coefficients are a physics uncertainty, not a missing capability.

The misalignment relic abundance and isocurvature estimate use standard semi-analytic formulas in m_a, f, theta_i, and H_inflation that are textbook-level and also covered by public misalignment calculators.

The step only outputs a detectability flag by overlaying the site-dependent spin coupling on CASPEr-Wind sensitivity projections, which are publicly compiled (e.g. in the AxionLimits repository) and make the comparison a simple lookup.

Two-fluid TOV integration with a BEC dark-matter EOS is a standard, routinely implemented numerical calculation with multiple public implementations in the dark-matter-admixed neutron-star literature.
Tidal Love-number integration on a two-fluid stellar profile is a well-established linear-perturbation calculation the card marks as valid analytic machinery.

gaps.description: No packaged likelihood pipeline maps two-fluid mass-radius and tidal-deformability predictions onto pulsar-mass measurements and GW170817 posteriors for dark-core neutron stars; the card records likelihood_available no/partial and recasting_needed yes for both constraints.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast module that samples the public LIGO/Virgo GW170817 posterior (LALInference samples) and the PSR J0348+0432 mass likelihood inside a Bayesian EOS-inference framework, extending the EOS parameterization with sigma_D/m_D^3 and the dark-core mass fraction as free parameters.

gaps.description: The dark-core mass fraction is an assumed benchmark: no capture/formation/population model exists to predict which neutron stars carry a dark core of a given fraction, so constraints cannot be converted into bounds on underlying particle parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-core mass fraction from the formation channels the paper sketches (neutron-to-DM conversion, bremsstrahlung production, accretion) as a function of m_D and sigma_D, and couple it to a neutron-star population synthesis model to predict the fraction distribution across observed pulsars and merger events.

route_step_status.reason: SARAH/SPheno spectrum generation is public and the paper states the S3 model files are in the SARAH model database.
HiggsBounds is a public tool and was used as the experimental filter in the primary scan workflow.
micrOMEGAs is public, was used by the authors, and standard thermal freeze-out for a Higgs-portal inert scalar is squarely within its regime.

Public machinery exists (micrOMEGAs direct-detection module with DDCalc-style likelihoods, SModelS/CheckMATE for LHC), but the S3-specific recast of inert-doublet limits has not been performed and tool_or_code is null.

gaps.description: Direct-detection and LHC missing-energy limits are only available as inert-doublet-context recasts; no S3-specific pipeline computes sigma_SI from the SARAH spectrum and confronts it with experimental likelihoods, and the card records likelihood_available partial with recasting_needed yes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the existing SARAH/SPheno-to-micrOMEGAs chain to compute sigma_SI for accepted S3 points and evaluate it against LUX/XENON-class likelihoods via DDCalc, and run the same spectra through SModelS or CheckMATE for the inert-scalar LHC missing-energy topologies, replacing the borrowed inert-doublet exclusion curves.

route_step_status.reason: Mass-matrix diagonalization and charged-state lifetime formulas in the small-mixing EFT are pen-and-paper analytics, so the null tool_or_code does not indicate a missing capability.

Public coannihilation-capable Boltzmann solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) exist, but the card identifies no model implementation for this singlet-quintuplet EFT and standard tools omit the electroweak Sommerfeld corrections relevant for a 5-plet.
MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes-style recasting frameworks exist as the card notes, but no packaged displaced-lepton or disappearing-track recast covering this compressed quintuplet spectrum is identified.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/UFO/CalcHEP files) exists for the Majorana singlet plus SU(2)_L quintuplet with dimension-5 mixing and dimension-7/8 operators, so neither relic-density codes nor event generators can be run on this model out of the box.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the singlet-quintuplet EFT in FeynRules including the higher-dimensional mixing and Z-coupling operators, export UFO files for MadGraph/MadDM and CalcHEP files for micrOMEGAs, and validate the coannihilation relic strip against the primary paper.

gaps.description: No reusable likelihood exists for the displaced-lepton and disappearing-track searches on the compressed quintuplet spectrum; the card marks likelihood_available no for both collider constraints and the source bound (five-plet masses below about 280 GeV) is a one-off recast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the ATLAS/CMS disappearing-track and displaced-lepton analyses for pair-produced quintuplet states in a long-lived-particle recast framework (CheckMATE, HackAnalysis, or the SModelS LLP database), parameterized by M, theta, and M-m, and validate against the quoted 280 GeV bound.

gaps.description: Standard relic-density codes do not include the electroweak Sommerfeld enhancement and bound-state effects that significantly shift the freeze-out abundance of an SU(2)_L 5-plet coannihilating sector.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add Sommerfeld-corrected (co)annihilation cross sections for the quintuplet multiplet to the micrOMEGAs/MadDM implementation, adapting the published electroweak-multiplet Sommerfeld/bound-state calculations to the mixed singlet-quintuplet spectrum.

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the singlet-triplet mass matrix and computing charged-state lifetimes in the small-mixing EFT is straightforward analytic work, so the null tool_or_code is not a gap.
Coannihilation-capable public solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) cover this regime, but the card identifies no public model implementation for the singlet-triplet EFT to feed them.

Standard MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes recast chains and compressed-spectrum analyses exist, but no packaged disappearing-track plus soft-dilepton recast for this model is identified and both constraints are marked likelihood_available no.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/UFO/CalcHEP files) exists for the Majorana singlet plus SU(2)_L triplet with dimension-5 mixing and dimension-6 Z-coupling operators, blocking automated relic-density and collider event generation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the singlet-triplet EFT in FeynRules with the higher-dimensional operators, export UFO files for MadGraph/MadDM and CalcHEP files for micrOMEGAs, and validate the coannihilation relic strip against the primary paper.

gaps.description: No reusable likelihood exists for the disappearing-track and soft-dilepton searches on the compressed singlet-triplet spectrum; both collider constraints are marked likelihood_available no and the source exclusions are one-off recasts sensitive to soft-lepton reconstruction thresholds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the ATLAS/CMS disappearing-track and compressed-spectrum soft-dilepton analyses in a recast framework (CheckMATE, MadAnalysis 5 PAD, or SModelS with its LLP database), parameterized by M, theta, and M-m, validating against the source-paper exclusion of the small-mixing relic strip.

route_step_status.reason: Assembling baryonic mass models and supernova/star-formation source terms from published galaxy data is a straightforward data-preparation task requiring no specialized missing tool.
No public code solves the dissipative dark-plasma steady state (local heating-cooling balance plus hydrostatic equilibrium); the paper's estimates are analytic and no tool is identified on the card.
The card states comparisons to satellites, velocity function, and halo structure are qualitative/semi-analytic with no public likelihood.
The local dissipative dark-plasma distribution with Earth shielding is model-specific, differs from the standard halo model, and no tool or derivation exists for it per the card.

Recoil-rate machinery for kinetically mixed dark nuclei exists in generic direct-detection codes, but it requires the nonstandard local flux/velocity distribution and detector-specific likelihoods the card notes are not packaged.

gaps.description: No public solver exists for dissipative dark-plasma halo steady states implementing the paper's local heating-equals-cooling and hydrostatic-balance equations with dark bremsstrahlung/atomic cooling functions and kinetic-mixing supernova heating.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop a semi-analytic steady-state halo code that takes a baryonic mass model and star-formation history, computes the kinetic-mixing supernova heating rate H and dark-plasma cooling rate C as functions of N_sec, epsilon, and dark metallicity, and solves the coupled hydrostatic profile, validated against the paper's N_sec=5, epsilon~1.2e-10 examples.

gaps.description: No cosmological hydrodynamic simulations exist for the N_sec-copy dissipative dark sector, so satellite abundance/planarity, the field-galaxy velocity function, and baryon-correlated halo structure predictions rest on idealized steady-state arguments (the card marks simulation_calibrated partial).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a galaxy-formation hydrodynamics code (e.g. GIZMO or AREPO) with a second dissipative fluid carrying dark-electromagnetic cooling and kinetic-mixing supernova heating, and run zoom-in simulations of Milky-Way-like and dwarf halos across the N_sec, epsilon parameter plane.

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline maps dissipative-halo predictions onto small-scale-structure data (Milky Way satellite counts, field velocity function, halo structure), so the small_scale_halo_phenomenology comparison remains pass/fail by eye.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt existing Milky Way satellite likelihoods (DES plus Pan-STARRS style) and velocity-function datasets to consume the suppressed low-mass halo function and dissipative profiles produced by the steady-state solver or simulations, exposing N_sec and epsilon as likelihood parameters.

gaps.description: The local dark-plasma phase-space distribution at Earth, including detector shielding and dark-metal composition, has not been derived, and without it kinetic-mixing direct-detection rates cannot be computed from standard Maxwellian halo assumptions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the local dark-plasma density, temperature, and velocity distribution from the steady-state halo solution, model dark-electromagnetic shielding and capture by the Earth for epsilon~1e-10, and feed the resulting flux into standard nuclear/electronic recoil-rate codes with detector-specific efficiencies.

gaps.description: No modified Boltzmann-code implementation exists for N_sec hidden Standard Model copies with colder sector temperatures, dark acoustic oscillations, and dark-photon diffusion damping, so the CMB/LSS consistency and the smooth transfer-function cutoff cannot be computed quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with a multi-fluid hidden sector (dark baryons, dark electrons, dark photons, dark neutrino-like radiation per copy) adapting existing atomic-dark-matter/ETHOS-style implementations, parameterized by N_sec, the sector temperature ratio, and epsilon, to produce transfer functions and Delta-N_eff for the CMB/LSS consistency check.

route_step_status.reason: Relativistic freeze-out abundance, Delta_N_eff, and a free-streaming proxy follow from standard analytic formulas given in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code reflects a pen-and-paper step.

CLASS/CAMB natively handle an extra massive thermal relic and public Planck/LSS likelihoods exist, but the card imports no likelihood and the model-specific (m_nuR, T_f, g_starS) to (Delta_N_eff, hot fraction) pipeline is not set up.
Computing C_RR^V Wilson coefficients, R_D(*), and EWP shifts from (m_Wprime, g_R, mixing) is analytic tree-level matching documented in the primary paper.

Public flavor-fit frameworks (flavio/smelli-class tools) and collider recast resources cover right-handed b-to-c operators, but the card lists no imported likelihood and the W-prime/vector-like sector recast is not implemented.

gaps.description: No assembled cosmological likelihood pipeline maps this model's right-handed-neutrino sector (m_nuR, T_f, g_starS, N_nuR) onto current CMB and LSS constraints; the card carries only the paper's rough 60 eV / 10 eV estimates and likelihood_available is 'no' for both cosmological constraints.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the nu_R as an extra ncdm species plus Delta_N_eff in CLASS, wire it to the public Planck 2018 + BAO + full-shape LSS likelihoods in Cobaya/MontePython, and add a thin wrapper translating (m_nuR, T_f, g_starS) into the ncdm temperature and mass inputs.

gaps.description: No numerical flavor/EWP/collider recast exists for the W-prime SU(2)_V sector that fixes the right-handed-neutrino parameters; the R_D(*), FCNC, EWP, and direct-search constraints are only described qualitatively (likelihood_available 'no', recasting_needed 'yes').
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the C_RR^V operator and right-handed mixing structure in a global flavor-fit package (e.g. extend flavio/smelli with the light-nu_R final state) and recast LHC W-prime and vector-like fermion searches for the model's benchmark spectra.

route_step_status.reason: Boundedness/unitarity checks and neutral-fermion mass diagonalization are standard analytic steps for a renormalizable 2HDM plus singlet-doublet Lagrangian, with public 2HDM tools (2HDMC-class) covering the scalar-sector checks.

micrOMEGAs handles thermal freeze-out for this class of model, but the card identifies no public model implementation (computational_representation null, associated code unknown), so a model file must first be built.

sigma_SI/sigma_SD from Higgs/Z exchange are computable with micrOMEGAs+DDCalc-class tools once a model file exists, but no implementation or direct-detection likelihood is attached (likelihood_available 'no') and blind-spot cancellations demand careful convention matching.

Public 2HDM constraint tools (HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals, flavor packages) exist and are named generically by the card, but the step's own validity note says updated experimental datasets and integration are required for production use.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP/UFO model files) of the 2HDM-portal singlet-doublet Majorana fermion model exists in the registry, so the micrOMEGAs-style relic calculation and the direct-detection cross sections cannot be run as-is (computational_representation is null and associated code is unknown).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules implementation of the 2HDM (types I/II/lepton-specific/flipped) plus singlet-doublet fermion Lagrangian, export CalcHEP model files for micrOMEGAs to compute Omega h^2, sigma_SI, and sigma_SD, and validate against the paper's red relic contours and blind-spot cancellations.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood is attached for the XENON1T blind-spot constraint (likelihood_available 'no', contours not digitized), so exclusion statements cannot be reproduced numerically or updated to XENONnT/LZ exposures.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the model's sigma_SI/sigma_SD outputs to DDCalc (XENON1T, LZ, XENONnT likelihoods), including a relic-fraction rescaling for underabundant points.

gaps.description: The combined 2HDM Higgs-sector, flavor, and invisible-width constraint evaluation (con_2hdm_higgs_colliders_flavor, likelihood_available 'partial') is not wired to current datasets for this model's spectra, including the dark-fermion contributions to invisible h/Z widths.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals (or HiggsTools) with current LHC Higgs data on the 2HDM spectrum, add SuperIso/flavio for B -> X_s gamma and related flavor bounds, and include the singlet-doublet loop and invisible-width contributions computed from the model file of gap_1.

route_step_status.reason: The paper's relic calculation relied on a modified micrOMEGAs with radiative, loop, Sommerfeld, and co-annihilation corrections whose public availability is unknown; stock micrOMEGAs covers the tree-level rates but not the QCD-corrected cross sections the validity note requires.

The loop-level matching of top/mediator loops onto gluon-nucleon operators follows published analytic results cited by the card (arXiv:1007.2601-type matching), making sigma_SI a standard semi-analytic computation.

A MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes-style chain is named and public, and pair-produced colored top partners decaying to top plus invisible scalar are a standard recast topology, though it was not run in this batch.

Experiment-specific likelihood components exist publicly (DDCalc for xenon limits, Fermi-LAT dwarf/spectral-feature likelihoods, SModelS/CheckMATE-class collider recasts) but the card imports none of them and no combined likelihood is assembled.

gaps.description: The authors' modified micrOMEGAs implementing radiative corrections, loop-induced channels, Sommerfeld enhancement, and mediator co-annihilation for the top-philic vector-like portal has unknown availability and no public repository, so the precision relic-density calculation the analysis depends on cannot be reproduced with stock tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recover or reimplement the corrections as a public micrOMEGAs extension: add the QCD-corrected annihilation/co-annihilation cross sections and Sommerfeld factors for the colored T mediator, and validate against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 contours; for y_t below about 1e-4 also add the coupled Boltzmann treatment the paper flags.

gaps.description: No direct-detection, gamma-ray spectral-feature, or LHC recast likelihood is assembled for this model (all three constraints have likelihood_available 'partial' and were not rerun), so the multichannel complementarity conclusions (m_S reach near 700 GeV, mediator reach near 6 TeV) cannot be re-evaluated or updated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a combined likelihood: DDCalc for XENON1T/LZ spin-independent limits on the loop-induced sigma_SI, the public Fermi-LAT dwarf and spectral-feature likelihoods applied to the t tbar plus internal-bremsstrahlung spectra, and a MadGraph+Delphes recast of Run-2 stop/top-partner searches (via CheckMATE or MadAnalysis PADs) including compressed-spectrum signal regions.

route_step_status.reason: The critical temperature and v_c/T_c follow analytically from the one-loop finite-temperature effective potential given by the source, and public codes of the CosmoTransitions class cover the same computation.
micrOMEGAs is named, public, and the Z2 singlet Higgs-portal model is a standard bundled use case for its relic-density solver.

Public direct-detection likelihood tools (DDCalc with XENON1T/LUX/LZ tables) cover Higgs-portal sigma_SI, but the card attaches no likelihood (likelihood_available 'no') and notes fresh curve digitization plus singlet-fraction rescaling are still required.

gaps.description: No machine-readable direct-detection likelihood is attached for the XENON/LUX exclusion of the simultaneous DM+SFOPT region; the card records only the paper's qualitative exclusion statement, and a proper treatment must rescale sigma_SI by the singlet relic fraction for subcomponent points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire micrOMEGAs sigma_SI output to DDCalc's XENON1T/LZ likelihoods with automatic (Omega_s/Omega_DM) rescaling, and rerun the (m_s, lambda_hs) scan to reproduce and update the source exclusion.

gaps.description: The EWPT observable is evaluated only through the gauge-dependent v_c/T_c > 1 critical-temperature proxy; no bubble-nucleation calculation (T_n, alpha, beta/H) exists for this model card, which blocks any quantitative baryogenesis-viability or gravitational-wave-spectrum statement.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run CosmoTransitions (or BSMPT) on the source's finite-temperature singlet/Higgs potential to compute nucleation temperature and transition strength parameters, replacing the v_c/T_c proxy and enabling a LISA-style gravitational-wave signal estimate over the surviving parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: Assembling kinetic, gravitational, and self-interaction energies for the angular-momentum ansatz is the analytic variational setup given explicitly in the primary paper.
Extremizing the energy functional at fixed N and L is a semi-analytic minimization reproducible with elementary numerics from the paper's formulas.

Follow-up rotating-Bose-star simulations exist in the literature the card cites, but no public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson code or systematic stability classification covering this model's full (l, self-interaction sign) space is attached.
Comparing R_90 to the Einstein radius to flag pointlike versus extended lensing is a simple analytic data transform.

No microlensing event-rate calculator or Subaru HSC likelihood handling finite-size clump lenses is attached, and the required clump mass function and halo fraction inputs are not predicted anywhere in the card.
Exporting the density/field profile of the variational solution is a trivial data transform once the clump branch is computed.
The Floquet photon-resonance criterion exists in the cited follow-up paper, but no public solver is available and it has not been applied to the non-spherical angular-momentum profiles.

gaps.description: No dynamical-stability certification exists for the l > 0 variational clump branch: cited follow-up simulations find rotating Bose stars with attractive or negligible self-interactions unstable, but no public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson simulation suite maps stability across (l, self-interaction sign and strength, M), so it is unknown which angular-momentum configurations survive as long-lived dark-matter clumps.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run 3D Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson evolutions of the paper's stationary l > 0 profiles across attractive, negligible, and repulsive quartic couplings, recovering the spherical l = 0 limit as validation, and publish a stability map plus lifetime estimates as a registry data product.

gaps.description: The model predicts no cosmological clump abundance: the mass function, halo fraction, and angular-momentum distribution of clumps are unspecified (the card notes 'no cosmological abundance for these clumps is derived'), so no event-rate or flux prediction can be normalized.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the clump mass and angular-momentum distribution from structure-formation simulations of the post-misalignment axion/scalar field (kinetic-relaxation or miniclusters-to-solitons pipelines), parameterized by (m, f_a, lambda), and store it as the input mass function for the microlensing and radio routes.

gaps.description: No microlensing event-rate calculator or likelihood handling extended (finite-size) clump lenses is available; published Subaru HSC limits assume pointlike lenses, and the card's compactness constraint says extended clumps weaken direct application of those limits.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public HSC/OGLE microlensing event-rate code with finite-lens-size magnification for the angular-momentum-modified R_90(M, l) relation and standard-halo kinematics, producing exclusion curves in (M, R_90, halo fraction).

gaps.description: The photon-resonance (Floquet) solver from the cited follow-up paper is not public and has never been applied to non-spherical l > 0 clump profiles, so the predicted angular-momentum-enabled radio resonance cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement an open-source Floquet-exponent solver for axion-photon parametric resonance that accepts non-spherical field profiles, validate it on the follow-up paper's spherical no-resonance result, then scan the l > 0 branch in (l, M, g_a_gamma).

route_step_status.reason: Integrating an inflaton/reheating FRW background is standard numerics with generic ODE solvers, but no named public inflation-reheating background pipeline is identified in the card and the result depends on the chosen inflaton model.

The QFT-in-curved-spacetime mode equations are well defined and solved semi-analytically/numerically in the paper, but no public gravitational-particle-production mode-function solver covering arbitrary (m_chi, xi, background) is indicated.
Summing gravitational, coherent, and thermal graviton-exchange contributions into Omega_chi h^2 is a simple analytic bookkeeping step requiring no dedicated tool.

Comparing the coherent fraction to the quoted S_DM < 9e-6 bound is trivial, but the card records likelihood_available: no, so only a fixed threshold cut exists rather than a proper scale-dependent CMB isocurvature likelihood.

gaps.description: No public code solves the scalar mode equations for gravitational particle production in a coupled inflaton/reheating background for general m_chi, xi, H_inf, and T_R; the paper relies on private semi-analytic and numerical estimates, so the relic abundance and coherent fraction cannot be recomputed or scanned by outside users.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop and release a Bogoliubov mode-function solver coupled to an inflaton background integrator: integrate the FRW plus inflaton-oscillation background for a parameterized potential, solve the chi mode equations with nonminimal coupling xi, output occupation numbers n_k, Omega_chi h^2, and the coherent-oscillation fraction, validated against the conformal-coupling suppression limit at xi = 1/6.

gaps.description: The CMB isocurvature constraint is applied only as a single quoted upper limit S_DM < 9e-6; there is no likelihood that propagates the model's scale-dependent (potentially blue) dark-matter isocurvature spectrum through a Boltzmann code to Planck data, which the card flags as the way small-scale spectra can evade the large-scale bound.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the model's isocurvature power spectrum shape from the coherent scalar fluctuations, feed it as a CDM-isocurvature initial condition into CLASS or CAMB, and evaluate against the Planck isocurvature likelihood so the constraint becomes a function of (R_chi, m_chi/H_inf, spectral tilt) rather than a fixed threshold.

route_step_status.reason: The near-resonant p-wave A'-mediated annihilation cross section is given as closed-form formulae in the primary paper, so this step is trivially analytic.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM-class) handle resonant p-wave freeze-out, but no model implementation is attached (tool_or_code null, no associated code) and near-resonance thermal averaging is sensitive to the xi offset, so files must be built and validated.

The card names only a generic '21-cm baryon cooling model'; the millicharged DM-baryon cooling calculation exists in the literature but no runnable public forward model producing T21 from (f_DM, epsilon, m_phi) is attached, and cosmic-dawn astrophysics remains external.
Dark-photon production cross sections for lepton fixed-target/collider setups are standard analytic results and the card records them as the tool for this step.

BaBar/NA64 invisible-A' bounds exist publicly but the card notes exact exclusion contours were not digitized and experiment-specific acceptances are needed; no likelihood is supplied (tool_or_code null).

gaps.description: No public forward model converts (f_DM, epsilon, m_phi) into a global 21-cm brightness temperature for a millicharged subcomponent: the velocity-dependent Coulomb-like scattering with hydrogen, residual electrons, and protons must be evolved through recombination to cosmic dawn together with baryon temperature and bulk relative velocities, and no such code is attached to the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the DM-baryon fluid cooling equations with the sigma proportional to v^-4 millicharged cross section (Munoz-Loeb-style treatment including relative bulk velocities and Coulomb heating of the DM subcomponent) coupled to a global-signal astrophysics model, exposing f_DM, epsilon, and m_phi as inputs and T21(z about 17) as output.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for the cosmic-dawn absorption target: the EDGES-motivated fraction/coupling window is recorded only as a qualitative parameter region (likelihood_available: no, recasting_needed: yes), with no statistical treatment of the EDGES amplitude, its contested systematics, or competing non-detections.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a global 21-cm likelihood that marginalizes over foreground/systematic models for the EDGES low-band data (and can incorporate subsequent global-signal measurements), returning a posterior on the excess-cooling amplitude that the baryon-cooling forward model can be scored against instead of the fixed f_DM 0.003-0.02 window.

gaps.description: The relic-fraction step has no implementation: computing f_DM from near-resonant p-wave freeze-out requires careful thermal averaging across the A' resonance (relic abundance is sensitive to the resonance offset xi per the card's validity domain), and no model files or solver configuration exist for the scalar millicharged phi plus invisible A' setup.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the phi/A' simplified model in a standard relic code (micrOMEGAs or MadDM) with resonance-aware thermal averaging, validate f_DM against the paper's quoted mass/fraction windows as the route's validation test specifies, then scan xi and e_D.

gaps.description: Digitized invisible dark-photon exclusion contours are missing: the BaBar and NA64 bounds for m_Aprime about 20-200 MeV are recorded only qualitatively (the coupling symbol is even noted as ambiguous in the extraction), so the collider route cannot produce quantitative excluded regions or Belle II/LDMX projections in the near-resonant EDGES-motivated parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published BaBar and NA64 invisible-search exclusion curves, resolve the coupling normalization against the original experimental papers, and encode them as limit tables with the invisible branching fraction (near unity per the route's validation test) and e_D dependence made explicit.

gaps.description: Direct-detection constraints cannot be applied or dismissed rigorously: the card's evacuation caveat (millicharged DM depleted from the Galactic disk by magnetic fields plus terrestrial shielding) rests on qualitative propagation assumptions with no dedicated model, leaving the XENON10/COHERENT applicability undetermined (robustness: low).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop a propagation model for the millicharged subcomponent in Galactic magnetic fields plus an Earth/atmosphere shielding calculation for epsilon about 1e-6 to 1e-4 and m_phi 10-80 MeV, yielding the local density and velocity distribution at detector depth needed to recast terrestrial scattering limits.

route_step_status.reason: The A'-mediated p-wave annihilation cross section near resonance is given by analytic formulae in the primary paper and is straightforward to evaluate.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) handle kinetic-mixing dark-photon freeze-out, but the vector millicharged model file is not implemented and near-resonance p-wave freeze-out needs careful thermal averaging beyond the default treatment.

Millicharged DM-baryon cooling models for the cosmic-dawn 21-cm signal exist in the literature, but no packaged public code takes (f_DM, epsilon, m_V) to a T21 absorption amplitude, and the astrophysical cosmic-dawn assumptions are external.

Dark-photon production cross sections at lepton fixed-target and collider setups are standard analytic results with public implementations (e.g. Darkcast-style rescaling of published production rates).

Published BaBar/NA64 invisible-A' limits can be rescaled, but the card notes no likelihood is supplied and experiment-specific acceptances plus the near-resonant invisible branching fraction in (epsilon, m_Aprime, e_D) space require a dedicated recast with digitized exclusion curves.

gaps.description: No public packaged code maps a millicharged DM subcomponent (f_DM about 0.003-0.02, epsilon about 1e-6 to 1e-4, m_V of 13.6-80 MeV) with velocity-dependent Coulomb-like scattering on hydrogen, electrons, and protons to a global 21-cm brightness-temperature prediction at z ~ 17; the route's key step is a semi-analytic cooling model that is not released.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public global-21cm framework (e.g. ARES or a released Munoz-Loeb-type DM-baryon fluid code) with the fraction-dependent millicharged drag/heating terms, including relative-velocity dependence and the residual-electron coupling, exposing (f_DM, epsilon, m_V) as inputs and returning T21(z).

gaps.description: The relic-fraction step has no implementation: the vector millicharged DM plus near-resonant invisible dark photon model is not available as a micrOMEGAs/MadDM model file, and the resonant p-wave thermal average (xi = m_Aprime/2m_V slightly above 1) is exactly the regime where default freeze-out treatments lose accuracy.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the V, A' model (kinetic mixing epsilon, dark charge e_D) in micrOMEGAs or MadDM via FeynRules/CalcHEP model files and validate the resonance-region thermal averaging against direct numerical integration of the Boltzmann equation, reproducing the paper's f_DM windows.

gaps.description: No digitized exclusion curves or likelihood exist for recasting BaBar/NA64 invisible dark-photon searches (and Belle II/LDMX projections) into this model's near-resonant (epsilon, m_Aprime, e_D) parameter space; the card records the bounds only qualitatively with an ambiguous coupling normalization.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published BaBar and NA64 invisible-A' exclusion curves, verify the invisible branching ratio is near unity across the scanned e_D range, and recast via Darkcast-style rate rescaling into the EDGES-motivated parameter plane, packaging the result as a reusable exclusion map or approximate likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The collapse probabilities beta(M) and the delta_c = 0.05 transition criterion are analytic formulae given in the primary paper and can be evaluated by hand for a specified sigma(M).
Turning beta(M) plus the reheating history into d f_PBH/dM with M_min and M_max is straightforward semi-analytic integration of the paper's expressions, requiring no dedicated tool.

Public monochromatic PBH constraint compilations (e.g. PBHbounds-style datasets) and the published extended-mass-function recast procedure exist, but the slow-reheating mass function has not been passed through them and the card says the primary paper leaves this evaluation undone.

Analytic PBH binary merger-rate frameworks exist in the literature, but no public model covers the enhanced initial clustering of PBHs formed during an extended matter-dominated reheating era, and the card notes merger-rate modeling is absent from the primary paper.

gaps.description: No pipeline applies the compiled monochromatic PBH constraints (microlensing, evaporation, dynamical, CMB, gravitational-wave) to the slow-reheating extended mass function with its delta_c-dependent M_min/M_max cutoffs; the card's key constraint entry is marked recasting_needed: yes and the primary paper explicitly leaves the observational abundance evaluation undone.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the slow-reheating d f_PBH/dM in an extended-mass-function recast (Carr et al. procedure) on top of a maintained monochromatic bounds compilation such as PBHbounds, parameterized by (T_reh, sigma(M), delta_c), and output allowed f_PBH as a function of reheating parameters.

gaps.description: The collapse probability during the matter-dominated reheating phase is not simulation-calibrated: the card flags critical-collapse behavior in a matter era as uncertain (possible low-mass tail below M_min), and beta(M) in matter domination depends on anisotropy and angular-momentum suppression factors known only from approximate analytic arguments.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity simulations of nonspherical collapse of overdensities in a matter-dominated (oscillating scalar condensate) background across the transition to radiation domination, calibrating the collapse threshold, anisotropy/spin suppression of beta(M), and the presence of a critical-collapse low-mass tail.

gaps.description: No merger-rate model exists for PBHs formed during slow reheating: converting the extended mass function and f_PBH into a LIGO/Virgo merger-rate prediction requires binary-formation and clustering modeling that must account for the enhanced small-scale clustering of matter-era-formed PBHs, which standard radiation-era merger-rate formulae do not cover.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend published analytic PBH binary formation rates (Ali-Haimoud/Raidal-type calculations) to extended mass functions with initial clustering statistics appropriate to matter-dominated formation, and compare the resulting rate against the LIGO/Virgo compact-binary population.

route_step_status.reason: The n -> chi + gamma branching ratio follows from the effective-operator calculation in the primary paper, an analytic computation using standard hadronic inputs that needs no dedicated tool.
The Delta B=2 amplitude from tree and box diagrams in the RPV MSSM is an analytic calculation, with the required six-quark hadronic matrix elements available from published lattice-QCD results.
Comparing the derived oscillation time against the quoted tau_nnbar > 1e8 s lower bound is a trivial pen-and-paper recast.

The paper's 6FQM thermodynamic estimates give the benchmark M_nugget and R_nugget analytically, but the controlling input (initial quark-pocket radius from the supercooled first-order transition) is not computed by any tool and the card flags it as a dominant uncertainty.
The halo flux of macroscopic dark matter from local density, mass, and a standard velocity distribution is a simple analytic calculation.

Published macro exclusion regions (EROS/MACHO/Subaru-HSC microlensing, femtolensing, seismic) exist in the literature, but the card notes no digitized exclusion curves or likelihoods are available, so the mass-radius recast cannot currently be run quantitatively.

gaps.description: The nugget mass function rests on an unmodeled phase-transition history: no calculation exists of bubble nucleation, pocket size R_i, and pocket trapping for a first-order six-flavor QCD transition under electroweak supercooling, nor of nugget evaporation/survival during cooling, leaving the benchmark M_nugget ~ 1e10 g and R_nugget ~ 1e2 cm uncertain by orders of magnitude.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the supercooled electroweak transition for the benchmark scalar potential with CosmoTransitions (nucleation temperature, bubble spacing), then run hydrodynamic simulations of quark-pocket shrinkage and baryon-number trapping through the six-flavor QCD transition, coupled to an evaporation-rate derivation, to produce a predictive nugget mass function beta(M_nugget).

gaps.description: No digitized, reusable compilation of macroscopic-dark-matter constraints exists in (M_nugget, R_nugget or sigma_geo, f_DM) space: the card's lensing/seismic/femtolensing constraint entry has likelihood_available: no and coverage of the 1e10 g benchmark region is patchy and undigitized.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published EROS, MACHO, Subaru/HSC, femtolensing, seismic, and red-giant macro exclusion curves and package them as a maintained mass-radius constraint database (analogous to PBHbounds but with explicit cross-section dependence), including finite-size and finite-source lensing corrections relevant at R_nugget ~ 1e2 cm.

gaps.description: No quantitative rate and signature model exists for the proposed transient probes: photon emission from nugget collisions with compact stars and with other nuggets is described only qualitatively, with no derived energy-deposition spectrum, event rate, or detectability estimate for the 6FQM benchmark.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the energy deposition and photon light curve for a 1e10 g, 1e2 cm nugget impacting a neutron star or white dwarf surface, combine with the halo flux calculation into a per-survey transient rate, and identify which existing transient surveys bound or could detect the predicted events.

route_step_status.reason: Generic multi-component relic solvers (micrOMEGAs multi-component mode, DRAKE-style solvers) exist, but the coupled psi/Z_D system with conversion processes and dark-Higgs-controlled depletion has no public model implementation (tool_or_code null, computational_representation null).

Velocity-dependent sigma_T/m for fermion DM exchanging a light vector mediator is standard analytic work with published Born/classical/resonant formulas, so the null tool_or_code does not block this step.

Planck energy-injection machinery (ExoCLASS/DarkHistory-style f_eff bounds) exists publicly, but the two-species annihilation with Z_D h_D and h_D h_D channels, dark-Higgs decay cascades, and recombination-era Sommerfeld factors has no ready recast; the card marks the likelihood only approximate and the step planned.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the coupled two-component Boltzmann system for psi and stable Z_D including psi-Z_D conversion processes, Z_D Z_D -> h_D h_D depletion, and Higgs-portal-controlled h_D decays; the relic abundances of both species feed every downstream observable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model in micrOMEGAs' multi-component dark-matter mode (or a dedicated coupled-Boltzmann code such as a DRAKE extension) with the conversion collision terms from the primary paper, and validate against the paper's benchmark relic-density contours.

gaps.description: No CMB energy-injection recast exists for this model's two-species annihilation (psi psi -> Z_D h_D plus residual Z_D Z_D -> h_D h_D) where visible energy arrives only after dark-Higgs decay; the required f_eff depends on species abundances, h_D visible branching, and recombination-era Sommerfeld enhancement.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute channel-weighted f_eff(z) with DarkHistory (or ExoCLASS) using h_D decay spectra for each mass point, include the Sommerfeld factor at recombination velocities, and compare to the Planck p_ann constraint to produce excluded regions in the mass-coupling plane.

gaps.description: The SIDM constraint is only a phenomenological target window (0.1-10 cm^2/g at dwarf velocities, <1 cm^2/g at cluster velocities), not a halo-observation likelihood, so parameter-space statements are qualitative (card lists likelihood_available: approximate and recasting_needed: yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt or build a velocity-binned sigma_T/m likelihood from published dwarf rotation-curve and cluster ensemble fits (Kaplinghat-style SIDM halo-model inference) and map the model's sigma_T/m(v) curve onto it.

route_step_status.reason: Public spectrum generators (SPheno, FeynHiggs) named in the card handle high-scale gaugino-mediation boundary conditions with nonzero trilinears and deliver the sparticle spectrum and Higgs mass.
