CMS HSCP results and generic BBN bounds exist publicly, but the card notes the 13 TeV reinterpretation is less detailed than Run 1, no efficiency-map recast tool is cited (tool_or_code null), and no BBN cascade calculation was run for the benchmarks.

gaps.description: No maintained public recast of current-luminosity CMS/ATLAS heavy-stable-charged-particle searches with efficiency maps applicable to the stau-NLSP benchmarks; the card only has the Run 1 recast plus a less detailed early 13 TeV reinterpretation, so collider viability of stau-NLSP points cannot be evaluated against present data.

gaps.description: BBN constraints on the long-lived NLSP (con_bbn_long_lived_particles, likelihood_available: no) have not been computed for this model's spectra: the NLSP freeze-out yield, lifetime, and hadronic/electromagnetic branching fractions were never fed into a light-element cascade calculation for the assigned benchmarks.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute NLSP relic yields with micrOMEGAs from the SPheno spectra, derive decay spectra into the gravitino, and evaluate light-element constraints with a public BBN injection code (ACROPOLIS-type), producing an exclusion in the (tau_NLSP, yield) plane per NLSP class.

route_step_status.reason: Setting up photon mode equations via vector spherical harmonics on a clump background is the primary paper's analytic framework and requires no external tool.

The numerical Floquet/mode solve for growth exponents on arbitrary (including rotating) clump profiles has no public code (tool_or_code null, associated_code unknown) and is not analytically tractable beyond special cases.

Converting growth exponents into observable radio flux requires a Galactic clump source population and plasma propagation model that the card says are not fixed by the primary paper and for which no tool is cited.
The clump mass function and encounter rate are explicitly not fixed by the primary paper and no semi-analytic population code is cited.
Related axion-clump merger simulations exist in the cited literature (src_2005_02405), but no reusable public pipeline maps initial clump masses to post-merger masses and profiles for this route.
No radio transient survey likelihood with selection functions is attached to the card and the step's tool_or_code is null; this comparison is not pen-and-paper.

gaps.description: No public numerical solver computes photon parametric-resonance (Floquet) growth exponents for finite, non-spherical or rotating axion clump profiles with backreaction and photon escape; only the paper's case-by-case analysis exists.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release a mode-equation solver built on the paper's vector-spherical-harmonic decomposition that integrates the coupled axion-photon equations on user-specified clump profiles (spherical and angular-momentum-carrying), outputs growth exponents versus escape rate, and is validated against the primary paper's resonance/no-resonance boundaries.

gaps.description: No likelihood connects predicted coherent radio emission or merger-triggered bursts to actual radio surveys: the card lists radio transient/line searches as target likelihoods but no survey selection functions, plasma propagation treatment, or detectability pipeline exists for this signal class.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a detectability pipeline that folds predicted burst luminosities and rates through Galactic plasma dispersion/absorption and the published selection functions of radio transient and spectral-line surveys (CHIME, SKA precursors, FRB catalogs), returning survey-level exclusion or discovery likelihoods.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the full G2HDM Lagrangian in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and run micrOMEGAs for relic density (including coannihilation with Delta, H+, W^(p,m), f^H) and direct detection, validating against the inert-doublet limit where the extra states decouple.

gaps.description: Inert-doublet direct-detection, indirect-detection, and LHC search limits used as proxies (LUX/XENON, Fermi/AMS, monojet, disappearing tracks) have no G2HDM recast: the gauge-origin stabilization and extra SU(2)_H states change production and decay topologies, and the card marks both constraints as recast_required with only partial likelihoods.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast pipeline: generate G2HDM signal events with MadGraph using the gap_1 model files and pass them through public recast frameworks (MadAnalysis5/CheckMATE for monojet and inert-scalar searches; DDCalc for XENON/LZ; likelihood from Planck Omega h2), producing combined exclusion contours in the (m_D, lambda_L, splitting) space.

route_step_status.reason: Annihilation and decay widths follow analytically from the fully specified N2HDM-plus-dark-U(1) Lagrangian; this is standard pen-and-paper tree-level work despite the null tool_or_code.

Standard Boltzmann solvers (micrOMEGAs) handle the conventional WIMP regime, but the unconventional and cannibally co-decaying regimes require a coupled hidden-sector-temperature treatment that no named public tool on the card provides.

Public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihood tables exist, but the card notes the likelihood was not reproduced and recasting onto the two-step cascade spectrum is still needed.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann solver covers the unconventional-WIMP and cannibally co-decaying freeze-out regimes of the secluded X/S system, which require evolving a separate hidden-sector temperature and mediator decay term; micrOMEGAs-style codes assume kinetic equilibrium with the SM bath.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a coupled-temperature relic code (e.g. build on micrOMEGAs' two-sector mode or a bespoke solver in the style of the cannibal-dark-matter literature) to evolve n_X, n_S, and T_hidden with the S decay rate through hidden-visible mixing, mapping the three freeze-out regimes over (m_X, m_S, g_X, mixing angle).

gaps.description: The Fermi-LAT Galactic-center and dwarf-spheroidal constraints have not been recast onto the cascade spectrum: the card marks con_1806_gce_dwarfs as recasting_needed with only a partial likelihood, and no combined GCE+dwarf+g-2 fit pipeline exists for this parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a recast pipeline feeding the gap_2 tabulated spectra into the public Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihood tables (and a GCE spectrum likelihood with profiled diffuse-background systematics), combined with the type-X 2HDM Delta a_mu and lepton-universality constraints, to produce joint posteriors over (m_X, m_S, m_A, tan_beta).

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level EFT matching of heavy scalar messengers onto baryon-number-violating operators is standard analytic work fully specified by the card's Lagrangian-level content.

Phase-space integration is analytic, but the required hadronic matrix elements of dimension-nine operators for K_L, B0, and neutron invisible decays have no dedicated public code and carry dominant uncertainties per the card's caveats.

The card names only an approximate 'thermal relic calculator plus neutron-star mapping'; no public multi-component hidden-sector Boltzmann solver or neutron-star recast tool covers this dark-photon-bath model, and the validity note says the calculation is approximate until a full treatment exists.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann relic-abundance code handles this multi-component dark-fermion sector with a massless dark-photon bath, hidden-sector thermalization, and messenger-mediated annihilation to SM fermions; the primary paper's relic estimates are approximate thermally-averaged cross-section arguments.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or a coupled-Boltzmann code such as that used for hidden-sector freeze-out) to track multiple stable dark-fermion species and a dark-photon temperature separate from the SM bath, with messenger-exchange annihilation channels implemented from the model Lagrangian.

gaps.description: Hadronic matrix elements of the dimension-nine baryon-number-violating operators that mediate K_L, B0, and neutron invisible decays are not computed for this model; the card notes they and narrow phase-space windows dominate the numerical rates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the relevant baryon- and meson-to-dark-sector matrix elements with lattice QCD (adapting existing proton-decay/neutron-antineutron matrix-element calculations to these dim-9 operators) or with QCD sum rules, and package them with the phase-space integration as a small public branching-ratio code.

gaps.description: No likelihood or validated recast exists for translating the laboratory neutron dark-decay operator into neutron-star constraints for this model; the card marks the constraint recast_required with likelihood_available: no and dense-matter blocking effects unquantified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion rate including Pauli blocking and dark-sector self-interactions, fold it into a neutron-star equation-of-state solver, and publish a mapping from (operator coefficient, dark final-state masses) to allowed/excluded regions against observed two-solar-mass pulsars.

route_step_status.reason: The one-loop C_9^NP and B_s-mixing amplitudes follow from published loop functions in the source papers and can be evaluated analytically or with standard flavor packages (flavio/smelli) once the Wilson coefficients are written down.

micrOMEGAs-style relic calculations cover standard freeze-out for this WIMP, but no public model implementation of the U(1)_X Majorana model exists on the card, so the solver cannot be run without first building the model files.

XENON1T-class limits are public and Higgs-portal spin-independent scattering is standard, but the card gives only benchmark contours with no bundled likelihood, so a recast against current detector limits is still needed.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP or micrOMEGAs model files) exists for the dark U(1)_X Majorana model with N_-/N_+, the q and lepton-like scalars, Z', and dark Higgs H_2, so the relic density across the Yukawa, dark-gauge, and Higgs-portal annihilation scenarios and the spin-independent cross section cannot be computed reproducibly.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the full Lagrangian in FeynRules, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and reproduce the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 contours in the three annihilation scenarios plus the sigma_SI(theta_H, M_-) predictions as validation.

gaps.description: No bundled or portable likelihood exists for either the flavor fit (R_K, R_K*, B_s -> mu mu, B_s mixing — whose world averages have shifted since the paper) or the direct-detection exclusion (only XENON1T benchmark contours were read); both constraints are flagged recasting_needed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the model's Wilson coefficients into flavio/smelli for a current global b -> s ll and B_s-mixing likelihood, and pass the sigma_SI predictions through DDCalc with XENON1T/XENONnT/LZ likelihoods, exposing a combined flavor+relic+direct-detection likelihood over (M_-, g_X, theta_H, m_H2, lambda_q, lambda_l).

route_step_status.reason: The washout/asymmetry-transfer Boltzmann equations are fully specified in the paper but exist only as a private paper-level implementation; no public leptogenesis-style code covers asymmetry transfer into the inert-doublet sector.

The inert-doublet thermal relic density in the TeV Higgs-coupling regime is a standard calculation covered by public tools such as micrOMEGAs with the inert doublet model file, consistent with the paper-level analytic treatment on the card.
Higgs-exchange spin-independent sigma_SI is a simple analytic formula given in the paper and also standard in public tools like micrOMEGAs.

gaps.description: No public implementation exists of the coupled Boltzmann network tracking lepton-number washout and asymmetry transfer between the lepton, Higgs, and Z2-odd inert-doublet sectors before the electroweak phase transition; the paper's equations are a private calculation, so the Y_B-L survival prediction cannot be reproduced or scanned.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public leptogenesis Boltzmann framework (e.g. ULYSSES) with the scotogenic y_eta-mediated washout terms and chemical-potential bookkeeping for the inert doublet, reproducing the paper's washout contours in (M_N, y_hat, lambda_5) as validation.

gaps.description: The route provides no machine-readable direct-detection likelihood: the XENON1T comparison is a digitized limit-curve overlay, and the card marks likelihood_available as unknown with partial recasting needed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the analytic sigma_SI(lambda_3, m_DM) into an existing public direct-detection likelihood package such as DDCalc (XENON1T/LZ modules) to replace the digitized limit curve with a proper likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The FSM framon RGE solution that yields the 17 MeV / sub-8 MeV and TeV hidden spectra is explicitly described as not a public solver and exists only qualitatively in the source.
Portal scattering and collider rates are order-of-magnitude estimates only; no quantitative cross-section calculation or code implied by the card exists.
Once masses and couplings are known, the survival filter is a simple kinematic comparison of H_low/G_low masses against the co-neutrino decay threshold, doable by hand.

gaps.description: No numerical implementation of the Framed Standard Model framon action, RG running, and Z-G/Higgs mixing exists, so the hidden-sector spectrum (17 MeV, sub-8 MeV, and TeV states) and mixing elements cannot be computed reproducibly from zeta_S and the RGE inputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the FSM RGE mass functions and mixing-matrix solution as a standalone spectrum code (analogous to a SARAH/SPheno-style spectrum generator for this non-standard framework), validated against the published fit values for zeta_S near 2 TeV.

gaps.description: Portal phenomenology is limited to order-of-magnitude estimates (scattering at a few percent of neutrino cross sections, unspecified collider bump rates); no quantitative cross sections, widths, or event rates have been derived from the Z-G and Higgs mixing elements.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive explicit differential cross sections for hidden-state scattering on nucleons/electrons through the Z-G mixing portal and production rates for TeV co-quark/co-lepton thresholds, then encode them in a FeynRules/CalcHEP model so standard event tools can be used.

gaps.description: The relic abundance of framonic C-ons is entirely qualitative: no production mechanism calculation (thermal history, composite formation, decay chains) exists, so the candidates cannot be assigned a predicted abundance or momentum distribution for any cosmological comparison.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the hidden-sector thermal history and freeze-out/formation abundance of the lightest neutral C-ons (including hidden confinement and binary composite formation), producing an Omega h^2 estimate and phase-space distribution as functions of zeta_S and the mixing portal strength.

gaps.description: The electroweak-precision floor on zeta_S is a model-internal comparison to the Z mass error, not a statistical constraint; no likelihood connects FSM Z-G mixing to the full set of electroweak precision observables.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the Z-G mixing shift into oblique/precision parameters and evaluate it with an existing global electroweak fit package (e.g. HEPfit or GFitter inputs) to obtain a proper likelihood on zeta_S.

route_step_status.reason: The parametric freeze-in yield estimate uses the paper's analytic formulas, a standard pen-and-paper calculation that needs no dedicated code.

The momentum-distribution-level Boltzmann solve exists only as the authors' private numerical implementation; public freeze-in tools (e.g. micrOMEGAs freeze-in routines) compute number densities, not f(p), for this resonant/non-resonant neutrino-portal production.

CLASS can propagate a tabulated ncdm f(p) to the linear power spectrum, but the Lyman-alpha comparison relies on approximate WDM-equivalent recasts rather than a ready likelihood, and the direct/LFV recasts are model-dependent and not packaged.

gaps.description: No public momentum-level Boltzmann solver covers neutrino-portal freeze-in with both resonant (on-shell N decay) and non-resonant (off-shell N) production, so the nonthermal f(p) that both the relic density and the free-streaming constraint depend on cannot be recomputed outside the authors' private code.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement (or obtain release of) an unintegrated Boltzmann solver for the L h -> N -> chi phi chain with resonant and 2-to-2 off-shell contributions, outputting tabulated f(q) in the CLASS ncdm psd-file format; extending micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module to momentum level is a natural host.

gaps.description: No ready Lyman-alpha likelihood accepts the nonthermal freeze-in momentum distribution directly; the card notes the thermal-WDM template can misestimate the bound, and the exact transfer-function-to-likelihood mapping was not reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the tabulated f(p) through CLASS ncdm to obtain T(k), then apply a shape-based Lyman-alpha recast (area criterion or the Murgia et al. alpha-beta-gamma parameterization with the MIKE/HIRES+XQ-100 likelihood) instead of the half-mode thermal-WDM mapping.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs 5 supports coupled two-component freeze-out with conversion channels, but no model file for this hidden U(1)_D Z2 x Z2' scalar sector is indicated by the card, so the coupled relic solve is not turnkey.

The Galactic boosted-DM flux from heavy-to-light annihilation is a standard semi-analytic halo-profile integral (Agashe et al. style) computable by hand given the annihilation cross section and component fractions.

Sub-10 GeV direct-detection recasting is served by public packages (DDCalc-type likelihoods), but the boosted-event and self-interaction filters have no likelihoods (card lists likelihood_available no for both).

gaps.description: No public Super-K/Hyper-K detector simulation or likelihood exists for boosted light dark matter with inelastic scattering followed by prompt decay (multi-ring topology); event forecasts are order-of-magnitude counts without efficiencies, angular reconstruction, or atmospheric-neutrino background modeling.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a detector-response module for large water-Cherenkov detectors (effective volume, ring-finding efficiency vs opening angle, decay-length acceptance, atmospheric background rates) calibrated on the published Super-K boosted-DM search, and expose it as an event-count likelihood for Hyper-K forecasts.

gaps.description: The two-component hidden U(1)_D scalar model (Z2 x Z2' stable states, dark photon and dark-scalar mediators) has no public model implementation, so the coupled Boltzmann relic calculation that fixes the 40-60 percent component split cannot be reproduced with existing multi-component solvers.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write the model in FeynRules/CalcHEP and run it through micrOMEGAs' two-component dark-sector mode, validating against the primary paper's benchmark relic splits and annihilation cross sections.

gaps.description: The self-interaction motivation is filtered only through qualitative sigma_self/m targets; no halo-shape or small-scale-structure likelihood connects the light component's dark-photon-mediated self-scattering to dwarf/cluster observables (card: no halo-shape likelihood attached).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt the standard velocity-dependent SIDM cross-section calculation for a light-mediator Yukawa potential and compare against the compiled dwarf/LSB/cluster sigma/m constraints (e.g. the Kaplinghat-Tulin-Yu data points) packaged as a simple likelihood over (m_Zprime, alpha_D, m_light).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the UCNA (and PERKEO) e- e+ exclusion versus pair kinetic energy, fold the model's predicted pair spectrum for each m_chi through the window and detection efficiency, and package the result as a branching-ratio likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The 3-to-2 WZW pion rate follows from standard chiral-EFT/WZW analytic formulas given the Lagrangian, a pen-and-paper computation despite the null tool_or_code.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast layer on an existing ALP-limit framework (e.g. extend a DarkCast/ALPINIST-style package) that takes the paper's ALP-SM coupling structure, computes tau_a and branching fractions, and re-derives beam-dump/collider/supernova exclusions with correct acceptance and lifetime weighting.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the model's injected-energy spectrum from ALP decay products, feed it through ExoCLASS/DarkHistory efficiency functions f_eff(z), and evaluate against the Planck annihilation likelihood (p_ann) to replace the approximate bound with a proper likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: Fixing the Littlest Seesaw Yukawa texture and deriving neutrino masses and the leptogenesis-compatible M_R range is standard seesaw algebra, a pen-and-paper step despite the null tool_or_code.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model (N_R, chi, phi with L_portal = y_DS N_R chi phi) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and extend the micrOMEGAs 5 freeze-in module — or write a dedicated coupled-yield solver — including RHN decay and 2-to-2 production channels, both mass orderings, and an explicit reheating-temperature dependence, validated against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.1188 and y_DS < 1e-4 viable band.

route_step_status.reason: Evolving the homogeneous scalar background to obtain w(a) and rho_a(a) is a simple ODE/cycle-averaged analytic calculation given (n, z_c, f_zc).

MontePython/Cobaya samplers with public Planck, BAO, and JLA/Pantheon likelihoods cover this step as done in the primary paper.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with the generalized ULA linear transfer functions as initial conditions (and quantum-pressure corrections where relevant), then build a small emulator or halofit-style correction for P_nl(k,z; n, z_c, f_zc) to plug into an EFT-of-LSS survey likelihood.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or DRAKE) for the Z2 scalar singlet with a user-supplied H(T) and entropy-injection history: integrate the rho_phi/rho_R background for given (w, F, T_end), pass it into the abundance solver, implement the freeze-in branch and thermalization check, and validate against the paper's radiation-dominated lambda_HS(M_S) curve.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the scan to DDCalc (LUX/PandaX-II/XENON1T likelihoods and DARWIN projections), applying the fractional-abundance rescaling of sigma_SI point-by-point to get proper likelihood-based contours instead of digitized limit curves.

route_step_status.reason: The paper supplies a (c_I, Delta) parameterization of the HBB size distribution, but deriving it from the Affleck-Dine potential and inflationary e-folding history requires model-specific stochastic field evolution with no tool recorded on the card.
The density contrast and collapse time in the QCD-transition and Q-ball-domination branches follow from the analytic formulas in the primary paper, a pen-and-paper step despite the null tool_or_code.

The horizon-mass mapping is semi-analytic and reproducible, but the collapse threshold and efficiency for baryon-isocurvature bubbles are assumed rather than simulation-calibrated, so the mass function is only an estimate.

Public PBH constraint compilations exist for the abundance overlay, but the card notes no external constraint curves, no merger-rate likelihood, and no inhomogeneous-BBN recast are encoded, so quantitative reuse needs assembly work.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Combine stochastic inflationary evolution of the AD phase (Fokker-Planck or lattice sampling of Hubble-induced mass flips) with existing lattice results for AD fragmentation into Q-balls to build a solver mapping (lambda, n, mediation scheme, N_CMB) to the HBB distribution and interior baryon/Q-ball content.

gaps.description: The collapse threshold and PBH formation efficiency for high-baryon isocurvature bubbles (QCD-softened equation of state or Q-ball-dominated interiors) are not calibrated by numerical-relativity or hydrodynamic simulations; standard curvature-perturbation thresholds do not directly apply to this seed type.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity/hydro simulations of horizon reentry for top-hat baryon-isocurvature bubbles through the QCD transition (and for Q-ball-dominated interiors), extracting delta_c and the M_PBH/M_H collapse efficiency to replace the assumed horizon-mass mapping.

gaps.description: The residual-HBB BBN constraint is applied only as the rough requirement eta_b^B/eta_b^ob <~ 1; no inhomogeneous-BBN calculation or likelihood exists for light-element yields from surviving high-baryon regions of the predicted size and density distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt a public BBN code (PRIMAT or AlterBBN) to inhomogeneous baryon patches with the HBB size/eta_b^in distribution, including post-BBN diffusion and mixing, and turn the resulting D/H and He-4 predictions into a likelihood on the residual-HBB parameters.

gaps.description: The LIGO-mass observable is only compared at the level of Omega_PBH estimates; no pipeline maps the predicted extended PBH mass function to binary merger rates and a GWTC catalog likelihood, which the card flags as unimplemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the HBB-derived M_PBH distribution into an established early-binary PBH merger-rate calculation and evaluate against public LIGO/Virgo population likelihoods (GWTC-3 rate and mass-spectrum data), alongside a PBHbounds-style overlay for the abundance constraints.

route_step_status.reason: Axion misalignment abundance, freeze-in axino abundance, decay width, and line energy follow from analytic formulas given in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code reflects pen-and-paper math rather than a missing capability.

Published decaying-DM X-ray/gamma-ray line limits exist and can be rescaled by the axino fraction, but the card records likelihood_available: no and no public recasting tool, so the comparison is a manual digitize-and-rescale exercise.

CLASS/CAMB can evolve a mixed cold-axion plus warm-axino cosmology as an ncdm species, but the card states the axino distribution function f(p) is not provided, so the required input to the transfer-function computation is missing.

Lyman-alpha and satellite-count constraints exist for thermal WDM, but no public likelihood covers a subdominant nonthermal warm component in a mixed cold+warm cosmology, so thermal-WDM bounds can only be applied approximately.

gaps.description: The freeze-in axino momentum distribution f(p) from PQ-suppressed weak scattering production is not derived (the card records distribution_function_available: no), so the warm transfer cutoff and mixed-DM matter power cannot be computed beyond rough free-streaming estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the unintegrated freeze-in Boltzmann equation for axino production from MSSM scattering with PQ-suppressed couplings, tabulate f(p) over (m_axino, f_a, T_RH), and feed it to CLASS as an ncdm species alongside a cold axion fluid.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for X-ray/gamma-ray line limits on a decaying keV axino that is only a fraction of the dark matter; the card notes limits must be rescaled by the axino fraction and records likelihood_available: no for con_axino_xray_gamma.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize published X-ray line (e.g. NuSTAR/XMM blank-sky) and soft gamma-ray decaying-DM lifetime curves, wrap them as a lifetime-versus-mass likelihood with an explicit Omega_axino/Omega_DM rescaling parameter, and connect it to the analytic (m_axino, lambda, lambda_prime, f_a) to lifetime map.

gaps.description: Structure-formation constraints (Lyman-alpha, MW satellites) are calibrated for fully thermal WDM, not for a mixed cold-axion plus subdominant nonthermal warm-axino cosmology, so no direct likelihood exists for the warm-fraction versus axino-mass plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the mixed-DM transfer functions from CLASS onto existing mixed cold+warm Lyman-alpha analyses (fraction-versus-mass exclusion surfaces) or re-run an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator on the suppressed power spectra, releasing the result as a (f_warm, m_axino) likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: Slow-roll n_s, r, A_s from a given potential are standard analytic formulas doable by hand or with any slow-roll calculator, so the null tool_or_code is not a gap.

Public lattice codes for preheating exist (LATTICEEASY/CosmoLattice class), but the card names only a generic 'preheating/reheating calculation' and notes precision requires a nonperturbative treatment not set up for annihilation-driven reheating of a stable inflaton.
Standard WIMP freeze-out with sigma_v near 2e-26 cm^3/s is textbook analytic math, and public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs-type) cover the Higgs-portal scalar benchmark.

XENON1T/LUX/PandaX limits are public and Higgs-portal sigma_SI recasting is standard (DDCalc-type tools cover it), but the card records likelihood_available: no and no assembled likelihood for this model.

gaps.description: No nonperturbative preheating/thermalization calculation exists for annihilation-driven reheating of a stable inflaton across the five studied potential classes; the card notes thermalization after reheating is model-dependent and precision requires a nonperturbative treatment, which controls whether the thermal freeze-out assumption holds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run lattice preheating simulations (CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY) for each WIMPflation potential class with the Higgs-portal coupling included, extract the reheating temperature and verify inflaton-SM kinetic equilibration, and publish fitting functions for T_RH(potential parameters, lambda_phiH).

gaps.description: No assembled joint likelihood connects the shared parameter space to both Planck slow-roll observables and xenon direct-detection limits; each constraint is only quoted as literature exclusion statements (likelihood_available: no on all three constraints).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Higgs-portal scalar in DDCalc/micrOMEGAs for sigma_SI limits and combine with the Planck n_s-r contours in a single scan over (potential parameters, m_phi, lambda_phiH), reproducing the quoted m_phi > 900 GeV bound as a validation test.

route_step_status.reason: Public freeze-in machinery (micrOMEGAs freeze-in module) can compute the N1 abundance from V decay, but the card requires phase-space densities of an out-of-equilibrium V and N1, and no public solver returns the momentum-level distributions this step lists as outputs.
Relic density from a fixed abundance and the standard radiative-decay rate proportional to sin^2(2theta) m_N1^5 are simple analytic formulas, so the null tool_or_code is not a gap.

ARS viability, BBN, and supernova exclusions rely on literature rate estimates and published contours; no public ARS kinetic solver includes B-L gauge equilibration terms and no packaged likelihood exists, so the recast is manual.

gaps.description: No public momentum-dependent Boltzmann solver computes the phase-space distributions of an out-of-equilibrium B-L gauge boson and the N1 population produced by its decay; existing freeze-in tools return integrated abundances only, while both the relic density and the warm-DM free-streaming scale here require f(p).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an unintegrated freeze-in solver to a two-stage cascade (bath -> V -> N1) tracking f_V(p,t) and f_N1(p,t) over the (m_V, g_B-L) plane, validated against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 curves, and export f_N1(p) in CLASS ncdm format.

gaps.description: Testing ARS compatibility requires a leptogenesis kinetic solver that includes the new B-L gauge-scattering equilibration terms for N2/N3; public ARS density-matrix codes implement only Yukawa-mediated rates, so the 'B-L interactions too slow to erase the asymmetry' condition is checked only by leading-rate estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add thermally averaged B-L gauge-boson production/scattering rates for the sterile states to a public ARS density-matrix solver (AMIQS-type code) and rerun the baryon-asymmetry scan over (g_B-L, m_V, Yukawas) to delimit the safe region quantitatively.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for the keV N1 branch: X-ray line limits and Lyman-alpha/satellite warm-DM bounds are calibrated for oscillation-produced or thermal spectra, and the card notes the nonthermal decay-produced spectrum must be translated before thermal-WDM bounds can be applied.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Given f_N1(p) from the freeze-in solver, compute transfer functions in CLASS, map them to equivalent-thermal-WDM masses or run them through an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator, and pair this with digitized X-ray line lifetime limits as a joint (m_N1, theta) likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The misalignment relic scaling and the QCD axion mass relation m_a(f_a) are standard analytic formulas quoted in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code reflects pen-and-paper math.
Comparing f_a against published rare-meson and stellar/supernova-cooling bounds is a direct lookup against well-established literature limits and needs no dedicated tool.

The ARS equilibration check and Delta N_eff estimate are doable at the leading-rate analytic level the step specifies, but the card itself flags that a full kinetic treatment could shift the allowed h_N and f_a, so the step is only approximate as implemented.

gaps.description: No public ARS leptogenesis kinetic solver includes the PQ-sector interaction rates (axion and radial-mode scattering with the sterile neutrinos via h_N), so the compatibility of the axion sector with the baryon asymmetry rests on leading-rate estimates rather than a density-matrix computation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add h_N-mediated production and scattering rates for the sterile neutrinos (axion and PQ radial-mode channels) to a public ARS density-matrix code (AMIQS-type) and scan (f_a, h_N, m_N) to replace the leading-rate ARS viability condition with a quantitative boundary.

route_step_status.reason: The majoron decay rate to light neutrinos from (m_J, f, m_nu) is a simple analytic tree-level formula, so the null tool_or_code reflects pen-and-paper math.

Generic freeze-out/freeze-in Boltzmann machinery (micrOMEGAs-type) exists, but the majoron sector of this model is not implemented anywhere on the card, and the paper's viable-majoron branch invokes an unspecified exotic production mechanism that no existing tool encodes.

X-ray/soft-gamma decay limits for an MeV sterile neutrino exist as published curves, but the card records likelihood_available: no and no recasting tool, so the lifetime bound is applied by manual digitization.

gaps.description: The majoron-DM branch has no specified production mechanism: the paper states ordinary freeze-out, freeze-in, and misalignment underproduce the majoron for 1-100 GeV sterile neutrinos, and the card leaves the required exotic production route undefined, so no abundance calculation can even be set up for this branch.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify at least one concrete UV production completion (e.g. majoron misalignment with an explicit soft-breaking potential, or production from lepton-number scalar decays after a first-order transition), derive its abundance formula, and only then implement it in a Boltzmann solver.

gaps.description: No implemented Boltzmann pipeline exists for this model's majoron freeze-out/freeze-in from the (m_J, f, m_N) couplings, which is needed even just to verify the paper's underproduction statement quantitatively (the s2 step lists a boltzmann_solver with null tool_or_code).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the singlet-majoron Lagrangian (majoron-neutrino and scalar-sector couplings) in micrOMEGAs' freeze-out and freeze-in modes and scan (m_J, f, m_N) to reproduce and delimit the underproduction region as a validation test.

gaps.description: No packaged likelihood exists for the two decay signatures: the CMB bound on majoron decay to neutrinos (bound not digitized from the primary figure, per the card) and the X-ray/soft-gamma lifetime limits on the MeV sterile-neutrino branch are both available only as literature exclusion statements.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the CMB constraint on DM decaying to invisible/neutrino final states with CLASS plus the Planck likelihood as a tau(m_J, f) bound, and digitize published MeV-scale X-ray/soft-gamma decay limits into a sin^2(2theta)-versus-m_N1 likelihood curve.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving mass eigenstates, trilinear/quartic couplings, and mediator decay channels from the given renormalizable scalar potential is straightforward pen-and-paper algebra requiring no dedicated tool.

Born-regime analytic formulas for light-mediator self-scattering are standard, but the card itself flags that classical/resonant regimes for a ~20 MeV mediator need care and no public partial-wave solver is identified in the card.

CalcHEP + micrOMEGAs 5.0.4 is a named public toolchain that covers relic density, direct detection, and decays, but the card states no public model implementation files were identified, so the step requires reimplementation before it can be run.

gaps.description: No public CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model files exist for the two-real-singlet Z2 x Z2-prime model, so the paper's relic-density, direct-detection, and invisible-Higgs computations cannot be reproduced without reimplementing the model from the Lagrangian.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the scalar potential (two real singlets plus Higgs, with Z2-prime-breaking trilinears and Majorana-neutrino couplings) in FeynRules or LanHEP, export CalcHEP model files, and validate against the paper's benchmark relic density and PandaX-II comparison at m_chi = 100 GeV in micrOMEGAs 5.x.

gaps.description: No solver is identified for the velocity-dependent self-scattering cross section sigma/m(v) across Born, classical, and resonant regimes, which is required for a light ~20 MeV scalar mediator where perturbative formulas can fail.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a partial-wave Schrodinger solver for the attractive Yukawa potential generated by the light singlet mediator (following standard SIDM transfer-cross-section treatments), tabulate sigma_T/m over the dwarf-to-cluster velocity range 10-1000 km/s, and verify the paper's target of ~1 cm^2/g at dwarf velocities falling below 0.1 cm^2/g at cluster velocities.

gaps.description: The self-interaction constraint is only an approximate astrophysical target range (about 1 cm^2/g at dwarf/Milky-Way scales, below 0.1 cm^2/g at clusters); no quantitative likelihood maps halo density-profile data onto the model's sigma/m(v) curve.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood from published rotation-curve and cluster core datasets (dwarf-to-cluster halo samples used in SIDM fits) parameterized directly in sigma_T/m as a function of velocity, so any velocity-dependent SIDM model, including this one, can be scored quantitatively instead of against rough target bands.

route_step_status.reason: SARAH/SPheno/FlavorKit is a named public toolchain that natively supports building the NMSSM plus Type-I seesaw and computing the spectrum, Higgs, and flavor observables in the scanned ranges.
micrOMEGAs 4.3.4 with SARAH-generated model files is public and covers relic density including coannihilation and spin-independent scattering for a sneutrino LSP.

EasyScan HEP and MultiNest are public, but the card states the assembled likelihood is a paper-level scan whose configuration, priors, and composed likelihood terms are not released as a reusable package.
The 2l+MET electroweakino constraint is only qualitative in the primary source, with no event simulation or recast tool applied to the Higgsino-to-sneutrino-LSP decay chains.

gaps.description: No public SARAH model files or standalone repository exist for the Type-I seesaw NMSSM with a CP-even sneutrino LSP, so the spectrum-to-observable pipeline must be rebuilt from the superpotential before any step can be rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct the NMSSM plus Type-I seesaw model in SARAH from the superpotential and soft terms given in the paper, generate SPheno and micrOMEGAs model files, and validate against the paper's benchmark near-degenerate Higgsino-sneutrino relic points; publish the model files.

gaps.description: The combined likelihood (Planck relic Gaussian, XENON1T upper limit, Fermi-LAT dwarf term, HiggsBounds/HiggsSignal and B-physics terms) exists only inside the authors' private EasyScan HEP setup; no reusable likelihood package or public posterior samples are released.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recompose the scan likelihood in a public global-fit framework (e.g. GAMBIT or a released EasyScan HEP configuration) with documented priors and experimental terms, and publish the configuration plus posterior chains so the Bayesian evidence comparison can be reproduced and updated with newer data.

gaps.description: No implemented LHC 2l+MET electroweakino recast exists for compressed Higgsino spectra decaying to a sneutrino LSP; the claim that favored regions survive direct searches is qualitative and cannot be checked against current or future data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Simulate Higgsino-like chargino/neutralino production with the modified decay chains to the sneutrino LSP (MadGraph plus Pythia) and recast the ATLAS/CMS compressed-spectrum dilepton+MET searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis 5, producing exclusion contours in the (m_chargino, m_snu1) plane.

The card states the collider recast of heavy-stable-charged-particle searches for the long-lived stau/neutralino NLSP was not performed and names no applied tool.

gaps.description: No implementation exists of the coupled freeze-in calculation for the L=2 right-sneutrino LSP: the full decay inventory of higgsinos and heavier superparticles into the sneutrino, plus the accompanying sterile-neutrino yield, is not encoded in any public Boltzmann setup for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the MSSM plus right-chiral neutrino superfields with L=2 Majorana and soft masses in SARAH/FeynRules, generate CalcHEP files, and use the micrOMEGAs 5 freeze-in module extended to include NLSP freeze-out-and-decay and the sterile-neutrino warm component, validated against the paper's hierarchy/cancellation viable regions.

gaps.description: The BBN constraint on late NLSP decays is applied only as a hard tau_NLSP <= 100 s cut; no light-element yield likelihood over the NLSP lifetime-abundance plane, including hadronic and electromagnetic cascades, is available for this model.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for f(p) of sneutrinos from freeze-in and late NLSP decays, compute the linear transfer function with CLASS, and map to an equivalent thermal-WDM mass so existing Lyman-alpha and Dodelson-Widrow-style bounds can be applied.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast ATLAS/CMS HSCP and displaced/long-lived searches for the 300-900 GeV NLSP benchmarks using SModelS long-lived results or a MadGraph+Pythia simulation with the published HSCP efficiency maps, producing exclusion contours in the (M_NLSP, tau_NLSP) plane.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain or reimplement the FeynRules model (Clockwork fermion sites, Majorana masses M_L/M_R, vector-like lepton doublet, and the Y L' H psi_R,N Yukawa), export to CalcHEP, and run the micrOMEGAs 5 freeze-in module, validating against the source relic bands at Y_eff ~ 1e-10 to 1e-13; publish the model files.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for the FIMP momentum spectrum from each production channel, feed the resulting f(p) into CLASS to compute the linear transfer function, and apply the thermal-WDM-equivalent mapping of arXiv:1907.04558 to confront existing Lyman-alpha bounds across the (m_psi0, q, N) parameter space.

gaps.description: No collider recast or likelihood exists for pair-produced Z2-odd vector-like leptons and Clockwork gears decaying to the FIMP plus Higgs or electroweak bosons; the source discussion of LHC and 100 TeV reach is purely qualitative.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Simulate electroweak pair production of the vector-like leptons with MadGraph+Pythia using the FeynRules model from gap_1 and recast ATLAS/CMS multilepton/electroweakino plus missing-energy searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis 5, giving exclusion contours in the (M_D, m) plane.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain or rebuild the FeynRules model for the N+1-site scalar Clockwork with Nth-site Higgs portal, export to CalcHEP, and run the micrOMEGAs 5 freeze-in module to reproduce the published relic bands; publish the model files.

gaps.description: No nonthermal phase-space distribution f(p) of the a0 zero mode from gear decays has been computed (card: distribution_function_available = no), so the transfer function needed to recast Lyman-alpha/WDM limits onto light scalar Clockwork FIMPs cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent freeze-in Boltzmann equation for a0 produced in gear decays to obtain f(p), feed it to CLASS as a non-cold dark matter species to compute T(k), and apply the nonthermal-to-thermal-WDM mapping of arXiv:1907.04558 to set the Lyman-alpha bound.

gaps.description: No collider recast or likelihood exists for the displaced b-jets plus missing energy signature of TeV-scale gear decays a1 -> h a0 at the LHC or a 100 TeV collider; the source discussion is qualitative only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement gear pair/associated production in MadGraph with the Clockwork UFO model, compute gear decay lengths, and recast existing long-lived-particle displaced-jet searches using CheckMATE or MadAnalysis LLP modules; extend to 100 TeV projections.

route_step_status.reason: Computing v_c/T_c from the thermal effective potential is not trivially analytic (thermal resummation, gauge dependence) and no tool is named, but public codes like CosmoTransitions can do it once the complex-singlet potential is implemented.
Standard thermal Higgs-portal freeze-out of a singlet scalar is fully covered by micrOMEGAs (the tool the primary paper used), which the card names for this step.

Public ingredients exist (XENON1T limit tables/DDCalc, Fermi-LAT dwarf and Planck annihilation likelihoods) but no assembled likelihood with the f_X subcomponent rescaling exists for this model, and the card marks all likelihoods unavailable or unknown.

gaps.description: No implementation of the complex-singlet finite-temperature effective potential with high-T CP and Z2 breaking exists, so the phase-transition strength v_c/T_c, the verification of CP/Z2 restoration today, and the associated gravitational-wave spectrum cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the complex-singlet scalar potential with one-loop thermal corrections and daisy resummation in CosmoTransitions, scan for symmetry non-restoration at high T, and pipe the resulting alpha and beta/H into the standard sound-wave GW spectrum formulas (PTPlot templates) for LISA-band comparison.

gaps.description: No assembled statistical pipeline applies the XENON1T spin-independent limit and the Fermi-LAT/AMS-02/Planck annihilation constraints to this model with the required f_X (subcomponent) rescaling of local density and annihilation rates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire micrOMEGAs outputs (Omega_X h^2, sigma_SI, sigma v with branching fractions) into DDCalc for the XENON1T likelihood and the public Fermi-LAT dwarf and Planck f_eff likelihoods, applying f_X scaling for direct detection and f_X^2 scaling for annihilation signals.

gaps.description: No quantitative transport-equation calculation of the baryon asymmetry from the dimension-6 top CPV operator during the singlet-assisted phase transition exists in the card's routing, so the baryogenesis side of the joint scan (a derived quantity of the route) cannot be evaluated with a public tool.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the CP-violating source from the Lambda-suppressed top operator across the computed bubble-wall profile and solve the standard WKB/VEV-insertion electroweak-baryogenesis transport equations, packaged as a scan module coupled to the CosmoTransitions output.

route_step_status.reason: The paper provides analytic EMDE relic-scaling formulas and solves the expansion-history Boltzmann equations privately, but no public axion relic code covers early-matter-dominated cosmologies out of the box.

Semi-analytic minicluster mass-scale estimates exist in the paper, but the card states nonlinear formation and survival are not simulation-calibrated, so present-day minicluster predictions remain approximate.

Published CMB isocurvature bounds can be recast analytically, but the EMD-modified mapping of f_a and theta_i to the isocurvature fraction has not been rerun through any likelihood (likelihood_available is only partial).

gaps.description: No public relic-abundance solver computes QCD axion misalignment plus string/domain-wall production through an early matter-dominated expansion history with entropy injection; the card's EMDE Boltzmann/relic calculation exists only as the paper's private solution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing axion relic-abundance code (e.g. the misalignment module used in public axion codes such as AxionNet-style solvers or a lightweight standalone ODE code) with a coupled matter-radiation-decay background (rho_M, rho_R, T_R as parameters) so Omega_a(f_a, theta_i, T_R) can be evaluated on a grid.

gaps.description: Nonlinear formation, mass function, and late-time tidal survival of axion miniclusters seeded by EMDE-enhanced small-scale perturbations (including the homogenized-field T_R < 58 MeV regime) have not been simulated, so the initial M_mc estimates cannot be propagated to present-day observables.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations initialized with the EMDE-enhanced axion perturbation spectrum (analogous to existing post-inflationary minicluster simulations) through matter-radiation equality, then couple to a semi-analytic tidal-stripping model to obtain the surviving minicluster mass function and compactness distribution.

gaps.description: No CMB isocurvature likelihood recast exists for the EMD-modified relation between (f_a, theta_i, H_I) and the axion isocurvature fraction; the existing bounds assume standard cosmological history and cannot be copied directly.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the EMD-modified isocurvature amplitude beta_iso(f_a, theta_i, T_R, H_I) using the gap_1 relic solver, then evaluate it against the Planck isocurvature likelihood (uncorrelated CDM isocurvature mode in the standard Planck chains) to produce exclusion contours in the (H_I, f_a) plane.

route_step_status.reason: The parafermi equilibrium distribution and blocking factors are closed-form expressions developed in the source paper, so this step is simple analytic evaluation despite the null tool_or_code.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, DarkSUSY) integrate the standard Maxwell-Boltzmann freeze-out equation but none supports parafermi blocking factors or finite-occupation equilibrium distributions, so the modified Boltzmann integration requires custom code.
Converting the asymptotic yield Y_chi(infinity) and m_chi to Omega_chi h^2 with standard entropy and critical-density factors is trivial pen-and-paper math.

gaps.description: No public relic-abundance solver implements the parafermi-statistics Boltzmann equation (finite maximum occupation order p, modified equilibrium distribution and blocking factors in the collision term); standard codes hard-wire Maxwell-Boltzmann or Fermi-Dirac/Bose-Einstein statistics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a standalone freeze-out ODE solver (or patch the micrOMEGAs collision-term module) that takes the parafermi order p as a parameter, uses the paper's equilibrium distribution and blocking factors in the thermally averaged collision term with <sigma v> = a + 6b/x, and validate by recovering the p=1 fermion limit and the paper's p>=2 abundance-enhancement benchmarks at 100, 500, and 1000 GeV.

route_step_status.reason: The n-nprime oscillation probability with mass splitting, mixing epsilon, and ordinary/mirror magnetic fields is a two-level quantum-mechanics formula developed analytically in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code does not block it.

Published degenerate-limit UCN storage bounds (tau_osc 414 s and 448 s) exist, but the card states they require a magnetic-field and mass-splitting recast for the Delta m ~ 1e-7 eV resonant scenario and no experiment likelihood is available.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast tool that evaluates the field-dependent oscillation probability from step s1 over each experiment's published magnetic-field settings, storage times, and event counts (UCN storage runs and beam proton-counting data), producing exclusion contours in the (Delta m, epsilon, mirror-field) space and reproducing the degenerate-limit tau_osc > 414 s and 448 s bounds as a validation test.

gaps.description: No public code computes neutron-star heating from in-medium n-to-mirror-neutron conversion: the calculation requires the conversion rate in degenerate nuclear matter, Fermi-sea refilling energetics, and a coupled thermal-evolution model, none of which is packaged for this model's (epsilon, Delta m) parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the in-medium conversion and heating-rate formalism of the related analysis (arXiv:2105.09951) as a module over a standard neutron-star cooling code (e.g. NSCool), with the equation of state as a nuisance input, and compare the predicted late-time temperature to cold pulsars such as PSR J2144-3933 to derive epsilon bounds as a function of Delta m.

Only a qualitative warm-relic free-streaming comparison exists; the paper explicitly defers a detailed Lyman-alpha investigation and no transfer-function calculation or likelihood has been run for the nonthermal T_dark < T_gamma distribution.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a stiff-ODE mode-function solver that takes (xi, m_phi, H_inf, H_reh, reheating equation of state w) and outputs the tachyonic occupation spectrum n_k, validating against the paper's abundance contours for quadratic and quartic reheating; a linear-mode module on top of a lattice reheating code such as CosmoLattice would also serve.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for the phi distribution with lambda phi^4 2-to-2 and 4-to-2 collision terms starting from the gap_1 tachyonic spectrum (extending existing dark-freeze-out/cannibal-sector Boltzmann codes), mapping out in (xi, lambda, m_phi) where instantaneous chemical equilibrium is a valid approximation.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha constraint exists for this model's light (sub-keV) relics: existing Lyman-alpha bounds and emulators are calibrated to thermal warm dark matter, while these relics have a nonthermal (or dark-thermalized, T_dark < T_gamma) distribution whose free-streaming differs from an equal-mass thermal relic, so sub-keV parameter points cannot be accepted or excluded.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the full relic distribution f(q) from gap_2 into a Boltzmann code that accepts arbitrary non-cold distribution functions (CLASS with ncdm psd files), compute the linear transfer function, and recast against Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints using the area-criterion or an existing WDM-emulator mapping generalized to non-thermal spectra.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the mass-basis nu_i -> nu_j + a decay and scattering rates from g_alpha_beta using the PMNS rotation, then evaluate the neutrino free-streaming modification with an interacting-neutrino extension of CLASS/CAMB against the Planck likelihood to produce exclusion contours in (m_a, g_alpha_beta) per flavor structure.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a transport calculation for neutrino spectra propagating through the ALP background (attenuation and flavor-ratio distortion as functions of g_alpha_beta, m_a, L_nu), and confront it with SN 1987A event counts and IceCube diffuse-flux/flavor-ratio measurements as binned likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: Misalignment abundance in the small-angle, standard-history regime is a standard analytic formula the paper itself supplies, evaluable by hand or in a few lines of code.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs can solve freeze-out for a scalar with derivative Higgs portal and bottom-induced operators, but no public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP files) of this SO(7)/SO(6) bottom-loop EFT exists per the card.
