route_step_status.reason: The nonlinear fluctuation growth was simulated with the authors' custom C++ classical-statistical lattice code (LATTICEEASY-like), but the card identifies no public release, so the step cannot be rerun for new parameters.
Extracting the equation of state, cold-by-equality check, and density-contrast scale from simulation spectra is straightforward redshifting/post-processing math once the lattice outputs exist.

Generic Boltzmann machinery (CLASS ncdm with tabulated f(p)) exists, but the card marks this recast as planned and no pipeline maps the simulated nonthermal ALP spectra to matter-power suppression and Lyman-alpha bounds; the thermal-WDM mapping is explicitly unavailable.

gaps.description: The classical-statistical lattice simulation of monodromy ALP fluctuation growth (quadratic-plus-cosine potential) exists only as the authors' unreleased custom C++ code, so fluctuation spectra, occupation numbers, and the equation of state cannot be regenerated across the (m_a, f, kappa, initial displacement) parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the monodromy potential V = m^2 phi^2/2 + Lambda^4 cos(phi/f) in a public lattice code such as CosmoLattice (or obtain and release the authors' code), reproducing the paper's O(1) fluctuation scale and equation-of-state evolution as validation, then scan wiggle strength and initial displacement.

gaps.description: No pipeline converts the lattice-produced nonthermal ALP momentum distribution (momenta up to ~10 m_a, frozen in comoving momentum) into a linear transfer function and Lyman-alpha matter-power constraint; the paper's cold-by-equality criterion is only a rough velocity cut and thermal-WDM bounds cannot be applied directly.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the tabulated lattice occupation numbers into CLASS as an ncdm species with an arbitrary distribution function, compute the suppressed matter power spectrum, and recast against Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints via an area-criterion or emulator-based comparison calibrated on thermal-WDM limits (rel_astro-ph0501562 template).

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the given scalar potential and Yukawa terms to obtain the Z2-odd mass spectrum and Higgs-portal couplings is standard pen-and-paper algebra fully specified in the source Lagrangian.

micrOMEGAs plus DDCalc cover scotogenic/inert-doublet WIMP recoil rates and the XENON1T likelihood, but no scoto-seesaw model implementation exists per the card and the scalar-vs-fermion identity of the lightest odd state must first be fixed.
The source derives the full two-loop RGE system, and public generators (SARAH/PyR@TE) can produce and run two-loop RGEs for this renormalizable field content.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the minimal scoto-seesaw (type-I seesaw plus Z2-odd fermion f and inert doublet eta) exists for relic-density and direct-detection codes, so the WIMP-nucleon cross section and thermal abundance cannot be computed for either the scalar or fermion lightest-odd-state branch.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/SARAH model file for the scoto-seesaw Lagrangian (Y_f L eta* f, M_f, lambda_3-lambda_5 potential terms), export to micrOMEGAs for freeze-out relic density and to DDCalc for the XENON1T-style spin-independent recoil likelihood, covering both scalar (eta_R/eta_I) and fermion (f-nu_R mixed) dark-matter branches.

route_step_status.reason: The Majoron lifetime follows analytically from the neutrino-mass-suppressed J -> nu nu coupling and m_J, a pen-and-paper formula the source uses with its quoted lifetime range.

Modified CLASS branches implement decaying dark matter and ncdm handles warm species, but no released solver combines a keV warm Majoron with decay to neutrinos, and the required input phase-space distribution is unavailable (distribution_function_available: no).
Generic WDM N-body techniques exist, but no simulation suite is calibrated for a decaying keV Majoron cosmology and the card marks nonlinear calibration as only partial.

gaps.description: The Majoron production mechanism and resulting phase-space distribution f(p) are not specified in the card (production 'not specified in detail', no distribution function), so the abundance-lifetime mapping and the warm free-streaming scale that drive both observables cannot be computed from model parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the Majoron relic abundance and momentum distribution for the natural production channels of this completion (freeze-in via the Higgs-singlet portal lambda_H_sigma and thermal production at the lepton-number-breaking scale with subsequent dilution), yielding tabulated f(p) as a function of m_J and the breaking scale for input to the Boltzmann step.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-solver implementation treats a warm keV Majoron with nonthermal f(p) that decays to neutrinos; existing CLASS decaying-DM branches assume cold DM decaying to dark radiation and do not combine warmness with the J -> nu nu channel needed for the CMB and matter-power predictions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a CLASS decaying-dark-matter branch to an ncdm species with tabulated f(p) and a decay term feeding the neutrino sector, validated by reproducing the cited decaying-Majoron CMB results (arXiv:0705.2406) in the cold limit.

gaps.description: The CMB lifetime bound tau_J > 50-160 Gyr is only quoted from a pre-Planck analysis under a thermal-Majoron abundance mapping; no current-data likelihood exists to re-derive the bound for this completion's actual abundance, mass, and distribution (likelihood_available: partial).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the gap_2 solver against Planck 2018 TTTEEE+lensing likelihoods (via MontePython or Cobaya) scanning (m_J, tau_J, abundance) to produce an updated, reusable lifetime-abundance exclusion surface replacing the quoted 2007-era bound.

gaps.description: Nonlinear small-scale predictions (halo statistics for the warm, decaying Majoron) lack a calibrated N-body suite; the source points to N-body simulation as the forward model but simulation_calibrated is only partial and no pipeline is attached to the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run WDM-style N-body simulations (e.g. Gadget-4 with truncated initial power from the gap_2 transfer functions, including thermal-velocity treatment) for representative keV Majoron benchmarks to calibrate the halo and subhalo mass-function suppression.

route_step_status.reason: AQN formation from axion domain-wall collapse is treated only by paper-level semi-analytic estimates with no public code producing the initial baryon-charge distribution.
The early-universe survival calculation is a rough estimate in the primary paper; the 'AQN survival simulation' listed under required_code_resources does not exist as a public tool.
Converting a surviving dN/dB and local dark-matter density into a macro flux through a detector is simple analytic kinematics (flux scaling inversely with B) that needs no dedicated code.

One-off solar-corona annihilation simulations exist in the related literature (arxiv:1805.01897), but there is no public, reusable code for solar energy deposition or galactic annihilation emission from AQNs.

gaps.description: No public code implements AQN formation from axion domain-wall collapse at the QCD epoch and subsequent early-universe survival, so the surviving baryon-charge distribution dN/dB (B_min, slope alpha, B_cut) cannot be computed from model inputs (m_a, T_form).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's domain-wall collapse and plasma-annihilation survival semi-analytics as a public code parameterized by (m_a, T_form, initial distribution), validated against the quoted T_form ~ 41 MeV and B_min ~ 1e24 survival benchmarks.

gaps.description: No detector-response model exists for macroscopic nuclear-density nuggets in IceCube/ANITA/ancient-mica; current bounds are approximate recasts of magnetic-monopole flux limits whose signatures differ from AQN tracks and cascades.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive AQN-specific energy-deposition and track/cascade signatures per unit path length as a function of B, and implement them as a detector-response module for IceCube-like volumes and mica track formation, replacing the monopole-search translation.

gaps.description: Solar-corona/flare energy deposition and galactic annihilation emission (511 keV line and diffuse continuum) from antinugget annihilation are modeled only by application-specific, non-public one-off calculations, with no reusable emission code taking dN/dB and the antinugget fraction as inputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a public emission module that combines the line-of-sight interaction integral I_AQN with a surface-annihilation spectral model, calibrated against the existing solar-corona simulation (EUV power ~1e27 erg/s) and applied to Galactic bulge geometry for the 511 keV and continuum predictions.

gaps.description: No statistical likelihood exists for any AQN channel: macro flux limits, solar EUV/nanoflare energetics, and galactic diffuse/511 keV emission are all compared to data only at the order-of-magnitude level (likelihood_available: no for both constraints).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct Poisson non-observation likelihoods for IceCube/ANITA/mica macro searches and template likelihoods for INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV and solar EUV data with explicit background models, parameterized in (B_min, alpha, B_cut, antinugget fraction).

route_step_status.reason: The cross section sigma = s^2/(192 M^6) is a closed-form analytic formula requiring no code.

Single-scattering attenuation and delay estimates are trivially analytic, but the spectral/angular reshaping observable needs a full UHE-neutrino transport code through DM columns (regeneration, multiple scattering, deflection) that does not exist for this model.

The thermalization/BBN-CMB check is done by order-of-magnitude rate estimates; the card explicitly notes a numerical Boltzmann solution is required for robust limits and no such tool exists for this operator.

gaps.description: No UHE-neutrino propagation code exists for transport through galactic-spike and intergalactic dark-matter columns with the strongly energy-dependent contact cross section sigma ~ s^2/(192 M^6), including multiple scattering, energy regeneration, angular deflection, and a consistent DM column-density (halo plus source spike) model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing neutrino cascade/transport framework (e.g. a nuSQuIDS-style Boltzmann transport code) with the differential nu-X cross section from the dimension-seven operator and a parameterized line-of-sight DM column (NFW halo plus optional source spike), outputting attenuated spectra and arrival-direction/time-delay distributions.

gaps.description: No numerical Boltzmann solver treats thermalization of the misalignment-produced vector condensate and distortion of the neutrino distribution via the dimension-seven neutrino-vector operator in a low-reheating (T_R ~ 5 MeV) cosmology, so the BBN/CMB constraint rests on single-scattering rate estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive and solve the coupled momentum-space Boltzmann equations for the nu-X system in a low-reheating background, extending the low-T_R neutrino thermalization framework of arXiv:1411.6005 with the s^2-scaling collision term, and map the result onto N_eff and BBN abundances.

gaps.description: No packaged likelihood exists for the multimessenger observables: neither a source-population coincidence likelihood (TXS 0506+056-type associations vs decorrelation probability) nor a diffuse spectral/anisotropy likelihood against IceCube data (likelihoods: 'none packaged', likelihood_available: no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a coincidence-statistics likelihood over the IceCube alert catalog (association probability as a function of survival probability per source) plus a binned diffuse-flux likelihood, taking the propagation-code outputs as signal templates and marginalizing over source spectra and DM column uncertainties.

route_step_status.reason: The realignment relic abundance in the harmonic approximation is a closed-form analytic calculation in (m_a, f_a, n, b) needing no dedicated code.
CLASS handles CDM-like ALP perturbations with a user-supplied white-noise isocurvature initial spectrum on the linear scales the paper uses.
Public Planck temperature/polarization likelihoods cover the isocurvature bound and the CMB-S4/SKA Fisher forecast is standard analytic machinery.

gaps.description: The white-noise isocurvature spectrum is derived in the harmonic approximation with axion strings, domain walls, and minicluster formation explicitly neglected, and no simulation-calibrated correction to the isocurvature normalization and cutoff scale exists for this generic ALP mass-temperature model (n, b).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run post-inflationary lattice field simulations of the ALP field with the temperature-dependent mass m_a(T) parameterized by (n, b), including string/domain-wall decay, and extract the corrected isocurvature power normalization, spectral cutoff, and minicluster fraction as fitting functions to feed the CLASS initial conditions.

route_step_status.reason: The parent/daughter continuity equations are simple coupled background ODEs solvable with any standard integrator; the null tool_or_code reflects trivially analytic content.
Standard public late-universe distance likelihoods (BAO, SNIa, H0) exist in MCMC frameworks such as Cobaya/MontePython and only need the model H(z) as input.

Linear two-body DDM perturbation treatments (modified-CLASS warm-daughter fluid approximation from the cited related literature, e.g. 2102.12498) exist but are not mainline CLASS/CAMB and card nonlinear predictions are not simulation calibrated.

gaps.description: No mainline Boltzmann-solver implementation of two-body decaying dark matter with a warm massive daughter is packaged for this card; the linear CMB/matter-power prediction relies on a modified-CLASS fluid approximation from related papers that is not integrated or validated for the full tau-epsilon range used here.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt the public modified CLASS with the two-body DDM warm-daughter fluid approximation (Abellan et al. line of work cited as 2102.12498), validate it against the paper's background solution in the LCDM limits (tau to infinity, epsilon to 0), and register it as the route's Boltzmann step.

gaps.description: No simulation-calibrated nonlinear matter power spectrum or halo mass function exists for the two-body decay scenario (card: simulation_calibrated 'no'), so weak-lensing and cluster-count S8 constraints can only be applied at linear or mildly nonlinear level.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with two-body decaying dark matter (parent decay to massless plus warm massive daughter, parameterized by tau and epsilon) and fit a nonlinear boost/suppression formula or emulator relative to LCDM for use in weak-lensing likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: The Boltzmann production calculation was solved numerically by the authors with a private code; public sterile-neutrino production codes (e.g. sterile-dm class of tools) do not include sterile self-interactions or the resonant runaway dynamics.
The critical-mixing-angle resonance criterion in the heavy-mediator in-medium approximation is a closed-form analytic estimate reproducible by hand.

Published X-ray line and structure exclusion curves exist and can be overlaid, but no packaged likelihood exists (card: likelihood_available 'no') and the structure bounds are spectrum-dependent for this nonthermal distribution.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver covers active-to-sterile conversion with sterile-sector self-interactions through a heavy mediator, including the in-medium self-interaction potential, the resonance criterion, and the runaway production phase; the calculation exists only as the authors' private numerical solution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public sterile-neutrino production code (e.g. the sterile-dm/LASAGNA family of momentum-resolved quantum-kinetic solvers) with a G_phi-parameterized sterile self-energy term and heavy-mediator contact self-scattering collision integrals, validating against the paper's runaway threshold theta_c and overproduction results.

gaps.description: No packaged X-ray line or structure (phase-space, subhalo, Lyman-alpha, reionization) likelihood exists for this model's nonthermal momentum distribution, which differs from both Dodelson-Widrow and thermal spectra; current constraints are overlaid exclusion curves derived for other spectra.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast pipeline that takes the solver output f_s(p), computes the transfer function with CLASS using a tabulated non-cold distribution, and applies Lyman-alpha emulator and Milky Way satellite-count likelihoods, plus a digitized X-ray line likelihood in the (m_s, theta) plane.

route_step_status.reason: The curvature spectrum is fully specified by the primary paper's equations plus a numerical mode integral, but only the authors' private implementation exists; no public thermal-inflation/fast-roll spectrum code is available.
Press-Schechter-style beta(M) with a critical-collapse prescription is a standard semi-analytic calculation reproducible directly from well-known formulas.

Public monochromatic PBH constraint compilations (e.g. PBHbounds-style envelope curves) exist, but the extended-mass-function convolution and a packaged abundance likelihood do not (card: likelihood_available no, recasting_needed yes).

gaps.description: No public code maps thermal-inflation parameters (m, H/m, g, V0) to the enhanced curvature spectrum P_R(k) and the resulting critical-collapse PBH mass function f_PBH(M); the calculation exists only as the paper's private numerical integral, so the model cannot be scanned beyond the quoted benchmark.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a small standalone integrator that solves the mode equations through the thermal-inflation and fast-roll phases to get P_R(k), then feeds it into a standard Press-Schechter/critical-collapse mass-function module, validated against the m~600 TeV, H/m~0.30 all-DM benchmark.

gaps.description: No packaged PBH abundance likelihood exists that convolves this model's extended (narrow but non-monochromatic) mass function with the mass-dependent microlensing, evaporation, and CMB-accretion bounds; the paper uses a monochromatic overlay proxy.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build an extended-mass-function recast on top of a public PBH constraint compilation (e.g. the bradkav/PBHbounds curve set), applying the standard Carr-et-al. convolution of f(M) against each mass-dependent bound, including the Subaru/HSC and CMB-accretion envelopes with their stated caveats.

route_step_status.reason: The card requires custom Boltzmann equations for coupled visible/mirror Dirac leptogenesis with flavour and washout effects; no public leptogenesis code (ULYSSES-type solvers target standard Majorana leptogenesis) covers this two-sector Dirac setup.
Converting lepton asymmetries through visible and mirror sphaleron factors and mapping to Omega_DM/Omega_b via the mirror baryon mass is simple analytic bookkeeping given the asymmetries.

Delta N_eff from a given Tprime/T and mirror light-species content is analytic and Planck N_eff constraints are public, but the required mirror thermal history with Z2 breaking is not supplied by the card.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver exists for Dirac leptogenesis with coupled visible and mirror sectors: heavy Dirac singlet-neutrino decays into both sectors, flavour effects, washout in each sector, and simultaneous tracking of Y_B and Y_Bprime; only the paper's unflavoured hierarchical analytic benchmark is available.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public leptogenesis solver (e.g. the ULYSSES framework) with Dirac-type asymmetry conservation, mirror-sector decay channels y and yprime, per-sector washout parameters, and dual sphaleron conversion, validating against the paper's M_1 lower-bound scaling in the unflavoured hierarchical limit.

gaps.description: The mirror-sector thermal history is not derived: Tprime/T evolution and the surviving light mirror degrees of freedom under the invoked Yukawa and QCD-scale Z2 breaking are unspecified, so Delta N_eff cannot be computed numerically even though the qualitative constraint direction is clear.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the mirror-sector entropy and decoupling history for specified Z2-breaking benchmarks (or an asymmetric-reheating parameterization of Tprime/T), compute Delta N_eff(Tprime/T, mirror light content), and feed it into the standard Planck/BBN N_eff likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the explicit fermion mass matrix and extracting Majorana masses and active-hidden mixings is standard analytic/linear-algebra work spelled out in the primary paper.
The radiative and invisible decay widths and lifetime follow from the paper's one-loop analytic formulas in terms of mass and mixing.

The kinked Kurie-plot spectrum is analytic, but a realistic KATRIN-like evaluation needs the experimental response, endpoint modeling, and resolution, for which no packaged public model is identified in the card.
COHERENT/reactor CEvNS data releases exist publicly, but no ready-made recoil-spectrum recast for hidden-fermion production through Z_s/H exchange is identified, so a dedicated recast must be built.
The invisible-Z width constraint is a published LEP measurement applied through the paper's analytic bound s_eta^2 c_eta^2 g_s^2 < 2.1e-4, requiring no new tooling.

gaps.description: The relic momentum distribution f(p) of the keV hidden fermion after relativistic freeze-out and entropy dilution by hidden-scalar decay is not derived (card: distribution_function_available 'no', free_streaming_length null), so the warm-dark-matter structure suppression cannot be quantitatively mapped to Lyman-alpha or satellite bounds beyond the rough 100 kpc free-streaming estimate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the freeze-out plus entropy-dilution Boltzmann evolution to obtain the diluted f(p), feed it to CLASS as a tabulated non-cold relic to get the transfer function, and map to thermal-WDM-equivalent Lyman-alpha and Milky Way satellite mass bounds.

gaps.description: No keV-scale kink-search beta-spectrum likelihood with realistic detector response exists for evaluating the |U_e4|^2, |U_e5|^2 branches in tritium spectra; only the analytic spectral formula is available.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a kink-search likelihood using the published KATRIN/TRISTAN keV-sterile sensitivity model (response matrix, resolution, endpoint systematics) applied to the two-branch spectrum with masses M_1, M_2.

gaps.description: No CEvNS recoil likelihood exists for hidden-fermion production in coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering through Z_s/H exchange; the card notes no final experimental exclusion contour and that thresholds and resolution are decisive.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a modified CEvNS recoil-spectrum calculator including the massive-final-state kinematics and coherence condition, and recast the public COHERENT CsI/LAr data releases (and reactor CEvNS data) into limits on the Z/H exchange couplings.

route_step_status.reason: The double-seesaw mass and mixing relations are explicit analytic formulas in the primary paper, requiring only matrix diagonalization.

The scalar-decay freeze-in Boltzmann solution and dilution-corrected distribution are solved in the paper (distribution_function_available 'yes') and the in-equilibrium decay spectrum has known semi-analytic form, but no public packaged solver reproduces it.

CLASS/CAMB accept a tabulated non-cold relic distribution to compute the transfer function and free-streaming cutoff, but the card notes a dedicated Lyman-alpha recast for this exact nonthermal spectrum has not been done; only thermal-equivalent mappings exist.

Published X-ray line search exclusion curves in the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane exist and can be overlaid, but no packaged X-ray likelihood is available (card: likelihood_available 'no', 'X-ray likelihood not run here').

gaps.description: No public solver reproduces the scalar-decay freeze-in production of the 7.1 keV sterile neutrino with entropy dilution, i.e. the nonthermal f(p) with p/T = 2.477/d^(1/3) and the Omega_DM h^2 = 0.1199 benchmark; the calculation exists only in the paper.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a scalar-decay freeze-in module (momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for in-equilibrium parent decay plus dilution factor, following the Merle-Totzauer formalism) that outputs f(p) and the relic abundance, validated against the paper's benchmark values.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha forest likelihood exists for this exact scalar-decay freeze-in spectrum; current constraints rely on thermal-relic or standard sterile-neutrino equivalent mappings that are not identical to the colder in-equilibrium decay distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the transfer function with CLASS using the tabulated freeze-in f(p) and apply a Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator (MIKE/HIRES/eBOSS-based grids) directly to the resulting matter power, replacing the thermal-equivalent mapping.

gaps.description: No packaged X-ray decay-line likelihood in the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane is available for evaluating the 3.55 keV line benchmark against cluster, Andromeda, and blank-sky searches; only qualitative overlays of published limits can be used.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published X-ray line search limits (clusters, M31, Milky Way blank-sky, diffuse background) into a combined likelihood over m_s and sin^2 2theta with a specified halo model, applicable to any full-DM sterile-neutrino card.

route_step_status.reason: Standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) cover the freeze-out and freeze-in limits, but the conversion-driven regime requires coupled number-density Boltzmann equations without chemical equilibrium, which no public tool provides out of the box and the card lists no code (tool_or_code null).
Mapping lambda and Delta m to the mediator proper decay length is a simple analytic two/three-body decay-width calculation, adequate despite null tool_or_code.

SModelS and LLP recasts exist and were used by the primary paper, but the card notes the reinterpretation is approximate without full detector efficiencies for slepton-like charged/disappearing tracks (recasting_needed: partial, likelihood_available: approximate).

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver handles the conversion-driven freeze-out regime of this leptophilic model, where chemical equilibrium between the Majorana DM and the charged scalar mediator breaks down and coupled per-species number-density equations with conversion terms must be solved; standard micrOMEGAs/MadDM coannihilation routines assume chemical equilibrium and misplace the viable feeble-coupling window.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or implement a standalone solver in the style of the conversion-driven freeze-out literature) to solve the coupled chi and phi number-density equations with explicit conversion rates chi l <-> phi and decay terms, scanning lambda from 1e-8 to 0.1 across the freeze-in/conversion/freeze-out transition, and validate against the paper's m_chi=150 GeV, Delta m=2 GeV benchmarks.

gaps.description: Only an approximate recast of CMS/ATLAS long-lived charged-particle and disappearing-track searches exists for this charged-scalar mediator: detector-efficiency maps and a reusable likelihood for slepton-like LLPs in the compressed (Delta m ~ 2 GeV) regime with soft leptons are not available (likelihood_available: approximate, likelihood_reference null).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add the relevant heavy-stable-charged-particle and disappearing-track efficiency maps to SModelS or the LLP Recasting Repository for a singly charged scalar decaying to chi plus a soft lepton, parameterized in (m_phi, Delta m, c tau), and publish the resulting acceptance-times-efficiency likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: The QCD sum-rule extraction of m_S and f_S is an analytic calculation already performed in the primary paper within stated Borel/threshold windows, so no external tool is required.

No S-nucleon scattering amplitude or cross-section calculation exists (tool_or_code null, 'not computed in batch'), and the required nonperturbative QCD/nuclear form factors have not been derived by any public tool.
The oxygen-stability and dibaryon-lifetime recast requires nuclear matrix elements that the primary paper explicitly leaves as requiring further analysis, with no tool identified.

gaps.description: No calculation of the S-hexaquark-nucleon elastic scattering cross section sigma_S-nucleon exists: the compact uuddss composite couples through flavor-singlet scalar exchange (sigma/f0(980)/glueball), and neither the couplings nor the composite form factor have been derived, so XENON/SuperCDMS limits cannot be mapped onto the model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the S-nucleon amplitude with QCD sum rules or lattice QCD for the scalar-singlet couplings g_{S S sigma/f0/G}, fold in the hexaquark compactness form factor, and publish sigma_S-nucleon(m_S, r_S) so standard light-DM detector recasts can be applied.

gaps.description: No nuclear-stability calculation exists for the predicted m_S = 1.18-1.24 GeV window: the double-weak conversion rates of nucleon pairs in nuclei (especially oxygen) into S, and the corresponding dibaryon lifetime, have not been computed with realistic nuclear matrix elements and compactness suppression.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute nn/pp/pn -> S conversion matrix elements in oxygen and other benchmark nuclei using a nuclear shell-model or ab-initio treatment combined with the hexaquark wavefunction-overlap suppression factor, following the Farrar-style compact-sexaquark formalism, and publish exclusion curves in (m_S, S-nucleon coupling).

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for any of the model's constraints (all three card constraints have likelihood_available: no); in particular there is no reusable direct-detection likelihood for a GeV-scale B=2 composite, only detector cross-section scales quoted from XENON/SuperCDMS.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once sigma_S-nucleon is derived (gap_1), recast XENON and SuperCDMS light-dark-matter analyses for a 1.2 GeV spin-independent composite with the appropriate nuclear response, and add a thermal pre-BBN freeze-out abundance likelihood tying m_S to the observed relic density.

route_step_status.reason: The Z-prime decay and Z-prime-mediated annihilation matrix elements are tree-level analytic formulae given by the model Lagrangian and were computed with SARAH/SPheno support per associated_code.
The freeze-in yield was solved with a custom (private) integrator; micrOMEGAs supports freeze-in but no public BLSMIS model implementation or released integrator is identified in the card.
Comparing Omega_S1 h^2 to the Planck relic-density band is a trivial approximate-Gaussian test that needs no dedicated tool.
Verifying that the Z2 charge assignment forbids active-neutrino mixing is a pen-and-paper Lagrangian/mass-matrix inspection.

gaps.description: No public model implementation exists for the BLSMIS freeze-in calculation: the paper used SARAH plus SPheno/micrOMEGAs and a custom freeze-in integrator for nonthermal Z' production, but no model files or repository are released, so the relic-density benchmarks cannot be reproduced or scanned by third parties.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release (or rebuild) the SARAH BLSMIS model files and implement the nonthermal-Z' freeze-in yield calculation in micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module, validating against the paper's single-component benchmark curves.

gaps.description: The final S_1^1 phase-space distribution and linear transfer function are never extracted (only the nonthermal Z' distribution is computed), so the keV warm FIMP cannot be confronted with Lyman-alpha or other small-scale-structure constraints; the route caveat explicitly notes Lyman-alpha transfer functions are not included and the structure_formation block is entirely unknown.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent freeze-in Boltzmann equation for f_S1(q) from Z' decay and annihilation, feed it to CLASS as a non-cold relic (ncdm with tabulated f(q)) to obtain the transfer function and half-mode mass, and map onto existing Lyman-alpha WDM-equivalent-mass bounds and emulators.

route_step_status.reason: Decay and annihilation rates for the BLSMIS spectrum are standard tree-level calculations, and the card records that SARAH/SPheno were used for masses and decay widths.

micrOMEGAs supports freeze-in yield integration, but the coupled two-component S_1^1 plus nu_H^1 system with Z' and h_2 sources needs a custom or adapted integrator, and no public model implementation was identified in the card.
A Gaussian comparison of Omega_total h^2 to the Planck value is simple arithmetic (the card itself labels it a Gaussian relic-density target).
Inspecting the Z2 charges and neutrino mass matrix to confirm zero active mixing is pen-and-paper model analysis.

gaps.description: No merger waveforms exist for binary boson stars with the logarithmic potential: GW detectability is inferred only from equilibrium mass and compactness, with no numerical-relativity or perturbative waveform model to distinguish such mergers from black-hole binaries in LIGO/Virgo searches.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity binary boson-star mergers for benchmark compactness values of the logarithmic potential (extending existing complex-scalar NR merger setups) and fit inspiral-merger templates or tidal-deformability corrections usable in LIGO/Virgo parameter estimation.

gaps.description: The MACHO/microlensing and CMB-isocurvature constraint mappings defining viable scalar-mass windows are only approximate: the excluded scalar-mass intervals are figure-level in the paper and were not digitized, so the (m_phi, f_DM) viability filter cannot be applied programmatically.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize published compact-object f_DM(M) exclusion curves (EROS/OGLE/Subaru-HSC, CMB accretion limits) and the Planck isocurvature bound, and recompute allowed (m_phi, coupling, f_DM) regions through the M_max(m_phi) relation from the solver of gap_1.

route_step_status.reason: Planck-suppressed modulus decay rates Gamma ~ m_mod^3/m_Pl^2 and decay times are simple analytic formulas the source itself evaluates by hand.
Scale-factor dilution of rho_dr and n_chi between the two modulus decays under matter domination is straightforward pen-and-paper cosmology given the branching ratios.

The coupled Boltzmann solve for moduli, dark matter with prompt annihilation, and dark radiation has tool_or_code null, was explicitly not run, and the route lists it under required_code_resources with route_status planned.

gaps.description: No coupled Boltzmann solver exists for the two-modulus nonthermal history (phi2 and phi1 energy densities, hidden-sector chi number density with prompt chi chi -> dark radiation annihilation, and rho_dr) beyond the instantaneous-decay analytic estimates, so the final relic density and Delta N_eff cannot be computed numerically.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled ODE system for (rho_phi2, rho_phi1, n_chi, rho_dr, rho_vis) with continuous (non-instantaneous) decay terms and the <sigma v>_ann sink, e.g. by extending an existing early-matter-domination/nonthermal relic code, and validate it against the source's dilution scalings and the m_mod > 50-100 TeV BBN floor.

gaps.description: No likelihood is implemented for any of the three constraints (BBN lifetime floor, relic-abundance overclosure, dark-radiation dilution): all cards list likelihood_available: no and recasting_needed for the Planck relic-density and Delta N_eff targets onto the model parameters (m1, m2, branching ratios, <sigma v>_ann).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the Boltzmann solve exists, wrap it in a likelihood that compares the predicted Omega_chi h^2 and Delta N_eff to the Planck 2018 posterior (Gaussian on Omega h^2 and the Delta N_eff bound) and imposes T_reheat > ~5 MeV as a hard BBN cut, exposing (m1, m2, B_2dm, B_2dr, m_chi, <sigma v>_ann) as sampled parameters.

route_step_status.reason: The conformal mass relations mapping (M_chi, M_2, theta) to M_Ax, g_X, g_S are closed-form analytic formulas from the scale-invariant potential.
CalcHEP + micrOMEGAs are public and cover this WIMP-like regime, but the model implementation is author code with no identified public location (availability unknown).

BR(h1->invisible) from theta and M_chi is a standard tree-level partial-width formula computable by hand.
Public tools of the HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals type cover mixed-singlet scalar recasts, but the card records only an approximate paper-level translation with no implemented interface for this model.
The A_X width and mixing-suppressed production estimate is a simple analytic/qualitative calculation the paper performs without code.

gaps.description: The CalcHEP model files and micrOMEGAs setup used for the relic-density and sigma_SI scan are author code with no public repository identified, so the resonance bands and direct-detection predictions cannot be regenerated or extended off the paper's benchmark mixing angles.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the renormalizable scale-invariant Lagrangian (given in full in the paper) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and run micrOMEGAs, validating against the published relic-density resonance bands and SI scatter plot, then archive the model files publicly.

gaps.description: No implemented likelihood combines the Planck relic-density target with LUX/XENON1T/SuperCDMS SI limits for this model; the card stores only scan-level approximate exclusions and paper-quoted benchmark bounds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the micrOMEGAs output in a DDCalc-based direct-detection likelihood plus a Gaussian Planck Omega_CDM h^2 term (GAMBIT-style), sampling (M_chi, M_2, theta) instead of the paper's fixed-theta benchmarks.

gaps.description: The collider route (invisible Higgs, h2 searches, triple-Higgs deviation, A_X production) has no implemented recast: scalar-mixing limits are translated only approximately in the paper and the route is marked planned with 'HiggsBounds-like scalar recast' listed as a required but absent resource.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-scalar effective couplings (theta^2-scaled h2 production, BR(h1->invisible)) in HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals and add the CMS invisible-Higgs and LHC ZZ resonance likelihoods, reproducing the paper's quoted theta^2 examples as validation.

route_step_status.reason: The Schwinger discharge and Hawking survival bounds are closed-form analytic formulas for the dark-Reissner-Nordstrom setup that the source evaluates by hand.

The merger-transient detectability step is explicitly planned: the binary merger rate is unknown and IceCube/HAWC transient likelihoods are listed as unavailable.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a BlackHawk-style Hawking-spectrum code to the dark-Reissner-Nordstrom metric, adding near-extremal temperature suppression, charged-particle greybody factors, and the dark-photon emission channel, validated against the ordinary Schwarzschild limit at zero charge.

gaps.description: Existing diffuse-gamma (COMPTEL/EGRET), BBN, and CMB injection limits apply to ordinary evaporating PBHs; no recast pipeline maps them onto the PeBH two-stage history (initial evaporation to the near-extremal state plus residual remnant emission) with the initial-to-remnant mass rescaling the source prescribes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast layer that takes the charged-remnant injection history from the extended Hawking code and rescales published f_PBH(M) evaporation constraints (and energy-injection BBN/CMB bounds) to f_eBH as a function of remnant mass and initial mass function, recovering the source's ~1.4e9 g BBN transition scale as validation.

gaps.description: The binary merger rate R_merge of oppositely charged PeBHs, which sets the predicted rate of Hawking-burst transients, is not computed anywhere: no population model exists that includes the attractive dark-Coulomb interaction in binary formation and coalescence.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt the standard early-universe PBH binary-formation formalism to charged pairs by adding the dark-electromagnetic force to the two-body dynamics and charge-pairing statistics of the initial distribution, yielding R_merge(M_eBH, f_eBH, charge distribution) as a semi-analytic model.

gaps.description: No IceCube/HAWC transient likelihood is implemented for short high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray bursts from evaporating merger remnants; the route lists all three detector likelihoods as unavailable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct a burst-search likelihood from published IceCube transient point-source and HAWC PBH-burst analyses, taking the predicted burst spectrum and R_merge as inputs and returning expected event counts against the measured burst-rate limits.

route_step_status.reason: PDMH formation (collapse redshift, halo mass) is currently a semi-analytic by-hand treatment whose outcome depends strongly on screening assumptions; the card lists a spherical-collapse solver with screening as a required but nonexistent resource.

CMB energy-injection machinery and Planck likelihoods exist from PBH accretion studies (arxiv:1612.05644), but they assume compact objects; the extended-halo accretion/luminosity model needed to recast them is not implemented.
The card states the local clump encounter / free-particle-fraction model for direct detection is not implemented and names no tool.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a spherical-collapse code coupling the dark-fermion fluid to the light scalar with effective coupling beta and an explicit screening prescription during radiation domination, outputting z_form, M_PDMH, and R_PDMH over the beta = 3-30, m_psi > 0.1 MeV window; validate against the paper's fiducial 0.03-16 M_sun window, then check with N-body simulations including the scalar fifth force.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement extended-lens magnification profiles for the assumed nonsingular isothermal PDMH density profile and recompute EROS/MACHO/OGLE/HSC event-rate likelihoods as a function of (M_PDMH, R_PDMH, f_DM), following the extended-lens treatment of the cited 1707.03310 framework.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the gas accretion rate and radiative efficiency for an extended isothermal-profile halo (replacing the Bondi-onto-horizon treatment of PBH studies), then feed the resulting energy-injection history into an ExoCLASS/HYREC-type ionization module with the Planck temperature/polarization likelihood.

gaps.description: No model exists for the present-day local encounter rate and residual free-particle fraction of PDMHs in the Milky Way (including tidal disruption and survival), so the predicted direct-detection depletion cannot be quantified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Model PDMH survival and tidal stripping in Milky Way-like potentials (semi-analytic subhalo-evolution machinery adapted to AU-scale, solar-mass clumps) to compute the unbound-particle density at Earth and the Earth-PDMH encounter rate versus M_PDMH.

route_step_status.reason: The nonrelativistic halo flux and event-rate scaling (about 0.23 per year per m^2) is a simple analytic formula from rho_DM, v_DM, and M_relic.

No recast of large-area, paleo-detector, or monopole-search exposures into a CPR bound exists; the route lists the detector likelihood as unavailable and tool_or_code is null.
The CMB charge-to-mass comparison and cosmic-censorship check are order-of-magnitude analytic comparisons the paper performs by hand.

gaps.description: No detector-response simulation exists for the CPR signature: energy deposition, ionization, scintillation, and bubble-nucleation yields for an order-e charged Planck-mass object moving at halo velocity, a regime (very slow, very heavy, straight track) outside the calibration range of standard SRIM/Geant4 workflows for each candidate technology.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute low-velocity electronic and nuclear stopping power for a unit-charge Planck-mass projectile (Lindhard-type formalism cross-checked with SRIM tables) and implement the track response in Geant4-style simulations for bubble chambers, liquid argon TPCs, and paleo-detector minerals, validating against published slow-monopole response studies.

gaps.description: No search likelihood or recast maps the CPR flux and track efficiency onto existing large-area, monopole (e.g. MACRO-type), or paleo-detector exposures; the route's detector likelihood is listed as unavailable, so no quantitative bound on f_CPR can be set.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compile exposure tables from published slow-monopole and heavy-track searches, fold them with the simulated CPR track efficiency from the detector-response gap, and release a Poisson counting likelihood on f_CPR(M_relic, q_CPR) that reproduces the paper's 4.3 m^2-per-event-per-year benchmark.

gaps.description: The relic abundance f_CPR is treated as a free input: there is no implemented calculation from an initial PBH mass function through Hawking evaporation with a Planck-scale halt and stochastic charge acquisition to the present-day charged-relic abundance and charge distribution (the route lists 'PBH mass-function calculation' as a required but absent resource).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public PBH evaporation code (BlackHawk-type) with a Planck-mass evaporation floor and a stochastic charged-emission random walk to output f_CPR and the relic charge distribution as functions of the initial mass function, checked against the ordinary full-evaporation limit.

route_step_status.reason: Verifying that the unbroken Z2 matter parity stabilizes the lightest neutral fermion is pen-and-paper group theory on the SO(10) charge assignments.

The spin-independent Higgs-exchange cross section from y_33, m_3, and f_N is a standard closed-form formula.

Slow-roll comparison to Planck 2018 n_s and A_s central values is analytic, but no implemented Planck inflation likelihood is interfaced to the SO(10) potential coefficients (likelihood_available: partial, recasting_needed: yes, not rerun).

gaps.description: No public implementation of this model's low-energy singlet-doublet sector (m_D, m_S, Y_H with the SO(10)-fixed charge assignments) exists in a relic/direct-detection code, so the 57.10-61.23 GeV allowed window and the y_33 <= 1.5e-2 XENON1T bound are stored only as paper-quoted numbers and cannot be re-derived or updated to newer data (route_status: planned, no associated code).

route_step_status.reason: The tool_or_code entry names a method (relativistic Bose-Einstein collision integrals), not a public code; no released solver handles self-thermalizing scalar freeze-out with 2-to-4 number-changing reactions and an effective chemical potential, and standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) do not cover this decoupled-sector regime.

Applying the summary bounds (sigma/m < 1 cm^2/g, lambda_HS < 1e-13) is trivial arithmetic, but no actual likelihood exists (all card constraints have likelihood_available: no), so only coarse exclusion-curve comparisons are possible.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver computes the relic abundance of a decoupled self-thermalizing real scalar with relativistic Bose-Einstein statistics, 2-to-4 number-changing self-reactions, dark-sector temperature evolution, and an effective chemical potential; the paper relied on private numerical integrations of the collision terms.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Tabulate the frozen-out f(q) with temperature and chemical potential and feed it to the CLASS non-cold dark matter (ncdm) module with a custom distribution file to obtain T^2(k) and the half-mode scale across the (m, lambda, T_dark, mu) parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: The freeze-in distribution from two-body decay has a known closed-form collision-term solution and the entropy/g_* rescaling of the effective temperature is analytic, so this step is essentially pen-and-paper plus quadrature.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level X-mediated annihilation amplitudes from the given axial-vector couplings and U(1)_X charges are standard pen-and-paper quantum field theory, so the null tool_or_code is not a gap.

route_step_status.reason: Public lattice codes for scalar-field self-resonance exist (CosmoLattice, LatticeEasy class), but the paper's own code is not identified as public and only benchmark points were simulated, not a parameter scan.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann/transfer-function solver handles a mixed dark-matter component of dense oscillons plus a homogeneous ultralight field; existing fuzzy-DM solvers (axionCAMB-type) assume a purely homogeneous wave-like component, so the modified small-scale power spectrum cannot be computed.

gaps.description: No public Ly-alpha flux-power likelihood is available to constrain the oscillon-modified ULAP power spectrum; published FDM bounds (m_FDM > 20-37.5 x 1e-22 eV) assume standard homogeneous fuzzy-DM transfer functions and cannot be applied without recasting.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE flux-power analysis with hydrodynamical simulations (or an emulator such as a LaCE-type framework) run on oscillon-modified initial power spectra, marginalizing over the IGM thermal history as in the original FDM analysis.

route_step_status.reason: The benchmark pre-BBN cosmologies (kination, scalar-tensor, low-reheating) are closed-form H(T) and entropy parameterizations given in the paper, which is pen-and-paper work.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Dodelson-Widrow solver (or implement the paper's closed-form production kernels) with a parameterized pre-BBN module taking H(T), T_tr, and entropy injection as inputs, outputting f_s(p) and Omega_s h^2 over the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane for kination, scalar-tensor, and low-reheating cosmologies.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs handles two-component freeze-out and semi-annihilation, but no public model files exist and the separately-evolving dark-sector temperature after decoupling needs the hidden-sector extension or a custom coupled solver.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model in the micrOMEGAs 5 hidden-sector/two-component framework (or a custom coupled solver tracking T_dark), including semi-annihilation channels, and validate against the paper's benchmark relic abundances with S subdominant.

gaps.description: No packaged numerical solver is available for the velocity-dependent transfer cross section sigma_T(v)/m_chi in the nonperturbative attractive (and Majorana-basis repulsive) Yukawa regime with an MeV-scale stable mediator, which is precisely the regime needed for dwarf-scale 0.1-10 cm^2/g values.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a numerical equation-of-motion solver for the complex PQ field with thermal potential and friction terms, evolving charge density from rotation onset through weak sphaleron freeze-out and QCD trapping, and validate against the paper's overproduction factor of about 140 at f_a = 1e8 GeV, T_ws = 130 GeV.

The domain-wall Delta T/T estimate is an order-of-magnitude analytic scaling that requires no tool.
