gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize and package the primary and rel_1908_00553 exclusion curves as interpolable likelihood surfaces in (mu_chi, m_chi, T_R), with the stellar bound expressed as a dark-luminosity limit so it can be re-evaluated when stellar modeling improves.

route_step_status.reason: Public resonant (Shi-Fuller) sterile-neutrino production solvers such as sterile-dm exist and cover the quantum-kinetic/averaged Boltzmann treatment, but they assume the standard radiation-dominated expansion history and would need modification to accept a parameterized non-standard H(T) with a transition temperature T_tr.

CLASS (and CAMB) accept a tabulated non-thermal ncdm distribution function f_s(p) and compute the resulting transfer function and matter power spectrum, covering this model's resonant spectra without code changes.

BBN/N_eff constraints can be evaluated with public codes (AlterBBN, PArthENoPE, PRIMAT) plus Planck N_eff posteriors, but Lyman-alpha limits for non-thermal resonant spectra exist only as thermal-equivalent WDM mappings and digitized curves rather than a reusable likelihood, as the card's recasting_needed and partial likelihood flags record.
The radiative decay rate and line energy follow from the standard analytic sterile-neutrino decay relation in m_s and sin^2(2theta), which is simple pen-and-paper math despite the null tool_or_code.

Published X-ray line and DEBRA diffuse-background limits exist and can be rescaled by the produced sterile density, but no packaged likelihood reconstruction with instrument response and target column densities is recorded (likelihood_available: partial, recasting_needed: yes).

gaps.description: No public resonant sterile-neutrino production solver supports a non-standard pre-BBN expansion history: existing quantum-kinetic/Boltzmann codes (e.g. sterile-dm for Shi-Fuller production) hard-code the standard H(T), so the model's central parameterization of a modified Hubble rate above T_tr cannot be scanned with existing tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Shi-Fuller solver (sterile-dm or an averaged-Boltzmann reimplementation) to take a parameterized H(T) with power-law index and transition temperature T_tr as inputs, tracking lepton-asymmetry depletion and entropy conservation, and validate against the paper's example cosmology wedges in the mass-mixing plane.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha likelihood exists that is valid for the sharply peaked, colder-than-thermal resonant sterile-neutrino spectra of this model; current practice maps to a thermal-equivalent WDM mass, an approximation the card flags as requiring validation for each non-thermal spectrum and DM fraction.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints directly on the CLASS-computed transfer functions of the resonant spectra, either via the area-criterion generalization of thermal-WDM bounds or by evaluating a flux-power emulator (e.g. trained on MP-Gadget/Sherwood-style grids) on the non-thermal T(k), including mixed cold+sterile fractions.

gaps.description: X-ray line and DEBRA diffuse-background decay limits are available only as published exclusion curves for the standard-cosmology relic density; no packaged likelihood exists that rescales the bounds by the model's cosmology-dependent sterile density Omega_s/Omega_DM across targets.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble published X-ray (galaxy, cluster, blank-sky) and DEBRA limits into a single interpolable likelihood in (m_s, sin^2(2theta)) with an explicit linear rescaling by the produced density fraction, documenting target column-density assumptions so bounds update consistently as production changes.

route_step_status.reason: Twin neutralino mass-matrix diagonalization and the effective h-B'-B' coupling are simple analytic algebra doable by hand despite the null tool_or_code.

Public Boltzmann solvers (micrOMEGAs/DarkSUSY class) handle neutralino-like freeze-out, but no public implementation includes the twin-sector final states, twin degrees of freedom, and partial SM-twin thermal contact this model requires.
The signal is standard spin-independent Higgs-mediated scattering, so published Xenon1T/LZ limit curves and public tools like DDCalc apply directly to sigma_SI.
Decay widths and proper lifetimes from small visible-twin mixing follow from standard analytic two-body width formulas.

Public recast frameworks (CheckMATE/MadAnalysis/SModelS) cover prompt stau and higgsino searches, but the card notes dedicated analyses are needed for the displaced-vertex regime from small visible-twin mixing.

gaps.description: No public relic-density implementation of the twin-sector spectrum exists: freeze-out proceeds through twin-fermion (especially twin tau) final states via a right-handed twin stau, with twin-sector degrees of freedom and only partial thermal contact with the SM, none of which is covered by stock micrOMEGAs/DarkSUSY model files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the twin bino/higgsino/stau sector in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and run micrOMEGAs with the twin-sector relativistic degrees of freedom and (if needed) a visible-twin temperature ratio to reproduce the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 contours.

gaps.description: No recast pipeline exists for the model's LHC signatures in the displaced-vertex regime, where small visible-twin neutralino mixing gives macroscopic stau/higgsino decay lengths outside the coverage of standard prompt electroweakino recasts.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate events in MadGraph with the mixing-controlled lifetimes and recast against ATLAS/CMS displaced-vertex and long-lived-particle searches using the LLP modules of MadAnalysis or CheckMATE, mapping exclusions onto the (mu, m_stau, mixing) plane.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level annihilation and coannihilation amplitudes from the explicit dark-sector Lagrangian are standard pen-and-paper nonrelativistic EFT calculations.

The card names only a generic 'Sommerfeld solver'; coupled-channel Schroedinger solvers exist in the literature but no standard public code handles the two-level p-wave problem with the resonance islands this model requires.
PPPC4DMID tables and public propagation codes (GALPROP/DRAGON) cover leptonic positron spectra from GeV-TeV annihilation to light mediators decaying to e/mu.

Public CMB energy-injection (ExoCLASS/Planck) and Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihoods exist but assume velocity-independent cross sections, so the strongly velocity-selective <sigma v>(v) requires a custom velocity-weighted recast that has not been run.

gaps.description: No public solver exists for the two-level Majorana p-wave Sommerfeld problem: computing S_p(v) across the resonance islands requires a coupled-channel Schroedinger solution with mass splitting Delta and light scalar/pseudo-Goldstone mediators, which per-paper private code handled but no released tool covers.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or extend an existing multi-state Sommerfeld coupled-channel code to include the p-wave partial wave with off-diagonal mediator potentials, parameterized by (m_chi1, Delta, m_eta, alpha), validated against the paper's 780 GeV benchmark and resonance islands; the same solver yields the velocity-dependent sigma_T/m_chi.

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline handles the model's nonmonotonic velocity-dependent annihilation: existing Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihoods and CMB energy-injection bounds assume a single velocity-independent <sigma v>, so the claimed suppression at dwarf and recombination velocities cannot be quantitatively tested.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build velocity-dispersion-weighted J-factors for the Fermi dwarf sample from stellar kinematics, fold <sigma v>(v) into the public Fermi dwarf likelihood, and integrate the low-velocity limit of S_p(v) into ExoCLASS for the CMB energy-injection constraint.

route_step_status.reason: The step is a bookkeeping data transform from the completed model card to a recovery observable and needs no external tool, but it performs no physical forward modeling.

gaps.description: No public code computes the relic abundance of a cold hidden confining sector populated at temperature ratio xi_i ~ 0.006: the dark-baryon case needs hidden-sector freeze-out with composite cross sections sigma ~ 1/Lambda_i^2 at T_i << T, and the pure Yang-Mills glueball case needs a 3->2 cannibalizing Boltzmann network, neither covered by standard relic tools that assume SM thermal contact.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the hidden-sector temperature-ratio machinery in micrOMEGAs (or a dedicated Boltzmann code) to solve the decoupled-sector network for (xi_i, Lambda_i), including glueball 3->2 cannibalism with lattice-calibrated Yang-Mills equation of state, and validate against the paper's Lambda ~ 50 MeV glueball and 10-100 TeV/xi_i dark-baryon estimates.

gaps.description: The card's only route stops at reading the card itself: no forward model maps (xi_i, Lambda_i, m_phi) to any concrete observable such as the small-scale-structure signature the observable channel names, glueball/dark-baryon self-interaction cross sections, or residual dark-radiation Delta N_eff from unconfined hidden sectors.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the model's transfer function and free-streaming scale for the cold composite relic (expected near-CDM given xi_i << 1), the self-interaction cross section sigma/m ~ Lambda_i^-3 for glueballs, and the Delta N_eff contribution of non-confining sectors, then encode these as proper observables and route steps checkable against CLASS/ETHOS-style pipelines and Planck N_eff bounds.

route_step_status.reason: Anomaly-cancellation and remnant-Z2 checks of the B-L charge table are pen-and-paper group-theory arithmetic requiring no tool.

micrOMEGAs 5 natively solves coupled two-component Boltzmann equations and the paper used the FeynRules/CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs chain, but the card notes no model files were generated or released, so the implementation must be rebuilt.
Delta N_eff from right-handed-neutrino decoupling follows from the standard analytic decoupling-temperature and entropy-ratio relation given in the source.

gaps.description: No public model implementation exists for this anomaly-free B-L variant: the fractional-charge chiral fermion sector, extended scalar potential, and two-component (psi_1, psi_2) coupled freeze-out with conversion annihilation must be re-encoded before micrOMEGAs can reproduce the paper's relic and direct-detection numbers.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the charge assignments, scalar sector, and Yukawa structure in FeynRules, export CalcHEP files, and run micrOMEGAs 5 in two-DM-component mode including psi_2 psi_2 -> psi_1 psi_1 conversion, validating against the paper's Omega_psi1 + Omega_psi2 = 0.120 benchmark regions.

gaps.description: The Delta N_eff constraint is applied only as the quoted static bound Delta N_eff <= 0.285 with an analytic decoupling estimate; no pipeline folds the g_BL- and M_ZBL-dependent right-handed-neutrino decoupling into a current CMB+BBN likelihood, which the card flags as a leading constraint that was not updated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute T_dec(g_BL, M_ZBL) with momentum-averaged collision rates, map to Delta N_eff via the entropy-dilution relation, and evaluate against the Planck 2018 + BAO (and forecast CMB-S4) N_eff posterior in CLASS/MontePython to replace the fixed 0.285 cut.

route_step_status.reason: FeynRules and CalcHEP are public and fully adequate, but the paper's cxSM Z2-breaking model files were not released, so the implementation must be rebuilt from the Lagrangian.

micrOMEGAs computes Omega h^2 and tree-level sigma_SI once model files exist, but near the pseudo-Goldstone cancellation (a_1 -> 0) the tree-level sigma_SI vanishes and the physical rate is loop-dominated, outside the default tool treatment.

Public building blocks exist (CosmoTransitions for the two-step SFOEWPT, standard sound-wave GW spectral fits, published CEPC/FCC-ee precision projections) but no assembled cxSM pipeline for the one-loop Higgs/EW shifts and GW spectrum is available.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the Z2-breaking cxSM exists: the FeynRules/CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs files with the a_1 and b_1 soft-breaking terms and h_1/h_2 mixing were not released, blocking reproduction of the relic-density and rescaled sigma_SI scan.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the cxSM potential with nonzero a_1, b_1 and singlet vev in FeynRules, export CalcHEP files, and run micrOMEGAs over the paper's scan domain, checking the exact tree-level SI cancellation as a_1 -> 0 as a validation test.

gaps.description: In the pseudo-Goldstone cancellation region the tree-level spin-independent cross section that micrOMEGAs returns is not the physical prediction: the surviving rate comes from one-loop and momentum-suppressed contributions, so XENON1T comparisons near a_1 -> 0 are unreliable without the loop-level amplitude for this Z2-breaking variant.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt the published one-loop pseudo-Goldstone dark-matter sigma_SI calculations (developed for the symmetric complex-singlet model) to include the a_1 soft-breaking term, and add the resulting effective DM-nucleon coupling to the micrOMEGAs direct-detection module.

gaps.description: No released implementation of the cxSM finite-temperature effective potential exists for the phase-transition leg: computing (alpha_pt, beta/H, T_n) for the two-step SFOEWPT benchmarks and the resulting LISA-band GW spectrum currently requires rebuilding the thermal potential by hand.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the one-loop daisy-resummed cxSM thermal potential in CosmoTransitions (or PhaseTracer), extract alpha_pt, beta/H and T_n along the scan, and map to GW spectra with the standard sound-wave spectral fits against the public LISA sensitivity curve.

gaps.description: Only approximate projection-level constraints exist for the Higgs-factory leg: the card records no packaged likelihood mapping the model's one-loop Higgs-coupling and S/T/U shifts onto CEPC/FCC-ee/ILC global-fit precision, so the complementarity claim cannot be quantified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the one-loop hZZ-coupling shift and oblique parameters as functions of (M_2, theta, v_s) and fold them into the published CEPC/FCC-ee global-fit covariance (e.g. via a Gaussian likelihood over the projected coupling precisions) to draw exclusion/discovery contours.

route_step_status.reason: The standard FeynRules/CalcHEP/MicrOMEGAs pipeline covers two-component scalar Higgs-portal relic density and SI cross-section calculations, matching the paper's own workflow.

Public finite-temperature phase-transition codes (e.g. CosmoTransitions-class tools) exist, but tool_or_code is null and no cxSM-specific implementation of the finite-temperature potential and GW-spectrum pipeline is provided by the card.

Only projection-level e+e- precision and LISA sensitivity curves exist (likelihood_available approximate, recasting_needed yes); comparison is doable but no implemented forecast likelihood is packaged.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the cxSM Z2-symmetric finite-temperature effective potential and SFOEWPT-to-GW pipeline (alpha, beta/H, T_n, GW spectrum) exists; the phase-transition step has null tool_or_code and the route lists an unnamed 'finite-temperature phase-transition code' as a required resource.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the cxSM one-loop finite-temperature potential (with daisy resummation) in CosmoTransitions or an equivalent bounce solver, extract alpha, beta/H and T_n over the paper's scan domain, and feed standard sound-wave/turbulence GW spectral templates compared against the LISA power-law-sensitivity curve.

gaps.description: The cxSM Z2-symmetric FeynRules/CalcHEP/MicrOMEGAs model files and scan machinery used for the relic-density and XENON1T comparison are not publicly released (associated_code has no repositories; the card notes the precise excluded region requires the original scan machinery), so the exclusion cannot be reproduced precisely.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the Z2-symmetric cxSM scalar potential in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files into micrOMEGAs, validate against the paper's relic and rescaled-SI benchmark behavior over the stated scan ranges, and release the model files.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled Boltzmann system with bound-state formation/dissociation is a custom private code of the paper; no public solver handles two asymmetric dark components with BSF/BSD and late freeze-in decay out of the box.
Two-body decay kinematics plus a freeze-in source term is straightforward analytic work, adequate at the stated benchmark level even though tool_or_code names no package.

Comparing relic fractions to the Omega_DM target is trivial, but the BBN/CMB energy-injection and boosted-DM parts of the step are explicitly not implemented (likelihood_available no, recasting_needed yes).

gaps.description: No public coupled Boltzmann solver exists for two asymmetric dark-matter components with Coulomb-limit bound-state formation/dissociation and late bound-state freeze-in decay; the paper's custom code is not released and standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY) do not cover this asymmetric two-sector BSF configuration.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement and release the coupled number-density equations (Y_light, Y_heavy, Y_bound) with the paper's Coulomb-limit BSF/BSD rates, optionally extending finite mediator-mass Yukawa corrections, validating against the published benchmark energy-density partitions.

gaps.description: No BBN/CMB energy-injection likelihood exists for late bound-state decays into boosted light dark matter with associated visible entropy injection near the BBN epoch; the card flags the timing but implements no likelihood (con_late_decay_bbn_injection has likelihood_available no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast that maps Gamma_B, T_decay, and visible branching assumptions onto existing BBN codes (AlterBBN/PArthENoPE) and CMB energy-injection machinery (ExoCLASS/DarkHistory), producing exclusion contours in the (Gamma_B, m_heavy/m_light, coupling) space.

gaps.description: The full nonthermal phase-space distribution f(p) of the boosted light component injected by late bound-state decays is not derived (distribution_function_available no; the decay step yields momentum injection but 'not a complete f(p)'), preventing free-streaming and small-scale structure assessment.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p,t) analytically from the two-body decay source term convolved with the bound-state decay history and redshifting, then feed it as a non-cold species (CLASS ncdm with tabulated psd) to obtain the transfer function and an effective free-streaming/half-mode scale.

route_step_status.reason: Generating benchmark spectra over the stated M_H3, lambda_L, and Delta M_A3 ranges is simple scripting over the tree-level scalar potential; null tool_or_code does not block this essentially analytic step.
micrOMEGAs handles inert-doublet-like relic calculations with co-annihilation, but the specific A4-Z4 three-Higgs-doublet model files (FeynRules/CalcHEP) are not publicly released.

Cut-based filters against published relic, invisible-width, direct- and indirect-detection limits are implementable, but the card supplies no machine-readable likelihoods (likelihood_available no/partial) and states they must be supplied externally.

gaps.description: No public FeynRules/CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model files exist for the A4-Z4 three-Higgs-doublet inert sector (associated_code lists no repositories), so the relic scan with H_3-A_3 co-annihilation and the mixing-angle-dependent effective Higgs portal cannot be reproduced with standard IDM implementations alone.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the A4-Z4 3HDM scalar sector in FeynRules, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and validate against the paper's benchmark points (42.2 GeV, 53.65 GeV, and the >536 GeV high-mass window) before public release.

gaps.description: No reusable joint likelihood exists for the constraint-filter step: the paper reports mass windows and exclusions (relic, W/Z/Higgs invisible widths, XENON1T, dwarf-galaxy indirect limits) only as qualitative cuts, with no machine-readable likelihood or scan files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compose an explicit likelihood pipeline from existing public components: Planck relic-density gaussian, HiggsTools/Lilith for invisible-width and Higgs signal strengths, DDCalc for XENON1T SI scattering, and Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihoods (gamLike) for the annihilation cross section, wired to the micrOMEGAs outputs of gap_1.

route_step_status.reason: Computing background energy density, pressure, and sound speeds from the two-state phonon EFT in the homogeneous effective-fluid treatment is analytic work already carried out in the source papers.

The MOND-like acceleration prediction is currently a rough analytic estimate in the phonon-dominated limit; no galaxy phonon solver for realistic baryon distributions exists per the card's required_code_resources.
The card states both the rotation-curve/RAR likelihood and the cosmological growth likelihood are unavailable and no likelihoods were run.

gaps.description: No linear perturbation solver exists for the unified two-state superfluid: the growth-rate difference from LCDM is the model's key cosmological signature, but no Boltzmann/fluid code implements the coupled two-state condensate perturbations with the Josephson/Rabi mixing potential and time-dependent sound speeds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-state superfluid as an effective dark-sector fluid in CLASS: evolve the background phase/occupation equations with the cosine interspecies potential, derive delta and theta equations with the EFT sound speeds c_s(a), and output H(z), CMB spectra, and f*sigma8(z).

gaps.description: No public galaxy-scale solver computes the superfluid condensate profile plus the phonon-mediated force for realistic baryon distributions, so the MOND-like radial acceleration relation prediction cannot be evaluated beyond the deep-phonon-limit analytic estimate, nor across the superfluid/normal-phase transition in clusters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a nonlinear Poisson-plus-phonon boundary-value solver (axisymmetric, taking SPARC-like baryonic mass models as input) that solves the P(X) phonon equation with baryon coupling alpha and the condensate density profile, outputting rotation curves and the RAR for given (m, Lambda, alpha).

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline connects the model's predictions to data: neither a SPARC/RAR rotation-curve likelihood for the phonon force parameters nor a background+growth likelihood (CMB/BAO/SNe distances plus f*sigma8) over (Delta E, M, Lambda_1, Lambda_2, state populations) has been assembled.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once gaps 1-2 provide forward models, wrap them in a Cobaya/MontePython sampler combining public Planck/BAO/SNe and f*sigma8 likelihoods with a SPARC rotation-curve chi-square, sampling the EFT parameters and initial state populations.

route_step_status.reason: The Mathieu-band growth rate and instability width are closed-form analytic results derived in the paper; null tool_or_code is not blocking for this pen-and-paper step.
The depleted mean-field (inverted-pendulum) evolution is an analytic/simple-ODE solution of the kinetic equations given in the paper, requiring no dedicated tool.

The energy-budget comparison to the photon background is analytic, but it depends on astrophysical population and radio-background assumptions for which only approximate estimates, not a survey-grade pipeline, exist.
The population-level recast for minicluster/burst signals has no tool, no clump-population model, and the card states external survey likelihoods are not supplied.

gaps.description: No survey-specific likelihood exists for the narrow photon line at E_gamma = m_a/2 from stimulated condensate decay, either against the late-time diffuse radio background or as a CMB-era spectral distortion from the recombination scenario; the card's diffuse-background constraint is only an approximate energy-budget estimate (recasting_needed yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast that maps (m_a, g_a_gamma, f_dm, converted fraction, line width) onto measured radio-background data (ARCADE-2-type absolute-temperature measurements and radio survey line sensitivities) and, for the recombination case, onto COBE/FIRAS-class spectral-distortion limits, including redshift and velocity broadening of the line.

gaps.description: No calibrated axion minicluster/axion-star population model (mass function, density profiles, and fraction of clumps satisfying the strong-resonance condition) is available to convert the per-clump burst estimate into predicted event rates and constraints.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Combine existing post-inflationary axion lattice/N-body simulation results for minicluster mass functions and internal densities with the paper's resonance condition (growth rate times clump light-crossing time) to construct a population model, then fold it through radio-transient survey sensitivities.

route_step_status.reason: The Galactic and extragalactic line-of-sight decay-flux integrals over an NFW profile are standard analytic formulas, but the step consumes dN/dE decay spectra at M_X = 1e7-1e11 GeV whose generation (hadronic/leptonic cascades with electroweak showering) is listed as a required code resource with no tool identified in the card.

Only an approximate chi-square over hand-selected IceCube flux points exists; the card states no IceCube likelihood or exposure model was rerun, and the best-fit mass shifts by orders of magnitude with the data selection.
The baryon-asymmetry estimate B_calculated(M_X, tau_X, epsilon) is a closed-form phenomenological relation from the primary source and is trivially analytic to evaluate.

gaps.description: No decay-spectrum generator is identified for the super-heavy regime: the neutrino dN/dE from X -> qq hadronization and leptonic cascades at M_X = 1e7-1e11 GeV requires fragmentation plus electroweak final-state showering far above the validity of standard PPPC4DMID-style tables, and the card lists a 'DM decay neutrino-spectrum generator' as a required but absent code resource.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Integrate a public super-heavy spectrum code such as HDMSpectra (DGLAP-evolved SM fragmentation up to the Planck scale) to produce dN/dE_nu for the paper's hadronic and leptonic channels, and feed it into the analytic Galactic-plus-extragalactic flux integrals.

gaps.description: No IceCube likelihood or exposure model is implemented: the constraint is an ad hoc chi-square over selected published flux points (sometimes including pink-band points), and the card documents that changing the selection moves the best-fit M_X between 1e7 and 1e11 GeV, so the mass/lifetime posterior is not robustly evaluable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a Poisson event-level likelihood from the public IceCube HESE 7.5-year data release (effective areas, energy-zenith response) for the summed Galactic plus extragalactic decay flux, marginalizing over an astrophysical power-law component, replacing the point-selection chi-square.

gaps.description: The baryogenesis sector has no microscopic decay model: the CP/baryon-violation parameter epsilon is a free phenomenological input with no Lagrangian-level derivation linking it to the same X decay operators that set the IceCube neutrino flux, so the joint neutrino-plus-baryogenesis explanation cannot be promoted beyond a consistency estimate or confronted with washout and sphaleron constraints.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify a minimal UV completion (e.g. B-violating X decay through heavy colored scalars with interfering tree and loop amplitudes), derive epsilon from its couplings, and solve the accompanying Boltzmann equations for washout so that the IceCube-fit (M_X, tau_X) and the Planck baryon density constrain one common parameter set.

route_step_status.reason: The Tsallis q-deformed phase-space distributions are closed-form analytic expressions derived in the paper, so this step needs no dedicated tool.

The freeze-out integration was done with a custom, unreleased integrator; standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, DarkSUSY) assume Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics and do not support q-deformed distributions with a relaxing q(x).

Public dwarf-spheroidal gamma-ray likelihood machinery exists for specified annihilation channels, but the framework defines no final states or spectra, so the recast cannot currently be executed (validity notes require a concrete final-state model).

gaps.description: No public freeze-out solver supports Tsallis q-deformed equilibrium distributions with a time-dependent q(x) relaxation in the Boltzmann collision term; the paper's custom integrator is unreleased and standard relic codes assume Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a lightweight single-species freeze-out integrator with the q-generalized distributions and collision term, parameterized by (q0, q(x) relaxation, m_chi, <sigma v>), validating against the paper's q0=1 canonical target (2.2-2.6e-26 cm^3/s) and the q0=1.05, 100 GeV benchmark near 3e-34 cm^3/s.

gaps.description: The framework specifies no concrete particle model (mediator, spin, annihilation final states), so no gamma-ray spectrum can be computed and the dwarf-spheroidal indirect-detection recast of the suppressed q0>1 cross-section targets cannot be performed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Embed the Tsallis freeze-out in benchmark simplified models (e.g. s-wave annihilation to b bbar and tau+ tau-), generate spectra with standard tabulations (PPPC4DMID or MadDM), and recast against the combined Fermi-LAT/MAGIC dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods used as context in the card.

route_step_status.reason: The reaction-rate density R(T) from the effective Z-prime-gluon and Z-prime-FIMP operators is an analytic tree-level calculation given in the paper and reproducible by hand below the EFT cutoff.

The card cites only custom coupled Boltzmann equations; public freeze-in tools such as micrOMEGAs assume radiation domination and do not implement non-instantaneous reheating with T_R and T_max, so the paper-level solver is private.
Converting the yield Y_X and m_X to Omega_X h^2 and comparing to the Planck 2018 value is a trivial analytic transform requiring no dedicated tool.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the GCS-operator reaction-rate density R(T) in a public freeze-in solver extended with an inflaton-dominated reheating phase parameterized by (T_R, T_max) — e.g. extend micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module or release a standalone coupled Boltzmann-fluid code — and validate against the published relic-density contours for the benchmark T_R and T_max.

gaps.description: No direct-detection or collider recast exists for the feebly coupled heavy Z-prime portal: the card records likelihood_available no/unknown for all constraints, and no detector-response or cross-section calculation for this benchmark was found, so the laboratory observable cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the nucleon-level scattering cross section from the effective Z-prime-gluon operator, then recast it through public direct-detection likelihood machinery (e.g. DDCalc/DirectDM against LZ and XENONnT releases) and map collider mono-jet limits onto the (m_X, m_Zprime, Lambda) plane.

route_step_status.reason: The production rate density from stress-energy-coupled massless and massive spin-2 exchange is a tree-level analytic calculation provided in the paper, valid across the light, resonant, and heavy mediator regimes below the EFT cutoff.

Only custom coupled Boltzmann equations are cited; no public freeze-in solver covers non-instantaneous reheating with T_R and T_max plus on-pole massive spin-2 production, so the paper-level implementation is private.
Mapping Y_X and m_X to Omega_X h^2 and comparing against the Planck 2018 abundance is a simple analytic transform needing no dedicated tool.

Scalar/Higgs-mediated spin-independent scattering is a standard calculation covered by public tools such as micrOMEGAs or DDCalc once the mixing parameters are specified.
A p-wave-suppressed halo annihilation flux estimate is a standard analytic computation with published halo parameters.

Public tools like CosmoTransitions can compute alpha, beta/H, and nucleation properties, but the card states the toy model's scalar potential is not specified, so the inputs to such a tool do not exist yet.
Forecast-level sound-wave/turbulence/collision GW spectrum formulas are published semi-analytic templates that map (alpha, beta/H, v_w, T_n) to Omega_GW(f).
Comparing Omega_GW(f) to LISA-like and other public sensitivity curves is a simple data transform with publicly available curves.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify a concrete renormalizable potential for phi (e.g. tree-level barrier or thermally driven), compute the finite-temperature effective potential and bounce action with CosmoTransitions to obtain (T_n, alpha, beta/H) and check wall-velocity consistency with the filtering benchmark v_w = 0.01, and derive sin theta and m_phi from the same potential.

Fuzzy-DM Lyman-alpha recast machinery exists for scalar ULDM (e.g. axionCAMB-style solvers and forest likelihoods), but no implementation covers this vector field's near-scale-invariant inflationary spectrum, and the card marks the step as not implemented.

gaps.description: No linear perturbation/transfer-function solver handles a massive vector (dark photon) dark matter field with the paper's inflationary near-scale-invariant transverse-mode initial spectrum; existing fuzzy-DM implementations (axionCAMB-type CLASS/CAMB modifications) treat scalar ULDM with misalignment initial conditions only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a CLASS/CAMB ultralight-DM module to evolve massive vector perturbations with the paper's I(phi)-produced mode spectrum as initial conditions, outputting the small-scale transfer suppression and an effective half-mode scale.

gaps.description: No model-specific likelihood recasts the Lyman-alpha forest and black-hole superradiance bounds for this vector spectrum; the paper only quotes external scalar fuzzy-DM bounds, so the low-mass exclusion boundary (m_A' near 1e-21 eV) is not quantitatively established for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the model transfer function from the extended Boltzmann solver into an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator, and recast published spin-1 superradiance rates (which differ from scalar rates) against black-hole spin measurements for the low-mass tail.

route_step_status.reason: The h -> A A partial width is a tree-level analytic formula given in the primary paper.

The stability criterion (m_A below the electron-pair threshold and lifetime exceeding the age of the Universe) is a simple analytic cut.
BR(h -> A A) and the tree-level Higgs-exchange nucleon cross section are analytic formulas from the quartic coupling.
The LHC invisible-Higgs branching-fraction limit is a published, directly applicable constraint on BR(h -> invisible).
Only an order-of-magnitude estimate of the loop-induced Majoron-photon coupling exists; the paper explicitly does not perform the full two-loop calculation.

gaps.description: No computed phase-space distribution f(q) exists for the Majoron produced by h -> A A freeze-in in this model, so its warm-dark-matter free-streaming imprint (transfer function, Lyman-alpha viability of the sub-MeV mass range) cannot be evaluated; the card lists all structure-formation entries as unknown.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Perform the two-loop calculation of the Majoron-photon coupling in the 3331 trinification field content (analogous to published two-loop Majoron electromagnetic-coupling calculations in seesaw models) and map tau(A -> gamma gamma) onto existing keV-MeV decaying-DM X-ray/gamma-ray line limits.

The plasma-mass formula is analytic, but it requires a cosmological dark-fermion abundance and phase-space model that the card leaves unspecified.

gaps.description: No public calculator produces the inelastic (keV-splitting, exothermic) dark-scalar-electron ionization spectrum in xenon for few-hundred-MeV to few-GeV dark matter with a light leptophilic scalar mediator; existing electron-recoil codes assume elastic scattering.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend QEdark or DarkELF xenon atomic response tables with down-scattering kinematics (energy deposit delta_m plus kinetic contribution) and a Maxwellian halo integral, validating against the paper's 1-5 keV spectrum with the roughly 2 keV peak.

gaps.description: No public relic-density implementation exists for the three-scalar model with nearly degenerate components, trilinear mediator couplings, and Z3 semi-annihilation, so the claimed simultaneous relic/CMB-safe solution cannot be recomputed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the full scalar potential and effective lepton Yukawas in micrOMEGAs (which supports Z3 semi-annihilation) and solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for both dark scalar components and the Z3 scalar, verifying the subdominant Z3 fraction below about 1e-3.

gaps.description: No machine-readable likelihoods exist for the route's statistical step: the XENON1T electron-recoil excess fit, the muon g-2 Gaussian target, and the Planck p_ann energy-injection bound with model-specific visible branching fraction are all unimplemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct a binned XENON1T ER likelihood from the published data release and background model, add a Gaussian Delta a_mu term with the current world average, and map annihilation channels through published deposition efficiencies f_eff to the Planck p_ann limit in one joint likelihood module.

route_step_status.reason: The axioelectric absorption rate for a keV ALP with coupling g_ae is a standard closed-form expression (photoelectric cross section rescaling) normalized by the ALP dark-matter fraction.
The two-photon lifetime and X-ray line flux follow from the standard analytic ALP decay-width formula once g_agamma including anomaly cancellation is specified.

The model-specific thermal production, reheating/diffusion, and entropy-dilution history that sets Omega_phi h^2 and the ALP momentum distribution exists only as paper-level estimates with no public code.

Public inflation pipelines (CLASS/CAMB plus Planck likelihoods, ASPIC-style potential modules) exist, but the two-sinusoid ALP-inflation potential with its constrained reheating history is not implemented in any of them.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann/thermal-history code computes the thermally produced ALP yield, its momentum distribution, and the required late entropy dilution for the anomaly-free ALP-inflaton scenario, so Omega_phi h^2 and the ALP fraction entering every other observable cannot be recomputed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the ALP-fermion scattering production rates, the inflaton condensate reheating/diffusion evolution, and a parameterized entropy-injection episode in a momentum-resolved Boltzmann solver (e.g. extending the machinery used for keV sterile-neutrino codes such as sterile-dm/LASAGNA-style solvers), outputting Omega_phi h^2 and f(p).

gaps.description: The warm-DM constraint on the keV thermal ALP is only an order-of-magnitude mapping to sterile-neutrino bounds; no Lyman-alpha or small-scale-structure likelihood exists for a mixed cold-plus-warm scenario with a subdominant (1-100 percent) thermal ALP fraction and its actual momentum distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute mixed CDM+thermal-ALP transfer functions in CLASS/CAMB from the gap_1 distribution function and confront them with a fractional-warm-DM Lyman-alpha likelihood or emulator (extending existing mixed cold-warm Lyman-alpha analyses to the diluted thermal ALP spectrum).

gaps.description: The ALP-inflation consistency claim (f_phi about 10^3 sqrt(m_phi M_P), n=3 potential) is not backed by an implemented CMB likelihood: the two-sinusoid potential and its reheating constraints are not coded into any inflation-fitting pipeline.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add the multi-natural ALP-inflation potential to an ASPIC-style slow-roll module or directly to CLASS/CAMB primordial-spectrum machinery, propagate the reheating efficiency epsilon, and fit n_s and r against the Planck likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: Binding energies and bound-state-existence thresholds (the parameter-above-0.84 criterion) follow from standard dark-QED Yukawa-potential formulas that are pen-and-paper or trivial numerics.

Semi-analytic dark-recombination (Saha/Peebles-style) treatments exist in the atomic-DM literature the card cites and were used by the paper, but there is no public code producing x_D for this massive-dark-photon model.

The paper performed the BSF-rate-to-Fermi-dwarf recast using improved numerical BSF cross sections and Pythia decay spectra, but neither the BSF calculator nor the supplementary limit grid is publicly released.

Modified Boltzmann codes for interacting dark sectors (ETHOS-type CLASS extensions and earlier atomic-DM CMB analyses) exist, but no maintained public implementation maps this model's massive-dark-photon atomic sector to DAO/CMB observables.

gaps.description: The improved numerical bound-state-formation cross sections for capture with emission of a massive (non-Coulombic) dark photon, and the resulting dark-photon decay spectra, exist only as the authors' private calculation; no public code reproduces the Fermi-LAT dwarf limit surface in the dark-photon mass/emitted-energy plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a BSF cross-section calculator for Yukawa-bound dark atoms with massive-mediator radiative capture, couple it to Pythia-generated dark-photon decay spectra and the public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihood, and validate against the paper's limit surface and bound-state-existence threshold.

gaps.description: No public dark-recombination solver computes the residual ionized fraction x_D for asymmetric atomic DM with a massive dark photon, even though the indirect signal scales quadratically with x_D.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code a Peebles-style effective three-level dark-recombination calculation generalized to massive-mediator binding energies and dark temperature ratio T_D/T_CMB, outputting x_D(z) as a reusable module validated against the atomic-DM literature results (arXiv:1209.5752).

gaps.description: No maintained Boltzmann-code implementation maps this model's dark protons, dark electrons, and massive dark photon to DAO features in the CMB and matter power spectrum, so the cosmological consistency of the residual ionization used for the indirect signal cannot be checked.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an ETHOS-style modified CLASS with the atomic-DM tight-coupling and dark-recombination physics (using the x_D history from gap_2), and run Planck plus matter-power likelihoods to bound B_D, T_D/T_CMB, and the DAO scale for this parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: The decayed fraction f = 1 - exp(-Gamma_X t_0) ~ Gamma_X t_0 and the resulting C abundance are trivial pen-and-paper expressions for rare decays.

Magnetic trapping and cooling of pico-charged C particles in the Galactic disk is handled only by rough Larmor-radius and cooling estimates with an assumed final velocity v_f=0.08c; no transport tool exists for this population.

No public XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood with detector response is implemented for the relativistic pico-charged scattering spectrum; the paper's f bound was not rerun and no likelihood file exists.

The 511 keV line and high-energy positron recast requires Galactic C-particle transport, annihilation morphology, and positron propagation for which no existing code applies to magnetically trapped pico-charged particles.

gaps.description: No simulation or transport code models the Galactic dynamics of pico-charged (q_C ~ 1e-11 e) relativistic particles: magnetic trapping in the disk, cooling to v_f, spatial distribution, and annihilation morphology, on which both the local C density at detectors and the 511 keV line prediction depend.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a propagation model for millicharged/pico-charged particles in Galactic magnetic-field models (e.g. adapting GALPROP-style diffusion machinery with Larmor-scale trapping and the paper's cooling channel on Y), outputting the steady-state C phase-space density near Earth and the annihilation rate map, validated against the v_f=0.08c and disk-retention benchmarks.

gaps.description: No XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood exists for the relativistic pico-charged C scattering spectrum, so the bound f < 1.5e-6 (and its sensitivity to the lowest energy bin) cannot be reproduced or updated with XENONnT data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the C-electron t-channel photon/dark-photon exchange recoil spectrum, fold it with the published XENON1T ER efficiency and background model to reconstruct a binned likelihood, and reproduce the f ~ 1.5e-6 (all bins) versus ~1e-5 (lowest bin excluded) bounds before extending to XENONnT.

gaps.description: No likelihood confronts the trapped C anti-C annihilation prediction with INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV line intensity and morphology data or with Voyager/in-flight-annihilation positron bounds; the paper's m_C < 12 MeV guidance is only a summary statement.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Combine the annihilation morphology from the gap_1 transport model with the INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV sky-map likelihood and published positron injection-energy constraints into a recast module over (m_C, q_C, f), recovering the m_C < 12 MeV positron-safety condition.

route_step_status.reason: Setting up the initial semi-thermal, underoccupied distribution f(p,t)=Z(t)exp[-p/T_dm(t)] is straightforward analytic work already done in the paper.

No public Boltzmann code (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, DarkSUSY) handles number-changing 2->k reactions in a chemically underoccupied, kinetically equilibrated hidden sector; the paper's treatment is semi-analytic and no tool_or_code is named.
The RFI-versus-cannibal-freeze-out check is an analytic rate comparison (no-cannibal criterion) evaluable by pen and paper once the yield evolution from s2 exists.

ETHOS-type modified CLASS/CAMB and SIDM halo analyses exist for related dark sectors, but no pipeline maps the RFI nonthermal distribution and self-interactions onto transfer functions and sigma/m, so recasting requires new work.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver integrates number-changing 2->k dark-sector reactions for a chemically underoccupied but kinetically equilibrated species, tracking the occupancy Z(t) and dark temperature T_dm(t) through the RFI phase and the subsequent cannibal-era check.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled (Z, T_dm) integrated Boltzmann equations with a parameterized 2->k collision term (rate coefficient plus exponent) as a standalone module or an extension of micrOMEGAs' hidden-sector freeze-in machinery, validated against the paper's semi-analytic yield-growth and no-cannibal criteria.

gaps.description: No transfer-function calculator maps the RFI final state (nonthermal f(p), evolving dark-to-SM temperature ratio, residual self-scattering) onto linear matter power, so the free-streaming and dark-acoustic-oscillation scales are only rough analytic estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an ETHOS-style modified CLASS to accept the RFI phase-space distribution and self-interaction rate from the s2 solver as input, computing P(k) with both free-streaming suppression and dark acoustic oscillations across the RFI parameter space.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists to confront RFI predictions with data: the relic constraint is only a target-density comparison (likelihood_available: no) and the Lyman-alpha/matter-power and SIDM halo constraints are flagged recast_required with no evaluated likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once gap_2 provides P(k), recast existing Lyman-alpha WDM/ETHOS emulator bounds onto the RFI suppression scale, and map the model's predicted sigma/m onto published SIDM dwarf-and-cluster constraint compilations for the example Majorana and scalar realizations.

route_step_status.reason: The freeze-in source functions for SM -> D Dbar / gamma-prime production are analytic formulas written in the paper and evaluable directly with micrOMEGAs-style thermodynamic tables.

The stiff two-temperature coupled Boltzmann system (Y_D, Y_gamma-prime, T_h/T) was solved with a custom unreleased code; micrOMEGAs' multi-sector machinery covers similar physics but would need model implementation and validation against the paper's benchmarks.
Comparing Omega_D h^2 to the observed value and checking that the dark-photon lifetime is shorter than the BBN epoch is simple analytic post-processing.
The Yukawa transfer cross section in the Born, classical, and resonant regimes has standard published analytic/parametric formulas that cover the model's MeV-mediator, GeV-fermion parameter space.

Dwarf-to-cluster sigma/m compilations exist, but no public simulation-calibrated likelihood is available (likelihood_available: no, recasting_needed: yes), so the fit relies on literature target ranges rather than a released pipeline.

gaps.description: No public released implementation of the coupled two-temperature Boltzmann system for this Stueckelberg U(1)_X hidden sector (equations y1-y3/y7: D and gamma-prime yields plus the hidden-to-visible temperature ratio with freeze-in sourcing and dark freeze-out); the paper used a custom stiff-equation solver.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model in micrOMEGAs' two-sector (hidden-sector temperature) freeze-in/freeze-out framework, or release a standalone stiff ODE solver for the (Y_D, Y_gamma_prime, T_h/T) system, validated against the paper's six benchmark relic densities and the allowed epsilon/m_gamma_prime band.

gaps.description: No public simulation-calibrated likelihood exists for the dwarf-to-cluster velocity-dependent sigma_T/m fit that selects the viable region; the DGC comparison is a literature target range (1.2-3.7 cm^2/g at low velocity) without a released statistical pipeline.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the model's sigma_T/m(v) curves through a published SIDM halo-inference framework (e.g. isothermal-Jeans or SIDM-simulation-calibrated rotation-curve/cluster likelihoods), packaging the dwarf, LSB, and cluster datasets into a reusable likelihood over (m_D, m_gamma_prime, g_X).

route_step_status.reason: The inelastic sterile-neutrino-electron cross section and dR/dE_R are given analytically in the paper, with loop functions evaluable via Package-X, so the step is reproducible pen-and-paper plus standard tools.

Only an approximate figure-level fit exists (likelihood_available: approximate); no public XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood with the exposure and background model is packaged for this model, so coupling bands must be extracted from paper plots.

The lifetime check is analytic, but the relic abundance requires an entropy-dilution factor or nonstandard expansion history that the paper leaves as an unsolved external input, so no complete calculator exists for Omega_N h^2.

gaps.description: No public likelihood implements the XENON1T low-energy electron-recoil fit for this model; the allowed (m_N, G_R^l) bands exist only as figures in the paper, blocking numerical recasting and updates with newer xenon (XENONnT/LZ) electron-recoil data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a binned chi-square likelihood from the released XENON1T SR1 electron-recoil spectrum and background model (and its XENONnT successor), convolving the model dR/dE_R with detector efficiency and resolution, validated against the paper's best-fit bands.

gaps.description: No calculator exists for the relic abundance of these keV right-handed sterile neutrinos: the thermal freeze-out estimate overproduces, and the required entropy-dilution or matter-dominated/kination history is not solved, so Omega_N h^2 and the diluted momentum distribution (needed for warm-DM free-streaming bounds) cannot be computed for a given (m_N, G_R).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a sterile-neutrino production code (e.g. the sterile-dm/DarkHistory-style Boltzmann treatments) with G_R-mediated decoupling plus a parameterized dilution sector (diluter mass/lifetime or kination onset), outputting Omega_N h^2 and f(p) after dilution for structure-formation recasts.

gaps.description: The radiative-decay channel is only checked against the age-of-the-Universe bound (tau_N > 4.4e17 s); no instrument-level x-ray line likelihood (XMM-Newton, Chandra, NuSTAR blank-sky) is recast onto the flavor-dependent couplings G_R^l, although such searches would be far stronger.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the model's N -> nu gamma rate (photon energy m_N/2) onto published sterile-neutrino x-ray line flux limits from XMM/Chandra/NuSTAR halo searches, converting sin^2(2theta)-style limits into bounds on G_R^l versus m_N.

route_step_status.reason: A CLASS-derived CanDM implementation with the T_ini shooting solver exists as author code, but no public repository is identified, so the capability is private.

The same unreleased CLASS patch computes CMB spectra and P(k); linear-theory capability is demonstrated in the paper but not publicly available, and nonlinear small-scale (Lyman-alpha) modeling is explicitly out of scope.
MontePython-3 with the Planck 2018 TT/TE/EE+lensing and BAO DR12/6dF/MGS likelihoods is public and was used in the paper; only the upstream CLASS patch limits reproduction.

gaps.description: The CLASS Einstein-Boltzmann implementation of CanDM (background w(a), c_s^2(a) with the 3-to-2 fluid closure and the T_ini shooting method) is author code with no identified public release, so no one else can compute CMB spectra or P(k) for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain and publish the authors' CLASS CanDM patch, or reimplement the paper's background and perturbation equations (fluid closure with negligible shear, n=0 and n=2 rate scalings) in current public CLASS, validating against the paper's benchmark spectra and LCDM limit.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha forest constraint pipeline exists for CanDM: the paper defers the recast, and existing forest likelihoods/emulators are calibrated on WDM-like thermal cutoffs, not the pressure-driven suppression shape from cannibal dynamics (the card flags the WDM mapping as misleading).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed CanDM linear P(k) suppression shapes into an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power framework (e.g. an area-criterion or emulator-based WDM-style analysis extended to general suppression shapes), running a small set of hydrodynamic simulations to validate the mapping for full and ten-percent CanDM fractions.

gaps.description: The S8 comparison uses only an approximate weak-lensing S8 baseline rather than a full cosmic-shear likelihood, so the claimed S8-tension relief and the 2-3 unit chi-square tradeoff are not evaluated against actual survey data vectors.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the MontePython analysis replacing the S8 proxy with a full public cosmic-shear likelihood (KiDS or DES Y3) using the CanDM P(k), including a nonlinear prescription checked against the model's scale-dependent suppression.

route_step_status.reason: The background energy flow from parent to massive daughter and dark radiation for given Gamma^-1 and epsilon is a simple analytic decay law, fully specified in the paper.

The warm-daughter viscous-fluid perturbation treatment is implemented in a modified CLASS by the authors, but no public repository is identified in the card, and the fluid approximation replaces the full momentum-dependent hierarchy.

MontePython-v3 with Planck/BAO/Pantheon likelihoods is public, but the weak-lensing input was an approximate split-normal KiDS S8 prior because the full KiDS likelihood was unavailable (likelihood_available: partial).

gaps.description: The modified CLASS implementation of the two-body DCDM -> WDM + DR perturbation equations (warm-daughter fluid hierarchy with the massive-neutrino-style viscous closure) is author code without an identified public release, so independent computation of the linear P(k) and S8 suppression is blocked.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain and publish the authors' CLASS DDM patch or reimplement the background plus warm-daughter fluid equations in current public CLASS, validating the fluid approximation against a full phase-space hierarchy run on benchmark (Gamma^-1, epsilon) points including the best fit near 56 Gyr, epsilon = 0.007.

gaps.description: The weak-lensing constraint was approximated by a split-normal S8 summary because the full KiDS-1000+BOSS+2dfLenS likelihood was unavailable, so the S8-tension preference (Delta chi^2 about 5.4) rests on a compressed statistic rather than the survey data vector.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the MCMC with the now-public KiDS-1000 (or DES Y3) cosmic-shear likelihood coupled to the DDM P(k), including a nonlinear prescription valid for the model's time-dependent suppression instead of the S8 prior.

gaps.description: No nonlinear structure-formation pipeline exists for this scenario: subhalo abundance, concentration, and dwarf-galaxy limits on daughter kick speeds (v_k of 3e-5 to 2e-3 c over lifetimes up to about 100 Gyr) are only mapped qualitatively from linear theory, with no simulation-calibrated likelihood (likelihood_available: no, recasting_needed: yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with two-body decay velocity kicks (extending existing decaying-DM simulation codes that inject v_k at rate Gamma) across the S8-favored region, calibrate a subhalo mass-function suppression model, and connect it to Milky Way satellite-count likelihoods with baryonic marginalization.

route_step_status.reason: Computing anomaly coefficients C_ag and C_a_gamma from the PQ charges and fermion spectrum is standard pen-and-paper anomaly algebra fully specified in the primary paper.
Mapping C_a_gamma/C_ag and f_a to g_a_gamma(m_a) uses the standard QCD-axion mass-coupling relations, a trivially analytic step despite the null tool_or_code.

Public compilations of digitized axion search limits exist (e.g. the AxionLimits-style databases), but the card notes the ADMX and stellar/cosmological curves were not digitized and likelihood_available is only partial, so the comparison is not yet wired up for this model.

gaps.description: The route to haloscope/helioscope comparisons stops at step s3 because no digitized g_a_gamma(m_a) exclusion curves or limit database are attached to the card; the ADMX 2.81-3.31 micro-eV curve and the review-level stellar/cosmological compilations exist in the literature but are not available as machine-readable assets for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Ingest a public digitized axion-limit compilation (AxionLimits-style g_a_gamma vs m_a curves for ADMX, IAXO, ABRACADABRA, MADMAX and stellar bounds) into the registry and implement a simple coupling-vs-limit comparison for the 3-3-1 anomaly-ratio benchmarks.

gaps.description: No misalignment relic-abundance calculation exists for this specific 3-3-1 axion, so the local axion dark-matter fraction entering haloscope power estimates is undetermined; the card explicitly flags that the relic-density calculation for the model was not performed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply the standard vacuum-misalignment relic formula with the QCD axion mass-temperature relation to the model's f_a ~ v_phi in the 10^9-10^12 GeV range, scanning the initial misalignment angle to derive the axion fraction that normalizes haloscope signal predictions.

route_step_status.reason: The reduced correlation function and PBH power spectrum follow from the analytic Poisson-seeded clustering formulae given in the primary paper, a pen-and-paper step despite the null tool_or_code.

The step names a class of cosmological N-body PBH clustering simulations to low redshift that the paper itself says are needed but that were not run, and no public dedicated PBH-clustering simulation suite is indicated by the card.
Both linked constraints have likelihood_available no and the card states no GW, microlensing, or CMB calculation was rerun; no clustering-aware recast likelihood exists for this step.

gaps.description: No cosmological N-body simulation suite follows the initially Poisson-distributed PBH population from matter-radiation equality to low redshift to validate the analytic clustering evolution xi(x,z), cluster occupancy, and the minimum core radius r_s, which the primary paper flags as required before firm conclusions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run direct-summation or tree N-body simulations (e.g. an adapted GADGET-class or NBODY6-class code with PBH discreteness noise in the initial conditions) for a grid of (M_PBH, f_PBH), evolving from equality to z~0, and calibrate xi(x,z), cluster mass functions, and r_s against the analytic model.

gaps.description: No binary-population code exists that computes PBH binary formation, hardening, disruption, and merger rates inside the evolving clustered environment; the card notes binary disruption is only modeled analytically, so the cluster-modified merger rate cannot be forward-modeled to LIGO/Virgo.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a PBH binary population-synthesis module that takes the simulated (or analytic) cluster population as input, evolves early- and late-Universe binary channels with three-body perturbations and cluster encounters, and outputs a merger-rate density R_PBH(z; M_PBH, f_PBH).

gaps.description: No clustering-aware likelihoods exist for recasting LIGO/Virgo merger-rate data, microlensing surveys, or CMB accretion limits onto (f_PBH, M_PBH); published homogeneous-PBH bounds are not valid once PBHs are significantly clustered, and both card constraints have likelihood_available no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing public assets — the LVK compact-binary rate posteriors, EROS/OGLE/Subaru-HSC microlensing likelihoods, and Planck PBH-accretion constraints — by inserting clustering-corrected line-of-sight densities and merger rates, packaging the result as a (f_PBH, M_PBH, xi) likelihood module.

route_step_status.reason: The analytic cooling and minimum-Jeans-mass scalings exist in the paper, but the card states they are order-of-magnitude only because dedicated simulations are needed to fix the numerical coefficients, and no cooling code is named.

Mapping (M_DC, M_DJ, f) to a DBH mass spectrum is a simple parameterized transform, but it rests on an assumed Population-III-like binary-formation scaling with no calibrated dark-sector population-synthesis tool behind it.

The primary analysis performed the Bayesian population inference on LIGO/Virgo data through 2019, but no reusable public likelihood was extracted and rebuilding it requires the catalog plus selection-function modeling adapted to the DBH mass spectrum.

gaps.description: No simulations exist of dark-atomic gas cooling, fragmentation, and direct collapse for this model's chemistry (heavy fermion x, light fermion c, alpha_D, molecular cooling gap), so the cooling curves and the numerical coefficient of the minimum dark Jeans mass — which set the DBH mass function — are only order-of-magnitude analytic estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamic collapse simulations with a dark-chemistry network (dark recombination, bremsstrahlung, atomic and H_D,2 molecular cooling, parameterized by m_x, m_c, alpha_D) to calibrate cooling functions and the minimum-Jeans-mass coefficient, analogous to Population-III star-formation simulations.

gaps.description: The dark black-hole binary formation rate and mass-pairing model is an uncalibrated Population-III-like scaling; there is no dark-sector binary population-synthesis capability, so predicted LIGO/Virgo event counts inherit an unquantified rate normalization.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt a binary population-synthesis framework to DBH progenitors, using the calibrated cooling/Jeans-mass outputs to set initial mass functions and binding fractions, and propagate rate uncertainties as nuisance parameters in the population model.

gaps.description: No reusable public likelihood exists for hierarchical inference of the DBH population parameters (f, M_min, slope) against the LIGO/Virgo compact-binary catalog including sub-solar-mass selection effects; the paper's Bayesian analysis was not released and the card records only partial likelihood availability.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the DBH mass-spectrum model in a public hierarchical GW population-inference code (gwpopulation-style) with LVK injection-campaign selection functions extended to the sub-solar regime, and release it as a reusable likelihood updated to current observing runs.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-solver implementation covers this model's dark-atomic linear cosmology (dark recombination and ionization history, dark acoustic oscillations for the x/c/dark-photon sector), so the large-scale-structure viability constraint on alpha_D, m_c, m_x is judged only qualitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with an atomic-dark-matter module (dark recombination via a rescaled RECFAST/HyRec treatment and ETHOS-like dark-photon tight coupling) to compute the linear power spectrum and delimit the CDM-like region of (alpha_D, m_c, m_x) parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: The homogeneous ULAP spectrum P_homo is computable with public AxionCAMB and the oscillon Poisson term P_osc is analytic, but the key input r_osc comes from the authors' unreleased lattice simulation code, so the step cannot be run independently across the potential family.

No public 21 cm forest minihalo-absorption likelihood or calculator exists; the card records only a forecast-level SKA-like sensitivity with likelihood_available no and states no real likelihood was fit.

gaps.description: No public 21 cm forest forward model and likelihood exists for this scenario: the pipeline from P(k) with an oscillon Poisson component to minihalo mass functions, absorption-line abundances, and a statistical comparison against (currently nonexistent) z~10 forest data is not implemented anywhere the card can point to, and the required high-redshift radio-loud background sources have not yet been observed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a 21 cm forest minihalo calculator (press-Schechter-style mass function from the modified P(k), minihalo optical-depth profiles as a function of T_IGM, line-abundance statistics) and wrap it as an SKA-era forecast likelihood, upgradable to a data likelihood once high-redshift radio-loud sources are detected.

gaps.description: The oscillon fraction r_osc, formation efficiency, and survival to z~10 are taken from the authors' unreleased lattice simulation code and were computed only for the p=-3/4 monodromy example, so the oscillon population inputs cannot be regenerated across the (m, F, p) parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run public 3+1D scalar-field lattice simulations (e.g. CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY-class codes) of oscillon formation and decay for a grid of monodromy-type potentials, and release fitted tables of r_osc, oscillon mass spectrum, and lifetime versus (m, F, p) for use in the power-spectrum step.

route_step_status.reason: The background continuity equations for rho_dm and rho_dr under the two-parameter conversion history are given analytically in the source and are trivially integrable by hand or in a few lines of code.

An official DMDR-CAMB Boltzmann patch implementing the modified perturbation hierarchy exists and was validated against the paper, but the card records it as available only on request via a Bitbucket link with author contact, not as an openly maintained public release.
The DES-Y1 3x2pt, Planck 2018, Pantheon, and BAO likelihoods are standard public assets runnable in CosmoSIS/Cobaya-style pipelines and cover exactly the data combinations the source used.

gaps.description: The only implementation of the DMDR background and perturbation equations, DMDR-CAMB, is on-request author code with unknown maintenance status, unspecified license, and no public validation suite, so independent registry evaluation of the CMB and matter-power route depends on emailing the authors.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain and archive the DMDR-CAMB patch or, more robustly, reimplement the two-parameter conversion source term Q and the sourced free-streaming dark-radiation hierarchy in current public CLASS or CAMB, validating against the paper's <0.037 combined converted-fraction bound and the S8 shift.

gaps.description: No nonlinear treatment of the DMDR matter power spectrum exists: the card records simulation_calibrated no and unknown halo-scale effects, so weak-lensing analyses must discard nonlinear scales (the source's linear-only DES scale cuts) and Lyman-alpha or thermal-SZ recasts of the conversion history cannot be performed.

gaps.description: The nonlinear response to the nonthermal hot sterile fraction is uncalibrated (halo and subhalo mass-function effects unknown, simulation_calibrated: no), and the route caveat notes that exact small-scale recasts such as Lyman-alpha are not possible; existing Lyman-alpha emulators are calibrated on thermal WDM or massive-neutrino histories, not this broader, higher-peaked f(q).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body/hydrodynamical simulations with the decay-produced f(q) as a fractional non-cold species over the preferred (m_eff, Delta N_eff) region to calibrate the nonlinear and Lyman-alpha flux response, or validate a mapping of the distribution's first moments onto existing massive-neutrino/WDM emulator grids.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled number-density plus temperature Boltzmann equations are defined in the source and a repository URL (github.com/dkaramit/BoltzmannEquation) is cited, but its contents are undescribed and standard freeze-in tools (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) do not evolve the temperature moment needed for semi-production.
Present-day annihilation and semi-annihilation rates follow from the tree-level matrix elements of the written renormalizable Lagrangian, which is straightforward analytic work.

Public CMB energy-injection and Fermi-LAT/MAGIC dwarf likelihood machinery exists, but the card's recast is only an illustrative shifted b-bbar limit because point-by-point photon spectra for the semi-annihilation final states are not generated.

gaps.description: No validated public solver exists for semi-production freeze-in: the mechanism requires coupled Boltzmann evolution of both the DM yield and a temperature-like second moment with an initial seed abundance Y_in, which standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) do not support, and the cited BoltzmannEquation repository is undocumented in the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Audit and document the cited dkaramit/BoltzmannEquation code against the paper's benchmark scans, or implement the coupled (n, T_DM) moment equations with Y_in as input in a DRAKE-style coupled-Boltzmann framework, validating that scan points reproduce Omega h^2 = 0.12.

gaps.description: Indirect-detection constraints are only an illustrative recast of shifted b-bbar limits: no pipeline generates the point-dependent photon spectra of the (semi-)annihilation final states through the Higgs-mixed light mediator and evaluates them against the Planck CMB energy-injection, Fermi-LAT/MAGIC dwarf, and CTA likelihoods.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate per-point photon spectra for mediator-cascade final states with Pythia/PPPC4DMID (via MadDM or a custom interface), compute f_eff for the Planck energy-injection bound, and evaluate the public Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihood and CTA projection instead of the shifted b-bbar curve.

gaps.description: The relic calculation closes the Boltzmann hierarchy with a thermal-shape ansatz at a separate dark-sector temperature; the full momentum-level distribution solution, which the authors explicitly leave to future work and which the semi-production rate depends on, has not been derived or implemented, and no resulting transfer function exists for structure-formation statements (all linear entries are unknown).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for f(p) of the Z3 scalar during semi-production (extending momentum-resolved freeze-in solvers), quantify the error of the moment ansatz on Omega h^2, and output f(p) so a CLASS non-cold-relic run can determine whether the model imprints any small-scale suppression.

route_step_status.reason: Fixing m_phi and y_phi from the relic-abundance and sigma_T/m_chi targets uses standard analytic thermal-relic and Born/Yukawa self-scattering formulas that are pen-and-paper (or trivially micrOMEGAs-checkable) for this benchmark.

Public TOV and tidal Love-number integrators exist, but the card notes the step requires reproducing the paper's specific effective chiral mean-field EoS with the dark Fermi gas and scalar-mediator terms, for which no public implementation is identified.

tool_or_code is null and the card states no GW/NICER likelihood or Higgs-portal direct-detection recast was run; no assembled pipeline maps the admixed-star observables and portal couplings onto GW170817/NICER posteriors and light-mediator search limits.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's mean-field chiral EoS with the g_phiNN-coupled dark Fermi-gas contribution as a CompOSE-style tabulated EoS module and couple it to an open TOV/Love-number integrator (e.g. the LALSuite or NSTOV-type solvers), validated against the paper's k_F^DM=0.01-0.06 GeV benchmark curves.

gaps.description: The in-star dark matter content is put in by hand as a constant density (rho_chi/rho_n = 1e-3) and constant Fermi momentum; no capture/accretion calculation predicts the dark matter profile inside the star for this feebly coupled scenario, which the card flags as a high-extrapolation-risk assumption.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the accreted/captured dark matter mass and radial profile from the model's sigma_chi-N cross section using standard neutron-star capture formalism (Goulding/Bell-type capture rates for light scalar mediators) and replace the constant-density ansatz with a two-fluid TOV profile.

route_step_status.reason: Z-prime partial widths to e+e-, nu nu, and N1 N1 are simple tree-level analytic formulas given in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code is not limiting.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a recast layer that maps (M_1, theta) onto published Chandra/NuSTAR line-flux limits and maps the freeze-in transfer function (once gap_1 is closed) onto existing Lyman-alpha WDM-style likelihoods or emulators via the standard m_WDM-equivalent matching.
