gaps.description: The nearly monochromatic mass function rests on the horizon-mass collapse approximation with delta_c = 0.45; no numerical simulations of the collapse of late-decaying false-vacuum patches exist to calibrate the threshold, the mass-to-horizon ratio, or the width of the mass function.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity or 1+1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics simulations of a false-vacuum Hubble patch decaying late into the surrounding radiation fluid, extracting the effective collapse threshold and extended mass function versus nucleation delay.

gaps.description: Neither the PBH-abundance constraints nor the stochastic GW predictions are connected to evaluable likelihoods: the card records only quoted LIGO-Virgo/NANOGrav context and no PTA, interferometer, or PBH-fraction likelihood is bundled.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the predicted Omega_GW(f) through public PTA free-spectrum posteriors (NANOGrav via PTArcade-style tools) and LVK isotropic stochastic-background likelihoods, and evaluate f_PBH(M) against the PBHbounds constraint compilation for the nearly monochromatic mass function.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs supports freeze-in from the visible bath, but no public solver tracks the coupled visible/hidden multi-temperature evolution this model requires, so the calculation currently relies on the source paper's bespoke formalism.

The velocity-dependent transfer cross section for light-mediator SIDM follows from standard analytic/partial-wave results (Tulin-Yu-type formulas), a well-established calculation despite the null tool_or_code.

Comparing Delta N_eff to the quoted BBN/CMB bound is simple once T_h/T is known, but the card records no direct-detection likelihood (likelihood_available: no) and no SIDM likelihood, so the recasting can only be done at the level of published exclusion curves and target bands.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver computes freeze-in production of the Dirac fermion D with coupled visible- and hidden-sector temperature evolution; the multi-temperature relic and T_h/T history are only available through the source paper's private formalism.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module (or write a standalone coupled-Boltzmann code) to evolve separate visible and hidden temperatures with kinetic-mixing energy transfer, outputting the freeze-in yield and T_h/T(z) for the (m_D, m_C, g_X, epsilon) parameter space.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood or recast exists for the sub-GeV hidden fermion with a light dark-photon mediator; XENON1T electron-recoil and PandaX-II light-mediator limits have not been mapped onto (epsilon, m_C, m_D) for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast XENON1T/XENONnT electron-recoil data with DarkELF/QEdark-style form factors and PandaX-II light-mediator nuclear-recoil limits into a likelihood over (m_D, m_C, epsilon), including the freeze-in relic fraction as the local-density normalization.

gaps.description: The dwarf-to-cluster SIDM constraint exists only as target cross-section bands from the literature (likelihood_available: no); there is no halo-level likelihood connecting sigma_T/m(v) predictions of this dark-photon model to rotation-curve and cluster data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood from published SIDM halo fits (e.g. the Kaplinghat-Tulin-Yu dwarf-to-cluster dataset) that accepts an arbitrary sigma_T/m(v) curve, so the model's velocity-dependent prediction can be scored rather than compared to bands by eye.

route_step_status.reason: The dark-photon decay width and lifetime follow from tree-level formulas in the two-sector mixing parameters, a pen-and-paper calculation fully specified by the paper's Lagrangian.

The relic density requires evolving two hidden-sector temperatures with kinetic and Stueckelberg mixing sources; no public code (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, etc.) implements this two-hidden-sector multi-temperature production, and no model-specific release is identified.

Given the temperature ratios, Delta N_eff is an analytic sum over hidden degrees of freedom, but only the source-level bound is used and no BBN/CMB likelihood evaluation is available for a precise limit.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver computes dark-photon production and relic density in a two-hidden-sector U(1)_X1 x U(1)_X2 setup with independently evolving temperatures T1 and T2 coupled through epsilon_1, epsilon_2, and Stueckelberg mixing; the calculation exists only in the source paper's formalism.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a coupled multi-sector temperature-evolution Boltzmann code (or extend micrOMEGAs' hidden-sector freeze-in machinery) that takes (m_gamma_prime, epsilon_1, epsilon_2, M3/M4, T1/T, T2/T) and returns Omega_gamma_prime h^2, T_i(z), and the lifetime check, validated against the paper's benchmarks.

gaps.description: The Delta N_eff constraint on the two hidden-sector temperatures is applied only as a quoted BBN/CMB/BAO bound; no likelihood pipeline propagates the model's redshift-dependent hidden radiation content through a CMB/BBN fit.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the solved T1(z), T2(z) histories onto a Delta N_eff(z) input for CLASS/CAMB and evaluate against the Planck+BAO likelihood (and PArthENoPE/PRIMAT for BBN), replacing the single-number bound with a proper posterior.

route_step_status.reason: The paper supplies the closed-form ratio R = Delta N_eff/Omega_chi h^2 ~ 0.11 g_*_dec^(1/3) keV/m_chi from integrated Boltzmann equations, so this step is simple analytic evaluation despite the null tool_or_code.

CLASS/CAMB can ingest an arbitrary non-cold-DM phase-space distribution f(p) and compute the transfer function, but the required unintegrated momentum distribution is not available (distribution_function_available: no), so the step cannot yet be executed for this model.

gaps.description: The unintegrated momentum distribution f(p) of chi from thermal two-body scalar decay is not derived; the paper only solves integrated number and energy Boltzmann equations, and the distribution depends on the unspecified spectrum (m_phi, m_psi), blocking any transfer-function computation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for freeze-in from thermal two-body decay (a known semi-analytic calculation for decay-produced FIMPs) to obtain f(q) as a function of m_phi/m_chi and g_*_dec, and package it as a CLASS ncdm psd input table.

gaps.description: Existing Lyman-alpha constraints are calibrated to thermal WDM (the card flags the thermal mapping as misleading) and no likelihood covers nonthermal freeze-in spectra with a free warm fraction f_warm in mixed cold-plus-warm scenarios.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply a transfer-function-level recast (area-criterion or a Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator such as those built on Sherwood/Nyx grids) extended to two-parameter (suppression scale, f_warm) mixed C+WDM shapes, validated against published mixed-DM Lyman-alpha analyses.

route_step_status.reason: Integrating out the heavier dark partner and writing the two-neutrino-exchange 1/r^5 potential is standard EFT matching given in the paper, a pen-and-paper step.

A phase-shift/shooting calculation exists in the paper (Born approximation invalid), but it is a private implementation; no public SIDM cross-section code handles the singular long-range r^-5 two-neutrino potential.

The comparison to SIDM bands and the Lyman-alpha elastic-scattering bound is paper-level only; the Lyman-alpha limit was derived for generic DM-neutrino scattering, not this EFT, and no likelihood is available.
Analytic Higgs/Z invisible-width formulas are supplied and the charged-lepton mode is handled with public FeynRules/MadGraph tooling.
The Delta N_eff mass floor is a primary-paper estimate; a full neutrino-decoupling recalculation with the MeV-scale dark states included has not been performed.

gaps.description: No public code computes the non-perturbative transfer cross section for the singular attractive/repulsive 1/r^5 two-neutrino-exchange potential; the paper's phase-shift/shooting solver is private, so sigma_T/m_DM cannot be reproduced or scanned by third parties.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a partial-wave solver for power-law long-range potentials (extending existing SIDM cross-section codes built for Yukawa potentials to regulated r^-5 profiles with the neutrino-mass IR cutoff), validated against the paper's Fig. 1 bands.

gaps.description: The collisional-damping cutoff and Lyman-alpha constraint are evaluated only by comparing to a generic DM-neutrino elastic-scattering bound; no Boltzmann-level computation or likelihood exists for this EFT's temperature-dependent DM-neutrino interaction and M_cut prediction.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the neutrino-portal scattering rate in a DM-neutrino-interacting modified CLASS (ETHOS-style nu-DM coupling), compute the linear power suppression, and score it against Lyman-alpha flux-power and Milky Way satellite-count likelihoods instead of the translated generic bound.

gaps.description: The Delta N_eff lower mass floor (~9 MeV) rests on an estimate; the full neutrino-decoupling calculation including MeV-scale dark states thermally coupled to neutrinos has not been done, which limits the precision of the CMB-S4 reach statement.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a neutrino-decoupling code (e.g. FortEPiaNO or NUDEC_B.C.) with the dark fermion/scalar pair coupled to the chosen neutrino flavor, recompute N_eff(m_DM, m_partner), and interface the result with Planck and CMB-S4 forecast likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: The nonstandard expansion history H(a) and the epochs a_dom, a_fz, a_rh follow from the paper's analytic cannibal-thermodynamics approximations, an executable pen-and-paper calculation.

The perturbation evolution through the ECDE was done with a custom hidden-sector solver that is not public; standard Boltzmann codes (CLASS/CAMB) do not include a cannibal fluid with number-changing pressure support.
Semi-analytic collapse machinery (Press-Schechter-type) exists for enhanced spectra, but the card states microhalo survival requires calibration that has not been done for ECDE-shaped power spectra.

An IGRB annihilation-boost recast methodology exists in related work (rel_2403_18893 for early matter domination), but it has not been applied to cannibal-modified spectra and applies only to annihilating DM, with the primary paper deferring the constraint analysis.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann code evolves perturbations through an early cannibal-dominated era: the cannibal fluid's 3-to-2-sustained pressure, sound speed after becoming nonrelativistic, and the model-dependent DM kinetic coupling/free streaming are all outside CLASS/CAMB, and the paper's solver is private.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the cannibal background and perturbation equations (cannibal fluid with time-dependent equation of state and sound speed, decay to SM radiation, optional DM-cannibal kinetic coupling) as a CLASS extension, validated against the paper's k_pk scaling at T_rh = 10 MeV and the CDM limit.

gaps.description: The mapping from the ECDE-enhanced transfer function to a present-day microhalo population is uncalibrated: no N-body simulations exist for cannibal-shaped peaked spectra, so microhalo mass function, concentrations, and tidal survival in the Galactic halo are unquantified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a suite of high-resolution N-body simulations seeded with ECDE transfer functions (peak plus Jeans cutoff) across the (k_pk, cutoff) plane to calibrate a semi-analytic microhalo mass-concentration model and survival fractions under tidal stripping.

gaps.description: No likelihood connects the boosted annihilation signal of ECDE microhalos to Fermi-LAT IGRB data for this model; the existing IGRB recast was built for early matter domination, not cannibal-modified spectra, and the primary paper explicitly leaves the constraint analysis to future work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt the early-matter-domination IGRB recast of rel_2403_18893 to cannibal-era boost factors: compute the annihilation boost from the calibrated microhalo model and evaluate it against the Fermi-LAT isotropic gamma-ray background likelihood over (annihilation cross section, k_pk, cutoff scale).

route_step_status.reason: The FB/B chemical-potential relation is a closed-form analytic formula from the paper, evaluable by hand under the second-order EWPT assumption.
Converting FB/B and the relic mass to Omega_FB/Omega_b is simple pen-and-paper arithmetic once m_FB is specified.

The recast to anomalous-isotope and direct-detection constraints needs a non-WIMP dark-atom terrestrial transport and nuclear-scattering calculation that no public tool provides and the card identifies none.

gaps.description: No public calculation of terrestrial transport, thermalization, and nuclear/atomic scattering of helium-bound fourth-generation dark atoms exists, so the abundance cannot be mapped to underground-detector and anomalous-isotope signatures; the card explicitly notes no accumulation or nuclear-scattering simulation was run.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop a dark-atom transport code: compute the helium-shell elastic cross sections for the charged heavy-hadron bound states, then propagate the local flux through the Earth's crust and detector overburden with a slow-down/thermalization Monte Carlo, following the O-helium/CHAMP transport formalism already in the stable-charged-relic literature, parameterized by relic charge, mass, and abundance.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for anomalous-helium isotope searches or dark-atom direct searches applicable to this model (all three card constraints have likelihood_available: no), so even a completed transport calculation cannot be turned into quantitative exclusions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published anomalous-helium/heavy-isotope search limits and package them as an abundance-versus-mass-and-charge exclusion likelihood module that consumes the terrestrial number density predicted by the transport calculation of gap_1.

route_step_status.reason: Deciding which scalar is boosted from the m2, m3 mass ordering is a simple analytic kinematic branching given in the paper.

Multi-component relic machinery exists publicly (micrOMEGAs two-component mode), but no model implementation of the Z4 two-scalar sector exists, so the coupled phi2/phi3 abundances and boosted flux cannot yet be computed with a named tool.

XENON1T electron-recoil response and efficiency information is public, but no packaged boosted-dark-matter electron-recoil recast pipeline or reusable likelihood exists for this model's light-Z-prime scattering.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a FeynRules/CalcHEP model file for the U(1)_N gauge sector with the Z4 charge assignments and run it through micrOMEGAs' two-component dark matter mode to solve the coupled Boltzmann equations, including the phi2 phi2 <-> phi3 phi3 conversion channels, over the small- and large-coupling regimes.

gaps.description: No public XENON1T-style electron-recoil likelihood or boosted-dark-matter detector-response module exists that maps the boosted scalar flux and light-Z-prime scattering cross section to a keV-scale electron recoil spectrum with detector efficiency for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a boosted-DM electron-recoil recast module: combine the free-electron/atomic ionization form factors from public DM-electron scattering tools (e.g. QEDark/DarkELF-style inputs) with the published XENON1T electron-recoil efficiency and background model, and expose it as a likelihood over (m2, m3, g_N, m_Zprime, boosted flux).

gaps.description: The beam-dump, neutrino-electron scattering, stellar-cooling, and SN1987A bounds on the light Z prime have not been recast for this model's specific U(1)_N charge assignments, so the shared-portal constraint con_z4_light_zprime_bounds cannot be applied quantitatively (likelihood_available: unknown, recasting_needed: yes).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the DarkCast recasting framework with the U(1)_N charge vector of this model to translate existing dark-photon beam-dump and low-energy limits into the (g_N, m_Zprime) plane, and add the stellar-cooling/SN1987A bounds from the light-mediator literature.

route_step_status.reason: The paper gives analytic freeze-out estimates, but an accurate F5/F6 relic split with the F5 F5 -> F6 F6 conversion channel needs a coupled two-component Boltzmann solve for which no model implementation in a public code exists.
The all-sky boosted F6 flux is a standard halo annihilation integral (J-factor times F5 annihilation rate) computable analytically with public halo-profile inputs.

XENON1T electron-recoil efficiency and background information is public, but no reusable boosted-DM electron-recoil recast pipeline or likelihood exists to map the F6 flux and sigma_e to a recoil spectrum.

gaps.description: No implementation of the Z6 dark-charge F5/F6 model (vectorlike fermions, phi7 mediator, Z prime) exists in any public relic code, so the coupled two-component freeze-out that fixes the cold F5 fraction and the depleted F6 fraction feeding the boosted signal cannot be computed beyond the paper's analytic estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the F5, F6, phi7, Z prime Lagrangian of the k=6 benchmark in FeynRules/CalcHEP and solve the coupled two-component Boltzmann equations in micrOMEGAs' multi-component mode, covering both the small-coupling boosted benchmark (m7 > m5 + m6, m5 > m6) and the large-coupling coexisting-WIMP regime.

gaps.description: No public XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood or machine-readable detector response is available to convert the boosted F6 flux and the g_N^4 m_e^2 / m_Zprime^4 scattering cross section into a fitted keV-scale recoil spectrum; the card notes the detector response is not provided in machine-readable form.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a boosted-DM electron-recoil likelihood module combining public atomic ionization form factors for xenon (QEDark/DarkELF-style) with the published XENON1T electron-recoil efficiency and background model, taking (m6, boosted velocity, sigma_e) as inputs.

gaps.description: The beam-dump, neutrino-electron scattering, stellar-cooling, and SN1987A bounds on the light Z prime have not been recast for the model's hyperdark charge assignment (1/3 + 2n), so con_z6_light_zprime_low_energy cannot be applied quantitatively and the OCR-degraded bound numbers in the card cannot be checked.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend DarkCast with the U(1)_N charge vector including the hyperdark charge parameter n to map existing dark-photon and light-mediator limits into the (g_N, m_Zprime, n) space, and overlay the stellar-cooling and SN1987A bounds from the light-vector literature.

route_step_status.reason: The Z2 FTH mass and coupling relations are analytic formulas given in the paper and evaluable by hand from (m_tau_prime, m_Aprime, hypercharge-breaking vev).

Standard WIMP freeze-out and scattering machinery (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) exists and the appendix gives analytic cross sections, but no public Z2 FTH model implementation exists and annihilation into twin bottoms/glueballs is outside the standard-tool final-state coverage.

Delta N_eff follows from a standard entropy-ratio calculation and the collider reach relies on quoted HL-LHC projections, but no implemented recast of charged-scalar searches or dark-radiation pipeline exists for this model.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the Z2 Fraternal Twin Higgs twin-tau sector (twin photon, twin Z, Y=2 scalars, Higgs-portal mixing) exists in a relic/scattering code, so Omega h^2, sigma_SI, and <sigma v> over the viable parameter space can only be reproduced from the paper's analytic appendix rather than computed systematically.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Z2 FTH Lagrangian (twin gauge sector, tau'_1/tau'_2 mixing, Y=2 scalars, Higgs portal) in FeynRules and run micrOMEGAs or MadDM for freeze-out and spin-independent scattering, validating against the appendix analytic cross sections and the paper's viable-region contours.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the twin-hadronization and twin-glueball spectrum for the fraternal twin QCD sector, compute the glueball Higgs-portal decay branching fractions, and shower the resulting SM final states with Pythia to produce gamma-ray and antiproton injection spectra as functions of (m_tau_prime, twin confinement scale, portal mixing).

gaps.description: No implemented collider recast exists for the visible Y=2 charged scalar decaying to leptons; the card relies on HL-LHC projection statements from the paper, so current LHC limits and future reach cannot be evaluated per parameter point.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate charged-scalar pair production and leptonic decays in MadGraph from the FeynRules model of gap_1 and recast existing multilepton/slepton-like LHC searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5, scanning the lepton-flavor coupling choices that control the branching fractions.

route_step_status.reason: The paper has its own SFDM-TF fluid perturbation treatment, but no public Boltzmann code (CLASS, CAMB, axionCAMB) implements the Thomas-Fermi-regime repulsive self-interacting scalar, so the solver is effectively private.
Extracting k_cut and M_cut from the transfer function uses the paper's analytic cutoff estimates, which are simple closed-form relations.

Standard Press-Schechter/Sheth-Tormen HMF machinery is public, but the SFDM-TF cutoff shape differs from WDM and FDM and the appropriate filter/barrier choice is only partially calibrated by simulations.
Constraints can only be applied through an approximate FDM-cutoff proxy; dedicated SFDM-TF Lyman-alpha and dwarf-core likelihoods are stated to be unavailable.

gaps.description: No public linear Boltzmann/fluid solver implements the Thomas-Fermi-regime self-interacting scalar-field perturbation equations, so the SFDM-TF transfer function as a function of (m, g, R_TF) cannot be reproduced outside the authors' private treatment; existing codes cover only quintessence-like scalars or non-self-interacting FDM (axionCAMB).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with an SFDM-TF fluid module: implement the equation-of-state evolution through the stiff-to-matter-like transition and the effective sound speed from the repulsive quartic self-interaction, validated against the paper's analytic cutoff estimates and published transfer functions.

gaps.description: No dedicated Lyman-alpha forest likelihood exists for the gradual SFDM-TF cutoff; current bounds are imported by matching to FDM transfer-function cutoffs, which the paper itself warns can overstate constraints on R_TF because the cutoff shapes differ.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamical Lyman-alpha simulations (or retrain an existing WDM/FDM flux-power emulator) on SFDM-TF initial power spectra parameterized by R_TF, and release the resulting flux-power likelihood so R_TF bounds no longer rely on the FDM proxy mapping.

gaps.description: No cosmological simulations of SFDM-TF structure formation exist to calibrate the halo mass function cutoff shape, the subhalo mass function, and the core-envelope profiles in realistic environments; existing results come from idealized isolated-collapse runs and the card leaves the full subhalo treatment to future work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological hydrodynamical-fluid simulations of SFDM-TF (Thomas-Fermi pressure added to a collisionless-Boltzmann or SPH solver, as in the paper's formalism) over a grid of R_TF from parsec to kiloparsec scales, calibrating the HMF filter/barrier, subhalo abundance, and core-envelope scaling used in steps s3 and s4.

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the 3x3 neutral Majorana mass matrix is simple pen-and-paper linear algebra fully specified by the paper's Lagrangian, so no tool is needed.

MicrOmegas covers thermal freeze-out with coannihilation for exactly this class of model, but the card identifies no public model implementation (associated_code unknown, required_code_resources lists a MicrOmegas model implementation as needed).

The Higgs-portal spin-independent cross section is a standard tree-level computation, but the card records no current direct-detection likelihood (likelihood_available unknown, recasting_needed yes), leaving only the paper-level XENON1T screening comparison.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the singlet-doublet Majorana plus Type-I-seesaw Lagrangian exists for micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP, so the relic-density scan with electroweak coannihilation and the sigma_SI computation cannot be reproduced or extended beyond the paper's private setup.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model in FeynRules (vector-like doublet, three RH neutrinos, Z2-odd sector) and export a CalcHEP model for micrOMEGAs, validating against the paper's Omega h^2 scatter plots and the absence of Z-mediated elastic scattering in the Majorana limit.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the micrOMEGAs sigma_SI output to DDCalc (which ships XENON1T, LZ, and XENONnT likelihoods) so the Higgs-portal recoil rate can be evaluated as a proper likelihood over (m_chi3, Delta M, theta, Y_1).

route_step_status.reason: The Fermi-ball mass/radius/number-density formula chain is analytic and given in the paper, but its inputs (T_*, beta/H_*, trapping fraction) rest on bubble-nucleation and trapping-efficiency estimates the card flags as sensitive and OCR-fragile, with no nucleation code named.

The stochastic GW spectrum uses the standard first-order phase-transition template formulas in (T_*, beta/H_*, alpha), a pen-and-paper computation with published SKA/THEIA/Ares sensitivity curves to compare against.

The point-lens event-rate calculation is standard semi-analytic work, but the card records no public Subaru-HSC M31 likelihood (likelihood_available no, recasting_needed yes) and extended-lens corrections for R_FB comparable to the Einstein radius are not implemented anywhere named by the card.
Converting an assumed T_f/T_SM and g_dark into Delta N_eff is a standard analytic entropy-counting formula requiring no tool.

Screening against the quoted Delta N_eff < 0.55 (CMB+BAO+BBN) and < 1 (BBN-only) limits is trivial, but the card notes a real likelihood requires the exact data combination, which is not packaged in the route.

gaps.description: No public event-rate likelihood exists for the Subaru-HSC M31 microlensing survey applicable to Fermi balls, including the survey detection-efficiency curves and finite-size (extended-lens) corrections needed when R_FB approaches the Einstein radius; the route can only screen against the paper's published exclusion curve.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a Poisson event-rate likelihood from the published Subaru-HSC seven-hour M31 dataset (8.7e7 stars, one candidate event) using the published cadence and efficiency functions, with the standard extended-lens magnification correction parameterized by R_FB/R_Einstein, and validate against the paper's compact-object exclusion curve.

gaps.description: The Fermi-ball population step depends on bubble nucleation dynamics and the fermion trapping/filtering efficiency at the bubble wall, which are taken as analytic estimates from a generic quartic thermal potential with no nucleation computation or simulation-calibrated trapping fraction backing the (T_*, beta/H_*, trapping) inputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the nucleation rate, T_*, and beta/H_* for the quartic thermal potential with CosmoTransitions, and calibrate the dark-fermion trapping fraction with 1D bubble-wall/fermion-reflection simulations of the kind used for filtered-dark-matter studies, replacing the order-of-magnitude trapping assumption.

route_step_status.reason: The GMSB mass spectrum and Higgs mass are computed with the named public code SOFTSUSY 4.1.10, which covers gauge-mediated boundary conditions for this benchmark.
The L H_u flat-direction slow-roll spectrum and perturbative reheating temperature follow from standard analytic supergravity slow-roll formulas written in the paper, a pen-and-paper computation.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the SU(5)-adjoint type-III messenger sector in SARAH and use the generated SPheno/FlavorKit code to compute BR(mu to e gamma) as a function of (M, Y_D, neutrino hierarchy), validating against the paper's quoted two-messenger window.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Evaluate the stau decay injection with an existing public BBN code (ACROPOLIS for late electromagnetic injection, cross-checked against the Kawasaki-Moroi-type charged-relic bounds including stau bound-state catalysis) over the benchmark (m_stau, tau_stau, m_3/2) region.

gaps.description: The card notes modern long-lived-particle collider limits were not recast: the heavy-stable-charged-particle exclusion for a 1 TeV stau with 10 s lifetime is quoted from an old CMS search, with no current LHC Run 2/3 recast or reusable likelihood attached.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast current ATLAS/CMS full-Run-2 heavy-stable-charged-particle searches for the benchmark stau mass and lifetime using SModelS long-lived-particle results or a CheckMATE implementation of the HSCP analyses.

route_step_status.reason: The perturbative reheating lower bound T_rh about 10^13.5 (M/1e13 GeV) GeV follows from the analytic messenger-decay formulas written in the paper, a pen-and-paper estimate adequate for this exclusion route.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a xenon likelihood framework (DDCalc or an XENONnT/LZ recast) with the dark-photon-propagator recoil spectrum from the primary paper's formula, summing the p-prime and pi-prime components with their asymmetry-fixed fractions at the 29.9 GeV benchmark.

route_step_status.reason: MadDM/micrOMEGAs handle freeze-out with coannihilation and the paper used MadDM with a FeynRules UFO model, but no public model implementation for the A_H plus vector-like-lepton simplified model is identified in the card.

Public recast frameworks (CheckMATE/MadAnalysis5) cover VLL pair production, but the compressed soft-lepton regime needs detector-level efficiencies the card flags as missing and only an approximate likelihood exists.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the SU(2)_X Lagrangian in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files to micrOMEGAs 5.x, and validate by recovering the published M_X = 0.5-2 TeV, g_X = 0.2-0.8 relic/g-2 band and the XENON1T small-mixing constraint.

gaps.description: No public CLASS implementation exists for the pseudo-WIMP late-decay history (S -> SIDM plus a small dark-radiation branch) with self-interacting daughter perturbations; the paper's modified CLASS/MontePython setup is not released, so the H0/S8 fit cannot be independently reproduced or extended.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the existing CLASS decaying-CDM (DCDM/DR) module to a two-branch decay with an SIDM daughter species and a tunable small dark-radiation fraction, publish the patch with a MontePython likelihood configuration, and validate against the source paper's reported regime-B/C posterior shifts.

gaps.description: The momentum distribution f(q) of the decay-produced SIDM component and its free-streaming or transfer-function imprint are not derived (distribution_function_available and free_streaming_length are unknown/null), so the linear perturbation treatment of the daughter species is incomplete.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-produced phase-space distribution from the two-body S -> SIDM kinematics as a function of tau_S and the symmetry-breaking parameter, and feed it into the CLASS extension of gap_1 as a non-cold daughter distribution (analogous to non-thermal WDM treatments of decay-produced dark matter).

gaps.description: No nonlinear halo modeling or simulation calibration exists for the two-component ultrastrong SIDM regime at tau_S > 10 Gyr (all nonlinear structure-formation fields are unknown), so galactic-scale predictions of this regime cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological N-body/hydro simulations with a two-component dark sector (residual pseudo-WIMP plus ultrastrong-SIDM daughter produced post-recombination), scanning tau_S and the self-interaction cross section, and calibrate halo density-profile and subhalo-population responses for comparison with galactic-scale data.

route_step_status.reason: EFT annihilation cross sections and DM-nucleon amplitudes from single contact operators are standard analytic matrix-element calculations, and the card confirms analytic formulas are available with FeynRules named for automated derivation.

MadDM and micrOMEGAs are adequate public relic-density calculators for a thermal WIMP EFT, but no paper-specific model files (FeynRules/UFO implementation of this operator basis) are released, so the step requires re-implementing the operators first.

The XENON1T and Fermi-LAT/H.E.S.S. comparisons are done against published limit and projection curves with likelihood_available marked no for all three constraints, so a fresh recast lacks the experiment-specific likelihoods the card says it requires.

gaps.description: No experiment likelihoods are wired into the route: the XENON1T spin-independent limits and Fermi-LAT/H.E.S.S. b bbar projections are used only as digitized curves (likelihood_available is no for con_xenon1t_si_wilson_limits, con_fermilat_hess_bbbar_projection, and con_relic_density_wilson_coefficients), so Wilson-coefficient constraints cannot be recomputed statistically, including the one-loop heavy-quark-to-nucleon matching that the card flags as model dependent.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the EFT predictions to the public XENON1T likelihood in DDCalc/GAMBIT (using DirectDM-style RG running and loop matching for the heavy-quark operators onto nuclear responses) and to the Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods (gamLike) for the b bbar/t tbar/gluon channels, replacing curve overlays with a proper joint likelihood.

gaps.description: No public model-specific implementation of the Majorana heavy-quark/gluon operator basis exists: the paper used MadDM, FeynRules, and micrOMEGAs but released no FeynRules/UFO model files, so the relic-density normalization of the Wilson coefficients cannot be reproduced without rebuilding the model from the Lagrangian.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the seven Majorana heavy-quark and gluon operators (scalar, pseudoscalar, axial-vector, twist-2, and gluonic structures) as a FeynRules model, export UFO files for MadDM/micrOMEGAs, and validate against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.1198 single-operator contours over 10 GeV to 2 TeV.

route_step_status.reason: The three-body decay widths are analytic and MG5_aMC (public) was used to sample the decays, but the MiniBooNE charged-meson flux parameterizations are listed as a custom requirement and no model files or flux pipeline are released.

The detector simulation exists only as the authors' private analysis; it requires MiniBooNE efficiencies and a visible-pair merging model that the card flags as analysis inputs with no public tool named.

The NA64/E141/BaBar recast is done against published limit curves under an assumed 50/50 branching, and the card states it is approximate unless experimental likelihoods (marked unavailable) are obtained.

gaps.description: No public MiniBooNE low-energy-excess likelihood exists for this signal: the chi-square fit to residual electronlike spectra depends on energy-dependent efficiencies, the 140 MeV E_vis threshold, and the <10-degree e+e- merging model, all of which are private analysis inputs, so the excess fit cannot be independently evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Package the MiniBooNE residual-event E_vis and angular histograms, efficiency tables, and pair-merging prescription into a public likelihood module (e.g. a GAMBIT/pyhf-style implementation) validated by reproducing the paper's benchmark chi-square fits.

gaps.description: No public end-to-end beam simulation covers charged-pion and charged-kaon three-body decays to a dark photon: the paper's MG5_aMC decay sampling and the MiniBooNE charged-meson flux parameterizations it feeds on are not released, so the dark-matter flux at the detector cannot be recomputed for new parameter points or facilities.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release the MG5_aMC model implementation of the pi/K three-body decays together with the focused charged-meson flux parameterization, or extend an existing public beam-dump dark-sector generator (BdNMC-style) to include charged-meson three-body production with the longitudinal-mode enhancement.

gaps.description: The visible/invisible dark-photon constraint recast (NA64, E141, BaBar) under the model's mixed 50/50 branching benchmark is only an approximate curve rescaling because the original experimental likelihoods are unavailable, so exclusion contours for non-benchmark branching fractions cannot be computed reliably.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public dark-photon recasting tool such as DarkCast to handle arbitrary visible/invisible branching splits of V1 (and the two-mediator V1/V2 case), using the published NA64 missing-energy and E141/BaBar visible-search yields to build branching-dependent limits.

route_step_status.reason: The baryon and dark asymmetry yields follow from the paper's analytic gravitational-genesis formulas (Hawking rates plus the curvature-current chemical potential), which are pen-and-paper computable without a dedicated tool.
The PBH relic fraction is a simple analytic bookkeeping step from the final relic mass and PBH number density under the stated relic-survival assumption.

NCDM Boltzmann machinery (CLASS/CAMB with an arbitrary phase-space distribution) exists, but the card states the evaporation-product distribution function is not available (distribution_function_available: no) and the step was not run, so the model-specific input is missing.

gaps.description: The phase-space distribution function of the particle component produced by PBH Hawking evaporation (including redshifting of momenta emitted over the evaporation history) has not been derived for this model, so the mixed cold-relic plus warm-particle NCDM transfer function cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the greybody Hawking emission spectrum for the dark particle as a function of PBH mass (e.g. with BlackHawk-style evaporation spectra), integrate over the evaporation history with cosmological redshifting to obtain f(q) today, and feed it to CLASS as a tabulated ncdm distribution alongside a cold PBH-relic fluid component.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha or small-scale-structure likelihood exists for this mixed cold (PBH relic) plus warm (evaporation-produced particle) dark matter scenario; the route explicitly lists the Lyman-alpha recast as unavailable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the computed mixed C+W transfer functions onto published Lyman-alpha WDM bounds using an area-criterion or half-mode matching for the warm fraction (following existing mixed cold+warm DM Lyman-alpha analyses), or run the transfer functions through a public Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator with a warm-fraction parameterization.

gaps.description: BBN/CMB energy-injection and PBH-evaporation constraint tables are not implemented in the pipeline; the route's likelihoods entry states BBN/CMB/PBH constraints are not implemented, so only abundance targets can currently be checked.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize and package published PBH evaporation constraints (BBN light-element yields and CMB energy-injection bounds as functions of M_PBH and evaporation time) into recast tables applied as cuts on the (M_PBH, M_f) scan, using existing PBH constraint compilations.

gaps.description: No detector response model exists for Planck-scale PBH relics: the card notes the relic interaction channel (neutral geometric versus charged) is unspecified, so the direct-detection observable cannot be forward-modeled at all.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify the relic interaction model (neutral geometric cross section versus charged relic), derive the corresponding terrestrial flux and energy-deposition signature, and recast onto existing macroscopic/charged-relic search limits such as those framed for charged Planck-scale relics in the cited related work.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the millicharge and gauge-boson masses from Stueckelberg mass mixing is straightforward analytic diagonalization given in the paper's Lagrangian; no tool is needed.

The paper numerically evolves the coupled thermal-history ODEs, but this is a private in-paper integration; no public code implements late Z1 decay injection of millicharged daughters with v^-4 baryon-DM scattering.

The T_b-to-T21 conversion formula is simple, but a realistic spin-temperature/Lyman-alpha coupling model at cosmic dawn requires an astrophysics code (21cmFAST/ARES-class) that is not linked to this pipeline.
The CMB/XQC/DMDD/collider exclusion curves were not digitized and no recast tool or constraint database is attached; the route lists these recasts as unavailable.

gaps.description: No public thermal-history solver evolves a two-component dark sector with late Z1 -> chi chi decay after recombination sourcing a millicharged daughter population that cools baryons through v^-4 Coulomb-like scattering; the paper's ODE integration is private.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing public DM-baryon temperature-evolution code (the Munoz-type millicharged 21cm cooling codes or CLASS with the dmeff/interacting-DM module) with a decay source term for n_chi(z) set by tau_Z1 and the Z1-2chi splitting, evolving T_b, T_chi, and the relative bulk velocity self-consistently.

gaps.description: No 21 cm global-signal likelihood is attached: the EDGES absorption-depth target is used only as a benchmark, with no foreground-marginalized likelihood and no incorporation of the SARAS 3 non-detection.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a global 21 cm likelihood combining the EDGES flattened-Gaussian absorption measurement with SARAS 3 constraints, marginalizing over astrophysical spin-temperature coupling parameters using an ARES or 21cmFAST-based global-signal emulator.

gaps.description: The millicharged-particle constraint database required by the route does not exist in the pipeline: XQC, underground direct-detection, SN1987A, SLAC, CMS, MiniBooNE, LSND, ArgoNeuT, and milliQan exclusion curves compiled by the paper were not digitized, and the lifetime-dependent abundance rescaling (f_chi(z) from tau_Z1) needed to apply them is not implemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published millicharged-particle exclusion curves in the (m_chi, epsilon) plane into a constraint table (or adapt an existing millicharged-limit compilation) and add an abundance-rescaling layer that maps each bound to the time-dependent fraction f_chi(z) implied by tau_Z1.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs 5.1 is a named public Boltzmann solver that covers thermal freeze-out for this pseudoscalar-mediated WIMP, with only a stated 10% leading-order theory allowance.
Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal b bbar limits and their public tabulated likelihoods exist and directly cover the b bbar-dominated annihilation regime used in the paper.

MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and Pythia 8 are public and adequate, but the card states the FeynRules/UFO implementation of the two-pseudoscalar model (with loop-induced gluon/photon couplings) is not confirmed public, so the step cannot be reproduced without rebuilding the model files.
Delphes and MadAnalysis 5 with public Run-2 recast analysis cards are named public tools covering the missing-energy signal regions used.

gaps.description: No public UFO/FeynRules (and matching micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP) implementation of the two-mixed-pseudoscalar model, including the NLOCT/MoGRe loop-induced P_i F Fdual and P_i G Gdual couplings and Higgs-pseudoscalar trilinears, is identified, so the relic and collider chains cannot be independently rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the mass-basis Lagrangian in FeynRules, generate loop-induced couplings with NLOCT/MoGRe, export UFO and CalcHEP model files, validate against the paper's benchmark relic-density and cross-section values, and publish the model files in a public repository.

route_step_status.reason: The effective coannihilation cross section and relic-target lambda_22 follow from standard analytic coannihilation freeze-out formulas (and are also within reach of micrOMEGAs/MadDM given model files), as done in the paper.
The s2 -> s1 f f width through an off-shell Higgs is an analytic three-body phase-space calculation given in the paper, requiring only routine numerical integration near heavy-fermion thresholds.

The MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes-style chain is public, but the step was not run, no public UFO model implementation is identified, and displaced-vertex acceptances for this signature have no attached recast.

gaps.description: No public UFO/FeynRules implementation of the pure-scalar inelastic coannihilation model (s1, s2, lambda_22 and lambda_12 Higgs-portal operators) is identified, so collider event generation and cross-checked relic calculations cannot be rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-scalar Higgs-portal Lagrangian in FeynRules, export UFO and CalcHEP files, validate the s2 lifetime against the paper's O(10 cm) benchmark and the relic lambda_22 bands with micrOMEGAs/MadDM, and publish the model files.

gaps.description: No public displaced-vertex likelihood or recast exists for the s2 long-lived-particle signature: the route carries only the paper's HL-LHC projection with no attached likelihood, and detector acceptances were not rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing ATLAS/CMS Run-2 displaced-vertex plus missing-energy searches for this topology using the LLP modules of MadAnalysis 5 or CheckMATE, and encode the HL-LHC 3 ab^-1 projection as an efficiency map over (m2, c tau_s2, production cross section).

gaps.description: A dedicated inelastic nuclear-recoil calculation (s1 + nucleus -> s2 upscattering with the Delta threshold) was not performed, so direct-detection evasion is encoded only qualitatively and cannot be checked quantitatively against XENON1T/PandaX data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the inelastic Higgs-portal scattering rate with the kinematic threshold v_min(Delta) and halo-velocity integration, implementing it in an existing rate code such as WimPyDD or DDCalc modified for inelastic kinematics, and compare with XENON1T/PandaX exclusion data.

route_step_status.reason: The relic-compatible lambda_22 is the same analytic partner-annihilation freeze-out target as the pure-scalar case, computed analytically in the paper with MadDM cross-checks noted in associated_code.
The s2 -> s1 f f width through A prime/Z mixing is an analytic calculation that the paper validates against MadGraph phase-space integration, so the capability exists at the needed level.

Public dark-photon recast machinery covers the dilepton/EWPT part in principle, but no recast was performed, no tool is attached, and the displaced inelastic-DM reach needs model-specific simulation of experiment acceptances.

gaps.description: No public UFO/FeynRules implementation of the scalar-vector inelastic model (s1, s2, dark photon A prime with kinetic mixing and the dark-current coupling) is identified, so event generation for A prime-mediated s1 s2 production and lifetime cross-checks cannot be rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the U(1)_D Lagrangian with Stueckelberg/kinetic mixing and the s1-s2 dark current in FeynRules, export UFO files, validate against the paper's m_Aprime = 3 m2 benchmark decay lengths, and publish the model files.

gaps.description: No implemented recast pipeline exists for the displaced inelastic-DM searches (HL-LHC displaced vertices, FASER forward decays, STCF-style low-mass searches); the route attaches no public likelihood and only qualitative reach statements from related work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Simulate A prime-mediated s1 s2 production with MadGraph+Pythia and build acceptance maps for displaced decays: use FORESEE for the FASER forward geometry and MadAnalysis 5/CheckMATE LLP modules for central displaced-vertex searches, packaged as an efficiency grid over (m2, Delta, epsilon, g_D, c tau_s2).

gaps.description: The dark-photon dilepton-resonance and electroweak-precision constraints have not been recast for this model, whose A prime branching fractions differ from the minimal dark photon because of the invisible/inelastic s1 s2 channel.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply a Darkcast-style rescaling of published dilepton-resonance and EWPT limits in the (m_Aprime, epsilon) plane using the model-specific A prime branching fractions including the s1 s2 mode, and store the result as a constraint table for the scan.

route_step_status.reason: The primary paper provides analytic evolution estimates, but a quantitative relic prediction needs a coupled ALP field-equation integrator through the EWPT background that the card lists as a required-but-absent custom code.
Spontaneous-baryogenesis chemical-potential formulae with the ALP velocity biasing electroweak sphalerons are standard analytic expressions given in the paper and computable by hand.

The hidden-sector sphaleron friction is treated phenomenologically with no derivation of the friction coefficient from a specified hidden gauge sector and no tool implementing the damped pre-EWPT attractor evolution.

gaps.description: No public code integrates the ALP equation of motion with the Higgs-dependent potential, the EWPT-induced minimum shift, and hidden-gauge thermal friction through the electroweak epoch, so the secondary-oscillation relic abundance and baryon asymmetry cannot be computed beyond the paper's analytic estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a dedicated ODE integrator for phi(T) coupled to the SM electroweak crossover background (using standard SM equation-of-state tables for g_*(T) and the lattice Higgs-VEV profile v(T)), with the hidden friction entering as a Gamma(T) phi-dot damping term, and validate it against the paper's quoted 0.01-30 eV viable mass window.

gaps.description: The hidden-sector sphaleron friction coefficient is never derived from a concrete hidden non-Abelian gauge sector (coupling, temperature ratio, confinement scale), leaving the pre-EWPT attractor and hence the relic normalization as an unspecified phenomenological input.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive Gamma_friction(T) from the hidden SU(N) sphaleron rate (Gamma_sph ~ alpha_hidden^5 T_hidden^4 scaled by the anomaly coupling 1/f^2) for a benchmark hidden sector including its thermal history and decay back to the SM, and publish it as a parameterized module usable by the evolution integrator of gap_1.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for the photophobic-longevity and electron-EDM consistency constraint: the card records likelihood_available=no and only qualitative excluded regions in (m_phi, f, ALP-photon coupling, ALP-Higgs mixing).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast published ALP-photon astrophysical bounds (AxionLimits compilations) and the ACME/JILA electron-EDM limits into a joint likelihood over (m_phi, f, theta_mix, anomaly charges), evaluated for the photophobic UV charge assignments the paper sketches.

route_step_status.reason: The Higgs-VEV/electron-mass history follows from the paper's analytic axi-Higgs equations with the oscillation-averaged axion treatment, a pen-and-paper mapping also encoded in aHCAMB.
The publicly released author code aHCAMB (modified CAMB) implements the m_e(t)-modified recombination and produces CMB spectra for the axi-Higgs parameters.
aHCAMB supports m_a and Omega_a in the ultralight-axion effective-fluid approximation, covering background and perturbation evolution for this route.
Planck, BAO, cosmic-shear, supernova, and SH0ES likelihoods are public in standard samplers (Cobaya/MontePython/CosmoMC) and can be driven by the aHCAMB Boltzmann outputs.
Mapping v(t)/v0 to Delta m_e/m_e is a trivial analytic relation given directly by the model equations.

Published atomic-clock drift and quasar absorption limits on varying constants exist, but the card records no quantitative likelihood for this model's specific v(t) relaxation history, so only order-of-magnitude comparison is currently possible.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists that confronts the axi-Higgs late-time Higgs-VEV relaxation history v(t)/v0, parameterized by (m_a, C, initial displacement), with atomic-clock frequency-ratio drift limits and quasar absorption-line constraints on electron-mass variation; the primary paper flags this channel as future testability without extracting any quantitative bound.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compile published clock frequency-ratio drift limits (e.g. Yb/Cs, Al+/Hg+) and quasar mu = m_p/m_e variation measurements into a redshift-binned likelihood on Delta m_e/m_e(z), and evaluate it on the oscillating-plus-relaxing v(t) trajectory output by the axi-Higgs background solver.

route_step_status.reason: The averaged tangential velocity field of parallel quantized point vortices with a Gaussian radial distribution is a closed-form analytic template given in the paper.

The authors ran an emcee MCMC fit, but no public analysis code exists and the card notes the filament-spin data covariance and selection effects were not reconstructed, so the likelihood is only partially reusable.
The healing-length/vortex-core radius estimate is a simple analytic formula in (m, g, density) given in the paper and its BEC-vortex references.
The packing bound N_V r_V^2 < R^2 and minimum-angular-momentum checks are pen-and-paper consistency inequalities, explicitly evaluated for the benchmark in the paper.
Public ultralight-axion Boltzmann solvers (axionCAMB, and CLASS-based ULA codes) compute the fuzzy-DM transfer function and matter power spectrum for a given mass and dark matter fraction.

Lyman-alpha and halo-abundance bounds on ultralight masses exist in the literature, but the card records only an approximate likelihood and no ready recast for the subcomponent/self-interacting regime this model allows.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for the cosmic-filament spin measurement used to fit (N_V/m, R): the observational spin proxy, filament selection function, and data covariance are not packaged, so the paper's MCMC constraint cannot be reproduced or reused by others.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a public likelihood from the filament-spin catalog of the source measurement (the 2106.05989 stacked line-of-sight velocity-difference analysis), including the filament selection function and an estimated covariance, exposing the vortex velocity template parameters (N_V/m, R) and nuisance parameters for orientation and stacking systematics.

gaps.description: The parallel, singly quantized, filament-aligned vortex configuration is a fitting ansatz with no simulation support: no Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson simulation of cosmic filaments has established whether vortices of the required number (~3000 for m=1e-22 eV), alignment, and survival actually form, which the paper itself flags as needing simulations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson (Schroedinger-Poisson with optional self-interaction g) simulations of filament formation in a cosmological setting, e.g. by extending AxioNyx or PyUltraLight-class solvers to filament-scale boxes, and measure vortex number density, alignment with the filament axis, and lifetime to calibrate or replace the Gaussian parallel-vortex template.

gaps.description: No dedicated recast likelihood links the ultralight mass m implied by any chosen interpretation of the N_V/m fit to Lyman-alpha and halo/subhalo structure bounds, particularly in the subcomponent or self-interacting-condensate regimes where published all-DM fuzzy bounds do not directly apply.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints (using public WDM/FDM emulators or the axionCAMB transfer functions mapped through a calibrated flux-power emulator) and Milky Way satellite/subhalo likelihoods into a joint likelihood over (m, dark matter fraction, g), covering the mixed cold-plus-ultralight case.

route_step_status.reason: The paper implements the finite-temperature effective potential in CosmoTransitions (with BubbleProfiler), a public tool that covers this renormalizable singlet potential.
Higgs-portal complex-singlet thermal freeze-out is standard and fully covered by public relic codes such as micrOMEGAs or MadDM, even though the card's tool_or_code field is null.
The GW spectrum uses the standard bubble-collision/sound-wave/turbulence fit formulae in (alpha, beta/H_*, T_n, v_w), which are simple analytic expressions with public implementations such as PTPlot.
The paper implements the triplet finite-temperature effective potential in CosmoTransitions (with BubbleProfiler), a public tool adequate for this renormalizable potential.

Public codes (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) compute triplet freeze-out with T+/-T0 coannihilation at tree level, but the near-TeV electroweak-multiplet regime that sets the ~1176 GeV full-relic mass requires Sommerfeld/bound-state corrections those default tools do not include.
The GW spectrum follows from the standard phase-transition fit formulae in (alpha, beta/H_*, T_n, v_w), simple analytic expressions with public implementations such as PTPlot.

gaps.description: No public relic-density tool includes the Sommerfeld enhancement and bound-state effects of SU(2)L gauge interactions for the Y=0 scalar triplet near the TeV scale, so the full-relic mass quoted as ~1176 GeV (and hence the quantitative severity of the relic/phase-transition tension) carries an uncontrolled O(10%) uncertainty from tree-level-only freeze-out codes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or interface a dedicated electroweak-multiplet code following the wino/minimal-dark-matter Sommerfeld literature) with the SU(2)L Sommerfeld factors and coannihilation network for the scalar triplet, and recompute the full-relic mass and the underabundance factor across the FOPT-compatible m_T < ~320 GeV region.

route_step_status.reason: No public sterile-neutrino production code covers B-L-vector NSI-modified interaction rates and thermal potentials with nonstandard pre-BBN expansion histories; existing quantum-kinetic codes (e.g. sterile-dm) implement only standard Dodelson-Widrow/Shi-Fuller production in a standard cosmology, and the card names no tool.

X-ray decay envelopes and the Tremaine-Gunn bound can be applied approximately (likelihood_available partial), but no packaged likelihood exists and the Lyman-alpha constraint requires a transfer-function recast the card explicitly defers (likelihood_available no).

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann/quantum-kinetic solver computes sterile-neutrino production including B-L-vector-mediator-induced neutrino interaction rates and thermal potentials together with parameterized nonstandard pre-BBN expansion histories H(T); the paper's solver is private.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled phi_a/phi_d field equations with kinetic angular-momentum terms as a dedicated background-plus-linear-perturbation code (a standalone stiff ODE solver coupled to a modified CLASS/axionCAMB fluid treatment, analogous to existing ultralight-axion solvers), validate against the paper's adiabatic limit, and output the effective equation of state and transfer function across the quoted mass range.

gaps.description: The normalization of the long-range spin-dependent force is not derived: the induced NG-mode coupling to Standard Model fermions (through the phi_a^2 H_u H_d portal and phi_d-phi_a mixing) has no quantitative expression, so the predicted force cannot be mapped onto laboratory spin-force exclusion curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the effective NG-fermion coupling and force range as functions of f_a and the angular-momentum constants, then recast onto existing monopole-dipole and dipole-dipole force-search compilations (torsion-balance, comagnetometer, and ARIADNE-class limits).

route_step_status.reason: Two-form mode growth has analytic solutions in the paper, but evaluating the sourced curvature spectrum requires numerically integrating mode functions and convolution integrals for which no public inflationary two-form solver exists.

The Press-Schechter/compaction abundance calculation is standard semi-analytic machinery, but it is applied with a Gaussian peak template although the sourced perturbations are intrinsically non-Gaussian and the abundance is exponentially tail-sensitive.

Scalar-induced GW kernels for a given curvature spectrum are publicly implementable (e.g. SIGWfast-class codes), but the paper's reducible and planar two-form source diagrams are a bespoke private calculation.

gaps.description: No public pipeline maps the inflaton-dependent two-form kinetic function I(phi) to the sourced small-scale curvature spectrum and the associated Omega_GW(k): the mode-function integration on the Starobinsky background, the source convolution integrals, and the two-form-specific GW diagrams exist only as the paper's private calculation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement and release a numerical solver for two-form mode growth under I(phi)^2 H^2 coupling with the sourced curvature and tensor convolution integrals (extending an existing inflationary perturbation code or SIGWfast-style induced-GW framework), validated by recovering the A about 3.2e-4, f_PBH=1 benchmark and the paper's Omega_GW peaks.

gaps.description: The PBH abundance is computed with a Gaussian Press-Schechter/compaction template although curvature perturbations sourced quadratically by two-form fields obey chi-squared-like non-Gaussian statistics to which the exponentially tail-sensitive f_PBH is uncontrolled; type-II perturbations are also neglected.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the full non-Gaussian probability distribution of the compaction function for the two-form-sourced perturbations and redo the threshold-collapse abundance (including type-II perturbations), calibrating the collapse threshold against existing numerical-relativity results for peaked spectra.

route_step_status.reason: ScannerS is public, implements the CxSM natively, and applies the theoretical plus HiggsSignals/HiggsBounds validity checks used by the paper.
micrOMEGAs, interfaced through ScannerS, is the public standard tool for the thermal freeze-out relic density of this Higgs-portal scalar.

FeynRules/FeynArts/FeynCalc/LoopTools/SARAH are public, but the model-specific one-loop electroweak h_i -> AA calculation with its counterterm and renormalization-scheme setup is a paper-specific implementation not stated to be released.
Comparing BR(h125 -> AA) against the published LHC invisible-branching-ratio bound is a trivial recast, and HiggsBounds/HiggsTools include invisible-width constraints.

The tree-level cross section is velocity suppressed, so direct detection requires the one-loop sigma_SI, which exists as a literature calculation but has no public code; micrOMEGAs gives only the (vanishing) tree-level rate.

gaps.description: The one-loop electroweak correction to the h125 -> AA invisible width (few-percent effect, needed as LHC invisible-width precision improves) exists only as the authors' private FeynArts/FeynCalc/LoopTools implementation with model-specific counterterms and renormalization schemes; no released code reproduces the NLO widths.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release the CxSM NLO invisible-width calculation as a public package (e.g. integrate it into the ewN-style NLO tools built on the same FeynArts/FeynCalc/LoopTools chain, or publish the model files and counterterm definitions), validated by reproducing the paper's few-percent correction factors in scenarios I and II.

gaps.description: No public calculator gives the one-loop spin-independent DM-nucleon cross section for the CxSM pseudoscalar: the tree-level rate is velocity suppressed to irrelevance, so the direct-detection observable cannot be evaluated with standard tools, which stop at tree level.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the published one-loop CxSM pseudoscalar-nucleon matching as a public module (extending micrOMEGAs or a DirectDM/DirectDet-style effective-operator pipeline) and compare against current XENONnT/LZ limits and the neutrino floor.

route_step_status.reason: The paper solved the two-temperature coupled Boltzmann system with a private code and the card identifies no reusable public solver; standard relic tools (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) do not evolve a separate hidden-sector temperature with feeble kinetic-mixing population out of the box.
Converting the S abundance and lifetime into Delta N_eff(z) via instantaneous-decay energy injection is simple analytic bookkeeping that needs no dedicated tool.

Public BBN and CMB N_eff bounds exist for a constant Delta N_eff, but the model's recombination-era injection requires a dedicated cosmological fit that the card says is not available (likelihood_available unknown/no).
Computing T_kd by equating the momentum-transfer rate to H(T) is a standard pen-and-paper estimate.

Linear Boltzmann solvers with dark-sector interactions (ETHOS-type modified CLASS) exist, but the card notes no model-specific transfer function was computed and the mapping of this hidden sector's scattering onto such a parameterization has not been done.

Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints and WDM-style recasting methods exist publicly, but no dedicated recast for this model's late-kinetic-decoupling transfer functions is available; only a crude T_kd > 100 eV criterion is quoted.

gaps.description: No public two-temperature coupled Boltzmann solver exists for this U(1)_X hidden sector: the relic density and N_eff history require evolving visible and hidden temperatures plus yields of D, A_prime, S, and the pseudoscalar under feeble kinetic-mixing population, which the paper did with a private code.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled visible/hidden-temperature Boltzmann system (collision terms for kinetic-mixing energy transfer plus dark-sector 2->2 reactions) as a public module, e.g. extending micrOMEGAs' hidden-sector/freeze-in machinery or releasing a standalone solver validated against the paper's benchmark points.

gaps.description: The model-specific linear transfer function has never been derived: the dark-fermion-pseudoscalar/scalar momentum-transfer rate has not been mapped onto an ETHOS-type dark-matter-dark-radiation parameterization, so no P(k) exists for the late-kinetic-decoupling regime.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the angular-averaged momentum-transfer cross section for D scattering off the massless pseudoscalar bath, map it to ETHOS (a_n, alpha_l) coefficients including the T_h/T temperature ratio, and compute transfer functions in an ETHOS-modified CLASS.

gaps.description: No Lyman-alpha likelihood or recast exists for this model's dark-acoustic-oscillation/late-decoupling transfer functions; the primary paper only quotes a qualitative T_kd > 100 eV lower limit of low robustness.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints (e.g. via a public flux-power emulator or the half-mode/area-criterion mapping calibrated for non-WDM suppression shapes) against the ETHOS-type transfer functions produced in gap_2.

gaps.description: No cosmological likelihood is available for the time-dependent Delta N_eff produced by the out-of-equilibrium S decay near recombination; published N_eff bounds assume a constant extra relativistic density, so the Hubble-tension benchmark cannot be properly tested.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the decaying-scalar-to-dark-radiation fluid in CLASS/CAMB and run a dedicated MCMC against Planck+BAO+SH0ES likelihoods (e.g. in MontePython or Cobaya) to constrain tau_S, m_S, and the injected Delta N_eff(z).

route_step_status.reason: The thermal gravitino abundance is a closed-form analytic scaling in T_r, m_3/2 and m_g quoted in the card, so the step is pen-and-paper even with null tool_or_code.
Nonthermal leptogenesis from inflaton decay to right-handed neutrinos uses standard analytic formulae for the baryon asymmetry and reheating temperature.

The metastable-string SGWB spectrum follows a published semi-analytic prescription, but no named public code is identified on the card and the result depends on loop-production and metastability modeling assumptions.

Public PTA stochastic-background likelihoods and BBN/relic bounds exist, but the card marks the likelihood as unavailable/not rerun and a joint recast for this model's combined SGWB-plus-gravitino parameter space has not been assembled.

gaps.description: No reusable public calculator exists for the metastable cosmic-string SGWB spectrum Omega_GW(f) as a function of G mu_CS and sqrt(kappa) in this model's window (sqrt(kappa) about 7.4-9.0); the paper's semi-analytic spectrum calculation is not released as code.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the metastable-string loop spectrum (monopole-pair breaking with the standard loop-production functions) as a public module, e.g. by extending the metastable-string templates in PTArcade or packaging the Buchmuller-Domcke-Schmitz-type calculation with configurable loop and decay modeling.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a scan that couples the gap_1 spectrum calculator to public PTA likelihood machinery (enterprise/PTArcade) and applies the analytic gravitino relic formula plus published BBN reheating bounds as priors, validated by recovering the paper's G mu_CS range of 1e-9 to 8e-6 and its viable T_r window.

route_step_status.reason: The DSMEFT/DLEFT operator basis and electroweak-scale matching are written out in the paper (basis cross-checked with BasisGen), so this step is analytic and served.

The invisible-Z width formula compared to the LEP 2.0 MeV bound and the benchmark-level direct-detection/collider estimates are analytic recasts the paper already performs.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the C_BX2 and C_tilde_BX2 operators in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and run the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module (or MadDM) to reproduce the paper's benchmark relic curves, releasing the model files publicly.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the model to an existing global-fit framework (e.g. a GAMBIT model entry) whose DarkBit likelihoods already implement Planck, XENON1T, and Fermi dwarf-spheroidal statistics, extending the direct- and indirect-detection likelihoods to rescale each component by Omega_i/Omega_T.

route_step_status.reason: Perturbative reheating in Higgs-R^2 inflation follows standard coupled inflaton-radiation Boltzmann equations, but no public reheating module for this specific model exists and the card identifies no code, so the step relies on paper-specific semi-analytics.

The gravitational/nonminimal and Higgs-portal freeze-in rate formulas are given analytically in the source, but combining thermal, nonthermal condensate, and graviton-exchange channels over the reheating history requires numerical integration that no public freeze-in tool (e.g. micrOMEGAs freeze-in mode) currently implements for this production mix.
Converting a freeze-in yield to Omega_s h^2 and comparing to the observed 0.12 target is simple pen-and-paper arithmetic.
The direct-detection null expectation is a trivial consistency check given lambda_hs ~ 0 and superheavy m_s, requiring no tool.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver computes UV freeze-in of a near-conformally coupled singlet scalar through the Higgs-R^2 reheating phase, including graviton-exchange scattering, nonminimal-coupling production, and inflaton-condensate scattering alongside the thermal-bath history (T_max, T_reh); the calculation currently exists only as the paper's private semi-analytics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a reusable reheating+freeze-in module (e.g. extending micrOMEGAs' freeze-in machinery or a standalone code like DRAKE-style ODE integration) that solves the coupled inflaton-radiation equations of unitary Higgs-R^2 inflation and integrates the gravitational, nonminimal-coupling, and condensate-scattering production rates over the temperature history, parameterized by (m_s, xi_s, lambda_hs, xi, alpha).

route_step_status.reason: Thermal freeze-out of a renormalizable scalar WIMP with Higgs-portal and Z' interactions is standard territory for micrOMEGAs or MadDM given a model file, even though the card names no specific tool.

micrOMEGAs 5 supports freeze-in and two-component evolution, but the coupled system with semi-production phi_1 phi_2 -> phi_2 phi_2 and phi_1 -> 3 phi_2 decay terms requires custom collision-term implementation not covered out of the box, and no paper code is public.

sigma_SI and <sigma v> are computable with standard tools, but the card flags recasting_needed with no likelihood available, and the WIMP-fraction rescaling against XENON-1T/AMS-02 contours exists only as the paper's private digitized comparison.
The one-loop Z' contribution to the muon g-2 from U(1)_{L_mu-L_tau} is a standard closed-form formula, so null tool_or_code is not an obstacle.

The paper used a modified, non-public version of CosmoTransitions; the public CosmoTransitions exists but needs this model's multi-scalar finite-temperature potential implemented before the step can be reproduced.
Mapping (alpha, beta/H, T_n) to a stochastic GW spectrum uses the standard published fit formulae, which are simple analytic expressions.
Overlaying the predicted spectrum on published LISA/DECIGO/BBO sensitivity curves is a trivial comparison requiring no dedicated tool.

gaps.description: No public implementation exists of the coupled two-component Boltzmann system for this model, in particular the FIMP semi-production channel phi_1 phi_2 -> phi_2 phi_2 and the three-body decay phi_1 -> phi_2 phi_2 phi_2 that couple the WIMP and FIMP abundances; the paper's numerical solver is private.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build the model file in micrOMEGAs 5's two-component mode and extend it with the semi-production and superWIMP-decay collision terms (or implement the coupled number-density equations in a standalone solver), validating against the paper's one- and two-component regime benchmarks.

gaps.description: No likelihood or reusable recast exists for the fraction-rescaled direct and indirect detection constraints on the WIMP component; the paper compares to XENON-1T and AMS-02 contours without a public statistical implementation for the two-component local-density rescaling.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the model into DDCalc (for XENON-1T-class spin-independent likelihoods) and an AMS-02 antiproton/positron likelihood, applying the Omega_1/Omega_DM rescaling of local density and annihilation rate computed from the relic solver.

gaps.description: The finite-temperature phase-transition analysis relied on a modified, non-public version of CosmoTransitions; the multi-scalar effective potential of this U(1)_{L_mu-L_tau} model is not implemented in any public phase-transition code, so (T_n, alpha, beta/H) cannot be recomputed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's one-loop finite-temperature effective potential (SM Higgs, U(1) Higgs phi_H, spectator dark scalars at zero VEV) in public CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer and validate the nucleation parameters against the paper's benchmark GW spectra.

route_step_status.reason: Fermion-annihilation freeze-in was cross-checked with micrOMEGAs 5.0, but the thermal plasmon-decay channel and the instantaneous low-T_RH (5-10 MeV) treatment are paper-specific in-medium calculations not covered by the public tool.

The Solar upscattering flux is a private semi-analytic calculation; public solar-scattering codes (e.g. DaMaSCUS-SUN) exist but do not implement inelastic transition-dipole upscattering to a keV-split excited state.

Xenon electron-recoil tools with atomic ionization factors (wimprates/QEdark-type) exist, but exothermic down-scattering of a keV-split dipole state is not implemented publicly and the card notes detector response was not reproduced.

The comparison combines digitized fixed-target, collider, SN1987A, and N_eff curves compiled by the paper; no reusable likelihood exists (likelihood_available: no, recasting_needed: yes), though curve overlay itself is straightforward.

route_step_status.reason: The one-loop Wilson coefficients and Delta a_mu are given as closed-form analytic expressions in the paper, and public flavor tools (flavio/smelli-type fits) map Wilson coefficients to observables.
micrOMEGAs fully covers freeze-out with coannihilation for this weak-scale scalar, but the required FeynRules/CalcHEP model file for Model 3 is not publicly released.
The Higgs-mediated sigma_SI is a standard tree-level calculation and the PandaX-4T, XENON1T, and LZ limit curves are public data suitable for direct comparison.

gaps.description: The Model 3 implementation files (FeynRules/CalcHEP model for the two Z2-odd scalar doublets plus vectorlike singlet fermion) used with micrOMEGAs are not public, so the relic-density and sigma_SI scan and the 42-76 GeV allowed window cannot be reproduced or extended.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rebuild the Model 3 Lagrangian (Yukawa terms y_Q, y_L and the scalar potential quartics) in FeynRules, export a CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model file, validate against the paper's reported 42-76 GeV mass window and portal-coupling scan, and release the files.

route_step_status.reason: One-loop Wilson coefficients for b -> s l+l- and Delta a_mu in this dark-loop topology are standard analytic formulas evaluable by hand or with generic flavor tools, so the null tool_or_code does not indicate a missing capability.
micrOMEGAs covers freeze-out with coannihilation, but the card notes a FeynRules/model file for Model 5 would be needed for reproduction and none is public.

gaps.description: No public FeynRules/CalcHEP model implementation of Model 5 (Z2-odd scalar SU(2)L singlets plus vectorlike fermion doublet) exists for micrOMEGAs, so the relic abundance with annihilation and coannihilation, and the sigma_SI input to direct-detection recasts, cannot be recomputed outside the original private setup.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules model file for the Model 5 field content and Z2 charges, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and validate by reproducing the paper's 30-350 GeV allowed scalar-mass window and the fermion-doublet Z-mediated exclusion.

gaps.description: No machine-readable combined likelihood or scan-point release exists for the joint flavor + relic + direct-detection + collider constraint region; the card records likelihood_available: no and that no scan points were recovered, so the allowed region can only be read off the paper's figures.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rebuild the global scan with public components (e.g. flavio/smelli for the b -> s l+l- and g-2 likelihood, micrOMEGAs for relic and sigma_SI, published DD curves) and release the scan chain so the 30-350 GeV window is reproducible with post-2022 flavor averages.

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the two coupled homogeneous scalar-field equations with the exponential kinetic function is a straightforward ODE problem fully specified by the paper's action.
