Planck, BAO, SN, and S8 likelihoods are public (Cobaya/MontePython), but no chains or likelihood pipeline exist for this model and only example parameter points were computed.

gaps.description: The modified CLASS implementation evolving the kinetically coupled axion-dilaton background and perturbations (f(chi) kinetic coupling, EDE-like injection, fuzzy-axion power suppression) is not publicly available, so neither the CMB nor matter-power predictions can be regenerated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recover or reimplement the two-field sector in public CLASS (starting from AxiCLASS/CLASS_EDE as a template), adding the exponential kinetic function to the background and perturbation equations, and validate against the paper's example with EDE fraction near 0.097 and the roughly 10 percent matter-power step at F = 0.01.

gaps.description: No MCMC analysis or likelihood pipeline exists for this model: the paper shows example parameter regions only, so quantitative H0/S8 tension relief and allowed regions for (kinetic-function slope, m_phi, f_phi, F) are not established.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the (re)implemented Boltzmann code to Cobaya or MontePython with Planck 2018, BAO, Pantheon, SH0ES, and DES/KiDS S8 likelihoods and run a full posterior scan over the model parameters, releasing the chains.

gaps.description: The S8/weak-lensing comparison uses linear theory only; no nonlinear prescription or emulator exists for the matter power spectrum of a percent-level fuzzy-axion fraction coexisting with CDM in this two-field cosmology, which weak-lensing scales require.

route_step_status.reason: The modified Press-Schechter mass-function construction from the broken-power-law-plus-spike spectrum is an analytic formula fully specified in the primary paper; null tool_or_code reflects simple pen-and-paper/numerical evaluation.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate Hawking spectra for the low-mass component with BlackHawk, integrate over the spiked mass function, and compare against extragalactic/Galactic gamma-ray background data (and relic-abundance bookkeeping for Planck-mass relics), wrapping the result as a reusable evaporation recast over arbitrary mass functions.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the 2-to-2 scalar glueball elastic cross section from the lattice-normalized glueball EFT self-couplings (sigma proportional to 1/(Lambda^2) times coupling factors), map sigma/m_gb onto the standard SIDM constraint plane, and recast published cluster/dwarf self-interaction bounds onto Lambda.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple CosmoTransitions output (phase sequence, T_n, v_eta(T)) to a modified freeze-in Boltzmann solver, e.g. extend the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module or write a dedicated ODE solver with temperature-dependent decay widths and thermal masses for the eta -> N_1 L production channels.

route_step_status.reason: The high-temperature one-loop effective potential for the two-scalar SU(2)_ell sector is a standard analytic construction developed in the primary paper and needs no dedicated tool.

The sound-wave, bubble-collision, and turbulence spectra follow the standard phase-transition GW fitting formulae given (T_star, alpha_PT, beta/H, wall velocity), an analytic step.

Published sensitivity curves for LVK, ET, CE, DECIGO, and BBO permit the benchmark overlay the paper performed, but the card states no stochastic-background likelihood exists, so only detectability flags rather than statistical constraints are possible.

gaps.description: No stochastic gravitational-wave background likelihood exists for confronting the predicted SU(2)_ell phase-transition spectrum with LVK data or projected ET/CE/DECIGO/BBO sensitivities; the card's detector comparison is a benchmark-level power-law-integrated-curve overlay, not a statistical constraint on (v_ell, alpha_PT, beta/H).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the model's Omega_GW(f) prediction in an existing stochastic-background analysis framework (LVK cross-correlation likelihood for current data, Fisher/mock likelihoods for ET/CE/DECIGO), parameterized by T_star, alpha_PT, beta/H, and wall velocity, so posterior constraints on v_ell can replace detectability flags.

gaps.description: The nearly degenerate Z2-related vacua of the SU(2)_ell scalar potential can form domain walls, but no calculation or simulation of the wall network's formation, annihilation time as a function of the vacuum-energy splitting Delta V, and gravitational-wave contribution exists for this model, leaving obs_vacuum_domain_wall_caveat unevaluable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply the standard biased-domain-wall evolution formalism (wall tension from the computed potential, annihilation temperature set by Delta V versus tension, and existing lattice-calibrated Omega_GW fitting formulae for collapsing wall networks) to the m12_squared parameter space, adding the wall signal and cosmological-safety bound to the GW pipeline.

route_step_status.reason: The first-principle formation formalism (QCD equation-of-state-dependent thresholds plus critical-collapse scaling from P_R(k)) is published, but the paper's numerical formation machinery is not released as a public code, so the mass function cannot be regenerated without reimplementation.

The early-Universe PBH binary merger-rate model is a published semi-analytic formalism, but its suppression and accretion factors are assumption-laden and no public implementation for extended QCD-shaped mass functions is identified in the card.

LVK GWTC-3 data and hierarchical population-inference frameworks are public, but the card marks the likelihood as only partially available and the PBH channel model with this mass function is not implemented in a released pipeline.

Monochromatic PBH bound compilations are public, but the card states a dedicated extended-mass-function recast against evaporation, lensing, CMB, gamma-ray, and dynamical constraints is required and no likelihood is available for it.

gaps.description: No public code maps a sampled curvature power spectrum P_R(k) through QCD-epoch equation-of-state-dependent collapse thresholds and critical-collapse scaling to the PBH mass function f(m); the paper's first-principle formation machinery is private, blocking regeneration of the population for new spectrum parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a formation module that tabulates the QCD-era equation of state, the corresponding collapse threshold delta_c(M_H), and the critical-collapse relation, taking (A, n_s, M_min, M_max) as inputs and returning f(m), validated against the paper's published mass functions.

gaps.description: No released likelihood pipeline connects the QCD-shaped PBH mass function to the LVK GWTC-3 catalog: the early-binary merger-rate model with its suppression and accretion factors and the hierarchical population likelihood for a mixed PBH/astrophysical population are not available as a runnable implementation for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the PBH early-binary merger-rate density R(m1,m2,z) for extended mass functions as a source model inside a public GW population-inference framework (gwpopulation or icarogw style) with GWTC-3 selection effects, exposing f_PBH and the spectrum parameters as sampled quantities.

gaps.description: All-dark-matter claims for the asteroid-mass ultra-slow-roll mapping cannot be evaluated because no recasting machinery convolves this broad, multi-featured mass function with the compiled monochromatic multi-messenger PBH bounds (evaporation, microlensing, CMB accretion, dynamical), whose statuses the card notes are themselves evolving.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply the standard extended-mass-function recast method to a maintained bound compilation (PBHbounds-style curves), integrating f(m)/f_max(m) over the QCD-shaped and USR-mapped mass functions to produce allowed f_PBH windows with per-constraint provenance flags.

route_step_status.reason: FeynRules itself is public and the paper built an NLHT implementation, but the card identifies no public release of the NLHT model files, so the spectrum-and-vertices step cannot be reproduced without them.
micrOMEGAs is a named public tool whose standard thermal co-annihilation machinery covers the A_H plus T-odd heavy lepton relic calculation once model files are supplied.

T3PS is a public scan driver and scan-level EWPD/LHC constraints were applied in the paper, but the card states no independent LHC recast exists for the compressed vector-like lepton to lepton plus A_H topology, on which the allowed mass ranges depend.

gaps.description: The FeynRules/CalcHEP model implementation of the simplified NLHT (heavy photon LTP, T-odd lepton co-annihilators, kappa_l/kappa_q Yukawa structure) used by the paper is not publicly released, so neither the micrOMEGAs relic scan nor any collider study can be rerun for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain or reimplement the NLHT Lagrangian in FeynRules and export CalcHEP/UFO model files, validating against the paper's benchmarks (m_lH approximately 1.16 M_AH relic band and kappa_l approximately 0.185 at f = 900 GeV) before public release.

gaps.description: No dedicated recast or likelihood exists for the compressed-spectrum signature of T-odd heavy leptons decaying to a single standard lepton plus A_H with mass splittings of only a few tens of GeV; the quoted allowed ranges (M_AH about 450-680 GeV, m_lH about 530-800 GeV) rest on scan-level statements rather than a detector-level analysis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast ATLAS/CMS compressed-electroweakino and slepton soft-lepton plus missing-energy searches for the vector-like lepton pair-production topology in CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5, producing exclusion contours in the (M_AH, m_lH) plane along the relic-density band.

route_step_status.reason: The paper states its freeze-in contours are public and micrOMEGAs-style freeze-in machinery exists, but no released code covers axion freeze-in from photon/electron plasma processes (inverse decays, plasmon effects) with a low reheating temperature, so the step needs a dedicated integrator.
Axion lifetime and branching fractions to gamma gamma and e+e- follow from standard closed-form width formulas given m_a, g_a_gamma, g_ae.

Published CMB/cosmic-background decay limits exist and the paper recasts them, but likelihood_available is 'no' and no public pipeline rescales these limits to a subdominant, possibly free-streaming freeze-in population.
Summing freeze-in and misalignment abundances is simple pen-and-paper arithmetic once each contribution is known.

The generalized recasting logic is described in the paper's supplement, but applying it to mixed couplings or other relics (e.g. sterile neutrinos) requires model-specific production/decay modules that no public tool provides.

gaps.description: No public, documented freeze-in integrator computes the irreducible axion yield from SM plasma processes (inverse decays, e+e- annihilation, photon conversions with thermal/plasmon effects) for axion-photon and axion-electron couplings with a low BBN-limit reheating temperature; the paper's contours are said to be public but no repository is identified on the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement the paper's freeze-in Boltzmann integration as a documented module (e.g. extend the micrOMEGAs freeze-in machinery or a standalone Python integrator) taking (m_a, g_a_gamma, g_ae, T_R) and returning the yield, Omega_a and the nonthermal momentum distribution, validated against the published blue contours.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for recasting CMB energy-injection and cosmic-radiation-background photon-line/continuum decay limits onto a subdominant freeze-in axion population with nonthermal momentum distribution; the card lists likelihood_available: no for all constraints and only published limit curves as inputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a recast likelihood that combines digitized X-ray/CRB decay limit tables with a CMB energy-injection calculation (e.g. DarkHistory or ExoCLASS with a decaying subcomponent) and rescales exclusion curves by the freeze-in fraction Omega_a/Omega_DM and decay epoch, exposed as a function of (m_a, g_a_gamma, g_ae, T_R).

route_step_status.reason: PBH Hawking temperature, evaporation time, and expansion history for a monochromatic mass function follow from standard analytic formulas given M_in and beta.
ULYSSES is public and handles PBH evaporation, but the model-specific neutrino-portal freeze-in collision terms are custom equations from the paper that are not released as reusable code.
Comparing the final yield to the Planck Omega_DM h^2 target and checking the pre-BBN evaporation condition is a trivial arithmetic validation once yields exist.

gaps.description: The coupled Boltzmann system for neutrino-portal freeze-in (Littlest-Seesaw dark-sector collision terms for y_DS-mediated scattering and decays) combined with the ULYSSES PBH evaporation source term exists only as unreleased custom code; no public tool computes the mixed freeze-in plus Hawking yield with entropy dilution for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's freeze-in collision terms as a ULYSSES extension (or a micrOMEGAs freeze-in model file coupled to BlackHawk/ULYSSES greybody-weighted PBH source terms), taking (y_DS, m_chi, m_phi, m_N, M_in, beta) and returning Omega_DM h^2 with entropy dilution, validated against the paper's benchmark contours and the M_in <= 1e9 g BBN window.

route_step_status.reason: The KK-graviton production rate from the SM brane is a closed-form analytic estimate in the primary paper requiring only pen-and-paper evaluation of the gravitational coupling and brane temperature.

The 'Boltzmann tower equations' for intra-tower decay evolution of the dense KK spectrum exist only as the paper's own treatment; no public code evolves a multi-level graviton tower distribution, and the governing inhomogeneity parameter is itself uncertain.

Published CMB/BBN decay limits and N_eff constraints exist, but no pipeline recasts them onto a decaying multi-mass graviton tower with a time-evolving mass distribution; the card notes external likelihoods are required for a precision recast.
The card marks this as a future concept only: no high-frequency gravitational-wave detector or response model exists at the ~1e8-above-LIGO frequencies implied by keV graviton masses.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver evolves the time-dependent mass distribution of a dense KK graviton tower under intra-tower cascade decays; the paper's tower equations are not released, so the present-day 1-100 keV dark-graviton distribution cannot be recomputed for other parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled tower Boltzmann equations as a standalone numerical code taking (T_i, m_KK, dark decay parameter, visible branching fraction) and returning the evolving graviton mass/abundance distribution, validated against the paper's benchmark of m_DM ~ 1-100 keV for T_i ~ 4 GeV.

gaps.description: The intra-tower decay widths depend on an unknown dark-dimension inhomogeneity parameter that has not been derived from the compactification geometry, so the dominant decay channels and cascade timescales are inputs rather than predictions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive graviton-to-graviton decay widths as a function of the metric inhomogeneity of the dark dimension (e.g. perturbative computation of KK-number-violating couplings for a warped or deformed circle) and publish them as a parameterized rate table for the cascade solver.

gaps.description: No likelihood recasts CMB/BBN energy-injection and N_eff constraints onto a decaying multi-component graviton tower whose mass distribution evolves in time; existing decay constraints assume a single decaying species with fixed mass and lifetime.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an energy-injection framework (e.g. DarkHistory or ExoCLASS) to accept a time-dependent superposition of decaying species drawn from the tower solver output, and combine with BBN photodissociation limits and Planck N_eff to produce exclusion contours in (T_i, m_KK, visible branching fraction).

gaps.description: No detector data or sensitivity model exists for gravitational waves at the characteristic frequencies of keV-mass dark gravitons, roughly 1e8 times above LIGO bands, so the proposed high-frequency GW probe cannot be evaluated at all.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop sensitivity curves for proposed high-frequency GW detection concepts (e.g. resonant cavities or levitated-sensor proposals) in the relevant band and build a forecast tool mapping (m_DM, coupling strength) to signal-to-noise in those concepts.

route_step_status.reason: The card states no executable COFI code was found; the conformal freeze-in collision term for the B_munu O_CFT^munu portal with general operator dimension d is not implemented in any public Boltzmann code.
Mapping the dark CFT energy density onto dark-hadron abundances across the confining transition is done by assumption in the paper; no quantitative nonperturbative tool exists for this step.
Public warm-DM and self-interaction constraints exist, but the card provides no dark-pion distribution function or thermal-WDM mapping, so the screens can only be applied at order-of-magnitude level.
The primary text gives only a qualitative analytic matching of the UV portal to the IR kinetic mixing epsilon and composite dark-photon mass; a quantitative matching needs nonperturbative CFT input.

Published dark-photon exclusion curves (e.g. Darkcast-style compilations) exist for the epsilon-m_A_D overlay, but composite form factors mean elementary dark-photon limits may not directly apply, as the card's caveat notes.
Comparing stellar temperature scales to the mass gap and dark-pion mass to decide which states are accessible is simple pen-and-paper threshold arithmetic.

The card states detailed stellar-emission rates were not available and no stellar-cooling likelihood was resolved; dark-sector emission rates from stellar plasmas have not been computed for this composite model.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann implementation exists for conformal freeze-in: the collision term for SM hypercharge coupling to a dark-CFT antisymmetric tensor operator of dimension d, transferring energy into the conformal sector without thermalization, is not available in any released code.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the COFI collision integral (parameterized by Lambda, d, and the reheating asymmetry) as a standalone freeze-in module or micrOMEGAs/DRAKE-style extension that outputs the dark-sector energy density versus temperature, validated against the paper's relic contours and nonthermalization screen.

gaps.description: There is no quantitative treatment of the confining transition that converts the dark CFT energy density into dark-pion (and heavier resonance) abundances and momenta; the matching is currently an assumption, leaving the dark-pion yield and phase space undetermined beyond scaling estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the confinement/hadronization of the near-conformal sector via a holographic (AdS/CFT dual) model or lattice simulation of a representative confining gauge theory, delivering a parameterized map from pre-confinement energy density to dark-hadron yields, momenta, and the IR kinetic mixing epsilon.

gaps.description: The dark-pion phase-space distribution and linear transfer function have not been derived, so warm-DM and Lyman-alpha screens cannot be applied quantitatively; the card records no f(q), no free-streaming length, and no thermal-WDM mapping.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) from the COFI production plus confinement history, feed it to CLASS as a non-cold relic to obtain the transfer function and half-mode scale, and map onto existing Lyman-alpha WDM bounds/emulators to produce a quantitative (m_DM, m_gap) exclusion.

gaps.description: Composite form factors for the vector-meson dark photon have not been computed, so elementary dark-photon search curves cannot be reliably recast onto the composite epsilon-m_A_D parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the composite dark photon's production and decay form factors (vector-meson-dominance or holographic estimate) and fold them into an existing recast framework such as Darkcast to rescale published fixed-target and collider limits.

gaps.description: Stellar emission rates of dark-sector states through the suppressed portal have not been calculated for this model, so stellar-cooling bounds on light benchmarks cannot be evaluated beyond threshold arithmetic.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive dark-sector emission rates from stellar plasmas (plasmon mixing into the composite dark photon and CFT-state pair emission) as a function of (T_S, m_gap, epsilon), then compare against standard HB/RGB/SN energy-loss budgets to obtain cooling exclusions.

route_step_status.reason: The axion/singlet effective matter potential V_eff(T) and its cancellation against the SM contribution follow analytically from the paper's operator given g_a, m_a, and the assumed singlet vev history.

Public momentum-dependent sterile-neutrino production solvers exist for the standard DW/Shi-Fuller potentials (e.g. sterile-dm-style codes), but none includes the axion-assisted temperature-dependent potential, so the solver needs modification.
Published X-ray line and dwarf phase-space exclusion curves in the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane can be overlaid, but the card notes no underlying likelihood grids are available for a proper recast.
The radiative decay rate is the standard analytic sterile-neutrino formula scaling as sin^2(2 theta) m_s^5.

Published Athena/eXTP sensitivity forecasts exist to compare against, but no public likelihood combining instrument response, exposure, and target dark-matter column is available, so the step is qualitative.

gaps.description: No public sterile-neutrino production code includes the axion-assisted temperature-dependent matter potential from the singlet vev; existing DW/Shi-Fuller solvers must be modified to compute the momentum-dependent distribution f_s(p,T) and Omega_s h^2 through the engineered resonance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public momentum-dependent sterile-neutrino production solver (e.g. the sterile-dm code of Venumadhav et al. or a DW-style quasi-classical Boltzmann integrator) to accept a user-supplied V_eff(T) built from (g_a, m_a, <phi>(T)), validated by recovering the paper's benchmark of lower mixing than DW at fixed relic abundance.

gaps.description: The sterile-neutrino momentum distribution and linear transfer function for the axion-assisted resonance are unresolved (the card flags both), so structure-formation and dwarf phase-space constraints can only be applied via generic WDM proxies rather than the model's actual smooth-cutoff suppression.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f_s(p) from the modified production solver, feed it to CLASS/CAMB as a non-cold relic to obtain the transfer function and half-mode mass, and map onto existing Lyman-alpha and subhalo-count WDM bounds to place quantitative structure constraints in the (m_s, sin^2 2theta, g_a) space.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for the X-ray decay-line and dwarf phase-space constraints or for Athena/eXTP forecasts; only summarized exclusion regions are available, preventing a proper recast of the suppressed X-ray signal and future-mission reach for this model's reduced mixing.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a decay-line likelihood from published XMM/NuSTAR/Chandra blank-sky and dwarf X-ray limits plus dwarf phase-space bounds, and add Athena/eXTP instrument-response forecast modules, exposing an exclusion/detectability flag as a function of (m_s, sin^2 2theta).

route_step_status.reason: Public finite-temperature phase-transition codes (CosmoTransitions, PhaseTracer) handle generic quartic potentials, but the hidden sector with its own temperature ratio xi requires model-specific modification and no tool is cited on the card.
Velocity-dependent Yukawa self-scattering cross sections follow from standard analytic Born/Hulthen/classical formulas, an adequate pen-and-paper treatment for this step.
The stochastic GW spectrum from sound waves/MHD uses standard analytic spectral templates rescaled by xi, and comparison to published detector sensitivity curves is straightforward.

Public energy-injection and BBN tools (ExoCLASS/DarkAges-type, ACROPOLIS-type) cover late-decaying light mediators in principle, but the card states the recast is not implemented and no likelihood is identified.

gaps.description: No phase-transition calculator handles the hidden-sector first-order transition with an independent dark temperature (hidden-to-visible ratio xi) entering nucleation, alpha, and beta/H; existing public codes assume the transitioning sector shares the visible-sector temperature.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer to evaluate the effective potential and nucleation rate at a dark temperature T_d = xi*T, propagating xi into the Hubble rate and the alpha and beta/H definitions for the GW template.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann/relic solver computes hidden-sector freeze-out with equilibrium densities and thermally averaged cross sections evaluated at the dark temperature and with hidden radiation degrees of freedom in the Hubble rate, as this model requires for Omega_chi h^2.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend micrOMEGAs (or implement a standalone modified Boltzmann solver) with a two-temperature freeze-out mode parameterized by xi(T) and hidden-sector g_star, validated against the paper's quoted 0.01-10 GeV viable mass range.

gaps.description: No small-scale-structure likelihood exists for the velocity-dependent self-interaction cross section of this model; the card states small-scale-structure likelihoods are not built and the joint SIDM/relic constraint has likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the model's Yukawa sigma(v)/m into published dwarf-to-cluster SIDM inference results (velocity-binned sigma/m posteriors from rotation-curve and cluster analyses) and package them as a reusable likelihood over (m_chi, m_phi, g_chi).

gaps.description: The visible-portal recast route has no implemented pipeline mapping portal coupling and mediator lifetime onto CMB energy-injection, BBN, and direct-detection limits for a late-decaying light dark scalar.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the mediator decay spectrum in ACROPOLIS for BBN and ExoCLASS/DarkAges for CMB energy injection, and add a portal-suppressed nucleon cross-section map for direct-detection recasting, scanned over (epsilon, tau_phi, m_phi).

route_step_status.reason: axionCAMB is a named public Boltzmann code that provides linear transfer functions and the Jeans scale for mixed CDM-ULA cosmologies across the modeled mass range.
axionHMcode is publicly released (github.com/SophieMLV/axionHMcode per the card) and implements the mixed-component halo model with soliton/NFW profiles and cross terms.
Mixed-ULA simulations (AxioNyx-type) exist for some masses and fractions, but the card states calibration requires mixed-DM simulations across the full mass/fraction range, which do not yet exist.

Planck and DES-Y1 shear likelihoods exist but assume all-FDM suppression; no likelihood pipeline connects the axionHMcode subcomponent P(k) to survey data (tool_or_code null, likelihood_available partial/no).

gaps.description: No mixed CDM+ULA simulation suite spans the model's applicability range (m_ax 1e-33 to 1e-21 eV, subdominant fractions of a few percent to ~25%), so the axionHMcode halo model is uncalibrated in nonlinear P(k), the halo cutoff mass M_cut, and soliton behavior at small ULA fractions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a grid of mixed-DM simulations combining N-body CDM with a Schrodinger-Poisson or Madelung ULA solver (extending AxioNyx or a PIC-based ULA code) over (m_ax, Omega_ax/Omega_d), and fit calibration residuals for axionHMcode's profiles, bias, and cutoff-mass prescriptions.

gaps.description: No survey likelihood pipeline exists for subcomponent ULA fractions: existing DES-Y1 plus Planck FDM constraints assume ULAs are all of the dark matter, and the route's likelihood step has no tool for propagating the mixed-model nonlinear P(k) into weak-lensing or clustering posteriors on (m_ax, Omega_ax/Omega_d).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap axionCAMB plus axionHMcode as a theory module in Cobaya or MontePython, interface it with DES/KiDS shear and galaxy-clustering likelihoods including baryonic-feedback marginalization, and rederive fraction-mass constraints for subdominant ULAs.

route_step_status.reason: A coupled PBH-radiation background solver exists per the paper (AXIONPBH-style, and public codes like FRISBHEE cover PBH evaporation histories), but the card notes the accompanying code was not fetched or validated as a public release.
The temperature-dependent axion field-equation solver is paper-internal; no validated public tool on the card solves misalignment in a PBH-dominated expansion history.
Iterating the axion mass to match the relic target is a simple numerical root-find on the outputs of the previous steps and needs no dedicated tool.

Published Planck Delta N_eff, BBN timing, and GW bound curves exist, but no assembled overlay pipeline for this PBH parameter space is identified on the card (likelihood_available unknown for most constraints).

gaps.description: No validated public release of the coupled PBH-radiation-axion solver (background evolution with evaporation and entropy injection plus the axion equation of motion with QCD temperature-dependent mass) is confirmed; the AXIONPBH material referenced by the paper was not fetched or validated, so the abundance route cannot be run independently.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain and validate the AXIONPBH code against the paper's density plots, or extend FRISBHEE's PBH-evaporation background module with an axion misalignment sector using the standard dilute-instanton m_a(T), and release it publicly.

gaps.description: No dedicated axion-minicluster simulations exist for a PBH early-matter-dominated cosmology; the card states such simulations are lacking, so the predicted shift to heavier miniclusters from delayed oscillation onset remains qualitative and has no likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run axion-field lattice simulations of density-perturbation growth and minicluster collapse with the modified H(T) and entropy-injection history from the PBH background solver, mapping the minicluster mass function versus (M_BH, beta).

gaps.description: No assembled joint constraint-overlay module maps (M_BH, beta, m_0, theta_i) onto the CMB Delta N_eff likelihood, BBN evaporation-timing bounds, isocurvature limits, and GW background curves; each bound exists in the literature but is not packaged for this parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize and package the Planck Delta N_eff posterior, pre-BBN evaporation-temperature bound, Planck isocurvature limit, and GW detector sensitivity curves into a single overlay/likelihood function evaluated on the background-solver outputs.

route_step_status.reason: The tree-level velocity-suppressed s-channel annihilation cross section in a renormalizable Yukawa theory is standard analytic work needing no dedicated tool.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) handle resonant and forbidden freeze-out, but no model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP model file) exists for this 2HDM+S+fermion setup and the calculation was not run.
CMB energy-injection tools (ExoCLASS/DarkHistory) and published laboratory limits on muon-philic light scalars exist, but the card states the recast was not run and no likelihood was extracted.

gaps.description: No model implementation exists for the light-2HDM plus real scalar S plus Z2-odd fermion dark matter Lagrangian in any public relic-density framework, so the resonant (m_H ~ 2 m_DM) and forbidden (m_H < m_DM) freeze-out branches cannot be scanned with proper thermal averaging near the resonance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/CalcHEP model file for the alignment-limit 2HDM with the mixed S-H light scalar and Y_chi, Y_l couplings, and run micrOMEGAs (or MadDM) relic scans over the resonant and forbidden branches, including the neglected H-prime state as a cross-check.

gaps.description: No CMB energy-injection recast exists for this model's p-wave (velocity-suppressed) sub-GeV annihilation into muons through the light scalar; the constraint card cites CMB limits only qualitatively with likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the late-time velocity-weighted annihilation rate including the resonance and feed the muon final-state injection spectra through ExoCLASS or DarkHistory to derive Planck exclusion contours in (m_DM, m_H, Y_chi, Y_l).

gaps.description: No laboratory recast maps existing muon-philic light-scalar searches (muon g-2, beam dumps, B-factory and meson-decay searches) onto this model's (m_H, Y_l, mixing angle) parameter space to test whether the couplings needed for the relic target survive.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast published muon-coupled light-scalar limits (g-2 preferred regions, NA64-mu type projections, meson and collider bounds) into a likelihood over the light-scalar mass and Y_l, joined with the relic-scan output.

route_step_status.reason: The forbidden annihilation rate near the lepton threshold follows from the standard Griest-Seckel analytic treatment of the tree-level SS to leptons cross section, which is pen-and-paper work.
Public CMB energy-injection tools (ExoCLASS/DarkHistory) cover sub-GeV leptonic injection, but the card states no Planck likelihood was evaluated and no model-specific recast exists.
The radiative (loop-level) annihilation amplitude and the resulting MeV gamma-ray forecast have not been computed, and no tool is identified; the signature is only discussed qualitatively.

gaps.description: No model implementation exists for the light-2HDM scalar forbidden dark matter Lagrangian in a public relic solver, so the Boltzmann-suppressed forbidden freeze-out (which requires careful thermal averaging across the lepton threshold with splitting Delta) cannot be scanned quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the 2HDM plus scalar-S model with lambda_ab portal couplings and leptophilic Y_l in FeynRules/CalcHEP and run micrOMEGAs relic scans over (m_DM, m_H, Delta, lambda_12, Y_l) in the forbidden branch, validating threshold thermal averaging against the analytic forbidden-DM treatment.

gaps.description: The one-loop radiative annihilation amplitude (SS to photon plus lepton pair or gamma-gamma through the muon loop) that produces the model's key MeV gamma-ray signature has not been derived, so no spectral prediction exists to compare with future MeV telescopes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the loop-level radiative annihilation cross section and photon spectrum for the leptophilic light-scalar mediator just below threshold, then fold it with published MeV telescope sensitivity curves (COSI, e-ASTROGAM/AMEGO-type) for a detectability forecast.

gaps.description: No implemented recast maps the Boltzmann-suppressed late-time annihilation and light-scalar couplings onto Planck energy-injection limits and laboratory muon-philic scalar searches; the constraint card cites both only qualitatively with likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the exponentially suppressed late-time annihilation rate through ExoCLASS/DarkHistory for a Planck exclusion, and recast published muon-coupled light-scalar laboratory bounds (g-2, beam dumps, meson decays) into a joint likelihood over (m_H, Y_l, lambda_12).

route_step_status.reason: Public multifield transport packages (PyTransport/CppTransport-class codes, alluded to in the card's associated_code summary) can integrate two-field backgrounds, but this specific nonminimal supergravity potential with its tuned saddle-point trajectory is not implemented in any released code.

The card names the transport method and public transport codes exist for multifield curvature/isocurvature spectra, but the ultra-slow-roll-enhanced supergravity model must still be implemented and validated in one of them; no model-specific released implementation is indicated.

The Press-Schechter-style collapse-fraction calculation from P_R(k) is standard semi-analytic formalism, but tool_or_code is null and the Gaussian-statistics assumption flagged in the card leaves USR non-Gaussianity uncovered.
The radiation-era scalar-induced GW spectrum is a standard analytic kernel integral over P_R(k), implementable directly and covered by public codes such as SIGWfast.

route_step_status.reason: MicrOMEGAs is public and was used for the relic and annihilation calculation, but the card notes no higgson model files (CalcHEP/FeynRules input) were released, so the calculation is not reproducible outside the authors' private implementation.

Public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods cover a 70 GeV WIMP annihilating to gauge bosons, but no likelihood was run or packaged for this model and the required annihilation spectra depend on the unreleased model implementation.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a low-threshold detector recast (e.g. via a DDCalc-style extension with sub-GeV nuclear-recoil response and Migdal channels for existing data, plus parameterized sensitivity curves for proposed kg-year experiments) mapped to the model's sigma_chi-n after relic matching.

gaps.description: The BBN guardrail on the light Z' (avoiding pion-producing decays and extra MeV-scale energy injection) is stated only qualitatively; no BBN network run or likelihood exists for this model's mediator mass and coupling range.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Z' decay channels and thermal abundance in a public BBN code (AlterBBN or PRIMAT with an injection module) to derive a quantitative exclusion in the (M_Zprime, g_z) plane, replacing the qualitative pion-threshold argument.

route_step_status.reason: FOPT parameters can be computed with public tools like CosmoTransitions, but the mapping from bubble dynamics to trapped-fermion remnant abundance and thermal-ball/Fermi-ball masses rests on uncalibrated source-level analytic approximations with no simulation.
The cooling-rate and degeneracy-supported collapse criterion giving z_form and the PBH mass fraction are analytic formulas provided by the source paper.

Public PBH constraint compilations (PBHbounds-style) and the BBN Delta N_eff bound exist, but they assume early-formed PBHs; no code applies accretion, microlensing, and dwarf-heating bounds as a function of a post-recombination formation redshift z_form.

gaps.description: No simulation calibrates the trapping of asymmetric dark fermions by FOPT bubble walls or the resulting thermal-ball population, so the remnant abundance, trapping fraction, and Fermi-ball mass function that seed the PBH prediction are order-of-magnitude analytic estimates only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run lattice or hydrodynamic simulations of a dark-sector FOPT with fermion transmission/reflection at the walls (extending existing bubble-wall friction and filtered-dark-matter simulation setups) to calibrate the trapping fraction and remnant mass function as functions of wall velocity, beta/H, and the Yukawa coupling.

gaps.description: Existing PBH constraint codes evaluate f_PBH bounds assuming formation deep in the radiation era; no tool applies CMB accretion, microlensing, and dwarf-heating limits time-dependently for objects that are extended thermal/Fermi balls until a formation redshift z_form after recombination.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a PBHbounds-style constraint package with a formation-redshift argument: switch each constraint on only for z < z_form, add pre-collapse compact-object limits (e.g. microlensing on Fermi balls) and the BBN Delta N_eff < 0.40 dark-radiation bound, producing f_PBH(M_PBH, z_form) exclusion surfaces.

route_step_status.reason: CLASS-based scalar-field-DM perturbation modules exist for neutral ultralight scalars, but the card states the charged complex-field perturbations still need implementation.
Public Schrodinger-Poisson solvers exist for uncharged fuzzy DM halos, but the card says the primary work uses analytic toy solutions and numerical validation of charged excited halo states remains.
No tool or derived emission-rate calculation exists to map (q, epsilon) to a Fermi-Bubble photon prediction, and the card notes foreground modeling would also be required.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-solver module implements linear perturbations of a charged complex scalar field with dark U(1) coupling; existing CLASS/axionCAMB fuzzy-DM implementations cover only the neutral real-field case, so the model-specific transfer function cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing CLASS scalar-field-DM branch (or axionCAMB) with the paper's covariant complex-field perturbation equations including the dark U(1) gauge sector, and validate against the neutral-SFDM limit.

gaps.description: No numerical Schrodinger-Poisson / Klein-Gordon-Poisson simulation exists for charged SFDM halos with excited 'atomic' states and dark-photon coupling; the paper's halo-state occupation results rest on analytic toy solutions only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Schrodinger-Poisson solver (e.g. PyUltraLight- or AxioNyx-class codes) to a two-component complex field coupled to a dark U(1) gauge field, and simulate ground/excited-state halo configurations to test the atomic-halo ansatz.

gaps.description: No quantitative derivation exists of the photon upscattering/emission rate from halo excited states as a function of dark charge q and kinetic mixing epsilon, so the proposed Fermi-Bubble signal cannot be forward-modeled at all.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-photon-mediated energy-transfer rate from excited SFDM halo states to starlight/CMB photons (transition rates between halo states times photon conversion probability for given epsilon), producing an emissivity map that can be compared to gamma-ray data.

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline exists for either constraint: Ly-alpha/satellite limits are only available as thermal-WDM templates that the card says must not be applied directly, and no Fermi-Bubble/gamma-ray likelihood with astrophysical foreground modeling is interfaced to the model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast Ly-alpha and Milky-Way satellite likelihoods through the charged-SFDM transfer function once gap_1 closes (e.g. via area-criterion or emulator-based transfer-function matching), and interface a gamma-ray sky likelihood with Fermi-Bubble templates for the emission channel.

route_step_status.reason: Freeze-in yields are computable with public tools such as micrOMEGAs, but the flavon-oscillation channel and the multi-species sequential-decay Boltzmann network have no public implementation.
Deriving dark masses, decay widths, and branching fractions from FN charges and the breaking scale is simple analytic tree-level work needing no dedicated code.

The relic target is a trivial comparison, but the BBN/CMB/indirect-decay recasts use literature curves without interfaced likelihoods and the Lyman-alpha constraint on boosted daughters rests on a free-streaming argument with no computed transfer function.

gaps.description: No public solver evolves the coupled system of out-of-equilibrium flavon production (freeze-in plus coherent oscillations) and sequential multi-species dark-fermion decays chi_i -> chi_j chi_k chi_l / chi_i -> chi_j q q; the paper's yields and two-component approximation exist only as private calculations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a multi-species Boltzmann yield network with flavon freeze-in and oscillation source terms and FN-charge-parameterized decay chains, either by extending the micrOMEGAs freeze-in framework or as a standalone code validated against the paper's relic-density contours and the sequential two-component limit.

gaps.description: No phase-space distribution f(p) has been derived for boosted daughter chi_1 fermions produced in late chi_2 decays, so the free-streaming suppression of small-scale power is only estimated with a qualitative lambda_FS argument and cannot be mapped to a transfer function or Lyman-alpha limit.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-produced daughter momentum distribution as a function of lifetime and mass hierarchy, feed it into CLASS/CAMB as a non-cold-DM species to compute the transfer function, and recast against Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints via existing WDM-style emulators or the area criterion.

gaps.description: No interfaced likelihoods exist for the late-decay probes: BBN light-element injection from long-lived flavons, CMB energy injection from intermediate-lifetime chi_i decays, and gamma-ray/neutrino limits on semi-visible decays are all applied only as literature exclusion curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Interface the decay-chain lifetimes and visible branching fractions to existing injection frameworks: an ACROPOLIS-class BBN code for tau_phi and visible flavon decays, ExoCLASS/DarkHistory for CMB energy injection from chi_i -> chi_j q q, and published decaying-DM gamma-ray/neutrino likelihoods for the semi-visible channel.

route_step_status.reason: Freeze-in yield calculations are supported by public tools such as micrOMEGAs, but the coherent flavon-oscillation production channel with thermal-correction misalignment is paper-specific and has no public implementation.
Mapping FN charges and the breaking scale to dark masses, widths, and branching fractions is straightforward analytic tree-level algebra requiring no dedicated tool.

The relic-density target comparison is trivial, but the BBN energy-injection lifetime recast for late flavon decays relies on published bound curves rather than an interfaced likelihood, and no likelihood was rerun.

gaps.description: No public solver computes the out-of-equilibrium flavon yield combining UV freeze-in from the SM bath with thermal-correction-driven flavon field oscillations, followed by decay into FN-charged dark fermions; the paper's yield formulas exist only as private calculations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the flavon-SM freeze-in collision terms and the coherent-oscillation yield in a coupled Boltzmann code, either by extending the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module with the FN-suppressed operators or as a standalone yield solver parameterized by (T_R, m_phi, Lambda, Q_FN^DM), validated against the paper's relic contours.

gaps.description: No interfaced BBN likelihood exists for late-decaying flavons with hadronic/visible energy injection; the constraint is applied only as literature exclusion curves, so the lifetime-branching boundary of the viable region cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Interface the flavon lifetime and visible branching fractions to an existing BBN energy-injection code (e.g. ACROPOLIS-class light-element solvers), mapping (tau_phi, Br_visible, m_phi) onto light-element likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: The mass-generation relations m_X = sqrt(2) f^2 / M_P and m_X = 3/R0 are closed-form analytic formulas from the primary paper requiring no tool.
The gravitational-production relic formula Omega_X/Omega_CDM as a function of m_X, H_i, and r A_s is given analytically in the primary paper and is pen-and-paper evaluable.
No KK-vector detection-rate calculation or recast of the branon gamma-ray/collider limits exists; the card states the related branon searches are context only and cannot be applied unchanged.

gaps.description: No rate calculation exists mapping the Planck-suppressed KK-vector coupling to the SM energy-momentum tensor onto gamma-ray or collider observables, so the branon search limits (which assume the unabsorbed branon EFT) cannot be recast onto this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the KK-vector annihilation/decay and collider missing-energy cross sections from the effective 4D massive-vector action with M_P-suppressed couplings, then recast the existing branon gamma-ray telescope and LEP/LHC missing-energy analyses onto the (f, m_X) plane with the corrected coupling structure.

gaps.description: No momentum distribution or coldness criterion has been derived for the gravitationally produced KK vector, and its isocurvature spectrum in the non-standard brane-world expansion is uncomputed, leaving the structure-formation behavior (transfer function, small-scale power) entirely unknown.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the mode-by-mode spectrum of the inflationary-produced massive vector (transverse and longitudinal modes) under the brane-world expansion law, derive the present-day momentum distribution and isocurvature power, and check the result against CMB isocurvature and small-scale structure coldness requirements.

route_step_status.reason: The paper gives only an order-of-magnitude analytic expression for the AD phase-fluctuation isocurvature amplitudes; the exact O(1) coefficients and unequal-phase-mass generalization needed for implementation are not derived.
CLASS and CAMB natively support baryon and CDM isocurvature initial conditions, including uncorrelated modes, covering this step's requirement.
Delta N_eff from a hidden-sector temperature ratio follows from standard entropy-counting formulas that are simple analytic work, and it is only needed if the sequestering assumption is relaxed.

gaps.description: The uncorrelated baryon and dark-baryon isocurvature spectra from independent Affleck-Dine phase fluctuations are known only at order-of-magnitude level with equal phase masses assumed; the exact O(1) coefficients and the unequal BAD/DAD phase-mass dependence needed to set Boltzmann-solver initial conditions are underived.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the isocurvature power spectra of the two AD phase fields during inflation (including spectral tilt from m_phase/H_I and independent phase masses for the visible and dark AD fields), yielding amplitude and tilt formulas that can be passed directly to CLASS/CAMB as uncorrelated baryon and CDM isocurvature initial conditions.

gaps.description: No likelihood analysis exists for the model's specific signature of jointly uncorrelated baryon plus dark-matter isocurvature; the constraint is applied only via the quoted Planck matter-isocurvature bound, which was derived for standard single-mode CDI templates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a Planck (and forecast CMB-S4/21-cm) likelihood analysis with CLASS/CAMB in Cobaya or MontePython, sampling the two uncorrelated baryon and CDM isocurvature amplitudes and tilts predicted by the AD phase spectra, to replace the quoted benchmark bound with a proper posterior on (H_I, m_phase/H_I, M).

route_step_status.reason: Deriving field masses, the critical value phi_c, and stability criteria from the hybrid potential is standard pen-and-paper analysis that needs no dedicated code.

Mapping the rapidly oscillating heavy field to a pressureless fluid with scalar coupling is a standard analytic time-averaging procedure documented in the paper and the coupled-dark-energy literature it builds on.

The authors adapted the public CLASS code for background and perturbation evolution, but the card indicates the model-specific patch is not publicly released, so no public solver covers the hybrid potential.

Public Planck, lensing, RSD, and weak-lensing likelihoods exist in MontePython/Cobaya, but the card lists them as unavailable for this model because no pipeline connects the hybrid-model predictions to them and no MCMC was run.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-solver implementation of the hybrid two-scalar dark sector exists: the authors' CLASS adaptation with the coupled scalar-fluid mapping (field-dependent DM mass, coupling function Q, modified G_eff) is not released, so CMB spectra, lensing potential, and P(k) cannot be recomputed for arbitrary hybrid-potential parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the hybrid-potential background and perturbation equations (pressureless fluid coupled to the light scalar, with coupling Q and field-dependent mass) as a public CLASS module, building on existing coupled-dark-energy CLASS forks, and validate against the paper's published CMB lensing and P(k) deviation figures.

gaps.description: No dedicated MCMC constraint pipeline exists for the exact hybrid potential: current bounds are only recast from related coupled-dark-energy analyses, and the card notes a dedicated run with Planck+lensing+BAO+SN+RSD+weak-lensing data is required to obtain posteriors on (M, g, lambda, phi_i, chi_i).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once the CLASS module exists, interface it with MontePython or Cobaya and run an MCMC over the hybrid-potential parameters against Planck 2018 (TT,TE,EE+lensing), BAO, SNe, and RSD/f sigma8 data, reproducing the coupled-dark-energy bounds as a validation limit.

route_step_status.reason: Two-body decay kinematics mapping (tau, masses, f) to daughter momentum and Delta N_eff in the instant-decay approximation is simple analytic work already done in the primary paper.

Generic public tools exist (CLASS decaying-CDM modules, ExoCLASS/AlterBBN/ACROPOLIS for energy injection, Planck likelihoods), but none is wired up for this massive relativistic-to-cold daughter with unfixed visible branching, and the card records that no likelihood was computed.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-solver implementation exists for this scenario's transient hot subcomponent: a massive daughter born relativistic at tau ~ 10^2-10^4 s that cools to cold DM by matter-radiation equality, with its nonthermal decay-produced momentum distribution; the public CLASS dcdm module treats massless daughters and cannot produce the H0 response or P(k) suppression for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS's decaying-CDM sector (or an existing two-body-decay branch with massive warm daughters) to evolve the exact decay-produced phase-space distribution f(q,t) as an ncdm-like species, parameterized by (tau, f, m_chi_prime/m_chi), including the phantom-like background option used by the paper.

gaps.description: No BBN/CMB energy-injection likelihood exists for the viable lifetime band: constraints on visible energy release at tau ~ 10^2-10^4 s were cited from generic late-decay studies but never recomputed for this model's branching fractions and abundance, so con_decay_bbn_cmb is a recast target without a likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run ACROPOLIS or AlterBBN for electromagnetic/hadronic injection and an ExoCLASS-style CMB energy-injection calculation over a (tau, f m_chi_prime/m_chi, visible branching) grid, and package the resulting light-element and CMB exclusion contours as a reusable likelihood.

gaps.description: No structure-formation likelihood exists for the hot fraction f: the limit f ~ 0.01 is an order-of-magnitude argument, with no transfer-function-based galaxy-clustering or Lyman-alpha likelihood computed for the decay-produced daughter velocity distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Using the extended Boltzmann solver from gap_1, compute P(k) suppression versus (f, k_fs) and confront it with galaxy power spectra at k = 0.02-0.2 h/Mpc and existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator constraints, recasting mixed cold+hot DM bounds onto (tau, f, mass ratio).

route_step_status.reason: The misalignment abundance Omega_A h^2(m_A, F_A, theta_0) follows from the standard analytic scaling given in the paper and requires no dedicated code.

Public ultralight-axion Boltzmann codes (axionCAMB/AxiCLASS) can compute the linear mixed fuzzy+cold transfer function at m_A ~ 10^-20-10^-19 eV, but the card supplies no mixed transfer function and no simulation-calibrated small-scale likelihood for a subdominant fuzzy fraction.
Inferring the local coherent axion field amplitude A(t) from m_A, F_A, and the local DM density is a standard analytic estimate in the coherent-field approximation.

Converting A(t) along photon paths into a pulsar-polarization-array observable requires a survey-specific cadence and noise model that the card says does not exist, and no public birefringence likelihood for pulsar arrays is identified.

The B+L-breaking operators are only treated qualitatively in the primary paper; the quantitative proton-decay operator coefficients are delegated to cited external work and not derived for this model's parameter choices.

Published Super-K/JUNO/Hyper-K nucleon-decay lifetime limits exist and comparing predicted rates to them is simple, but no experiment-specific likelihood or model-specific recast is included and the input rates from the operators step are not computed.

gaps.description: No simulation-calibrated small-scale structure likelihood exists for a mixed fuzzy+cold scenario with m_A ~ 10^-20-10^-19 eV and free axion fraction Omega_A/Omega_DM: existing fuzzy-DM bounds mostly assume 100 percent ULA dark matter, so the card's fractional suppression observable cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute linear mixed fuzzy+cold transfer functions with axionCAMB/AxiCLASS over (m_A, axion fraction), calibrate the nonlinear cutoff with mixed-DM fuzzy simulations (e.g. AxioNyx-type runs with a CDM component), and recast Lyman-alpha flux-power and Milky Way subhalo/stellar-stream likelihoods onto the fraction-mass plane.

gaps.description: No pulsar-polarization-array likelihood exists for the local oscillatory birefringence signal from the A F Ftilde coupling: the proposed probe lacks a signal template with survey cadence, noise model, and line-of-sight DM density treatment, so no exclusion region can be derived on (F_A, m_A).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a time-domain polarization-rotation signal model (amplitude ~ A(t)/F_A with frequency m_A) and a matched-filter likelihood using existing pulsar polarization datasets (e.g. NANOGrav/PPTA polarization products), including stochastic field-amplitude variation over coherence patches.

gaps.description: The proton-decay rates implied by the B+L-breaking operators that generate the EW axion mass are not derived for this model: branching ratios and operator coefficients as functions of the flavor charges and gravitino mass are delegated to cited work, so the nucleon-decay prediction cannot be confronted with data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the effective proton-decay operators from the model's B+L-breaking terms with the paper's flavor-symmetry charges, evaluate rates with standard lattice/chiral-Lagrangian nucleon matrix elements, and compare channel-by-channel with published Super-Kamiokande limits and JUNO/Hyper-K sensitivities.

route_step_status.reason: Kerr PBH mass/spin evolution and the spin-dependent lifetime factor are covered by semiclassical analytic formulas plus the public BlackHawk package cited in the card.
The public FRISBHEE package, named in the card, solves the coupled Friedmann/Boltzmann evolution for PBH domination, dilution, and Hawking-produced DM and radiation densities.

The Delta N_eff bookkeeping is analytic, but no public code maps the spinning-PBH domination history to the doubly peaked induced stochastic GW spectrum; the calculation exists only in the source papers, not as a released tool.

gaps.description: No public pipeline computes the induced stochastic gravitational-wave background for a spin-dependent PBH-dominated era: the doubly peaked ISGWB spectrum (from scalar perturbations amplified during PBH domination plus the abrupt spin-dependent evaporation transition) is not implemented in any released code coupled to the FRISBHEE background history.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the induced-GW kernel integrals for a PBH-dominated-to-radiation transition (extending a public scalar-induced-GW code such as SIGWfast) with the equation-of-state history and spin-dependent evaporation time taken from FRISBHEE/BlackHawk, and validate against the doubly peaked spectra in the source paper before comparing to LISA/ET sensitivity curves.

gaps.description: No warm-DM structure-formation likelihood exists for the Hawking-emitted phase-space distribution: the card notes lighter evaporation-produced particles need a distribution check before Lyman-alpha-like limits apply, but no released chain converts the FRISBHEE/BlackHawk emission spectrum into a transfer function and small-scale bound in the (M_PBH, a_star, m_chi) plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extract the redshifted Hawking phase-space distribution f(q) for Kerr PBHs from BlackHawk/FRISBHEE, feed it into CLASS as a non-cold ncdm species to obtain the transfer function, and recast published Lyman-alpha WDM mass bounds onto the (M_PBH, a_star, m_chi) parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: The dark binding energy is a simple analytic formula and the dark recombination history is computed inside the public class_twinadm author code cited in the card.
A public official-author CLASS implementation of atomic dark matter (github.com/srbPhy/class_twinadm) computes the CMB spectra and linear matter power over the card's aDM parameters.
The primary paper already ran MontePython MCMC with public Planck/BAO/SN/H0/S8 likelihoods against the CLASS aDM predictions, so this step is implemented with standard public tools.

The nonlinear small-scale step (Lyman-alpha, SHMF, dark-disk observables from DAO-suppressed transfer functions and atomic cooling) is explicitly left unimplemented by the primary paper and has no tool on the card.

gaps.description: No nonlinear structure-formation pipeline exists for minimal atomic dark matter: there are no simulations spanning the (f_D, r_DAO, alpha_D, m_pD, m_eD) space that evolve the DAO-suppressed initial conditions with dissipative dark-atom cooling, so the Lyman-alpha forest, subhalo mass function, halo-shape, and dark-disk observables warned about for f_D > 0.1 cannot be evaluated and the high-f_D posterior remains unconstrained at small scales.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body plus hydrodynamical simulations initialized with class_twinadm transfer functions, adding a dark-atom cooling/chemistry module for the dissipative component; calibrate an ETHOS-style halo and subhalo mass-function parameterization and a Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator on the runs, then recast existing Lyman-alpha and Milky Way satellite/SHMF likelihoods onto (f_D, r_DAO).

route_step_status.reason: No public solver evolves the PQ radial field with combined Coleman-Weinberg, thermal, and curvature corrections from inflation through reheating; tool_or_code is null and the card says dedicated numerical evolution is required.
Parametric-resonance and tachyonic axion/saxion production for this corrected potential has no released code and the card labels the treatment approximation-dependent.

CLASS/CAMB can propagate a mixed cold-plus-warm component via a non-cold relic with an arbitrary distribution function, but the card notes no transfer function was computed for the source-specific nonthermal spectrum, which must first be supplied.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a dedicated PQ-field evolution solver (homogeneous-mode ODEs plus linear mode functions for resonance/tachyonic bands, or an adapted CosmoLattice run for the nonlinear regime) parameterized by f_a, lambda, H_I, S_i, reheating temperature, thermal couplings, and curvature couplings, releasing yields and momentum spectra on a benchmark grid.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extract f(p) from the production simulation (gap_1) and feed it to CLASS as a non-cold-dark-matter species alongside a CDM component, tabulating transfer functions and half-mode scales versus warm fraction and axion mass.

gaps.description: Only an approximate analytic H_I/S_i isocurvature bound exists (likelihood_available is partial); there is no recast of the evolving-PQ-field isocurvature spectrum into the Planck isocurvature likelihood for mixed cold/warm axion components.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the model's isocurvature power spectrum from the PQ-field evolution and map it onto the Planck CDI-isocurvature likelihood (e.g. via CLASS + MontePython/Cobaya), including the ALP dark-matter fraction as a nuisance direction.

route_step_status.reason: The primary paper releases FRISBHEE, which computes time-dependent Hawking emission rates for arbitrary PBH mass and spin distributions using BlackHawk-style greybody spectra.
FRISBHEE solves the coupled Friedmann/Boltzmann equations for PBH, radiation, and dark-matter densities through evaporation, which is exactly this step.

Relic-density and pre-BBN evaporation checks can be applied as simple published cuts (Planck Omega_DM h^2, T_ev above roughly 10 MeV, N_eff bound), but no packaged BBN/CMB likelihood is interfaced to FRISBHEE outputs for extended distributions with late-evaporating tails.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Interface FRISBHEE's time-dependent entropy and radiation injection histories with a BBN code (AlterBBN or PRIMAT) and a Planck N_eff likelihood, so that distribution-tail-dependent light-element and Delta N_eff constraints are evaluated statistically rather than by a single evaporation-temperature cut.

gaps.description: The card records a smooth-cutoff suppression of small-scale power and a Lyman-alpha warmness check, but no transfer function computed from the actual Hawking-emitted phase-space distribution integrated over extended mass/spin distributions exists (distribution_function_available is only approximate, simulation_calibrated is no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the emitted f(p) by integrating greybody spectra over the PBH distribution and redshifting through the evaporation-modified expansion history, then feed it to CLASS as a non-cold species to derive transfer functions and a rigorous Lyman-alpha bound instead of the equivalent-warm-DM estimate.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs supports freeze-in abundance calculations from out-of-equilibrium decays, and the card names a micrOMEGAs/source Boltzmann setup for this step.
The dark-scalar lifetime from lambda_ds, theta, and m_phi is a tree-level analytic decay-width formula that needs no dedicated tool.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend CLASS with a decaying-species module that injects energy into the neutrino sector (plus a small electromagnetic branch handled by an exoCLASS/DarkAges-style deposition), parameterized by (tau_phi, f_phi, m_phi, branching fractions), and couple it to Planck and BBN (PRIMAT/AlterBBN) likelihoods in Cobaya or MontePython.

gaps.description: No detector-level recast exists for the displaced-vertex reach of a sterile neutrino with m_N < m_W whose branching includes the invisible N -> chi phi mode, nor a combined Higgs-invisible recast for this spectrum; the card notes detector acceptance and production modeling were not reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model in a MadGraph5 UFO, generate sterile-neutrino production with the modified branching ratios, and recast against existing displaced-vertex HNL analyses (ATLAS/CMS long-lived-particle searches and MATHUSLA/FASER projections), adding the Higgs invisible width as an analytic constraint on lambda_Hphi.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p) for chi from the out-of-equilibrium N decay kinematics (standard decay-produced spectra), compute the free-streaming length versus (m_chi, m_N, decay epoch), and map to a thermal-WDM-equivalent mass for Lyman-alpha comparison via CLASS ncdm.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the wall velocity for representative FOEWPT benchmarks using a public friction framework (e.g. WallGo or the local-thermal-equilibrium approximation coupled to the CosmoTransitions potential) and propagate it, with alpha and beta/H, through the standard sound-wave template and LISA-band sensitivity curves (PTPlot).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the micrOMEGAs sigma_SI output, rescaled by Omega_S h^2/0.120, into DDCalc likelihoods for XENON1T/PandaX-4T (and LZ), and encode the ATLAS doubly-charged-scalar mass limits as decay-assumption-dependent hard cuts in the same scan.

route_step_status.reason: The photon spectrum from the boosted mediator decay follows the primary paper's analytic spectral formulae, and Hazma provides the public sub-GeV final-state radiation and mediator-decay spectrum machinery the step names.
Converting dN_gamma/dE to a diffuse Galactic flux is a standard J-factor line-of-sight integral implemented in public indirect-detection tools and easily done analytically for a chosen halo model.

Archival COMPTEL/EGRET/INTEGRAL/Fermi limits exist only as digitized upper-limit curves; the card records likelihood_available: no, so exclusions are approximate comparisons rather than a proper likelihood.
micrOMEGAs natively supports Z3 semi-annihilation freeze-out and the paper itself states micrOMEGAs was used for the numerical relic density.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for the archival MeV diffuse gamma-ray data (COMPTEL, EGRET, INTEGRAL, Fermi-LAT low-energy) against which the semi-annihilation continuum is compared; the primary paper reports only cross-section bound curves, so limits on <sigma v>_semi cannot be recomputed with proper background/covariance treatment or extended to new benchmarks and halo models.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a gamLike-style likelihood module for the archival MeV diffuse spectra (energy binning, effective area, and background model per instrument) plus the projected e-ASTROGAM response, taking arbitrary dN_gamma/dE inputs so semi-annihilation spectra with one boosted mediator in the final state can be constrained directly.

route_step_status.reason: Checking anomaly cancellation of the U(1)_H charge assignments and the remnant Z2 is straightforward pen-and-paper algebra against the primary charge table.

Standard WIMP freeze-out solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) cover this thermal s-wave scenario, but no model implementation exists and the primary relies on an analytic s-wave estimate, so the full annihilation channel structure with inert scalars is not yet in any tool.
Delta a_mu and LFV branching ratios follow from the one-loop analytic formulas given in the source, standard exotic-lepton/scalar loop functions computable by hand or with generic packages.

Self-interacting-neutrino CMB Boltzmann fits exist in the literature the card cites (Planck G_eff fits), but the model-specific mapping and joint likelihood run were explicitly not performed, so only the generic external fit is reusable.

gaps.description: No model implementation (FeynRules/SARAH/CalcHEP files) exists for the hidden U(1)_H radiative-seesaw model, so the relic density rests on the paper's analytic s-wave estimate; coannihilation, p-wave pieces, and the full inert-scalar channel structure across the normal- and inverted-hierarchy mass windows (50-140 GeV vs 0.2-0.5 GeV) cannot be computed with public freeze-out machinery.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model (gauge sector, exotic fermions, inert scalars, neutral-fermion mixing) in SARAH/FeynRules, generate CalcHEP model files, and run micrOMEGAs for the relic density plus SPheno/FlavorKit for correlated g-2 and LFV observables, validating against the paper's scan windows.

gaps.description: The H0/self-interacting-neutrino observable has no model-specific pipeline: the mapping from (g_H, m_Z', neutral-fermion mixing) to the effective coupling G_eff and a CMB Boltzmann+likelihood fit were not performed, so the claim that the model realizes the strong (~5 MeV^-2) or moderate (~100 MeV^-2) Planck-fit regimes cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive G_eff(g_H, m_Z', mixing) for the light hidden Z' including the tree-level neutrino-mass consistency condition, then run a modified CLASS with self-interacting neutrinos coupled to MontePython/Cobaya against Planck+BAO, reusing the existing self-interacting-neutrino likelihood setups the card cites.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving annihilation amplitudes and the hSS coupling from the chiral EFT and top-partner embedding is pen-and-paper work using the primary-paper formulas.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the pNGB effective Lagrangian (S, H_2, dark top partners T, C_hS and y_L/y_R couplings, quartic SSVV terms) as a FeynRules model, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and validate against the paper's C_hS = 0 benchmark mass window of about 190-230 GeV.
