route_step_status.reason: Rate-versus-Hubble thermalization estimates are semi-analytic, but no public solver tracks dark-sector self-thermalization of the N/s bath at a given temperature ratio xi with full quantum statistics.

Public relic codes (micrOMEGAs with a decoupled-sector temperature ratio, DRAKE-style solvers) cover nonrelativistic Maxwell-Boltzmann freeze-out, but the full Fermi-Dirac/Bose-Einstein treatment with chemical potential needed for the relativistic freeze-out regime is not in any public tool.
The lifetime-versus-BBN check is analytic, but the card states the SM decay operator of the scalar is unspecified, so the input width cannot actually be computed.
No transfer-function calculation exists for this model's momentum distribution; the card marks it as not implemented and the structure observable explicitly awaits it.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver performs dark-sector freeze-out with full Fermi-Dirac/Bose-Einstein distributions and an effective chemical potential at arbitrary dark-to-visible temperature ratio xi, which is required for the relativistic-freeze-out regime and for the thermalization check of the N/s bath; existing codes assume Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics and/or an SM bath.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a decoupled-sector relic solver (e.g. the micrOMEGAs hidden-sector mode or a DRAKE-style dedicated integrator) to evolve the integrated Boltzmann equation with FD/BE phase-space distributions and a tracked chemical potential, parameterized by (M, m_s, lambda, xi), and validate against the paper's nonrelativistic limit.

gaps.description: The sterile-neutrino momentum distribution at freeze-out has not been propagated to a linear matter power spectrum, so no transfer function, free-streaming scale, or Lyman-alpha comparison exists for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the model's Fermi-Dirac distribution with effective chemical potential and temperature ratio xi into the CLASS ncdm module as a tabulated f(q), compute T(k) and the half-mode scale over the (M, xi) plane, and map onto thermal-WDM Lyman-alpha bounds for the constraint recast.

gaps.description: The higher-dimensional operator coupling the singlet scalar to the Standard Model is left unspecified, so the scalar lifetime entering the decay-before-BBN requirement cannot be computed from model parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify a minimal decay portal (e.g. a Higgs-portal mixing or dimension-five operator), derive the scalar width analytically, and delimit the coupling range that gives tau_s shorter than about one second while keeping the dark sector decoupled from the SM bath.

route_step_status.reason: The m_a(f_a) relation and DFSZ axion couplings are standard analytic QCD-axion formulas requiring no dedicated tool.

Misalignment abundance is computable with standard semi-analytic formulas or public solvers, but the topological-defect contribution needed in the post-inflationary scenario has no settled public calculation.
Astrophysical f_a bounds exist as published exclusion compilations, but no likelihood implementation is available (likelihood_available: no) and the card supplies only a broad 10^8-10^17 GeV window.
Diagonalizing the DFSZ scalar potential into masses and mixings is analytic and fully set up in the primary paper.
The one- and two-loop oblique-parameter and lepton g-2 contributions are analytic formulas given in the paper and standard 2HDM literature.
2HDM-type extra-Higgs recast tools exist publicly, but the card notes the quoted bounds are imported from MSSM/2HDM contexts and DFSZ-specific production and decay rates have not been prepared.

gaps.description: The axion relic density from topological-defect (string and domain-wall) decay is not calculable for this model with any public tool; the defect contribution in the post-inflationary PQ-breaking scenario carries order-of-magnitude uncertainty, leaving Omega_a h^2 undetermined beyond the misalignment estimate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt a parameterized defect-decay emission spectrum calibrated to large-scale axion-string network simulations, implement it alongside a standard misalignment solver, and propagate the simulation spread as a systematic band on Omega_a h^2(f_a); track convergence of ongoing community string simulations for the N_DW = 6 DFSZ domain-wall structure.

gaps.description: The astrophysical axion constraints are available only as a hard 10^8-10^17 GeV window on f_a, with no likelihood over (f_a, couplings) that reflects the DFSZ-specific photon and electron couplings.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble published stellar-cooling, SN 1987A, and haloscope exclusion curves into a joint likelihood evaluated at the DFSZ g_agamma and g_ae predictions, replacing the flat f_a window in the recast.

gaps.description: No DFSZ-specific collider recast exists: the extra-Higgs exclusions quoted in the card are borrowed MSSM/2HDM limits, and the model's charged, CP-even, and CP-odd scalar production and decay rates with the PQ singlet admixture have not been implemented in a recast chain.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the DFSZ scalar spectrum and Yukawa pattern (2HDM Type-II-like with PQ-singlet mixing) as effective-coupling input to HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals (HiggsTools), and validate against the paper's benchmark m_H+ and m_A regions before scanning.

route_step_status.reason: Solving for g_E from the s-wave coefficient a_eff at v_rel ~ 0 is an analytic formula given in the paper.
The relic abundance follows from the standard freeze-out approximation with the a_eff/b_eff velocity expansion and x_F ~ 24, an analytic calculation, though the truncated expansion limits precision.
The one-loop vectorlike-lepton contribution to Delta a_mu is a closed-form formula provided in the paper.

gaps.description: The Fermi-LAT Galactic-center GeV-excess constraint is applied only as an approximate 1-2 sigma window on (m_chi, <sigma v>) for the mu+ mu- channel; no proper GeV-excess likelihood with the muon-channel gamma-ray spectrum and halo-profile uncertainty is available in the route.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood from a published Fermi-LAT GCE spectral measurement, folding in the mu+ mu- annihilation spectrum (PPPC4DMID-style tables including final-state radiation) and marginalizing over the generalized-NFW profile parameters, replacing the fixed <sigma v>_FL window.

gaps.description: No numerical model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs) exists for the eta_I plus vectorlike-lepton Lagrangian; the relic density relies on a velocity expansion truncated at d-wave with fixed x_F ~ 24, which is untested against a full Boltzmann solution for this p-wave-sensitive leptophilic annihilation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the eta_I, eta_R, E_1/E_2 interaction Lagrangian in FeynRules, export to micrOMEGAs, and recompute Omega_DM h^2 over the scan ranges (m_1, m_2 in 90-1000 GeV, y_E, s_E in 0.01-1) to quantify the error of the analytic freeze-out approximation.

route_step_status.reason: The radiative decay rate Gamma proportional to sin^2(2theta) m_s^5 and line energy E_gamma = m_s/2 are simple closed-form analytic formulae requiring no dedicated code.

Public sterile-neutrino production solvers exist (e.g. sterile-dm for Dodelson-Widrow/Shi-Fuller production with lepton asymmetry), but the card names only a generic solver and no pipeline connects the MES A4 parameters to a momentum distribution and transfer function.
The card records likelihood_available: no for both the X-ray line and Ly-alpha constraints, tool_or_code is null, and the route is explicitly recorded as planned with no likelihood run.

gaps.description: No X-ray line-flux likelihood exists for the keV sterile-neutrino radiative decay signal in this model; the card records only summary mixing-angle bounds from XMM-Newton/Chandra/Suzaku/Swift/NuSTAR with no halo-profile marginalization or line-flux recast implemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published X-ray mixing-angle exclusion curves (or wrap public stacked-observation likelihoods such as the NuSTAR/XMM blank-sky analyses) into a line-flux likelihood in (m_s, sin^2(2theta)) with marginalization over the Milky Way and cluster density-profile uncertainty.

gaps.description: No Ly-alpha forest or phase-space likelihood is available for the nonthermal sterile-neutrino momentum distribution of this model; existing Ly-alpha likelihoods and emulators are calibrated on thermal-WDM transfer functions, and the mapping for Dodelson-Widrow versus Shi-Fuller spectra is production-mechanism dependent.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the production-solver momentum distribution into CLASS/CAMB to obtain the linear transfer function, then recast onto an existing Ly-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator (thermal-WDM-equivalent mapping validated against non-resonant and resonant spectra), and add the Tremaine-Gunn phase-space bound analytically.

gaps.description: No end-to-end production pipeline connects the MES A4 model parameters (mass matrices, active-sterile mixing, lepton asymmetry) to a sterile-neutrino momentum distribution, relic density, and transfer function; the card names only a generic 'sterile-neutrino production solver' with no implementation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap an existing public sterile-neutrino production code (e.g. sterile-dm for resonant/non-resonant oscillation production) with an interface that takes the MES A4 seesaw output (m_s, sin^2(2theta), lepton asymmetry) and returns f(p), Omega_s h^2, and a CLASS-ready momentum distribution.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the P proportional to rho^3 equation of state and the degeneracy condition from the hexic Hamiltonian is closed-form analytic work already displayed in the source, needing no dedicated tool.
The n=1/2 Lane-Emden profile with the source boundary conditions is a standard one-dimensional ODE integration that is trivially implementable despite the null tool_or_code.

No forward model exists from the superfluid rho(r) to shadow, strong-lensing, or lensed-GW observables; the card records that external ray-tracing/waveform code is required, none is named, and no likelihood is available.

gaps.description: No ray-tracing/imaging forward model exists that takes the three-body superfluid density profile (n=1/2 Lane-Emden core plus inner degeneracy-breakdown region) around an SMBH and predicts photon-sphere shifts, shadow size, or strong-lensing deflections.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing black-hole ray-tracing code (e.g. GYOTO or ipole) with a metric solved for the black hole plus the P_3 superfluid mass distribution, parameterized by (m, Lambda, rho_0, M_BH), and output shadow/lensing observables on a grid of model parameters.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the lensing amplification factor for the black-hole-plus-superfluid-core mass profile in the wave-optics regime and implement it in a GW lensing code, scanning source/lens geometry for Sgr A*-like systems.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists comparing the predicted three-body superfluid black-hole-environment observables to EHT shadow, strong-lensing, or GW data; the card records likelihood_available: no and the route as planned.

gaps.description: The zero-temperature, static, spherical, DM-only profile omits baryons, stellar scattering, accretion, and finite-temperature corrections, which the source explicitly defers; without these the profile cannot support observational exclusions near the black hole.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamic or semi-analytic galactic-nucleus models that add a realistic baryon potential, stellar heating, and accretion onto the black hole to the P_3 superfluid equation of state, and quantify the shift in r_deg and the inner profile relative to the idealized Lane-Emden solution.

route_step_status.reason: The quartic-contact P proportional to rho^2 equation of state and sound speed follow analytically from the two-body Hamiltonian and scattering length, needing no dedicated tool.

Filtering scan points on the relic-density target, out-of-equilibrium condition, and pre-BBN partner lifetime is a trivial data transform; only exact figure reproduction needs the original scan ranges.

gaps.description: No assembled forward-model pipeline converts (m_DM, tau_DM) into a Galactic plus extragalactic neutrino flux for this model: the flux_model step has null tool_or_code and requires external halo, electroweak-cascade, and exposure assumptions not packaged anywhere.

route_step_status.reason: The birefringence angle sourced by a homogeneous ADM current through the Chern-Simons operator is given by closed-form formulae rederived in the primary text.
Inverting the analytic alpha formula to the required g/M^2 band for the quoted Planck PR4 angle is trivial algebra.

Only the paper's self-described crude heavy-mediator mapping of the LZ limit exists (likelihood_available: approximate, robustness low), with no dedicated loop-level direct-detection recast or wrapped birefringence likelihood.

gaps.description: The loop-induced ADM-quark interaction from the dimension-six current-photon Chern-Simons operator has only an order-of-magnitude heavy-mediator estimate with simplified quark-charge/log factors; no dedicated loop-level matching and RG running to nuclear-recoil operators exists, so the claimed LZ exclusion of the 5 GeV benchmark is low-robustness.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the one-loop matching of J_mu A_nu Ftilde/M^2 onto quark-level effective operators, run them to the nuclear scale with standard DM EFT running tools (e.g. runDM/DirectDM), and evaluate the recoil rate against the LZ exposure with a standard direct-detection rate code.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the published Planck PR4 isotropic birefringence measurement (0.30 +/- 0.11 deg, foreground-improved 0.36 +/- 0.11 deg) as a Gaussian likelihood on alpha and chain it to the analytic alpha(M_chi, M, asymmetry) formula from step s1.

gaps.description: For the 5 keV warm benchmark no momentum distribution or linear transfer function exists (distribution_function_available: no, thermal_wdm_mapping unavailable), so the small-scale structure implications mentioned by the paper cannot be evaluated against warm-dark-matter bounds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Specify a concrete asymmetry-generation/production history for the 5 keV benchmark, derive f(p), compute the transfer function with CLASS/CAMB, and map to an equivalent thermal-WDM mass to apply existing Ly-alpha and subhalo-count bounds.

route_step_status.reason: No public Q-ball boundary-value solver exists; thin-wall profiles are analytic but the card explicitly requires numerical profiles beyond the thin-wall limit and lists the solver as a required-but-absent code resource.

EROS-2/OGLE point-lens limits and methodology exist (likelihood_available: partial) but no machine-readable survey-efficiency tables or likelihood adapted to extended Q-ball lenses were recovered.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a shooting/relaxation ODE solver for the radial Q-ball equation over the (potential parameters, omega) space, validated against the analytic thin-wall limit and the stability criterion dM/dQ, and release profile tables of M_Q(Q), R_Q(Q), and rho(r).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement an extended-lens magnification calculator (Abel-projected surface density plus lens-equation solve with finite source size), following existing finite-size PBH/boson-star microlensing recasts, and verify it reduces to the point-lens light curve as R_Q -> 0.

gaps.description: No machine-readable EROS-2/OGLE-IV survey-efficiency tables or event-rate likelihood usable for extended Q-ball lenses; existing MACHO/PBH limits are published only as point-lens f_DM exclusion curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize EROS-2 and OGLE-IV detection-efficiency curves and exposure, build an event-rate Poisson likelihood over a standard halo model that accepts arbitrary magnification thresholds from the finite-size kernel, and validate by recovering the published point-lens f_DM limits.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/CalcHEP model file for the full Z2-odd scalar spectrum plus Z' and run micrOMEGAs freeze-out including A_2 A_2 -> Z'Z' and suppressed electroweak channels, validating against the m_A2 = 271 GeV benchmark.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood or recast handling this model's inelastic gauge-mediated scattering with O(10) GeV splitting combined with a tunable Higgs-portal elastic component; existing xenon limits assume elastic SI scattering.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend DDCalc (or an equivalent xenon recast package) with the inelastic kinematic threshold for Delta m up to O(10) GeV plus the elastic Higgs-portal term, and recast LZ/XENONnT limits onto (m_A2, Delta m, lambda_portal).

route_step_status.reason: Checking that the Z8 charge assignments and VEV pattern leave a residual Z2 and the Nelson-Barr texture is a pen-and-paper group-theory/texture verification.

Published LZ/XENONnT SI limit curves apply directly to elastic scalar-portal scattering, but the card records only partial likelihood availability and no digitized detector likelihood for an exact recast.
The theta_bar and radiative-CKM estimates are analytic loop/operator formulas taken from the source and need no external tool.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP files) of the Z8 Nelson-Barr dark sector for a relic-density solver, so the eta_1 freeze-out including the Higgs-resonance dip and the H_1/H_2-mediated channels beyond the minimal singlet case cannot be recomputed or scanned.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the inert scalars eta_i, even scalars H_1/H_2, and portal couplings in FeynRules, export to micrOMEGAs, and validate by recovering the m_eta1 ~ 62.6 GeV Higgs-resonance dip and the H_1/H_2 annihilation regions reported in the paper.

gaps.description: theta_bar corrections and Nelson-Barr quality are handled with qualitative loop/operator-order estimates; no explicit higher-loop calculation of the induced theta_bar from the dark-sector Yukawas exists to confirm the nEDM-driven theta_bar < 1e-10 requirement across the WIMP-viable parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the leading two-loop contributions to the down-quark mass-matrix phase from the B, D_i, and dark-scalar sector and evaluate theta_bar numerically over the relic-viable scan points, mapping where the quality condition fails.

route_step_status.reason: The authors' multi-ULA effective-fluid Boltzmann code exists and works in the studied mass range, but the card says public availability is not stated, and public solvers such as axionCAMB/AxiCLASS handle only a single ULA species.

Press-Schechter-style halo-mass-function post-processing of a given linear power spectrum is standard semi-analytic math implementable directly, though its calibration for multi-ULA cutoffs is limited.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements the accurate effective-fluid approximation for multiple ultralight axion species plus a CDM component; the paper's multi-ULA code is not stated to be public, and existing public codes (axionCAMB, AxiCLASS) treat a single ULA only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend AxiCLASS (or axionCAMB) to N axion species with independent masses m_i and fractions Omega_ai using the paper's accurate effective-fluid approximation, validating against the published two-ULA transfer functions and the CDM limit.

gaps.description: No public Lyman-alpha likelihood or recast exists for multi-ULA transfer-function shapes; the cited 2e-20 eV bound assumes all-DM single-ULA spectra and the card marks likelihood availability unknown with recasting needed, while the WDM mapping is explicitly warned to be inaccurate.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator (e.g. hydrodynamic-simulation-based emulators used for WDM/ULA bounds) onto the multi-ULA transfer-function parameter space (m_i, f_i, m_r), rather than relying on approximate WDM-equivalent masses.

gaps.description: No strong-lensing or stellar-stream subhalo likelihood is available recast for the multi-ULA halo/subhalo mass function; the cited exclusions near 2.1e-21 eV assume a single all-DM ULDM transfer function.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast public subhalo mass-function likelihoods from strong-lensing flux ratios and stellar-stream gap statistics in terms of the computed multi-ULA halo mass function, parameterized by the effective mass m_e and fraction f_12 instead of a single-ULA cutoff.

gaps.description: Nonlinear structure-formation simulations for multi-ULA (and mixed ULA+CDM) cosmologies are lacking, so the halo and subhalo mass-function predictions rest on uncalibrated semi-analytic Press-Schechter mappings.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a suite of nonlinear simulations for two-ULA and ULA+CDM mixtures (N-body with multi-ULA initial transfer functions, plus targeted Schrodinger-Poisson or fuzzy-DM-solver runs where wave effects matter) to calibrate the halo-mass-function cutoff against the semi-analytic prediction.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled Gross-Pitaevskii/kinetic/Poisson equations are derived analytically in the primary paper via the Schwinger-Keldysh effective action, so this pen-and-paper step is complete.

tool_or_code is null and the card states no validated likelihood exists; Lyman-alpha and dwarf-galaxy limits require a recast of one-component FDM bounds that has not been performed.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public pseudo-spectral Schroedinger-Poisson code (e.g. AxioNyx or PyUltraLight-class solvers) with a coupled N-body or Vlasov module for the incoherent component plus the g^2 condensate-particle exchange terms, and validate against the CDM and pure-FDM limiting cases listed in the card's validation tests.

gaps.description: No linear Boltzmann/perturbation module implements the hybrid two-fluid (condensate plus particle) pressure and self-coupling terms needed to produce the model's matter power spectrum; the hydrodynamic-limit results exist only as paper-level calculations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled condensate and particle fluids with their effective sound speeds and quartic self-coupling g in CLASS (following the axionCAMB/ultralight-axion pattern), parameterized by m, g, and initial condensate fraction, reproducing the related hydrodynamic paper's perturbation examples as validation.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for confronting the hybrid transfer function with data: standard one-component FDM Lyman-alpha boson-mass bounds cannot be applied without mapping the full hybrid transfer function, and no dwarf-galaxy/core likelihood is packaged.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast Lyman-alpha flux-power constraints by feeding the hybrid model's transfer functions through an existing Lyman-alpha emulator/likelihood pipeline over the (m, g, condensate fraction) space, and build an analogous recast of soliton-core and dwarf-galaxy density-profile constraints.

route_step_status.reason: Public multifield background/perturbation solvers (PyTransport/MultiModeCode class) cover two nonminimally coupled fields, but this potential is not implemented in any of them and the transient ultra-slow-roll peak requires careful model-specific numerics.
The Planck 2018 likelihood is public (Planck/Cobaya) and the step just constrains A_s, n_s, r as in the source MCMC.

Gaussian threshold-collapse (Press-Schechter/peaks) mass-function estimates are semi-analytic and standard, but the card flags exponential sensitivity to small-scale statistics and no tool handles the model's non-Gaussian tail.
Second-order scalar-induced GW spectra from a given P_R(k) are computed by public codes (SIGWfast-class) and compared to published LISA/DECIGO/ET/CE/LIGO sensitivity curves.

gaps.description: No public implementation of this two-field nonminimally coupled potential in a multifield inflation solver, so the USR-amplified P_R(k) — the input to the CMB, PBH, and induced-GW steps — cannot be regenerated independently of the paper's private MCMC pipeline.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Einstein-frame two-field system (curved field-space metric from the nonminimal couplings plus the dimension-4 potential) in PyTransport or MultiModeCode, and validate against the paper's quoted n_s region and P_R peak amplitude ~1e-3.

gaps.description: The PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to the curvature-perturbation tail, but no calculation of the non-Gaussian P(zeta) tail from this model's multifield USR phase exists; Gaussian threshold-collapse estimates leave f_PBH uncertain by orders of magnitude.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the nonperturbative zeta distribution via stochastic delta-N on the two-field USR trajectory and feed it into a compaction-function threshold-collapse mass-function calculation, replacing the Gaussian Press-Schechter estimate.

gaps.description: No machine-readable likelihood for the PBH-fraction constraints (evaporation, microlensing, accretion, induced-GW) around the 1e-16 to 1e-11 M_sun window is attached, so whether a predicted mass function fits inside the open window cannot be scored quantitatively (card records likelihood_available: no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt a public f_PBH(M) constraint compilation (PBHbounds-style) and wrap it as an extended-mass-function likelihood that convolves the model's predicted mass function with each per-mass-bin bound.

route_step_status.reason: The annihilation amplitudes for N1 N1 -> JJ, Jh/H, leptons, and SM final states are tree/loop analytic formulas given explicitly in the paper's Lagrangian and used in its scan.

micrOMEGAs-class solvers handle this freeze-out and the paper itself used micrOMEGAs, but no public model implementation with the majoron channels is identified, so the relic scan is not reproducible as released.
The card states the nucleon amplitude is computed with micrOMEGAs, a public tool covering scalar-mediated SI scattering.
XENON1T and LZ spin-independent limit curves are published and directly applicable to standard elastic SI scattering, so the overlay is a straightforward comparison.
One-loop scotogenic cLFV rates use standard published formulae (and are implemented in public flavor tools), requiring only the model's Yukawas and masses.
Comparison against MEG-II/Mu3e current and projected branching-ratio limits is a simple published-number comparison.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Build and release a FeynRules/CalcHEP model file with the singlet fermions, inert doublet, B-L singlet, majoron, and scalar mixing, run micrOMEGAs freeze-out, and validate by recovering the vanilla scotogenic overabundance when the majoron channels are switched off.

route_step_status.reason: Standard coherent-oscillation misalignment evolution of a(t) and Omega_a is simple analytic cosmology covered by textbook formulae, so the null tool_or_code is not a blocker.

The primary derives the linear-response Chern-Simons susceptibility analytically, but only in Minkowski spacetime as a proof of principle; the expanding-universe version needed for cosmological observables is explicitly deferred.

Public CMB birefringence measurements and EB/TB rotation likelihoods exist, but the card states the dedicated cosmological propagation from the condensate to a rotation angle beta(z) is not supplied, so the recast cannot yet be executed for this model.

gaps.description: The renormalized Chern-Simons condensate is computed only in Minkowski spacetime at leading order in g; no derivation exists of the induced E dot B condensate and photon polarization rotation angle beta(z) in an expanding FRW background with the thermal photon bath redshifting, which is the quantity every CMB observable needs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the paper's linear-response susceptibility calculation to an FRW background below the EFT cutoff, deriving beta(z) from the oscillating a(t) condensate including the vacuum-subtraction renormalization, and validate against the paper's high-temperature Minkowski limit.

gaps.description: No packaged pipeline maps (m_a, g, axion fraction) to CMB EB/TB spectra and a birefringence likelihood for this model; the con_cmb_birefringence_recast constraint is marked recast-required with only a partial likelihood and no model-specific beta(z,nu) computation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once beta(z) is derived (gap_1), implement the rotation in a modified CLASS/CAMB polarization module and recast the published Planck/WMAP isotropic-birefringence rotation-angle posteriors (Minami-Komatsu-style EB analyses) into a likelihood over g and m_a.

gaps.description: The structure-formation floor on the ultralight axion fraction (con_ultralight_axion_structure_floor) is only a generic review-level bound, not recast for this model's mass-fraction parameter space; the card's transfer-function shape is unknown so the mapping is not yet quantitative.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run axionCAMB (or the ULA branch of CLASS) over the model's (m_a, axion fraction) grid and recast existing CMB plus Lyman-alpha ultralight-axion bounds onto the misalignment parameter space, since the condensate behaves as a standard ULA for structure formation.

route_step_status.reason: The vector relic abundance and curvaton dilution factor follow the paper's closed-form homogeneous-background formulae, a pen-and-paper scan that needs no dedicated tool.

Planck isocurvature and statistical-anisotropy bounds are published, but no packaged likelihood exists for a statistically anisotropic dark-matter isocurvature component, so the comparison is only an approximate recast of quoted limits.

gaps.description: No public likelihood evaluates a nearly scale-invariant, statistically anisotropic dark-matter isocurvature spectrum (the model's smoking-gun signature) against CMB data; the card's cons_2303_cmb_iso_aniso is only 'approximate' and the route caveat notes a modern likelihood update is needed for current exclusions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the quadrupolar (g_*-type) anisotropic isocurvature transfer in a modified CLASS/CAMB plus a Planck-likelihood MCMC recast, extending the existing Planck axion-isocurvature and statistical-anisotropy analyses to the correlated anisotropic CDM-isocurvature case parameterized by (m_A, H_inf, R_A, Gamma_chi).

gaps.description: The paper's viable-region contours exist only as figures; no reusable scan code maps (m_A, H_inf, R_A, Gamma_chi, kinetic-function exponent) to Omega_A, isocurvature power, and anisotropy amplitude, so the registry cannot re-evaluate the allowed region or extend it to new data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's analytic abundance and perturbation formulae in a small public scan package (Python) that reproduces the quoted m_A = 1e-21 eV to 1 eV window and H_inf/R_A boundary, exposing the derived isocurvature and g_* amplitudes for downstream likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: The QCD axion misalignment abundance and bubble overdensity follow standard analytic formulae given in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code is not a blocker.

Public compilations of PBH mass-fraction constraints exist (e.g. the PBHbounds compilation), but no assembled recast connects this model's clustered, high-mass PBH and minicluster populations to those external limits.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run dedicated lattice/N-body simulations of large-misalignment axion overdensities through the QCD mass turn-on (extending existing large-misalignment minicluster simulations) to calibrate the collapse threshold delta_c and the bubble-to-PBH/minicluster mass functions as functions of f_a, N, and the bubble theta_i distribution.

gaps.description: No code maps the model parameters (f_a, N, theta_i distribution, bubble fraction) to Omega_a, the bubble statistics, f_PBH(M), and a comparison against compact-object constraints; the route's required PBH-constraint recast is currently unimplemented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's vacuum-selection probability and misalignment formulae in a small pipeline that outputs f_PBH(M_PBH) and feeds it to the public PBHbounds constraint compilation (supermassive-window limits from CMB accretion, dynamical friction, and mu-distortions), validating against the quoted O(5e5) M_sun minimum PBH mass at f_a ~ 1e16 GeV.

gaps.description: No observational likelihood exists for the predicted clustered axion-minicluster population; existing minicluster microlensing analyses (e.g. HSC/OGLE) assume standard post-inflationary minicluster spectra, not the rare high-density bubble-seeded population, and the card notes no minicluster likelihood was found.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing microlensing (HSC, OGLE) and photometric-survey minicluster constraints for the bubble-seeded mass-and-density spectrum produced by gap_1's calibrated collapse model, packaging the result as a likelihood over (f_a, N, bubble fraction).

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level annihilation cross sections into WW/ZZ, HH, and Dirac-neutrino final states follow the source's analytic formulae from the given Lagrangian, a standard pen-and-paper computation.

Mature thermal relic calculators (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) handle inert-doublet-like scalars including coannihilation, but no public model implementation of the Dirac scotogenic scalar sector exists on the card, so the tool cannot be run as-is.

Public xenon likelihoods (e.g. DDCalc with LZ) cover the tree-level Higgs-quartic scattering, but the decisive electroweak gauge-loop sigma_SI for doublet-dominated eta1 is uncalculated for this model, as the primary paper itself leaves open.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/UFO/CalcHEP files) of the Dirac scotogenic scalar sector exists, so micrOMEGAs or MadDM cannot compute the relic density through the gauge-annihilation window, coannihilation with eta2/eta3/eta_plus, or tree-level sigma_SI for benchmark scans.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules model of the eta-doublet plus singlet plus Dirac N_Dk sector with the card's potential and Yukawas, export to CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs, and validate against the source benchmarks (thermal target 3e-26 cm^3/s and the lambda3+lambda4+lambda5 ~ 1e-5 suppression).

gaps.description: The one-loop electroweak gauge-mediated spin-independent scattering cross section for doublet-dominated eta1 (including singlet mixing through the trilinear A term) has not been computed; the primary only expects it to be 'challenging', yet it is the decisive viability test against the quoted xenon bound of 6.5e-48 cm^2.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt the established Hisano-et-al electroweak one-loop direct-detection formalism (as applied to the inert doublet model) to eta1 with arbitrary doublet-singlet mixing, implement it on top of the gap_1 model files, and confront the result with the LZ likelihood via DDCalc.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level Higgs-portal annihilation rates and sigma_SI follow the source's closed-form formulae in (m_eta1, lambda_7), standard pen-and-paper Higgs-portal calculations.

Translating sigma_SI into a lambda_7 upper bound is a direct comparison against the published xenon limit, and public direct-detection likelihoods (DDCalc with LZ/XENONnT) cover this generic spin-independent Higgs-portal scattering.
The Higgs-funnel bb exclusion uses standard indirect-detection limits, and the public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods apply directly to a thermal bb annihilation rate below 300 GeV.

gaps.description: The exclusion of the singlet-dominated eta1 rests on analytic estimates at quoted benchmarks; no public model implementation of the Dirac scotogenic scalar sector exists for micrOMEGAs/MadDM, so the relic density, funnel region, and exclusion boundary cannot be re-derived quantitatively or re-tested under relaxed assumptions (subcomponent DM, coannihilation with eta2/eta3).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/CalcHEP implementation of the eta-doublet plus singlet plus Dirac N_Dk sector (shared with the doublet-DM variant of this model), run micrOMEGAs relic and direct-detection scans, and verify the source's lambda_7 < 4.8e-5 bound near 100 GeV and the singlet nonviability conclusion.

route_step_status.reason: The trapped-misalignment release time and resonance condition follow from analytic formulas given in the paper, so a null tool_or_code is not blocking.

Public axion-gauge-field lattice frameworks (e.g. CosmoLattice-type codes) exist, but no simulation covering the trapped-release benchmark with backreaction has been run, and the card notes lattice work is left to the future.
Redshifting a source spectrum to present-day GW frequency/amplitude and Delta N_eff is standard analytic cosmology once the source spectrum from s2 exists.
The card explicitly lists both the GW detector likelihood and the N_eff likelihood as unavailable, with no tool named.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run 3+1D lattice simulations of the coupled axion-dark-photon system (extending an existing axion-gauge-field lattice framework such as CosmoLattice) initialized from the trapped-then-released axion configuration, scanning alpha/f_a, m_a/H_release, and trapping-potential heights, and output the dark-photon spectrum, polarization fractions, and final energy partition.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists to compare the predicted stochastic GW background and Delta N_eff from trapped-axion dark-photon production against PTA/interferometer sensitivities and CMB dark-radiation bounds; kinetic-mixing bounds on a massive dark photon also require recasting.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a likelihood step from published pieces: evaluate the predicted Omega_GW(f) against NANOGrav/EPTA free-spectrum posteriors and LISA/ET power-law-integrated sensitivity curves, use the Planck N_eff posterior for the Delta N_eff component, and recast existing dark-photon kinetic-mixing exclusion tables for the massive stable case.

route_step_status.reason: The paper solved the dEGB Friedmann-plus-scalar system numerically, but no public integrator for the dilatonic Gauss-Bonnet background with BBN boundary conditions was identified, so the step must be re-implemented.
Standard thermal relic solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, DarkSUSY) exist and are public, but they assume a standard radiation-dominated H(T) and need modification to ingest the dEGB expansion history.

Public channel-by-channel indirect-detection limits (Fermi dwarf likelihoods, Planck annihilation bound) exist for the <sigma v>-m_chi comparison, but the compact-object dEGB bounds are only summarized in the paper and the card marks recasting as needed with at best partial likelihoods.

gaps.description: No public code integrates the dilatonic Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet background (scalar field with f(phi)=alpha exp(gamma phi) coupled to R_GB^2) from pre-freeze-out temperatures to BBN and feeds the resulting H(T) into a WIMP freeze-out Boltzmann solver; every observable on the card depends on this modified expansion history.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a standalone ODE integrator for the dEGB Friedmann and scalar equations with (phi_BBN, phidot_BBN) boundary conditions enforcing BBN recovery, and couple its H(T) output to micrOMEGAs' modified-cosmology (alternative expansion) interface or to a custom freeze-out solver, validated by recovering the standard 3e-26 cm^3/s cross section when alpha goes to zero.

gaps.description: No combined likelihood exists to confront a dEGB parameter point with the joint constraint set: channel-specific indirect-detection limits are only partially available, the BBN-recovery requirement has no numerical likelihood, and the late-universe compact-object bounds on (alpha, gamma) are summarized rather than reproduced as usable exclusion data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a recast pipeline that combines published Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods and the Planck CMB annihilation bound per channel with digitized dEGB compact-object exclusion contours from the GW literature, plus a simple BBN consistency criterion on H(T_BBN), so allowed/excluded regions become reproducible likelihood evaluations.

route_step_status.reason: The paper computed mode functions and f_chi(q,t) numerically, but no public release of the inflationary-plus-reheating mode-function integrator was identified, and the card's agent notes say the paper-specific numerical setup still needs implementation.
Mapping the computed phase-space distribution to a warm-DM-equivalent cutoff via its second moment is a simple analytic transform, so a null tool_or_code is not blocking.

The Planck beta_iso < 0.038 bound and published thermal-WDM Lyman-alpha limits exist as usable contours, but no assembled recast pipeline applies them jointly with the relic target, and the card lists all three likelihoods as only partially available.

gaps.description: No public solver computes spectator-scalar mode functions through inflation and reheating for the phi^2 chi^2 inflaton coupling in Starobinsky/T-model potentials, outputting the occupation numbers f_chi(q), the isocurvature spectrum P_S(k) down to the CMB pivot, and the relic abundance; all three observables depend on this upstream calculation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement (or obtain and release) a mode-by-mode integrator for the chi field on the inflaton background: evolve the Starobinsky/T-model background plus perturbative reheating, solve the mode equations with effective mass m_chi^2 + lambda_phi_chi phi^2 from horizon exit through the end of reheating, and tabulate f_chi(q), P_S(k), and Omega_chi h^2 over the (m_chi, lambda_phi_chi, T_reh) grid, validated against the paper's m_chi ~ 0.5 H_* and 0.34 meV benchmarks.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the tabulated f_chi(q) into CLASS as a non-cold-dark-matter species with an arbitrary phase-space distribution to compute the exact linear transfer function, then evaluate it against a Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator/likelihood (e.g. a Sherwood/eBOSS-calibrated WDM-area emulator) instead of the thermal-WDM equivalence.

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the trans-Planckian collision tail of the thermal plasma into a black-hole formation rate is an analytic calculation given in the paper, needing no dedicated code.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the redshifted phase-space distribution f(q) from the spin-dependent Hawking spectra of the instantaneously evaporating black-hole population, feed it into CLASS or CAMB as a non-cold species with a tabulated distribution, and recompute the half-mode scale and Lyman-alpha-equivalent mass floor across the (T_RH, M_min, m_dm, spin) space.

gaps.description: The high-reheat CMB target (high-frequency gravitational-wave background from the near-Planckian thermal plasma contributing to N_eff) has no step in the forward-model chain and no calculational pipeline or likelihood: the card marks the likelihood as unknown and recasting as needed, so the observable cannot currently be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the thermal-plasma graviton-emission calculation to obtain Omega_GW(T_RH) integrated over the expansion history, convert it to Delta N_eff, and compare against the Planck N_eff posterior and forecast CMB-S4-class sensitivities as a simple likelihood step appended to the route.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reuse the thermal-plasma graviton-emission pipeline needed for the companion HBBH evaporation model: compute Omega_GW(T_RH), convert to Delta N_eff, and compare against the Planck N_eff posterior and forecast next-generation CMB sensitivities as an appended likelihood step.

route_step_status.reason: Yukawa transfer cross sections are standard analytic/tabulated results and the card states the public code CLASSICS is used for elastic self-scattering in this regime.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a coupled Boltzmann solver tracking the dark-sector temperature xi(T) and the chi, anti-chi, A', S_1 number densities with secluded annihilation to dark mediators (inputs Y_chi, alpha', xi_ini, m_chi, m_A'), for example by extending an existing hidden-sector relic framework, and validate against the paper's r_infinity examples and the Delta N_eff < 0.29 room.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-dark-Higgs finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce solver), compute T_n, alpha_PT, and beta/H over the MeV-scale transition benchmark, and feed them into standard sound-wave/bubble-collision GW spectral templates compared against PTA and microHz-band sensitivities.

route_step_status.reason: The phase-space-integrated form-factor function f(s) for each multipole operator is a closed-form analytic computation within the EFT, so the null tool_or_code does not block it.

Standard stellar/SN energy-loss criteria and environment models exist and the paper implemented them, but no public code computes vector pair-production emissivity for these multipole operators, so the step must be re-derived rather than run.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM-class) can handle freeze-out once the operators are implemented, but no implementation of this vector-multipole EFT exists and UV-dominated freeze-in with reheating dependence needs a custom Boltzmann treatment.

The card notes experiment-specific direct/indirect likelihoods were not extracted, so only digitized published limits can be overlaid, not likelihood-grade recasts of the momentum-dependent scattering.

gaps.description: No public model implementation of the complex-vector electromagnetic multipole EFT (dimension-five dipoles, dimension-six quadrupole/anapole/toroidal/charge-radius operators) exists in any relic-abundance code, so neither the freeze-out lines nor the UV-dominated, T_RH-sensitive freeze-in lines can be reproduced outside the paper.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the multipole-vector Lagrangian in FeynRules and export to micrOMEGAs or MadDM for freeze-out, and add a light-weight freeze-in Boltzmann module with UV-dominated production integrated from T_RH (benchmarks 0.1-1 GeV), validating against the paper's operator-by-operator relic lines.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the vectorlike-fermion and Z_2-odd scalar loop contributions in a public flavor package (e.g. flavio or SPheno/FlavourKit via a SARAH model file) and combine with current B-physics and muon g-2 measurements into a joint chi-square usable in the scan.

route_step_status.reason: SPheno/FlavourKit are public tools and were used in the source workflow, but the Z8 hybrid scoto/type-II model implementation (SARAH model files with the specific flavour texture) is not publicly released, so the step cannot be rerun as-is.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct the model in SARAH from the published Lagrangian and Z8 charge assignments, generate SPheno/FlavourKit and CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model files, and validate against the paper's quoted relic windows (near 60 GeV and 68-90 GeV) and cLFV benchmark rates before public release.

gaps.description: No joint statistical pipeline exists combining the Planck relic-density target, the LZ spin-independent limit, LEP Z-width, LHC Higgs invisible/diphoton data, and MEG/MEG II cLFV bounds for this model; the source applies constraints as sequential pass/fail cuts on scan points rather than a likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a GAMBIT-style or standalone composite likelihood using DDCalc for the LZ limit, HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals for the Higgs sector, the LEP Z-width measurement, and published cLFV limits, taking sigma_SI, branching ratios, and Omega h^2 from the gap_1 model implementation.

route_step_status.reason: The N1 radiative decay rate and photon luminosity follow from the standard analytic formula in (m_s, sin^2 2theta), which the card names explicitly.
The line-of-sight decay flux integral over a halo profile is a standard, well-documented data transform (D-factor calculation) that needs only an assumed profile and field of view.

Public X-ray spectra and fitting tools (XMM/Chandra/Hitomi, XSPEC-class fitters) exist and likelihood_available is 'partial', but there is no unified released likelihood reconciling the claimed 3.55 keV detections with the stacked non-detections for this benchmark.

Public resonant-production codes named in the card (Venumadhav16 sterile-dm and Ghiglieri15) compute the N1 momentum distribution and L_6 in exactly this regime, though the card flags code-to-code systematics.
CLASS/CAMB accept tabulated non-thermal ncdm distribution functions and were used in the source to obtain transfer functions and M_hm in the linear regime.

gaps.description: The N1 momentum distribution, required lepton asymmetry L_6, and derived half-mode mass differ depending on whether Venumadhav16 or Ghiglieri15 production code is used and on the CAMB vs CLASS solver choice, and the paper shows thermal-relic WDM mappings can misestimate the true N1 power spectrum; no calibrated cross-code error budget exists.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Perform a controlled code-comparison of the Venumadhav16 and Ghiglieri15 production calculations (fixed neutrino-interaction rates, fixed cosmology) coupled identically to CLASS ncdm input, publish the resulting (m_s, sin^2 2theta, L_6) -> f(p) and M_hm tables with quantified systematic bands, and deprecate the thermal-WDM equivalent-mass shortcut for resonant spectra.

gaps.description: No unified public X-ray likelihood exists for the 7.1 keV benchmark that jointly treats the reported 3.55 keV detections (clusters, M31, Milky Way) and the strongest non-detection limits with consistent instrument responses and halo D-factors; the card records a disputed constraint landscape with only partial likelihood availability.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a joint spectral likelihood over the archival XMM/Chandra/Hitomi datasets (and XRISM velocity-resolved spectra as they arrive) with shared nuisance parameters for halo profiles and instrumental lines, released as an XSPEC/3ML-compatible module returning constraints in the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane.

gaps.description: Structure-formation constraints on this model are applied only through the approximate half-mode-mass summary statistic; no released Milky Way satellite or Lyman-alpha likelihood consumes the full resonant (non-thermal) N1 transfer function directly, so limits inherit the thermal-WDM mapping error the paper warns about.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing satellite-count likelihood (e.g. the Milky Way subhalo framework used for WDM limits) and a Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator to accept arbitrary suppressed transfer functions, then evaluate them on the gap_1 calibrated resonant T(k) grid rather than on thermal-relic equivalents.

route_step_status.reason: The Mukhanov-Sasaki mode functions and tree-level P_R(k) for the piecewise transient constant-roll history are computed analytically in the primary paper; null tool_or_code is not blocking for this pen-and-paper step.

The one-loop perturbativity check exists as an analytic calculation, but the paper evaluates only representative cubic-action loop terms, so the validation does not cover the complete one-loop correction.

Public scalar-induced GW integrators and PBH abundance calculators exist for Gaussian or fNL-parameterized spectra, but no pipeline propagates the constant-roll squeezed non-Gaussian tail and the required collapse-threshold/reheating assumptions for this specific spectrum, and no numerical computation was done in the source.

gaps.description: No public pipeline maps the transient constant-roll curvature power spectrum plus its squeezed bispectrum to a PBH mass function beta(M) and a scalar-induced Omega_GW(f): existing abundance calculators assume Gaussian or simple fNL statistics, while PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to the model's non-Gaussian tail.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the paper's analytic P_R(k) and bispectrum to a non-Gaussian PBH abundance calculation (compaction-function/threshold statistics with the constant-roll tail, extending an open abundance code) and to a public induced-GW integrator such as SIGWfast, parameterized by (eta, phase duration, transition times, H_inf) with explicit collapse-threshold and reheating settings.

gaps.description: The astrophysical and cosmological constraints on the light Higgs-mixed scalar and the dark matter decay (SN1987A, HB-star cooling, invisible meson decays, diffuse X-ray limits) are only available as digitized literature curves; no combined machine-readable likelihood over (m_phi, theta, m_chi) exists for joint scans with the relic constraint.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the SN1987A, HB-star, meson-decay, and diffuse X-ray exclusion curves used by the paper into interpolated one-sided likelihoods (following the standard light-scalar compilation format) so the relic-versus-signal tension can be scanned as a joint fit.

route_step_status.reason: The pNREFT bound-state-formation and dipole-transition rates up to n about 1000 are a published framework realized only in the authors' private numerical implementation; no public rate code covers this high-n network.

The coupled bound-state plus mediator-yield Boltzmann network exists as the paper's private calculation; public relic codes (micrOMEGAs, DRAKE) do not include excited-bound-state ladders or the lifetime-dependent superWIMP depletion.

The relic-density comparison is trivial, but the Lyman-alpha transfer-function recast and the long-lived-collider recast are explicitly not implemented (card caveat; likelihood_available no/partial for those constraints).

gaps.description: No public code computes high-n bound-state formation, bound-to-bound electric/chromoelectric dipole transitions (n up to 1000), and the coupled mediator-yield Boltzmann network for the colored scalar t-channel mediator, so the excited-state relic depletion and its mediator-lifetime dependence cannot be reproduced or scanned outside the private implementation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement the excited-bound-state rate calculation and network solver as a public package (e.g. extending DRAKE-style yield equations with the paper's Coulombic BSF/transition rate tables), validated against the paper's order-of-magnitude relic reduction and n_max convergence tests.

gaps.description: The nonthermal dark matter momentum distribution from late mediator decay is not derived or tabulated, so the claimed Lyman-alpha relaxation cannot be turned into a quantitative bound; the paper states the relaxation only qualitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(q) for dark matter produced by decays of the depleted mediator population (including bound-state fractions), feed it through CLASS as a non-cold relic transfer function, and apply an area-criterion or emulator-based Lyman-alpha likelihood to map the viable (m_chi, tau_mediator) region.

gaps.description: No dedicated collider recast exists for the long-lived colored charged mediator in the cosmologically favored lifetime and compression region; limits are only mapped approximately from adjacent t-channel LLP studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast HSCP, displaced-vertex, and soft-object searches for the down-type colored scalar with SModelS/CheckMATE LLP modules over (m_tilde_q, Delta m, tau_mediator), targeting the superWIMP-viable lifetime band.

route_step_status.reason: The retarded self-energies and damping rates below the electroweak crossover are closed-form real-time finite-temperature results derived analytically in the paper.

Only the paper's coarse momentum/temperature integration exists; a full momentum-dependent Boltzmann scan is deferred and public sterile-neutrino codes (e.g. Dodelson-Widrow oscillation solvers like sterile-dm) do not implement thermally corrected HNL/Higgs decay freeze-in.

X-ray line limit curves exist in the literature but no machine-readable likelihood is identified, and the Lyman-alpha/phase-space recast requires the production-specific distribution function that is only approximately available (tool_or_code null).

gaps.description: No public momentum-dependent Boltzmann code computes freeze-in production of keV sterile neutrinos from HNL, Higgs, and weak-boson decays with the paper's thermal self-energy corrections; existing sterile-neutrino tools implement oscillation (Dodelson-Widrow/Shi-Fuller) production only, and the paper itself used a coarse integration with the full scan left to future work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's finite-temperature production rates Gamma_s(T,p) in a momentum-grid freeze-in solver (extending a framework like sterile-dm or a ULYSSES-style density-matrix code) to output f_DM and the full distribution function over the seesaw parameter space.

gaps.description: No production-specific structure-formation likelihood exists: Lyman-alpha, satellite-count, and phase-space bounds are quoted from thermal-relic or DW-based mappings, but constraining this model requires propagating its colder freeze-in distribution function to the matter power spectrum.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the computed f(q) benchmarks into CLASS as non-cold dark matter to get transfer functions, then apply Lyman-alpha forest likelihoods/emulators and Milky Way satellite-count likelihoods, reporting mass bounds as a function of the freeze-in channel mix and f_DM.

gaps.description: X-ray line constraints on (m_N1, theta) are applied only as literature exclusion curves; no machine-readable, target-by-target line likelihood (dwarfs, clusters, Milky Way blank sky) is attached for joint scans with the freeze-in abundance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compile published NuSTAR, XMM-Newton, and Chandra sterile-neutrino line limits into an interpolated likelihood over (m_N1, sin^2 2theta) rescalable by the model's f_DM, for direct use in the registry scan.

gaps.description: Production above the electroweak crossover via 2-to-2 scatterings is not computed (the paper's thermal decay-rate treatment applies only below T_SSB about 160 GeV), leaving the high-temperature contribution to the abundance and spectrum of heavy-HNL scenarios undetermined.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the symmetric-phase 2-to-2 and 1-to-2 production rates (following established thermal leptogenesis/HNL rate calculations at T > T_SSB) and add them to the same freeze-in solver so the abundance is complete across the crossover.

route_step_status.reason: The axion interaction-rate integration through LTR/EMD/kination eras is a paper-specific calculation with no released public code, though the rates and method are documented.
Projecting the axion yield and temperature to Delta N_eff and Omega_a^thermal is standard analytic bookkeeping (relativistic-decoupling formulae) requiring no dedicated tool.

CLASS/CAMB can treat a thermal axion as a non-cold (ncdm) species with a specified temperature, but the card provides no configured pipeline or LSS likelihood for the nonstandard-history axion temperature.
The misalignment abundance in a kination-like history is a standard analytic estimate that the paper itself performs with pen-and-paper formulae.
Same paper-specific thermal-production calculation as route_thermal_axion_history/s1; no public implementation of the nonstandard-history axion thermalization solver exists.
No public likelihood or Boltzmann pipeline exists for a mixed cold-misalignment plus warm-thermal axion population; the card notes an external mixed-DM LSS analysis is needed and none is identified.

gaps.description: No public code computes thermal axion production (gluon- and photon-coupling rates) through nonstandard pre-BBN expansion histories (low-temperature reheating, early matter domination, kination); the interaction-rate integration exists only as the primary paper's private calculation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's axion interaction rates and modified Hubble/entropy evolution as an open momentum-averaged Boltzmann solver (e.g. a standalone Python module or an extension of a thermal-relic code) parameterized by m_a, f_a, T_end, and w, validated against the paper's LTR/EMD/kination benchmarks.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann-to-likelihood pipeline exists for the mixed cold-misalignment plus warm-thermal axion population: CLASS-style ncdm setups handle a single thermal species with a nonstandard temperature, but no configured run or LSS/CMB likelihood covers the two-component (cold fraction plus warm fraction) case this model predicts.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Configure CLASS with a cold axion fluid plus an ncdm species at the computed axion temperature T_a0, and couple it to Planck and galaxy-clustering/Lyman-alpha likelihoods in MontePython or Cobaya, scanning (m_a, f_cold, f_warm) to produce reusable mixed-population constraints.

route_step_status.reason: Coupled density-and-temperature Boltzmann solvers beyond kinetic equilibrium exist publicly (DRAKE-style; micrOMEGAs assumes kinetic equilibrium), but none ships a two-state pseudo-Dirac setup with resonant annihilation and excited-state tracking, and the card names no tool.
The late-time velocity-averaged resonant annihilation rate is an analytic Breit-Wigner thermal average over the s1 velocity distribution, doable with standard formulae once s1 output exists.

Generic CMB energy-injection tools (ExoCLASS/DarkHistory) and dark-photon recast frameworks exist, but the velocity-dependent resonant injection history and inelastic/excited-state accelerator acceptances are not covered by any bundled likelihood.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver handles the resonant pseudo-Dirac thermal history: coupled chemical and kinetic (temperature) evolution of chi_1/chi_2 with early kinetic decoupling near a narrow s-channel dark-photon resonance and tracking of the surviving excited-state fraction f_*.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a beyond-kinetic-equilibrium relic solver such as DRAKE (or add a coupled-temperature module to micrOMEGAs) to two pseudo-Dirac states with off-diagonal dark-photon coupling, delta_R-parameterized resonance, and chi_2 depletion equations, validated against the paper's delta_R = 0.001-0.1 scan and high-f_* benchmarks.

gaps.description: No CMB (or BBN photodissociation) energy-injection likelihood accepts the strongly velocity-dependent resonant annihilation rate of this model; standard Planck p_ann limits assume a constant s-wave cross section and cannot be applied blindly, as the card itself notes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the redshift-dependent <sigma v>(v(z)) from the resonant thermal history into ExoCLASS or DarkHistory to compute the recombination-era injection and rerun the Planck anisotropy likelihood; add a BBN photodissociation check for the small-delta_R edge using the same injection history.

gaps.description: No accelerator recast exists for the resonant inelastic-dark-matter target: beam-dump and collider dark-photon limits must be remapped to the model's epsilon-g_D plane with the near-threshold m_A = 2 m_chi(1+delta_R) kinematics, semi-visible/displaced chi_2 decay modes, and the CMB-allowed coupling targets.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a dark-photon recast framework (e.g. DarkCast plus experiment acceptance maps) with the inelastic chi_1-chi_2 branching structure and chi_2 lifetime, and recompute existing beam-dump/collider exclusions along the resonant relic-target curve.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level annihilation and mono-photon cross sections for a simplified vector mediator are computable with public FeynArts/FeynCalc (plus LHAPDF for pp), as the source itself did.

The named 'omega-relic' code is not identified as public; public solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) handle resonant Breit-Wigner freeze-out for simplified models but no released model implementation exists for this Lagrangian.

Direct-detection operator matching is served by public tools (DirectDM/DDCalc) once the model is implemented, but no detector-level mono-photon likelihood exists for CLIC or the 14 TeV LHC projection.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Lagrangian in FeynRules, export UFO and CalcHEP model files, run micrOMEGAs or MadDM for the resonant freeze-out grid (validating the Omega h^2 = 0.120 boundary and the 0.8 < 2 m_DM/M_med < 1.0 window), and match couplings through DirectDM/DDCalc for nuclear-recoil limits.

gaps.description: No detector-level likelihood or acceptance exists for the mono-photon plus missing-energy search at CLIC (sqrt(s)=3 TeV) or the 14 TeV LHC projection; the source rates are parton-level with backgrounds and efficiencies unmodeled.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate signal and SM-background mono-photon events with MadGraph/WHIZARD plus Delphes using a CLIC detector card and an HL-LHC card, and build a binned missing-energy likelihood (e.g. via MadAnalysis or CheckMATE) covering the M_med = 3 TeV near-resonance benchmark scan.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Lagrangian in FeynRules, export UFO and CalcHEP model files, run micrOMEGAs or MadDM for the resonant freeze-out grid (validating the Omega h^2 = 0.120 boundary and the 0.8 < 2 m_DM/M_med < 1.0 window), and match couplings through DirectDM/DDCalc for nuclear-recoil limits.
