gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate signal and SM-background mono-photon events with MadGraph/WHIZARD plus Delphes using a CLIC detector card and an HL-LHC card, and build a binned missing-energy likelihood (e.g. via MadAnalysis or CheckMATE) covering the M_med = 3 TeV near-resonance benchmark scan.

route_step_status.reason: The Higgs-scalar mixing angle and decay width from the dimension-five S_2 H^4/Lambda_QG operator follow from simple analytic formulae given in the card, requiring no tool.

Domain-wall tension is analytic and the T_ann/SGWB scaling laws are published lattice-calibrated formulae, but no public code implements the biased-wall annihilation and spectrum calculation for this model and the card names no tool.

Public building blocks exist (PTA likelihoods such as PTArcade/NANOGrav releases; CMB injection tools like DarkHistory/ExoCLASS), but no assembled likelihood for the decaying-DM plus domain-wall SGWB combination is provided or identified in the card.

gaps.description: No public calculator produces the domain-wall stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum Omega_GW(f) with its PTA likelihood for the biased S_1 wall network: wall tension from (v_1, lambda_1), bias from the Lambda_QG-suppressed operators, T_ann, and the lattice-calibrated spectral shape are not wired into any reusable pipeline.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the lattice-calibrated scaling-law domain-wall spectrum (Hiramatsu-Kawasaki-Saikawa parameterization) as a function of (v_1, lambda_1, Lambda_QG), and evaluate it against NANOGrav 15-yr/IPTA data through PTArcade's new-physics likelihood, including the BBN wall-decay safety cut.

gaps.description: No recast pipeline converts the QG-induced S_2 decay (heavy scalar decaying via Higgs mixing to photons, e+e-, and neutrinos) into CMB energy-injection lifetime limits and SKA-band radio synchrotron sensitivity for this model's mass and Lambda_QG range.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute decay spectra for the heavy scalar with HDMSpectra (or PPPC-style tables at lower masses), feed them to DarkHistory/ExoCLASS for a Planck lifetime bound as a function of (m_DM, Lambda_QG), and model Galactic synchrotron from the e+e- channel with an RX-DMFIT-style code for the SKA projection.

gaps.description: The card specifies no relic-production mechanism for S_2 (production and relic-density calculation are 'unknown'), so the assumed S_2-dominated abundance that normalizes all decay observables is undetermined within the model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the S_2 abundance from the tree-level potential's Higgs-portal and S_1-S_2 quartic couplings (freeze-out or freeze-in as coupling size dictates) using micrOMEGAs with the two-singlet model implemented, mapping which (m_DM, coupling) regions realize Omega h^2 = 0.12.

route_step_status.reason: RECFAST is public, but the Co-SIMP 2-to-3 leptophilic heat-exchange modifications used by the paper were not released, so the thermal history cannot be recomputed with the stock code.
The z~85 brightness-temperature projection is semi-analytically straightforward but depends entirely on the unreleased Co-SIMP-modified thermal-history code, and no tool is named.
CLASS is public, but the modified perturbation equations implementing sigma_int and alpha for the Co-SIMP energy exchange are described only in the paper and no patch was released.
MontePython with public Planck 2018 and BAO likelihoods is a standard public workflow; it only awaits the upstream modified-CLASS spectra.

gaps.description: No public release of the Co-SIMP-modified RECFAST thermal-history and CLASS perturbation code implementing the DM + e -> DM + DM + e heat-exchange terms (parameters <sigma v>_2to3, alpha, sigma_int), so none of the 21-cm or CMB/BAO predictions can be reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the paper's Co-SIMP energy-exchange terms as a public patch: add the 2-to-3 electron-coupled cooling term to the RECFAST/HyRec thermal equations and the sigma_int, alpha dependence to the CLASS baryon temperature and perturbation sector, validated against the paper's EDGES band and near-flat Planck/BAO posteriors.

gaps.description: No global 21-cm likelihood exists for this model: the EDGES band is used only as a visual target, no joint EDGES/SARAS 3 likelihood is encoded, and all card constraints have likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a joint EDGES low-band plus SARAS 3 global-21-cm likelihood (e.g. within MontePython or a 21cmMC-style framework) with marginalization over foreground and astrophysical parameters, and apply it to the Co-SIMP T_21(z) predictions.

gaps.description: No quantitative sensitivity forecast or likelihood exists for the Dark Ages second-trough discriminator at z~85; the card notes instrument sensitivity for LuSEE Night, DAPPER, and PRATUSH was not forecast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct Fisher or mock-likelihood forecasts for LuSEE Night/DAPPER/PRATUSH-class instruments (noise plus foreground model over z~50-100) and evaluate the distinguishability of the alpha-dependent second-trough curves.

route_step_status.reason: The dE/dVdt energy-injection rate from <sigma v>_SADM, f, M_DM, and rho_DM is a closed analytic formula quoted in the paper and needs no dedicated tool.
RECFAST is public, but the paper's semi-annihilation injection terms and the ARCADE-2-inspired excess radio-background model were not released as usable code.
The z~85 projection is a simple extension of the thermal history but depends on the same unreleased modified-RECFAST implementation, with no tool named.
CLASS and MontePython are public with standard Planck 2018/BAO likelihoods, but the modified CLASS equations implementing sigma_int and f for SADM were not released and no chains were extracted.

gaps.description: The modified RECFAST/CLASS implementation of Z3 semi-annihilation energy injection (sigma_int, f) and the accompanying excess radio-background parameterization used for the EDGES fit are not publicly released, so the 21-cm and CMB/BAO predictions cannot be recomputed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or re-implement a public patch adding the SADM energy-injection term to the RECFAST/HyRec thermal equations and the sigma_int, f dependence to CLASS, together with the ARCADE-2-style radio-background module, validated against the paper's M_DM = 50 and 100 GeV EDGES curves and the Planck/BAO consistency result.

gaps.description: No global 21-cm likelihood is available for the SADM scenario: the EDGES trough is used as a visual target, no joint EDGES/SARAS 3 likelihood is encoded, and no Dark Ages instrument forecast for LuSEE Night/DAPPER/PRATUSH exists.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode a joint EDGES/SARAS 3 global-21-cm likelihood with astrophysical and radio-background nuisance parameters, and build Fisher/mock forecasts for Dark Ages instruments over z~50-100 to quantify the f-dependent second-trough discriminating power.

gaps.description: The energy deposited in the gas is modeled by a single constant fraction f with no spectrum- and redshift-dependent deposition-efficiency calculation for the DM + DM -> DM + SM final states; the card notes a spectrum-dependent calculation could replace this parameterization and no deposition table is included.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute injected SM spectra for representative semi-annihilation final states and process them through DarkHistory (or the Slatyer f_c(z) deposition tables) to replace the constant f with channel-resolved deposition efficiencies into heating, ionization, and excitation.

route_step_status.reason: LanHEP is a public tool and the renormalizable five-parameter Z4 Lagrangian is fully specified in the paper, so the micrOMEGAs model implementation can be regenerated even though the paper's model files were not released.
micrOMEGAs is public and its freeze-in and freeze-out routines cover the decay, scattering, and mixed FIMP-from-WIMP production regimes analyzed in the paper.
Projecting component yields and rescaled cross sections onto mass-coupling planes for cases 1-3 is simple bookkeeping on solver outputs and needs no dedicated tool.

gaps.description: The paper's LanHEP/micrOMEGAs model implementation of the Z4 fermion-plus-scalar model and its scan scripts were not publicly released, so reproducing the relic contours requires re-implementing the model from the written Lagrangian.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rebuild the Z4 model in LanHEP (or FeynRules/CalcHEP), export to micrOMEGAs, validate against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 contours for the three mass hierarchies, and publish the model files and scan scripts.

gaps.description: No packaged direct-detection likelihood exists for the mixed FIMP-WIMP case: the xi_S-rescaled scalar SI cross section is compared only to experiment curves quoted in the paper, with likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the micrOMEGAs sigma_SI output to a public direct-detection likelihood (DDCalc or the LZ/XENONnT likelihoods) with the xi_S abundance rescaling applied, so the stable-scalar case-3 parameter space gets a statistically defined exclusion rather than a curve overlay.

route_step_status.reason: The public SARAH/SPheno/micrOMEGAs/MadGraph chain the paper used covers all quantities, but the 2HDMS-specific model files were not released, so the pipeline must be regenerated before Omega h^2, sigma_SI, signal strengths, and MET rates can be recomputed.

The Planck relic comparison is trivial and HiggsTools provides public 95 GeV/Higgs-search checks, but no LZ likelihood or HL-LHC MET recast was bundled and all card constraints have likelihood_available: no.

gaps.description: The SARAH model definition and derived SPheno/micrOMEGAs implementation of the Type-II 2HDMS with pseudoscalar singlet A_S were not publicly released, so the full spectrum-to-observables pipeline cannot be rerun without re-creating the model files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-create the CP-conserving Type-II 2HDMS in SARAH, regenerate the SPheno spectrum code and micrOMEGAs model files, validate against the paper's benchmark point (m_h1 ~ 95 GeV, BR_inv ~ 0.25) and Planck/LZ filters, and publish the model package.

gaps.description: No statistical likelihoods are packaged for the DM-side filters: the Planck relic value and LZ SI limit are applied as pass/fail cuts on scan points rather than as likelihoods (likelihood_available: no for con_2hdms_planck_lz).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the micrOMEGAs outputs into a Gaussian Planck Omega h^2 likelihood and a public LZ spin-independent likelihood via DDCalc (with sub-abundance rescaling when A_S is a subcomponent) inside a GAMBIT- or MontePython-style scan.

gaps.description: No implemented collider recast exists for the invisible/MET signatures: the HL-LHC monojet and 2j+MET reach statement is a cut-and-count estimate for one representative benchmark with no simulation run and no reusable likelihood (con_2hdms_hllhc_met is recast_required).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate MadGraph monojet and 2j+MET samples for the 2HDMS benchmark grid and recast existing ATLAS/CMS MET analyses with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5, producing a parameter-space exclusion/projection likelihood instead of a single-point estimate.

route_step_status.reason: Public neutralino relic codes (micrOMEGAs, DarkSUSY) cover generic MSSM neutralinos, but no interface from the SO(10) split-SUSY benchmarks to a low-scale spectrum was built and the paper only quotes mass guidance, not a computed scan.
The dimension-five proton-decay partial lifetimes are computed analytically in the paper from M_SUSY, M_W, and the fitted Yukawa structure, which is a pen-and-paper capability that exists.

Metastable cosmic-string GW spectrum templates and PTA likelihood tools exist publicly (e.g. NANOGrav 15-yr pipelines/PTArcade), but no tool is attached and the model-specific spectrum and PTA recast were not run.

gaps.description: No pipeline connects the SO(10) split-SUSY benchmark parameters (M_SUSY, M_W, GUT-scale boundary conditions) to a low-scale neutralino spectrum and a quantitative relic-density calculation; the paper relies on generic wino/higgsino mass guidance, and the composition-dependent relic abundance and direct-detection predictions for BP1-BP3 are never computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a split-SUSY spectrum interface (RGE running from the GUT benchmarks to the electroweakino sector) feeding micrOMEGAs or DarkSUSY, including Sommerfeld-corrected annihilation for TeV winos/higgsinos and coannihilation/heavy-Higgs resonance effects, to turn the quoted mass windows into computed Omega h^2 and sigma_SI values per benchmark.

gaps.description: The metastable cosmic-string gravitational-wave prediction has no model-specific spectrum calculation or PTA likelihood recast: the PTA-favored region is described qualitatively and con_so10_pta_string_region has likelihood_available: no.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the stochastic GW spectrum for the model's M_B-L and sqrt(kappa_GUT) values using a metastable-string template and evaluate it against the NANOGrav 15-yr and IPTA data with a public PTA likelihood framework such as PTArcade/enterprise, mapping the posterior onto the (M_B-L, kappa) benchmark plane.

gaps.description: No likelihood connects the analytic proton-decay lifetimes to current Super-K limits and projected Hyper-K/JUNO sensitivities; the comparison is stated only as qualitative testability of benchmark regions (con_so10_proton_decay_tests, likelihood_available: no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Encode the published Super-K exclusion and Hyper-K/JUNO projected sensitivities for the relevant channels (p -> K+ nu, p -> e+ pi0) as simple lifetime likelihoods and evaluate the benchmark partial lifetimes, including an uncertainty budget for hadronic matrix elements and threshold corrections.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled EDE-SFDM background and perturbation equations are written out in the primary paper and deriving them is analytic work requiring no tool.
The authors modified CLASS to implement the KCS model (associated_code: partial), but no release URL is given and public availability is not established, so the solver capability is private.
The Planck 2018, BAO, Pantheon, SH0ES, and DES-Y3 likelihoods and MCMC samplers (MontePython/Cobaya-class tooling) are standard public infrastructure once the Boltzmann output from s2 exists.

gaps.description: The KCS-modified CLASS (SFDM with EDE-dependent kinetic term beta(psi) multiplying the kinetic term, plus shooting for the SFDM initial value) is author-private with no release URL, so neither observable can be recomputed or the beta/H0/S8 posteriors reproduced outside the original group.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain the authors' CLASS patch or re-implement the KCS equations in public CLASS by extending an existing EDE+ultralight-scalar branch (e.g. AxiCLASS) with the exponential kinetic-coupling function and its perturbation terms, validating against the published beta = 0.030 +/- 0.026, H0 = 72.38, and S8 = 0.8134 fit values.

gaps.description: The S8/structure-growth comparison uses only the linear matter power spectrum with no nonlinear prescription calibrated for SFDM suppression plus dark-energy drag (simulation_calibrated: no); standard halofit-type corrections are calibrated on CDM and may misestimate the DES-Y3 comparison.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Calibrate a nonlinear correction for KCS cosmologies, e.g. by running N-body simulations with the KCS linear transfer function and modified growth (or adapting an FDM-aware emulator) and fitting a halofit-style modification valid at the m_phi ~ 1e-22 eV suppression scale.

route_step_status.reason: The Solar-System capture rate of axion stars is an order-of-magnitude hand estimate in the paper; no public capture Monte Carlo or dedicated code exists for macroscopic dark-matter capture with a realistic compact-object phase-space distribution.
The spontaneous two-photon decay luminosity, line frequency, and flux at Earth follow from standard analytic axion-decay formulas explicitly given in the card, so a null tool_or_code is not limiting.

Published HSC/OGLE compact-object microlensing constraints exist and can be recast, but the card notes the recast requires a lens-profile treatment of extended dilute axion stars and no event-rate likelihood was run (likelihood_available: partial).

gaps.description: No public Solar-System capture code exists for macroscopic axion stars: the capture probability of a 5-15 Earth-mass axion star into a 300-1000 AU Planet 9 orbit is currently an order-of-magnitude analytic estimate depending on the poorly known low-relative-velocity tail of the axion-star phase-space distribution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a three-body capture Monte Carlo (Sun-Neptune or Sun-passing-star perturber) sampling axion-star masses and a Galactic-halo velocity distribution, validated against existing free-floating-planet and PBH capture-rate calculations, and output capture probability as a function of M_AS, Omega_AS/Omega_DM, and velocity-dispersion parameters.

gaps.description: No radio line-search likelihood or sensitivity pipeline exists for a narrow axion-decay line from a single localized outer-Solar-System source: the card records FAST/SKA detectability only as quoted sensitivity estimates with likelihood_available: no and no telescope pipeline run.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct a point-source narrow-line sensitivity model for FAST and SKA1-Low/Mid (system temperature, bandwidth matched to the line width, integration time) and wrap it as a likelihood over (m_a, f_a, r_9), reusing existing radio axion-line search frameworks developed for neutron-star axion searches.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level annihilation cross sections into Z' and scalar final states are straightforward analytic formulae, but the velocity-dependent light-mediator self-scattering rate requires a partial-wave/nonperturbative treatment (Tulin-Yu-type solver) for which the card cites no implementation.

Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs, MadDM, DRAKE) exist but assume standard radiation-dominated expansion; the required modified Hubble rate H(T) with a fast-redshifting component (index n, transition temperature T_r) needs a custom extension and no model implementation is public.

Standard Planck energy-injection recasts (Slatyer f_eff tables) cover electromagnetically visible channels, but the card notes that the neutrino-dominated Z' decays require a dedicated final-state-specific CMB/N_eff treatment that has not been run.

gaps.description: No Boltzmann/relic solver is set up for freeze-out in the model's fast-expansion cosmology: existing public codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) assume standard radiation domination and there is no public LSIDM model implementation, so the enhanced relic abundance with H(T) boosted by a component redshifting as T^(4+n) down to T_r cannot be computed off the shelf.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the LSIDM Lagrangian in FeynRules/micrOMEGAs and modify the solver's Hubble rate to include the fast-redshifting component parameterized by (n, T_r), following micrOMEGAs' non-standard-cosmology hooks; validate by recovering the paper's relic contours and the T_r > (15.4)^(1/n) MeV BBN condition.

gaps.description: No implementation exists for the velocity-dependent N self-scattering cross section through the MeV-scale Z': the resonant/classical light-mediator regimes require partial-wave or Hulthen-approximation solutions of the Yukawa scattering problem to map (m_N, m_Zprime, g_D) onto sigma_T/m at dwarf through cluster velocities.

gaps.description: No SIDM halo likelihood exists to confront the predicted velocity-dependent sigma_T/m with data: the card's SIDM constraint is a literature target band (likelihood_available: no) and no halo-simulation-calibrated likelihood over dwarf-to-cluster scales was run.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the published Kaplinghat-Tulin-Yu halo-inferred sigma_T/m(v) points for dwarfs, LSBs, and clusters into a Gaussian likelihood over the model's predicted velocity-dependent cross-section curve, optionally cross-checked against SIDM N-body-calibrated halo models (e.g. the isothermal Jeans method).

gaps.description: No dedicated CMB/N_eff treatment exists for the model's neutrino-dominated energy injection: the quoted Planck s-wave annihilation bound uses visible-channel f_eff, while Z' -> nu nu injection near recombination and its N_eff imprint for an MeV-scale mediator coupled to active neutrinos have not been computed for this model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the effective f_eff for the model's branching-weighted final states using Slatyer's transfer functions for the subdominant visible component, and evaluate the N_eff shift from MeV-scale Z'-neutrino interactions with a CLASS run modified for neutrino self-interaction/heating, then apply the Planck injection and N_eff likelihoods.

route_step_status.reason: Slow-roll inflation and heating consistency for a quadratic potential with a linear non-minimal coupling are analytic calculations the paper carries out with compact scaling relations, requiring no dedicated tool.
The spin-dependent partial width for inflaton decay to a DM pair is a tree-level two-body formula, and the paper computed the vertices and widths with the public tools LanHEP and CalcHEP.

Converting the decay branching to a yield Y_DM and imposing Omega_DM h^2 = 0.12, m_DM < m_phi/2, and heating consistency is a standard semi-analytic freeze-out-free calculation reproducible from the paper's scaling relations.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Re-implement the linear non-minimal coupling vertices in LanHEP/FeynRules, regenerate the spin-dependent decay widths in CalcHEP, and script the beta scan (inflation observables, heating temperature, yield, relic target) as a small public notebook validated against the paper's quoted mass-beta scalings.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a lattice preheating study (e.g. with CosmoLattice extended to the Einstein-frame interactions induced by the linear non-minimal coupling) of inflaton fragmentation and gravitational particle production for representative beta in the O(0.1)-O(100) range, and publish correction factors to the perturbative yield.
