gaps.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological N-body simulations initialized from the ADM-modified linear transfer functions across a grid in (f_adm, T_d^0, B_d/T_d^0), and calibrate a nonlinear P(k)/halo-mass-function correction (e.g. a halofit-style or emulator fit) usable in weak-lensing sigma8 analyses.

gaps.description: No survey-specific weak-lensing likelihood can consume cool-ADM predictions: the sigma8-tension claim rests on linear theory, and the route lists survey weak-lensing likelihoods as unresolved because they require the missing nonlinear matter-power model.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Once a nonlinear P(k) prescription exists (gap_2), interface it with public weak-lensing likelihoods (e.g. DES/KiDS 3x2pt in Cobaya/CosmoSIS) so the low-sigma8 interpretation can be tested directly against lensing data.

route_step_status.reason: The reheaton baryogenesis calculation (branching ratios, CP violation, washout) was performed at paper level, but no public code implements it, so the route lists a baryogenesis Boltzmann solver as a required-but-absent resource.

A CLASS/ETHOS-style atomic-dark-matter solver is named, and such modified-CLASS implementations exist in related MTH/aDM studies, but the card identifies no public release covering this model's twin recombination and Delta N_eff mapping, and the imported Planck/BAO bounds were not rerun.
Nonlinear simulations of dissipative twin atoms (dark disks, dwarf-galaxy morphology) have no tool_or_code and the card records simulation_calibrated: no with the constraint likelihood unavailable.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann-solver implementation of Mirror-Twin-Higgs atomic dark matter exists for this model: twin recombination (twin hydrogen and twin helium), twin BAO features, and the f_aDM/Delta N_eff parameterization needed to reproduce the imported Planck/BAO bounds are only available in private modified codes from related studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the twin-sector fluid (twin baryons coupled to twin photons with a twin recombination history including twin helium) as a public CLASS extension parameterized by (f_aDM, Delta N_eff, f/v, twin binding energies), validated against the published twin-BAO bounds, and expose it to Cobaya/MontePython likelihoods.

gaps.description: The reheaton baryogenesis step (coupled asymmetry generation in visible and twin sectors with washout) is a paper-level analytic Boltzmann calculation with no released solver, so the mapping from (m_N1, m_phi_A, Y_phi, f/v) to visible and twin baryon asymmetries cannot be scanned or reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the paper's coupled Boltzmann equations for reheaton decay, CP asymmetries, and two-sector washout as a small public package (e.g. an extension of a leptogenesis solver such as ULYSSES), outputting f_aDM and the twin reheating temperature over the m_h < m_N1 < m_WB window.

gaps.description: No hydrodynamic simulations exist for a dissipative twin-atomic subcomponent at f_aDM up to about 0.2 with this model's dark cooling parameters, so dark-disk formation, dissipative collapse, and dwarf-galaxy morphology predictions cannot be computed and the self-interaction constraint has no likelihood (likelihood_available: no).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run zoom-in galaxy-formation simulations including a dissipative dark-atom fluid with dark Coulomb cooling (extending existing dissipative-DM simulation frameworks), scanning f_aDM and the dark fine-structure/binding-energy parameters, and derive dark-disk and dwarf-kinematics constraints as a recastable likelihood.

gaps.description: No model-specific collider recast or likelihood exists for the TeV-scale top-philic color-triplet scalar phi_A with Y_phi = -1/3; the card notes no detector-level collider likelihood is encoded.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules/UFO model for the visible color triplet with its top-philic and right-handed-neutrino couplings, simulate production in MadGraph, and recast existing LHC squark/leptoquark searches with SModelS or CheckMATE to obtain mass-coupling limits.

route_step_status.reason: The radiative Majoron mass and effective potential are closed-form loop-level formulas given in the primary paper, evaluable analytically without a dedicated tool.
Standard (kinetic) misalignment relic-abundance formulas from the paper map (m_a, f_a, initial angle, dot theta_i) to Omega_a h^2 analytically under the stated post-inflationary assumptions.

The lepton-asymmetry estimate is an analytic paper-level formula, but the route notes a Boltzmann/transport implementation would be needed for a quantitative likelihood, and no such code exists for this Weinberg-operator spontaneous-leptogenesis setup.

gaps.description: No numerical transport/Boltzmann implementation exists for spontaneous leptogenesis sourced by the rotating Majoron with Weinberg-operator lepton-number violation, so the baryon-asymmetry and relic-density benchmark can only be reproduced as an order-of-magnitude analytic estimate rather than scanned or used in a numerical likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement coupled equations of motion for the rotating Majoron field plus lepton-number transport equations (chemical potentials with Weinberg-operator and sphaleron rates), e.g. as an extension of an axiogenesis/leptogenesis solver such as ULYSSES, outputting Y_B and Omega_a h^2 over (m_a, f_a, dot theta_i, T_W).

gaps.description: The anomaly-induced a-Z-gamma coupling and possible inverse-Primakoff-like laboratory signals are only sketched qualitatively in the primary paper; no derived coupling values or recast against existing ALP search limits exist for this Majoron.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive g_aZgamma and the effective photon coupling from the electroweak chiral anomaly for this lepton-number charge assignment, then recast published ALP photon-coupling limits (helioscope, haloscope, astrophysical) onto the (m_a, f_a) plane.

route_step_status.reason: Static string tensions and core profiles come from a classical ansatz plus a standard ODE profile solver, which the primary paper already carried out and validated.

Lattice field-theory cosmic-string simulation codes exist for conventional global/gauge strings, but none has been run or adapted for this U(1)_Z x U(1)_PQ heavy-core Y-junction network, and the paper explicitly says scaling validation is not yet performed.

Semi-analytic string-radiation-to-relic conversion formulas exist for standard axion strings, but the emission spectrum from heavy-core strings is unknown, so the Omega_a h^2 prediction is order-of-magnitude only.
Comparing axion versus graviton radiated power is a standard analytic estimate given in the primary paper.
Standard cosmic-string loop GW plateau formulas exist, but the required loop distribution for this hybrid network is unknown pending network simulations, leaving the estimate order-of-magnitude.

Published CMB string-tension likelihoods exist for standard Nambu-Goto/Abelian-Higgs networks, but the primary text only applies them qualitatively and no recast exists for the Y-junction network's abundance and tension spectrum.

gaps.description: No cosmological field-theory simulation exists for the two-scalar U(1)_Z x U(1)_PQ defect network with heavy-core global strings, gauge strings, and Y-junctions; the scaling density xi, loop distribution, and crucially the axion emission spectrum from heavy-core strings are all unquantified, so the enhanced-relic claim (m_a > 1e-5 eV as all of DM) rests on an assumed scaling regime.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend existing axion-string lattice simulation frameworks to evolve the two complex scalars plus the U(1)_Z gauge field with hierarchical VEVs, measure the Y-junction scaling parameters, loop distribution, and per-string axion emission spectrum, and feed these into the semi-analytic relic calculator to sharpen the opened axion mass window.

gaps.description: CMB angular-power constraints on string tension have not been recast for this model's mixed Y-junction network of global, heavy-core, and gauge strings; the primary paper invokes G_mu bounds only qualitatively, so no quantitative allowed region in (v_1, v_2, e) exists.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the simulated network's string abundance and effective tension spectrum onto the unconnected-segment-model templates used in Planck string analyses and rerun the CMB likelihood to derive quantitative G_mu limits for the hybrid network.

route_step_status.reason: Public relic solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) handle Z-prime-portal freeze-out including resonances and freeze-in generically, but the card identifies no SWSM model implementation, so the freeze-in and freeze-out branches cannot be run without first building one.
Published NA64, beam-dump, and g-2 exclusion curves exist, but the SWSM-specific mapping onto U(1)_z charge assignments has not been done and no curves were digitized for this card.

The sterile-neutrino lifetime is a standard analytic decay-width calculation, but the card records no lifetime or RGE run, and the vacuum-stability flag requires a model-specific renormalization-group analysis that has no implementation here.

gaps.description: No computational implementation of the superweak U(1)_z model exists on the card (no FeynRules/CalcHEP/UFO model file), so the sterile-neutrino relic abundance in either the resonant freeze-out branch or the small-coupling freeze-in branch cannot be computed with public solvers, and the published relic-density lines cannot be reproduced or scanned.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a FeynRules model of the SWSM (Z-prime with anomaly-free U(1)_z charges, three sterile neutrinos, mixed scalar) and export to micrOMEGAs/MadDM for the resonant freeze-out branch and to micrOMEGAs' freeze-in mode for the small-g_z branch, validating against the paper's relic-density lines at fixed M_N1.

gaps.description: Laboratory and BBN constraints (NA64 dark-photon searches, beam dumps, charged-lepton g-2, pion-threshold BBN requirement) have not been recast onto the SWSM's specific U(1)_z charge and mixing conventions; no digitized exclusion curves or masks exist, so the viable (g_z, M_Zprime) window cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Use the Darkcast recasting framework to map published dark-photon and beam-dump limits onto the SWSM Z-prime coupling structure, digitize the g-2 and BBN pion-threshold masks, and package them as overlay curves in the (M_Zprime, g_z) plane.

gaps.description: The dark matter phase-space distribution is entirely unspecified: the freeze-in branch produces a nonthermal momentum distribution that has never been derived for the SWSM, and the card explicitly flags that no thermal-WDM mapping exists, so free-streaming and structure-formation viability of the candidate cannot be assessed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for Z-prime-mediated freeze-in production of N1 to obtain f(p), derive the resulting transfer-function suppression (or a validated thermal-WDM equivalent mass), and check it against Lyman-alpha warm-dark-matter bounds.

route_step_status.reason: Selecting the BDM candidate subset from neutrino/LFV-allowed points is conceptually simple, but the underlying neutrino/LFV chi-square scan code is private and no scan chain is published with the paper.

micrOMEGAs 5.2.7 is a public code that handles coannihilating scalar-triplet relic calculations, but the card records no public model implementation (CalcHEP/model files) for this specific radiative-neutrino inert-triplet model, so the calculation cannot be rerun as-is.

The Higgs-portal spin-independent direct-detection recast has no tool_or_code, the card states no direct-detection likelihood is available (likelihood_available: no), and the source did not perform the numerical recast.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (CalcHEP/LanHEP model files for micrOMEGAs) exists for this Y=0 inert-triplet radiative-neutrino model with the eta_R bosonic DM candidate, so the gauge-coannihilation relic calculation and the source scan counts (325 NH, 20 IH points) cannot be reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model Lagrangian (inert triplet, N_R, vector-like leptons, charged scalar S+) in LanHEP/FeynRules and export micrOMEGAs 5.x model files, packaging the neutrino-oscillation/LFV filter as a reproducible scan script that recovers the 166 MeV charged-neutral splitting and the published scan counts.

gaps.description: No direct-detection likelihood or numerical recast exists for the Y=0 BDM Higgs-portal spin-independent cross section; the paper only notes the bound qualitatively, so the current LZ/XENONnT exclusion status of the surviving BDM points is unknown.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the tree-level Higgs-portal SI cross section for eta_R from the scalar-potential couplings (available once the model files of gap_1 exist, or by hand from the standard Higgs-portal formula) and recast against current SI limits using DDCalc, including the relic-fraction rescaling for underproducing points.

route_step_status.reason: The chi-square scan against neutrino oscillation data and LFV bounds uses standard published data but the source scan code is private and no reproducible scan chain is released.

Selecting points with an N_R-dominant lightest neutral fermion (|(V_N)_11| > 0.9 and D_N1 lightest) is a trivial mass-matrix diagonalization and filtering operation doable with pen-and-paper linear algebra plus a few lines of script.

micrOMEGAs 5.2.7 is public and handles t/u-channel leptophilic freeze-out, but the card records no public model implementation for this radiative-neutrino model, so the relic calculation cannot be rerun without rebuilding the model files.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (CalcHEP/LanHEP model files for micrOMEGAs) and no released neutrino/LFV scan code exist for this Y=0 inert-triplet radiative-neutrino model with the D_N1 fermionic DM candidate, so the thermal relic calculation and the published scan counts (4312 NH, 206 IH points) cannot be reproduced.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the full Lagrangian (N_R, vector-like lepton doublets, inert triplet, charged scalar S+) in LanHEP/FeynRules, export micrOMEGAs 5.x model files, and package the neutrino-oscillation/LFV chi-square filter as a reproducible scan script validated against the 4312/206 published scan counts and the 5-percent relic window.

gaps.description: The loop-level spin-independent direct-detection cross section for the N_R-dominant fermionic DM is not derived anywhere in the card or source (the paper only argues tree-level Z-portal avoidance qualitatively), so the direct-detection constraint con_fdm_zportal_direct_detection_condition cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the one-loop effective DM-quark operators (photon/Z/Higgs penguins and box diagrams with charged scalars and leptons) following standard leptophilic-DM loop calculations, then recast against current SI/SD limits with DDCalc for the relic-compatible scan points.

route_step_status.reason: The coherent-vector gravitational-potential (Shapiro-type) time-delay perturbation is a closed-form analytic formula in m and rho_dm given in the paper, requiring only pen-and-paper evaluation.
The pulsar Doppler oscillation sourced by neutron-star muon charge follows from the given analytic coupling formula (g, N_mu, m, rho_dm) with N_mu about 1e55 estimated in the paper appendix.

The chi-square fit to NANOGrav binned angular correlations is reproducible from public 15-year data products, but no public PTA likelihood module implements the vector-ULDM deterministic correlation signal, and the card notes the likelihood is only approximate and was not rerun.

Binary-pulsar orbital-period-loss bounds on the L_mu-L_tau g-m plane exist in the cited literature, but the card records the exclusion contours as undigitized figure boundaries with only a partial likelihood and no recast code.

gaps.description: No public PTA likelihood implements the deterministic vector-ULDM signal (vector gravitational-potential time delay plus muon-charge-sourced Doppler oscillation) for L_mu-L_tau dark matter; the primary fit is a binned chi-square on published angular correlations rather than a full timing-residual likelihood, so the alpha <= 0.477 region cannot be verified or updated on future PTA data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the vector-ULDM correlation curve and Doppler source term as a deterministic signal model in ENTERPRISE/PTArcade against the NANOGrav 15-year data set, fitting m, g, and rho_dm jointly with the SMBHB background and validating against the paper's alpha interval.

gaps.description: The binary-pulsar exclusion boundary in the g-m plane used to check consistency of the PTA fit region exists only as an undigitized figure from the cited literature, with no machine-readable contour or public radiation calculator for muon-charge-sourced ultralight L_mu-L_tau emission.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published binary-pulsar g-m exclusion contours (e.g. from arXiv:2210.03880) and reimplement the analytic orbital-period-loss formula for ultralight vector radiation from muon-charged neutron-star binaries as a small script producing machine-readable bounds.

gaps.description: No cosmological production calculation exists for this ultralight (m ~ 1e-23 eV) L_mu-L_tau vector: the card records production as unspecified and relic density as purely phenomenological (normalized to local rho_dm), so whether the field can actually constitute the dark matter with the required coherent amplitude is not evaluable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the relic abundance from a concrete production mechanism for ultralight vectors (misalignment with the required non-minimal coupling, inflationary fluctuation production, or tachyonic production from an axion-like coupling) and check consistency of the resulting rho_dm and coherence properties with the PTA-fit m and g.

route_step_status.reason: The classical-regime velocity-dependent transfer cross section for Yukawa-potential scattering (m_X v >> m_Y) is given by standard closed-form fitting formulas from the SIDM literature, evaluable analytically from m_X, m_Y, and alpha_D.

Higgs-decay and annihilation freeze-in yields are semi-analytic and micrOMEGAs 5.0 (public, with a freeze-in module) was used for the relic projection, but no public model implementation of the X/Y dark sector exists and the Sommerfeld-corrected late-time depletion requires paper-specific numerics.

Higgs-invisible, direct, indirect, CMB, Voyager, and Lyman-alpha limits exist as published curves, but the card states the external detection likelihoods are not machine-readable and no recast pipeline exists for this benchmark.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP model files or released freeze-in scripts) exists for the two-field X/Y Higgs-portal dark sector, so the Sommerfeld-corrected freeze-in relic calculation (Omega_X and the Y overproduction check) cannot be reproduced from the paper alone.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the renormalizable X/Y Lagrangian with the feeble portal couplings in micrOMEGAs 5.x using its freeze-in module (or a standalone yield integrator for H->XX decay and HH->XX annihilation with Sommerfeld factors), validated against the paper's Planck-saturating benchmark.

gaps.description: The model's central prediction — velocity-dependent self-interactions solving small-scale-structure tensions — is not simulation-calibrated (simulation_calibrated: no): no SIDM structure-formation simulation or calibrated halo model exists for this specific classical-regime cross section (alpha_D 0.1-0.9, m_Y 2-7 MeV, m_X 60-500 GeV), so quantitative core-size, profile, and subhalo predictions are unavailable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological zoom-in SIDM N-body simulations (e.g. with the SIDM modules of GIZMO or Arepo) sampling the classical-regime sigma_T(v)/m curves of this model, or calibrate the existing isothermal-Jeans/gravothermal halo models to this velocity dependence to produce testable density-profile predictions from dwarf to cluster scales.

gaps.description: No likelihood exists for either the SIDM target region (dwarf/group/cluster sigma_T/m inferences are used as a heuristic band, likelihood_available: no) or the null-signal detection constraints (Higgs invisible width, Fermi-LAT, CMB energy injection, Voyager, Lyman-alpha are quoted as non-machine-readable curves), so the compatible parameter region cannot be statistically evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a composite likelihood: recast published halo-scale sigma_T/m inferences (e.g. the Kaplinghat-Tulin-Yu data points) into a velocity-binned likelihood, and wrap the detection channels using existing public machinery (DDCalc for SI scattering, Higgs invisible width formula, published CMB f_eff and Fermi-LAT dwarf likelihoods) for this model's annihilation spectra.

route_step_status.reason: The active-sterile mixing angle theta ~ v_s v_h/(Lambda_QG m_DM) and the resulting decay widths (chi -> nu gamma, chi -> nu e+ e-) follow from analytic formulas given in the paper, evaluable by hand.

The UV freeze-in yield has an analytic scaling (Y ~ T_RH M_Pl/Lambda_FI^2) and IR decay freeze-in is computable with existing tools like micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module, but no code implements this model's combined dimension-five UV plus s/h-decay IR production, and the momentum distribution needed downstream is not computed at all.
The domain-wall GW peak frequency and amplitude follow from the standard analytic estimates of the cited domain-wall review (tension, bias, T_ann scaling relations), a pen-and-paper calculation.

The PTA leg is coverable with the public NANOGrav 15-year new-physics likelihood (PTArcade includes domain-wall spectra), but the indirect-decay CMB/X-ray/gamma-ray limits and the Lyman-alpha bound exist only as published curves with no machine-readable likelihoods, and no joint combination was run.

gaps.description: No solver exists for this model's freeze-in production combining UV scattering through dimension-five operators (reheating-sensitive) with IR production from s and h decays, including the resulting chi momentum distribution f(q); the paper works only at yield level, so the relic contours cannot be reproduced and no phase-space output exists for structure-formation use.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the unintegrated freeze-in Boltzmann equation for this model at the distribution-function level (extending existing FIMP phase-space frameworks in the style of the Konig-Merle-Totzauer sterile-neutrino codes, or micrOMEGAs freeze-in plus a dedicated f(q) integrator), covering both the T_RH-dominated UV contribution and the s/h decay IR contribution, validated against the paper's T_RH-Lambda_FI and v_s-m_DM relic contours.

gaps.description: The Lyman-alpha mass floor (m_DM > ~15 keV) is imported from a cited study assuming a different freeze-in momentum spectrum; no recast exists for this model's mixed UV/IR production histories, so the small-scale-structure constraint on the v_s-m_DM plane is not actually evaluable across parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the model-specific f(q) from gap_1 into CLASS as a non-cold relic to compute the linear transfer function, then apply the standard half-mode/WDM-equivalent mapping or an existing Lyman-alpha flux emulator to set the mass floor as a function of T_RH, Lambda_FI, and v_s.

gaps.description: The decaying-DM indirect constraints (CMB energy injection plus HEAO-1/INTEGRAL/COMPTEL/EGRET/Fermi-LAT diffuse-photon limits on chi -> nu gamma and chi -> nu e+ e-) are applied only as digitized literature curves with no machine-readable likelihood, so the triangular allowed region in the v_s-m_DM plane cannot be recomputed or combined statistically with the PTA and Lyman-alpha legs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a decaying-sterile-neutrino-style likelihood module: compute decay spectra with HDMSpectra or analytic two/three-body formulas, wrap the published diffuse X/gamma-ray flux limits and a CMB f_eff(z) energy-injection likelihood (ExoCLASS), and combine with the PTArcade domain-wall likelihood for a joint scan over Lambda_QG, v_s, and m_DM.

route_step_status.reason: The regularized/renormalized/DRG-resummed MST-EFT scalar spectrum exists only as paper equations reconstructed by hand; no public implementation of the multiple-sharp-transition loop-corrected spectrum exists.

Press-Schechter/peaks PBH abundance formalism is standard and documented, but no public calculator covers the equation-of-state-dependent collapse threshold for general w in [0.2, 1/3] with c_s up to 1.17.
Public induced-GW integrators (SIGWfast, named in the card's required resources) exist, but their kernels must be verified or extended for the general-w, c_s > 1 regime this model favors.
PTArcade provides a public PTA likelihood and microlensing limit curves are public, but no assembled pipeline connects this model's f_PBH(M) and Omega_GW(f) outputs to them.

gaps.description: No public code implements the MST-EFT scalar power spectrum with multiple sharp SR/USR transitions including loop renormalization and DRG resummation; P_zeta(k) must currently be reconstructed by hand from paper equations, and it feeds every downstream prediction.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's regularized-renormalized-resummed spectrum as a standalone module (or a primordial-spectrum plugin usable by SIGWfast/CLASS-style pipelines) parameterized by the six transition-scale pairs, transition sharpness, w, and c_s, with a built-in perturbativity check.

gaps.description: No public PBH mass-function calculator handles the equation-of-state-dependent collapse threshold delta_c(w, c_s) needed for this model's favored 0.2 <= w <= 1/3 window; abundance results are exponentially sensitive to this threshold.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a standard Press-Schechter/peak-theory PBH abundance code with the w-dependent threshold prescriptions (Musco-type) tabulated over the model's w and c_s ranges, and validate against the radiation-era w = 1/3 limit named in the card's validation tests.

gaps.description: The scalar-induced GW kernel for general post-inflation equation of state with effective sound speed c_s between 1 and 1.17 is not covered by standard radiation-era induced-GW implementations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive and implement the general-(w, c_s) induced-GW transfer kernel as an extension of SIGWfast, cross-checking the w = 1/3, c_s = 1 limit against the existing implementation.

gaps.description: No packaged joint likelihood combines the PTA stochastic-background fit (NANOGrav 15-year/EPTA) with microlensing PBH-fraction limits for this model's parameter space; the paper's comparison is text-level only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the model's Omega_GW(f) output in a PTArcade new-physics likelihood and confront f_PBH(M) with public digitized microlensing constraint curves (PBHbounds-style), producing a joint posterior over the transition parameters, w, and c_s.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving chiral couplings and matrix elements from the dark chiral Lagrangian (including WZW and 3pi->pi rho terms) is standard pen-and-paper EFT work fully specified by the paper within its validity window.
The effective thermal width is an analytic estimate the paper itself computes and shows to be negligible except near resonance; no dedicated tool is needed.
Standard relic codes (micrOMEGAs, MadDM) do not implement 3-to-2 SIMP freeze-out with 3pi -> pi rho reactions and thermal widths, and the paper's numerical solver is not public.

The step as defined is an approximate pass/fail comparison of the analytic sigma/m against the quoted Bullet Cluster bound, which is trivially doable by hand (a proper likelihood is recorded as a gap).
Dark-rho width and lifetime from kinetic mixing follow from standard analytic decay formulas once the portal is specified.

Pythia8's Hidden Valley module provides a public dark-shower generator, but it must be configured and tuned for this specific spectrum (m_rho/m_pi < 2, rho -> SM only, stable pions), which is nontrivial model-specific work.
Public recast frameworks exist, but ATLAS/CMS emerging-jet and semi-visible-jet searches have limited reusable recast implementations and none tailored to this model's long-lived dark-rho signature.

gaps.description: No public Boltzmann solver implements SIMP freeze-out with the 3pi -> pi rho number-changing process, WZW 3-to-2 rates, detailed balance, and the dark-rho thermal width; the paper's numerical solution is not released, so the relic curve m_pi ~ 150 MeV / xi^(1/3) cannot be reproduced without reimplementation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled dark-pion/dark-rho Boltzmann system with chiral-EFT matrix elements as a standalone solver, or extend micrOMEGAs' number-changing-process machinery to 3-to-2 reactions with a resonant rho final state, validating against the paper's relic-density curves.

gaps.description: No public dark-shower configuration exists for this spectrum: a Pythia8 Hidden Valley setup with mass-degenerate dark quarks, stable dark pions, and dark rho mesons that decay only to SM particles through kinetic mixing (m_rho < 2 m_pi), including hadronization tuning for the confining SU(N_c) sector.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build and publish a Pythia8 Hidden Valley card set for this model (N_c, N_f, m_pi, m_rho, f_pi, epsilon), fixing the visible/invisible fractions and rho lifetime consistently with the thermalisation lower bound on the portal width.

gaps.description: No reusable likelihood or recast exists for confronting the model's semi-visible/emerging-jet and displaced-vertex signatures with ATLAS/CMS dark-shower searches over the (m_pi, m_rho, epsilon) plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast the existing ATLAS/CMS emerging-jet and displaced-vertex searches in a public framework (MadAnalysis5/CheckMATE-style) using the gap_2 shower samples, and publish efficiency maps over lifetime and mass ratio.

gaps.description: The Bullet Cluster self-interaction comparison is a single-number pass/fail against ~2 cm^2/g with no merging-cluster likelihood or velocity-dependence treatment, so the claimed relief of self-interaction tension carries no quantified confidence.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Map the chiral-EFT dark-pion self-scattering cross section (with its velocity dependence) into an existing SIDM cluster-merger and halo-shape likelihood framework instead of the single Bullet Cluster threshold value.

route_step_status.reason: Integrating the log-normal c_s^2/w template into a thermal-history background is a straightforward analytic/ODE exercise fully specified by the paper's ansatz.

Analytic threshold prescriptions calibrated on spherical-collapse simulations exist, but they are calibrated for constant or radiation-like equations of state and the paper itself notes further simulations are needed for very soft time-dependent w and c_s.
Peak-theory/Press-Schechter mass-function evaluation from a given amplitude, threshold, and horizon mass is standard semi-analytic work reproducible from the paper's equations.
The induced-GW computation was done with a new Julia code the paper mentions but does not release, so the capability exists but is private.

PBH constraint compilations and LISA/DECIGO/BBO sensitivity curves are publicly available, but the card records that no constraint curves were digitized and no packaged comparison pipeline exists for this template.

gaps.description: The PBH collapse threshold during a smooth crossover with time-dependent softened w and c_s^2 rests on spherical-collapse prescriptions outside their calibrated regime; the abundance is exponentially sensitive to this threshold and the source itself flags that very soft equations of state need dedicated simulations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run Musco-style numerical-relativity collapse simulations across the crossover template (varying c_s^2_min, crossover width, and mass scale) and fit a threshold formula delta_c(w(t), c_s^2(t)) usable in the semi-analytic mass-function step, including non-spherical checks for the softest cases.

gaps.description: The scalar-induced GW spectrum through the crossover was computed with a non-public Julia code; no public induced-GW integrator handles the fully time-dependent w(t) and c_s^2(t) background this model requires.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain public release of the paper's Julia induced-GW code, or extend SIGWfast's kernel computation to arbitrary tabulated w(t)/c_s^2(t) thermal histories, validating on the pure-radiation limit and the paper's model A/B detector-band shift.

gaps.description: No assembled pipeline confronts the template's outputs with data: PBH abundance/evaporation constraint curves are not digitized into the workflow and no LISA/DECIGO/BBO sensitivity or PBH likelihood is packaged for the (A, crossover scale, c_s^2_min) parameter space.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire f_PBH(M) into a public PBH-constraint compilation (PBHbounds-style, including asteroid-mass-window evaporation limits) and Omega_GW(f) into standard LISA/DECIGO/BBO power-law-integrated sensitivity curves, producing an automated observational-status verdict per template point.

route_step_status.reason: The dressed-halo profile (M_h ~ 97*(31/(1+z_c))*M_PBH, rho_h proportional to r^-9/4) is given as closed-form analytic expressions in the primary text and is evaluable by hand.

Public wave-optics lensing solvers exist for point and simple extended lenses, but computing amplification factors for the specific r^-9/4 dressed profile and folding them into a survey-level GW/FRB likelihood requires substantial model-specific extension not supplied by the card.

gaps.description: No public wave-optics amplification-factor calculator handles the dressed-PBH extended lens with the steep rho_h proportional to r^-9/4 accreted-halo profile; existing diffraction-integral codes target point-mass or standard (SIS/NFW) profiles, so the event-by-event dPBH vs bare-PBH waveform discrimination cannot be computed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing public wave-optics diffraction-integral code to accept the dressed-PBH density profile parameterized by (M_PBH, M_h, R_h), tabulating F(f) over the LIGO/ET/CE band for the 10-100 M_sun window and verifying recovery of the bare point-mass limit.

gaps.description: No event-level lensed-waveform likelihood exists for confronting dressed-PBH amplification templates with LVK O3 (and future ET/CE) data, so non-detections cannot be converted into f_PBH bounds in the stellar-mass window.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build dPBH F(f) templates into an existing Bayesian lensed-GW search pipeline (of the kind used for LVK microlensing analyses) and run population-level rate calculations to translate O3 non-detection into f_PBH(M_PBH) exclusion curves.

gaps.description: The FRB lensing channel lacks an optical-depth and time-delay likelihood for extended dressed lenses: CHIME-like burst samples constrain point masses, and no public tool maps the effective lens mass M_PBH^eff of a dressed halo into an FRB lensing rate bound.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an FRB lensing optical-depth calculation to the dressed-lens Einstein-radius/effective-mass mapping from the related work, and recast the existing CHIME FRB non-detection statistics into f_PBH bounds for the 10-10^3 M_sun dressed window.

gaps.description: Survival of the accreted r^-9/4 halos against tidal stripping and late-time galactic evolution is unmodeled, leaving the low-redshift lens profile (and hence all lensing predictions) systematically uncertain.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations of dressed PBHs orbiting in Milky Way-like potentials to quantify stripping of the accreted halo, and publish a survival-fraction correction to (M_h, R_h) as a function of environment and redshift for use in the lensing step.

route_step_status.reason: Setting up the phenomenological (rho_core, M_nugget, Gamma_heat) scan and the nugget density/temperature inputs is simple semi-analytic work fully specified by the paper within the optically thin regime.
Cloudy is a public spectral-synthesis code and the paper states its input cards and full results are released at github.com/davidrcurtin/mirror_star_emissions.
Convolving synthetic spectra with published Gaia passbands to get colors and absolute magnitudes is a standard data transform with public passband data.

gaps.description: No search likelihood exists for the predicted mirror-star HR-diagram locus: the Gaia DR3 comparison is illustrative only, with no selection function, white-dwarf contamination model, or statistical machinery to turn candidate counts (or their absence) into bounds on (rho_core, M_nugget, Gamma_heat).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a Gaia DR3 candidate-search likelihood over the published color-magnitude locus with a G<30 completeness/selection model and a white-dwarf population contamination model, so that follow-up non-confirmation converts into exclusion regions over the paper's scan parameters.

gaps.description: The local mirror-star number density is unpredicted: no simulation of dissipative atomic/twin-baryon cooling, fragmentation, and mirror-star formation efficiency connects the underlying dark-sector parameters to a population, so per-object spectra cannot be converted into expected Gaia or X-ray detection rates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamic simulations of dissipative atomic-dark-matter collapse (extending existing atomic-DM cooling simulation work) to derive a mirror-star formation efficiency and mass function versus atomic-DM fraction, yielding a local number-density prior for the search likelihood.

gaps.description: The radiative-transfer treatment covers only optically thin nuggets; the optically thick part of the (M_nugget, Gamma_heat) scan is explicitly deferred by the paper, so signal predictions are unavailable in that regime.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the published Cloudy-based pipeline with a stellar-atmosphere-style optically thick radiative-transfer solution for high-mass nuggets, matching onto the optically thin results at the regime boundary of the existing scan.

route_step_status.reason: Relativistic freeze-out yield of N1 through W_R interactions is a standard analytic calculation (equilibrium yield at decoupling), doable pen-and-paper despite the null tool_or_code.

The paper solved the N2 matter-domination, entropy-dilution, and secondary-N1 spectrum Boltzmann evolution, but no public packaged solver for a dilutor with partial branching into hot secondary DM is identified on the card.

CLASS (per associated_code) can propagate the mixed cold+hot N1 distribution to the matter power spectrum, but the card states the recast needs updated likelihoods (likelihood_available partial/no) and the X-ray overlay uses dated line-search data.

gaps.description: No public released solver for the N2 dilutor cosmology: coupled Boltzmann evolution of N2 matter domination, entropy injection with BBN timing, and the momentum distribution of the hot secondary N1 component from partial N2 decays; the paper's calculation is private.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a semi-analytic dilutor module (e.g. building on public early-matter-domination codes or a light Boltzmann-hierarchy wrapper feeding CLASS) that takes (m_N2, tau_N2, Br_N1, M_WR) and outputs the dilution factor and the two-component N1 f(p), validated against the paper's 6.5-30 keV window.

gaps.description: No current LSS/Lyman-alpha or X-ray line likelihood exists for mixed cold+hot sterile-neutrino spectra of this type; the card's SDSS-era branching bound and X-ray window are stated to need recasting with updated data before precision use.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast modern Lyman-alpha (e.g. eBOSS/MIKE-HIRES emulator-based) and X-ray line-search (NuSTAR/XMM blank-sky) likelihoods onto the two-component N1 transfer functions computed with CLASS, replacing the SDSS-scale comparison used in the paper.

gaps.description: Nonlinear structure formation for the mixed cold+warm/hot N1 population is uncalibrated: the card marks halo and subhalo mass-function effects unknown, simulation_calibrated no, and the paper defers nonlinear Boltzmann corrections to future work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with two-component initial conditions (cold diluted N1 plus hot secondary fraction Br_N1) to calibrate a halo/subhalo mass-function fitting formula versus (m_N1, Br_N1), analogous to existing mixed-WDM suites.

route_step_status.reason: The ultra-relativistic N1 freeze-out yield is a standard analytic equilibrium-decoupling calculation, available despite the null tool_or_code.

The paper computed triplet-scalar matter domination, entropy dilution, and the suppressed secondary-N1 fraction semi-analytically, but no public packaged dilutor code covering a scalar with Higgs-mixing and off-shell-W_R decay channels is identified on the card.

CLASS is used for the linear matter power (per associated_code) but requires the non-thermal two-component N1 distribution as input, the treatment is linear-only, and the SDSS/Lyman-alpha comparison has only a partial likelihood needing recasting.

gaps.description: No public solver exists for the right-handed triplet-scalar dilutor cosmology: coupled evolution of scalar matter domination, entropy release before BBN, and the secondary N1 momentum distribution from the suppressed Delta_R -> N1 N1 branch, including scalar widths set by Higgs mixing and off-shell W_R channels not fully encoded on the card.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a semi-analytic dilutor module taking (M_DeltaR, lifetime, Br_Delta_to_N1, theta_h, M_WR) that outputs the dilution factor and two-component N1 f(p) for CLASS, including a scalar-width calculator for the two-body, off-shell-W_R, diphoton, and Higgs-mixing channels; validate against the paper's percent-level branching bound.

gaps.description: The LSS constraint on the secondary hot N1 fraction rests on an SDSS DR7/Lyman-alpha era comparison with only a partial likelihood; no modern packaged LSS/Lyman-alpha or X-ray line likelihood exists for this mixed cold+hot sterile-neutrino spectrum.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast current Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihoods (emulator-based eBOSS/MIKE-HIRES pipelines) and updated X-ray line searches onto CLASS transfer functions for the two-component N1 population, replacing the paper's SDSS-scale bound.

gaps.description: Nonlinear structure formation is uncalibrated for the mixed cold+hot N1 population: halo and subhalo mass-function effects are unknown, simulation_calibrated is no, and the paper's matter-power treatment is explicitly linear-only.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run mixed cold+hot dark matter N-body simulations parameterized by (m_N1, Br_Delta_to_N1) to calibrate nonlinear power and halo/subhalo mass-function suppression, following existing mixed-WDM simulation suites.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled background and perturbation equations are derived analytically in the primary paper from the Yukawa-coupled action, so the null tool_or_code reflects completed pen-and-paper work.

CLASS was modified by the authors to include the coupled CDM velocity equation and EDE initial conditions, but the card identifies no public release, so the patch must be reproduced before the step is usable.
Public MCMC samplers (MontePython/Cobaya) and the Planck 2018, BAO, Pantheon, SH0ES, and DES-Y3 likelihoods all exist; this step only awaits the upstream Boltzmann patch.

gaps.description: The modified CLASS implementing the Yukawa-coupled EDE-CDM system (scalar-dependent CDM mass rho_c(phi), coupled CDM velocity equation, and EDE perturbation initial conditions) is not publicly released, so the entire forward model from parameters to CMB/matter-power spectra cannot be run.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the paper's coupled background and perturbation equations as a patch on a public EDE-capable Boltzmann code (CLASS_EDE or AxiCLASS), adding the beta-dependent CDM mass term and momentum-exchange in the CDM Euler equation, and validate by recovering the uncoupled EDE limit at beta=0 and the paper's quoted H0 and S8 values.

gaps.description: Nonlinear structure is not modeled for this scenario: the scale-dependent coupled growth invalidates LCDM-calibrated halofit/HMcode prescriptions, degrading the DES-Y3 weak-lensing (S8) side of the analysis, which probes mildly nonlinear scales.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a small suite of N-body simulations with the scalar-dependent CDM mass and fifth-force terms (e.g. extending an interacting-dark-energy N-body code) to recalibrate a halofit/HMcode-style nonlinear boost over the viable beta and EDE parameter range.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled mediator-freeze-out plus DM-freeze-in Boltzmann system was solved in the paper and a public repository (LFDM_at_MuC) exists, but its contents are unverified on the card and no validated model implementation in a standard tool like micrOMEGAs is identified.
The tree-level mediator decay width to a charged lepton plus DM is a simple analytic formula, available despite the null tool_or_code.

LEP/LHC slepton and HSCP recasts exist and the paper performed event simulation with detector-level selections, but muon-collider detector design, backgrounds, and systematics are prospective and no reusable packaged recast or likelihood is provided.

gaps.description: No validated, reusable implementation of the coupled mediator-freeze-out plus DM-freeze-in relic calculation is confirmed: the LFDM_at_MuC repository's contents, inputs, and validation status are unknown on the card, and no model files for standard relic codes are identified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Audit and document the LFDM_at_MuC repository against the paper's Omega h^2 = 0.12 contours and tau_med boundary, or implement the model (charged scalar mediator plus neutral fermion with lepton-portal Yukawa) in micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module to reproduce the reported upper DM mass near 3.6 TeV.

gaps.description: The nonthermal freeze-in DM phase-space distribution and resulting linear transfer function are not computed anywhere: the card records distribution_function_available no, transfer_function_shape unknown, and the small-scale-structure observable enters only as a quoted 10 keV mass floor with no likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p) for DM produced by mediator decays (during and after mediator freeze-out) from the unintegrated Boltzmann equation, feed it to CLASS as a non-cold relic to get the transfer function, and map onto existing Lyman-alpha/subhalo-count WDM bounds to replace the generic 10 keV floor.

gaps.description: No reusable likelihood or detector simulation exists for the muon-collider prompt lepton and long-lived charged-track/displaced-lepton signatures; the paper's prospective 5-sigma discovery criterion and LLP counting depend on unfixed detector geometry, timing, and backgrounds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Package the paper's event-simulation and selection chain as a parameterized recast (signal efficiency maps over m_med, tau_med, branching fractions for a reference muon-collider detector), so exclusions/reach can be re-evaluated as detector designs firm up.

route_step_status.reason: This is a trivial data-transform step (restructuring the completed model card into a recovery observable) that requires no external capability, though it performs no physics forward modeling.

gaps.description: No public solver is identified for the coupled two-species hidden-sector Boltzmann system (dark photon plus millicharged fermion with hidden-sector temperature evolution) needed to compute the dark-photon freeze-in relic fraction f_Zp and its lifetime; the paper's benchmark calculation is not released and the card has no computational representation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled number-density and hidden-temperature Boltzmann equations for (M_Zp, m_chi, g_X, epsilon, delta) in a freeze-in framework such as micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module or a standalone code, validated against the paper's benchmarks including the f_Zp <= 0.05 ceiling.

gaps.description: No phase-space distribution or linear transfer function exists for the keV dark-photon subcomponent (distribution_function_available unknown, all structure_formation fields unknown), so the card's small-scale-structure observable channel cannot be forward modeled even qualitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-photon f(p) from the freeze-in and hidden-sector production channels, then compute the mixed CDM plus up-to-5-percent keV-vector transfer function with CLASS as a non-cold subcomponent and compare against Lyman-alpha bounds on mixed hot/warm subcomponents.

gaps.description: The card itself is a recovery placeholder: its single constraint is a limitation record, its route performs no physics, and related-paper citation enrichment (real observables, constraints, likelihood references for the keV dark-photon window such as X-ray and stellar-cooling limits) was never completed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the normal enrichment pipeline on paper 2312_03837 for this variant to populate genuine observables, constraints, and routes from the paper text and its citation network before gap analysis is treated as final.

route_step_status.reason: This is a trivial data-transform step (restructuring the completed model card into a recovery observable) that requires no external capability, though it performs no physics forward modeling.

gaps.description: No public implementation exists for the paper's coupled visible/hidden-sector Boltzmann system (dark fermion and dark photon number densities plus hidden-sector temperature ratio eta) that sets the millicharged freeze-in relic abundance, including plasmon-decay production and dark freeze-out; the eight-benchmark calculation is private and the card has no computational representation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the coupled number-density and hidden-temperature evolution for (m_chi, M_Zp, g_X, epsilon, delta, eta) including plasmon decay and hidden-sector reactions, either as a standalone solver or by extending micrOMEGAs' freeze-in machinery, validated against the paper's eight benchmarks.

gaps.description: No phase-space distribution or transfer function is available for the freeze-in millicharged fermion (distribution_function_available unknown, all structure_formation fields unknown), so the card's small-scale-structure observable channel cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p) for the freeze-in plus dark-freeze-out chi population from the unintegrated Boltzmann equation, and compute the linear transfer function with CLASS treating chi as a non-cold, millicharged species (including any DM-baryon drag via its ETHOS-like coupling) for comparison with Lyman-alpha and CMB small-scale data.

gaps.description: The card carries only a placeholder limitation record instead of real constraints: no likelihoods or recasts are attached for the millicharge bounds the card says constrain delta (e.g. direct detection, CMB DM-baryon scattering, stellar cooling, accelerator millicharge searches), because related-paper enrichment was not completed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the enrichment pipeline on paper 2312_03837 to attach the actual millicharge constraint set, then map published millicharge exclusion curves onto the (m_chi, effective charge) plane as reusable likelihood or exclusion-region records.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs (with native Z3 semi-annihilation support) and DRAKE both exist publicly, but the combined treatment of semi-annihilation with early kinetic decoupling used custom FeynCalc matrix elements and no paper-specific model implementation is released.

sigma_SI is computable with micrOMEGAs and public tools like DDCalc carry XENON1T/LZ likelihoods, but the card records likelihood_available as partial and no current-detector likelihood is wired to this model's outputs.

Generic finite-temperature/bounce tools (CosmoTransitions-style) and standard GW spectrum templates exist, but no public implementation of this Z3 scalar potential is available and the card notes no independent run was performed.

gaps.description: No public model implementation combines the Z3 inert doublet-singlet matrix elements (annihilation, co-annihilation, semi-annihilation) with a DRAKE-style coupled Boltzmann treatment of early kinetic decoupling; the paper's FeynCalc+DRAKE+micrOMEGAs pipeline is not released.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the Z3 model files in micrOMEGAs (CalcHEP model) and couple its semi-annihilation rates into DRAKE's cBE mode with the gamma/H(x=100) switching criterion used in the paper, then release the model files.

gaps.description: The relic-plus-direct-detection viability step relies on recasting published XENON1T/PandaX-4T/LZ curves; no current xenon-detector likelihood is connected to the model's predicted sigma_SI and relic-fraction rescaling.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the model's sigma_SI and Omega-rescaled local density into DDCalc (or the LZ public likelihood) so the direct-detection constraint is evaluated as a likelihood rather than a digitized-curve cut.

gaps.description: No public implementation exists of the Z3 doublet-singlet finite-temperature effective potential (with loop and thermal corrections) and the downstream T_n, alpha_PT, beta/H and stochastic GW spectrum computation; the GW observable currently rests entirely on source-paper figures.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the Z3 scalar potential with one-loop and daisy-resummed thermal corrections in CosmoTransitions, extract T_n, alpha_PT, beta/H from the bounce action, and feed standard sound-wave GW spectrum templates plus LISA-class sensitivity curves for SNR.

route_step_status.reason: Generic bounce/nucleation tools like CosmoTransitions exist, but the Coleman-Weinberg U(1)_D potential with the non-minimal xi phi^2 R coupling that completes the supercooled transition has no public implementation and tool_or_code is null.

Standard semi-analytic sound-wave/collision GW templates are public, but they are calibrated for moderate transitions and their extrapolation to strongly supercooled alpha >> 1 transitions is uncertain, as the step's validity note flags.
The late-blooming PBH abundance from false-vacuum decay statistics is exponentially sensitive and exists only as paper-level analytic estimates; no public calculator implements it.
Public PTA new-physics fitters (PTArcade/ceffyl-style tools on NANOGrav 15-yr data) exist, but no likelihood was run and the model's GW spectrum is not connected to them.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the classically scale-invariant U(1)_D effective potential with the non-minimal gravitational coupling exists to compute the nucleation action, T_n, alpha, and beta/H_n for the supercooled transition; all transition thermodynamics currently come from the source paper.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the one-loop Coleman-Weinberg plus thermal U(1)_D potential including the xi phi^2 R term in CosmoTransitions (or FindBounce), and validate the bounce-action tracking through deep supercooling against the paper's benchmark region.

gaps.description: Semi-analytic GW spectrum templates (sound waves, bubble collisions, turbulence) are calibrated for weak-to-moderate transitions; their normalization and spectral shape in the strongly supercooled, vacuum-dominated regime relevant here are uncalibrated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run or adopt hydrodynamic/lattice simulations of strongly supercooled transitions (large alpha, relativistic walls) to calibrate an extended template parameterized by (alpha, beta/H_n, wall velocity), and propagate the resulting shape uncertainty into the PTA fit.

gaps.description: No public calculator implements the late-blooming PBH mass and abundance from patch-to-patch false-vacuum decay statistics, and f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to the transition-tail assumptions, so M_PBH and f_PBH cannot be independently evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Code the late-blooming formalism (survival probability of late-nucleating Hubble patches, overdensity threshold, horizon-mass collapse) as a module taking (T_n, beta/H_n, alpha) from the effective-potential step, and quantify sensitivity to the decay-rate tail by varying the nucleation-rate expansion.

gaps.description: The PTA compatibility claim is figure-level: the model's GW spectrum has never been passed through a public PTA stochastic-background likelihood, and no PBH-abundance likelihood against microlensing/evaporation limits is wired up either.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Insert the model's phase-transition GW spectrum as a custom signal in PTArcade (NANOGrav 15-yr free-spectrum likelihood) and compare f_PBH(M_PBH) against compiled PBH constraint curves (e.g. via the public PBHbounds compilation) as a likelihood mask.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled phi_1/chi/nu_R abundance equations are published in the paper but the solver is a private custom implementation with no public release.
Comparing the predicted Delta N_eff against the quoted Planck 2018 and BBN intervals is a trivial pass/fail check requiring no tool.
The free-streaming length follows from the paper's appendix formulae applied to the computed momentum distribution, which is simple analytic work.

The FSL-threshold comparison is doable by hand but only qualitative; a quantitative structure constraint needs the nonthermal transfer function passed through a Lyman-alpha likelihood, which is not connected.
Overlaying the published ATLAS/CMS dilepton exclusions and the LEP m_Zprime/g_BL > 7 TeV bound on the parameter plane is a straightforward recast of quoted limits.

gaps.description: No public solver implements the coupled Boltzmann system for phi_1 freeze-out, chi freeze-in from phi_1 decay, and thermal plus nonthermal right-handed-neutrino energy density in the gauged B-L setup, so Delta N_eff and the relic abundance cannot be evaluated at new parameter points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the paper's coupled abundance and energy-density equations in a public freeze-in framework (e.g. extend micrOMEGAs freeze-in routines or a standalone ULYSSES/odeint solver) tracking Y_phi1, Y_chi, and rho_nuR through the Z' and scalar portals, validated against the paper's Delta N_eff contours.

gaps.description: The structure-formation constraint is only a free-streaming-length threshold; no pipeline maps the model's nonthermal FIMP momentum distribution to a linear transfer function and a Lyman-alpha (or Milky Way satellite) likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the computed f(q) into CLASS as a non-cold dark matter species to obtain T(k), then constrain it with an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator/likelihood (or the area-criterion mapping to thermal WDM bounds) instead of the 0.1 Mpc FSL cut.

route_step_status.reason: The coherent vector relic abundance follows from the paper's closed-form analytic formulas in (m, g, T_osc), which is pen-and-paper work needing no dedicated tool.

Published dark-photon and cluster sigma/m limit curves exist, but applying them requires a nontrivial component-fraction, normalization, and wave-effect recast that has not been performed and has no tool_or_code.

gaps.description: No worked recast maps published dark-photon dark-matter limits onto this model: the effective kinetic mixing epsilon ~ lambda m^2/(g^2 f^2) applies to only one of three degenerate SU(2) components, so limits must be rescaled by component fraction and degeneracy-breaking assumptions, and the cluster sigma/m ~ g^4/m^3 comparison is only a dimensional estimate with unquantified wave-regime corrections.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the mixed-component energy fraction and effective epsilon across the (m, g, f) plane, rescale existing dark-photon DM absorption/haloscope exclusions by that fraction, and compute the actual non-Abelian vector self-scattering cross section (including wave-regime suppression at low m) for comparison with cluster sigma/m bounds.

gaps.description: The small-scale-structure requirement (T_osc > 1.3e6 GeV, z_T > 5.5e6) is a quoted estimate: no Boltzmann-code implementation of the dark-radiation-to-matter transition of the coherent SU(2) condensate exists to compute the linear power suppression and make the oscillation-onset bound quantitative.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the oscillating vector condensate as a species in CLASS/CAMB with an equation of state transitioning from radiation-like to matter-like at T_osc, compute the transfer-function cutoff, and confront it with Lyman-alpha and Milky Way satellite constraints instead of the quoted threshold.

route_step_status.reason: The self-heating temperature-evolution Boltzmann system is published and was solved by the authors, but the implementation is private and no public tool tracks T_1(a) for this model.
The coupled two-component perturbation equations with the heated species' sound speed are given in the paper but are not implemented in any public Boltzmann code such as CLASS or CAMB.
GADGET-4 is public and the step is a standard collisionless N-body run from a modified initial linear power spectrum.
FOF/SUBFIND halo finding and extraction of N(>V_max) are standard public GADGET-4 tooling.
Translating an MCVF-fitted benchmark into particle parameters (m_1, m_2, r_1, cross sections) is a simple parameter mapping requiring no tool.
No tool computes the local boosted chi_1 flux from chi_2 annihilation and the resulting event rates with detector response in Super-Kamiokande/XENONnT/JUNO; the paper explicitly defers this.

gaps.description: No public code implements the chi_1 self-heating temperature evolution and the coupled two-component linear perturbation equations (heated species with time-dependent sound speed plus cold chi_2), so the suppressed and oscillatory P(k) that seeds every downstream prediction cannot be regenerated at new parameter points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model as a CLASS extension: an interacting two-fluid module with the paper's T_1(a) heating equation sourced by the chi_2 chi_2 -> chi_1 chi_1 rate and chi_1 self-scattering, outputting P(k) validated against the paper's benchmark spectra.

gaps.description: Lyman-alpha constraints exist only as a qualitative argument that thermal-WDM mass bounds are weakened; no dedicated recast maps the model's nonthermal, fraction-and-splitting-controlled suppression onto Lyman-alpha flux-power data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the model's transfer functions through an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator or apply the area-criterion mapping calibrated on hydrodynamic simulations, scanning (r_1, m_1, m_2, sigma_self_1) to replace the qualitative weakened-bound statement with contours.

gaps.description: The MCVF comparison is benchmark-level: no likelihood connects the simulated subhalo N(>V_max) to observed Milky Way satellite counts, and baryonic-feedback and halo-profile systematics were explicitly left untreated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing Milky Way satellite likelihood (subhalo mass function conditioned on suppressed P(k), including a disk-disruption and galaxy-halo connection model) to this model's transfer functions, calibrated with a small suite of zoom-in simulations including baryonic corrections.

gaps.description: No calculation exists of the present-day boosted chi_1 flux from Galactic chi_2 annihilation and the resulting elastic-scattering event rates with detector response in Super-Kamiokande, XENONnT, or JUNO, so the proposed terrestrial-detection observable cannot be evaluated at all.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the local boosted chi_1 flux from the Galactic chi_2 density profile and annihilation rate, then extend an existing boosted-dark-matter event-rate framework with kinetic-mixing-mediated electron/nucleon cross sections and published detector efficiencies for Super-K, XENONnT, and JUNO.

route_step_status.reason: Fokker-Planck stochastic-inflation solvers exist as private research codes, but no public tool implements the required finite-duration, time-dependent H(N) evolution of the spectator axion distribution that this paper argues invalidates the equilibrium treatment.
The theta_end-to-Omega_a h^2 misalignment mapping is a standard analytic QCD axion abundance formula, and public codes such as MiMeS implement it if numerical precision is wanted.

Planck/BICEP inflation and isocurvature likelihoods are public, but the recast propagating the quasi-flat theta_end distribution into axion isocurvature power P_S is not implemented (card lists both likelihoods as unavailable and likelihood_available is no/partial).

gaps.description: No public stochastic-inflation Fokker-Planck solver evolves the QCD axion misalignment-angle probability distribution through a realistic finite-duration inflation with time-dependent H(N), which is the central ingredient replacing the equilibrium stochastic-window assumption.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or reimplement a Fokker-Planck / Langevin lattice solver for a spectator axion in stochastic inflation, parameterized by f_a, the inflationary potential (or H(N) trajectory), and inflation duration, validated against the constant-H equilibrium limit and the paper's quasi-flat regime.

gaps.description: No likelihood pipeline maps the non-equilibrium (quasi-flat) end-of-inflation axion distribution into isocurvature power P_S and confronts it jointly with Planck isocurvature and tensor (r_0.002) constraints; only equilibrium-distribution isocurvature bounds exist in the literature.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the isocurvature power spectrum from the quasi-flat theta_end distribution (including the hilltop enhancement), feed it as a CDM-isocurvature component into CLASS/CAMB, and build a recast against the public Planck 2018 + BK inflation likelihood over (f_a, H_end).

route_step_status.reason: Diagonalizing the two-axion mass matrix from (Q_ni, Lambda_2, f_a1, f_a2) and estimating the collapse hierarchy is pen-and-paper linear algebra valid for the two-axion effective setup.
