gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast existing ultralight-DM fraction constraints by running axionCAMB (or the CLASS ultralight-axion module) over the (m_phi, eta) plane and applying published CMB, Lyman-alpha, and subhalo bounds on the suppressed power spectrum, producing an eta_max(m_phi) curve for the registry.

route_step_status.reason: The vacuum-misalignment abundance for a pre-inflationary QCD axion is a standard analytic formula written in the primary paper, so a null tool_or_code does not make it missing.
The isocurvature contribution S_DM(F_a, H_inf) and the quoted H_inf bound are standard analytic expressions given explicitly in the primary text.
Applying the Planck 3-sigma band 0.1172-0.1226 and the quoted isocurvature limit is a direct numerical comparison; a full Planck likelihood is only needed for precision beyond the paper's use.
The QCD axion mass relation is standard analytic, but the model-specific electromagnetic anomaly ratio E/N and hence g_a_gamma for this extended Type-II 2HDM is not computed anywhere in the card.
Public haloscope exclusion compilations exist, but the card carries only quoted mass ranges rather than coupling-limit curves, and no comparison tool is attached (route_status planned).

gaps.description: The model-specific axion-photon coupling has not been derived: the electromagnetic-to-color anomaly ratio E/N of this extended Type-II 2HDM with U(1)_{B_i-L_i} and two PQ-charged singlets is never computed, so the model cannot be placed on the (m_a, g_a_gamma) haloscope plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute E/N from the PQ charge assignments of the Type-II fermion content (including the B_i-L_i charged leptons and right-handed neutrinos) using the standard anomaly-coefficient formula, and record g_a_gamma(F_a) with the model-independent chiral correction E/N - 1.92.

gaps.description: No haloscope exclusion-curve data is integrated: the card quotes only experiment mass windows (ADMX 2.7-4.2 micro-eV, CAPP, MADMAX, KLASH, ABRACADABRA), not coupling-limit curves, so covered/excluded flags cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Ingest the publicly maintained AxionLimits compilation of haloscope g_a_gamma(m_a) exclusion and projection curves into the registry comparison step and score the model's g_a_gamma(F_a) line (from gap_1) against it.

route_step_status.reason: The Type-X ALP has no QCD anomaly and its mass must come from PQ-violating (Planck-suppressed) terms that the paper never specifies or derives, so the potential curvature cannot currently be computed at all.
Once m_a and F_a are fixed, the ALP misalignment abundance is a standard analytic formula, so this step is pen-and-paper despite the null tool_or_code.
The lifetime check requires model-specific ALP couplings and decay channels that are underdetermined in the card (decay_channels 'unknown'), so the validation is not currently performable.
The Delta a_mu contribution uses standard 2HDM plus gauge-boson loop expressions for which public precision codes (e.g. 2HDMC/GM2Calc-class tools) and the paper's own formulas exist.
Applying the M_N <= ~1 TeV consistency bound from the Planck-suppressed operator estimate is a simple analytic validation given the paper's quoted scaling.

gaps.description: The Type-X ALP mass, couplings, and lifetime are underived: without the QCD gluon anomaly the pseudoscalar's potential must come from the model's Planck-suppressed PQ-violating operators, but no explicit m_a(F_a) relation, photon/lepton couplings, or decay-width calculation exists, blocking both the misalignment abundance and the cosmological-stability check.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Enumerate the leading Planck-suppressed PQ-violating operators allowed by the Type-X charge assignment and U(1)_{B_i-L_i}, derive m_a and the ALP-photon/lepton couplings from them, compute the decay width to check cosmological stability, and only then run the standard ALP misalignment formula against the Planck relic-density band.

route_step_status.reason: Mediator partial widths from the dimension-6 four-Fermi operators are a standard tree-level pen-and-paper calculation, so a null tool_or_code is not a blocker.

Only the qualitative decay-before-one-second criterion is available (likelihood_available: no); a quantitative BBN light-element likelihood for late leptonic energy injection is not wired in, though public codes for this class of constraint exist.

The flux formula is analytic, but the cascade photon yields require boosting public leptonic spectra (e.g. PPPC4DMID-type tables) through the mediator two-body decay, and no such convolution is packaged for this model.
Public Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal likelihoods exist, but no target selection or recast of this model's cascade spectra against them has been set up (likelihood_available: unknown).

The paper solves three coupled Boltzmann equations for T_D, n_DM, n_med privately; micrOMEGAs' two-temperature dark-sector machinery could cover this regime but this EFT with the fast-expanding H(T) option is not implemented in any public code named by the card.
Comparing Omega_DM h^2 and Gamma/H outputs against the relic target and off-equilibrium boundary is a trivial post-processing/validation step.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the secluded-sector coupled Boltzmann system (dark-sector temperature T_D plus DM and mediator number densities) for this Type-X portal EFT, including the fast-expanding cosmology option (n=1, T_r); the paper's solver is private.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the four-Fermi portal and dark-sector conversion operators as a micrOMEGAs model with its two-temperature dark-sector evolution, adding a user-defined H(T) for the fast-expanding branch, and validate against the paper's n=0 and n=1 benchmark plots.

gaps.description: No quantitative BBN light-element likelihood is connected to the late-decaying mediator: only a qualitative one-second lifetime criterion is used, so the bbn_decay_before_one_second constraint cannot be evaluated as a proper exclusion in (C_l, m_med).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run the mediator's electromagnetic and neutrino injection through a public BBN injection code such as ACROPOLIS or AlterBBN, tabulating the excluded region in mediator lifetime versus abundance, and attach the result as a likelihood to the route.

gaps.description: No packaged indirect-detection pipeline for the secluded cascade: boosted photon spectra from DM DM -> mediator mediator -> leptons are not tabulated for this model, and no Fermi-LAT target and likelihood have been selected for the recast.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Convolve public leptonic photon-yield tables (PPPC4DMID-style) with the mediator two-body decay boost to obtain dN_gamma/dE, then evaluate against the published Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal bin-by-bin likelihoods for the NFW J-factors assumed in the card.

route_step_status.reason: Reading the completed model card into a structured recovery observable is a trivial data transform that needs no external tool.

gaps.description: The paper's freeze-in production rates use closed-time-path finite-temperature field theory with one-loop resummed fermion propagators, evaluated by private VEGAS-based numerical integration; public freeze-in machinery (e.g. micrOMEGAs' freeze-in module) implements only vacuum/Boltzmann or HTL-approximated rates, so the thermally corrected relic density cannot be reproduced with existing tools.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module (or release a standalone rate library) with the CTP one-loop resummed decay and 2-to-2 production rates for the F f s vertex, parameterized by (m_s, m_F, Delta, lambda, G) in the electroweak-unbroken phase, validated against the paper's Boltzmann-versus-resummed comparisons.

gaps.description: No late-time phase-space distribution f(p) is derived for the frozen-in scalar (the paper computes number densities only), so the free-streaming scale and linear transfer function needed for the card's small_scale_structure observable channel cannot be evaluated.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive f(p) by integrating the unintegrated CTP production rate over temperature (decay plus scattering contributions), then feed it to CLASS as a non-cold-DM species to obtain the transfer function and half-mode mass for comparison with Lyman-alpha and subhalo-count constraints.

gaps.description: The routing block is a recovery placeholder: the single route contains only a card-reading data transform and defines no forward-model chain from (lambda, G, m_s, m_F, Delta) to any concrete observable or constraint, so there is no evaluable path even where tools exist.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rerun the standard enrichment on the primary paper to build real routes: a freeze-in relic-density route (rate calculation to Omega h^2 target) and a structure-formation route (f(p) to CLASS transfer function to small-scale-structure likelihoods), with citation-supported constraints replacing the placeholder record.

route_step_status.reason: NMSSMTools 6.0.0 is a named public spectrum generator that covers the GUT-scale constrained NMSSM inputs used by the paper.
micrOMEGAs (relic density, direct detection), HiggsSignals, HiggsBounds, and SModelS are all public and are the exact tools the paper used to accept or exclude scan points.
Identifying the dominant g-2 loop and coannihilation mechanism from accepted points is simple post-processing of tool outputs, so a null tool_or_code is not a blocker.

gaps.description: The exact scan configuration and combined likelihood are not released: the paper's cuts (Omega h^2 < 0.131, 2023 muon g-2 window, LZ/XENONnT acceptance) are applied as tool-level pass/fail selections with no public combined likelihood or input files, so the surviving light-smuon sample cannot be exactly reproduced or reweighted.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct the scan as NMSSMTools input files with the quoted GUT-scale ranges and the m_smuon1 < m_stau1 selection, and package the constraint chain as a composite likelihood (e.g. in a GAMBIT- or EasyScan-style wrapper) so the paper's acceptance cuts become reproducible and reweightable.

route_step_status.reason: The initial rotation and phase-fluctuation mass follow analytically from the Hubble-induced quadratic potential, but the named 'PQ-field effective potential solver' is generic, not a public code, and accurate rotation initial conditions require numerical evolution of the complex PQ field.

Public axion-abundance codes (e.g. MiMeS-class misalignment solvers) cover standard misalignment, but no public integrator evolves a rotating PQ charge Y_PQ through reheating and the QCD transition to Omega_a h^2 in the kinetic-misalignment regime.

Axiogenesis/lepto-axiogenesis conversion formulas exist in the cited literature, but the model-dependent sphaleron and lepton-number transport coefficients are not packaged in any public tool named by the card.

gaps.description: No public solver evolves the rotating Planck-scale PQ field from its inflationary initial conditions (Hubble-induced plus Planck-suppressed potential terms) through kinetic misalignment to the axion relic abundance; both the rotation setup (s1) and the Y_PQ-to-Omega_a h^2 integration (s2) are done with private, paper-specific calculations.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public misalignment code such as MiMeS (or release a standalone ODE package) to evolve the complex PQ field with a quadratic Hubble-induced potential and conserved-charge kinetic-misalignment tracking, taking (f_a, m_a, H_I, T_R, Hubble-induced mass coefficients) as inputs and returning Y_PQ, Omega_a h^2, and the inflationary phase mass m_theta/H_I; validate against the paper's joint-abundance solutions.

gaps.description: The PQ-charge-to-baryon-asymmetry conversion (axiogenesis/lepto-axiogenesis) depends on model-dependent sphaleron and lepton-number transport coefficients that are not derived in reusable form for this scenario's operator choices, so Y_B cannot be computed for a general point without redoing the transport analysis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive and tabulate the transport/conversion coefficients c_B for the relevant B-L violating operators (following the lepto-axiogenesis literature cited by the card) as functions of T_R and the operator scale, and package them as a lookup usable with the gap_1 solver output.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs is public and supports two-component dark matter with semi-annihilation, but the model-specific implementation files used by the paper are not released, so the coupled Y_chi/Y_eta bouncing evolution cannot be run as-is.

The zero-velocity rate formulas are analytic, but the indirect-detection target rates need model-specific h_1/h_2 branching fractions and semi-annihilation spectra that follow from the same unreleased model implementation.

Public LZ likelihood implementations (e.g. DDCalc-class tools) and quoted collider mixing bounds exist, but the recast requires two-component local-density rescaling and a second-Higgs search recast that are not set up (LZ likelihood listed as unavailable/partial).

gaps.description: No public model implementation exists for the singlet-Dirac-fermion plus pNGB two-component model: the CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model files the paper used to solve the coupled bouncing yields are not released, blocking the relic-density step and the model-specific cross sections and spectra downstream.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the low-energy Lagrangian (fermion-pNGB coupling, h_1/h_2 mixing, scalar potential) in FeynRules/CalcHEP and register it as a micrOMEGAs two-component model with semi-annihilation, validating against the paper's 500/700 GeV inverse-hierarchy benchmarks and the Omega_chi + Omega_eta = 0.12 target.

gaps.description: No two-component direct-detection likelihood: the LZ spin-independent bound must be applied with each component's local density rescaled by Omega_i/Omega_c and with the pNGB Goldstone cancellation at zero momentum transfer, and no such rescaled recast is packaged (card notes the batch did not compute one).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public direct-detection likelihood package such as DDCalc with the LZ 2022 exposure, feeding it sigma_chiN_SI from the gap_1 model files and weighting event rates by the component relic fractions from the coupled Boltzmann solution.

gaps.description: No gamma-ray likelihood is attached to the enhanced present-day annihilation prediction: the route lists the gamma-ray likelihood as unavailable, so the above-thermal <sigma v>_0 values from bouncing freeze-out cannot be tested against dwarf-galaxy or Galactic Center data, including the nonstandard kinematics of semi-annihilation final states.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate photon spectra for the h_i-mediated annihilation and semi-annihilation channels (micrOMEGAs or PPPC4DMID tables, with the boosted single-scalar kinematics for semi-annihilation) and evaluate them against the published Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal bin-by-bin likelihoods with component-density-squared weighting.

route_step_status.reason: Setting lambda_phi=0 and solving the tree-level scalar-sector relations is simple pen-and-paper algebra needing no tool.
micrOMEGAs covers Higgs-portal scalar freeze-out, but the paper's FeynRules model file is not identified as publicly released, so the model implementation must be rebuilt.
The perturbativity cut is analytic, but the XENONnT limit-curve comparison is not implemented; only qualitative/numeric edges from the paper exist.
The 2:1:1 W+W-:ZZ:H1H1 channel ratio is an analytic amplitude result quoted in the paper.
Public spectral tables (PPPC4DMID-type) and Fermi-LAT dSph / Planck likelihoods exist, but the recast pipeline for these multi-TeV channels is not assembled per the card.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP model files for the lambda_phi=0 linear-breaking scalar singlet) is released, so the micrOMEGAs relic-density workflow used in the paper cannot be reproduced without rebuilding the model files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the scalar potential with the linear U(1)_X breaking term in FeynRules, export CalcHEP model files, and validate against the paper's few-TeV to ~70 TeV allowed window in micrOMEGAs.

gaps.description: No implemented XENONnT spin-independent upper-limit recast exists for the scan's validation step; the card records likelihood_available as unknown and only qualitative window edges from the paper.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the XENONnT SI limit curve and wire it into the scan via DDCalc or the micrOMEGAs direct-detection module, reproducing the ~2.7 TeV low-mass edge.

gaps.description: The indirect-detection route lacks an assembled pipeline from W+W-/ZZ/H1H1 annihilation at multi-TeV masses to Fermi-LAT dwarf and CMB energy-injection constraints; spectra and experimental likelihoods are external and unwired.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Combine tabulated PPPC4DMID (or HDMSpectra for the heaviest masses) final-state spectra with the public Fermi-LAT dSph likelihood and a Planck f_eff energy-injection bound to produce a channel-weighted sigma-v constraint.

route_step_status.reason: Building the scalar mass eigenstates and mixing angle from the tree-level potential is straightforward analytic algebra given in the paper.
micrOMEGAs handles this Higgs-portal pNGB freeze-out including resonances, but the paper's FeynRules model file is not identified as publicly released.
The non-momentum-suppressed scalar-mediated SI cross section is a tree-level analytic formula quoted in the paper.
The Higgs-invisible formula is given and stability/perturbativity cuts are analytic, but the exact XENONnT limit curve is flagged as needed and not implemented.
Public tabulated spectra (PPPC4DMID/Pythia) cover the b bbar, W+W-, ZZ and scalar final states, but the card records no spectra implementation for this model.
Fermi-LAT dSph and Planck energy-injection likelihoods are public, but the external recast is not assembled in this batch per the card.

gaps.description: No public model implementation (FeynRules/CalcHEP files for the linear-breaking pNGB complex singlet) is released, so the micrOMEGAs relic workflow and resonance structure cannot be reproduced without rebuilding the model files.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the complex-singlet potential with the soft linear breaking term in FeynRules, export to micrOMEGAs, and validate that the SI amplitude vanishes only for degenerate H1 and H2 as the paper states.

gaps.description: The constraint-comparison step lacks an implemented XENONnT SI upper-limit recast (the card explicitly notes the exact limit curve is needed for numerical recast), preventing quantitative exclusion of scan points.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the XENONnT SI limit curve and integrate it via DDCalc or micrOMEGAs' direct-detection routines alongside the paper's Higgs-invisible Br<0.11 cut and analytic stability/unitarity flags.

gaps.description: The indirect-detection recast route has no assembled pipeline from per-channel sigma-v to Fermi-LAT dwarf-spheroidal and CMB energy-injection constraints for this model's mixed W+W-/ZZ/fermion/scalar final states.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Generate channel spectra from PPPC4DMID tables (or Pythia for the H_i H_j cascades), then evaluate against the public Fermi-LAT dSph joint likelihood and a Planck f_eff energy-injection bound.

route_step_status.reason: The coupled GR scalar-fermion equilibrium equations require a numerical solver and no public code exists for this scalarized false-vacuum-pocket system (associated_code identifies none).
Turning-point stability analysis along a computed mass-radius sequence is a standard pen-and-paper criterion once the equilibrium sequence exists.
The halo-model microlensing population formalism is standard and semi-analytic, but the model-specific soliton mass function it needs is not predicted by any existing formation calculation.
OGLE and Subaru/HSC efficiency curves and constraints are published, but no ready likelihood implementation exists for recasting them onto this population (likelihood_available: no).

gaps.description: No numerical solver exists for the coupled Einstein-scalar-fermion equilibrium problem of vacuum-scalarized false-vacuum pockets, so mass-radius curves, M_max, compactness, and tidal Love numbers cannot be computed outside the paper's own benchmarks.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a shooting-method solver for the paper's action (Thomas-Fermi fermion fluid plus real scalar in GR), extending existing fermion-soliton/boson-star structure codes, and add the metric-perturbation equations needed for k2 tidal response.

gaps.description: No quantitative formation calculation exists: solitosynthesis/solitogenesis abundance and the resulting soliton-star mass function are not derived, so f_DM and the mass spectrum feeding the microlensing population step cannot be predicted from model parameters.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the soliton mass function and relic fraction by extending Fermi-ball/solitosynthesis formation calculations (charge-fluctuation statistics plus phase-transition history) to this Yukawa-coupled scalar-fermion sector, with accretion evolution to the stable branch.

gaps.description: No microlensing likelihood implementation exists for this model: the OGLE/HSC event-rate recast (survey efficiency convolution and f_DM limits or anomaly-region fit) is not assembled.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a standard compact-object microlensing event-rate code using published OGLE and Subaru/HSC efficiency curves, producing f_DM(M) limits and the anomaly-region likelihood for the ~1e-6 M_sun benchmark.

route_step_status.reason: Public NMSSM spectrum generators (NMSSMTools, SPheno/SARAH) fully cover the Z3 NMSSM neutralino and Higgs sector used in the scan.
micrOMEGAs computes NMSSM relic density including coannihilation and funnels plus sigma_SI/sigma_SD, and comparison to public xenon/fluorine limits is standard (e.g. via DDCalc).

MadGraph/Pythia/Delphes and recast frameworks are public, but the specific ATLAS soft-photon electroweakino analysis for compressed radiative decays is not implemented in public recast tools per the card (likelihood_available: no).

gaps.description: No public recast implementation exists for the ATLAS photon-rich electroweakino searches (soft photons from compressed chi_i -> gamma chi_1 decays with multilepton or b-jet objects), so LHC/HL-LHC exclusions on the singlino-bino coannihilation spectra cannot be evaluated numerically.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the ATLAS photon electroweakino analysis in CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 with validated Delphes photon thresholds for the compressed regime, and validate against the overlap regions quoted in the paper's figures.

gaps.description: The paper's scan benchmark cards (SLHA input files for the blind-spot and coannihilation regimes) are not released, hindering validation of the registry pipeline against the published relic-density, sigma_SI, and branching-fraction benchmarks.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct SLHA benchmark cards from the paper's quoted parameter values (e.g. the M1 ~ 90 GeV, sigma_SI ~ 1e-48 cm^2 blind-spot point) using NMSSMTools, and verify Omega h^2 and radiative branching fractions against the paper figures.

route_step_status.reason: Numerical-relativity collapse simulations exist and were run by the primary paper, but no public threshold library covers QCD-era profiles, and the paper itself states refined simulations are needed.
Only an approximate analytic Boltzmann treatment of hot-spot sphaleron baryogenesis exists, with the Standard Model CP treatment flagged as uncertain in the card.

Integrating the fluctuation distribution over the two nearby thresholds to obtain global eta_b and f_PBH is a Press-Schechter-style threshold integral doable analytically once the thresholds from s1 are given.
The card records no PBH binary-formation/merger-rate model and no GW catalog likelihood (likelihood_available: no, 'no GW likelihood included'), so the joint GW-baryon recast is not currently doable.

gaps.description: No refined numerical-relativity determination of the QCD-epoch collapse thresholds delta_c (PBH formation) and delta_baryo (aborted-collapse hot spot) as functions of curvature profile and the QCD equation of state; the whole eta_b-f_PBH link rests on the small, currently uncertain separation between these two thresholds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a suite of numerical-relativity collapse simulations across curvature-profile shapes with the lattice-QCD equation of state, tabulating delta_c, delta_baryo, and hot-spot peak temperature versus profile and horizon mass, and release the results as a public threshold/mass-function library.

gaps.description: The local baryon asymmetry produced in an aborted-PBH hot spot is computed only with an approximate Boltzmann treatment; a quantitative calculation of sphaleron rates and the effective Standard Model CP violation in the transiently reheated hot-spot environment is missing, so the eta_b normalization (the factor 2-3 times f_PBH) is uncertain.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the out-of-equilibrium sphaleron transition rate and CP-violating source in the expanding/cooling hot-spot background (extending electroweak-baryogenesis transport-equation machinery to this geometry) and validate against the primary paper's approximate treatment.

gaps.description: No PBH binary-formation and merger-rate model coupled to a gravitational-wave catalog likelihood exists for this scenario's tens-to-hundreds solar-mass, QCD-epoch mass function, so the predicted mass-gap merger signal cannot be confronted with LVK data or combined with the baryon-abundance target.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a merger-rate forward model (early-binary and cluster channels) taking the QCD-epoch PBH mass function as input, and recast it through a public GW population-inference likelihood (e.g. GWTC hierarchical population tools) jointly with the eta_b constraint.

route_step_status.reason: CosmoTransitions-class public tools can compute bounce actions and nucleation rates, but the model-specific Coleman-Weinberg ALP potential and supercooled nucleation/reheating pipeline is not implemented anywhere per the card.
Standard semi-analytic FOPT GW spectral templates and public power-law-integrated detector sensitivity curves cover this step as done in the paper.
The delayed false-vacuum-patch collapse estimate is a published semi-analytic formula, but only in the monochromatic, instantaneous-reheating approximation with no public implementation.
Public PBH constraint compilations and ALP limit databases exist, but the recast onto (f_a, g) is not assembled and the card flags OCR-corrupted mass-window exponents needing PDF verification.

gaps.description: No implementation exists of the supercooled ALP-sector phase-transition dynamics: the model's finite-temperature Coleman-Weinberg potential, bubble nucleation rate, beta/H, transition strength, and reheating temperature over the (f_a, g) plane are not computable outside the paper.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the radiative U(1)-breaking scalar potential with the SU(2) gauge-sector running in CosmoTransitions (or a bespoke bounce solver for the near-conformal flat direction) and output nucleation/percolation parameters and T_RH on an (f_a, g) grid.

gaps.description: PBH formation is treated only in a monochromatic, instantaneous-reheating approximation; the extended PBH mass function and non-instantaneous reheating/dilution corrections needed to robustly evaluate f_PBH — and to test whether the NANOGrav-preferred region truly overcloses — are not derived.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend the delayed false-vacuum-decay calculation to the full late-patch statistics, deriving an extended PBH mass function and adding prolonged-reheating and entropy-dilution branches, then rerun the f_PBH=1 contour and the NANOGrav overclosure check.

gaps.description: The PBH constraint inputs are unverified: the f_PBH=1 mass-window exponents (~1e-16 to 1e-10 M_sun) are flagged as vulnerable to OCR minus-sign loss, and no machine-readable PBH constraint tables are attached for the constraint-mapping step.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Verify the mass-window exponents against the source PDF and import a machine-readable PBH constraint compilation (e.g. the public PBHbounds tables) plus AxionLimits data for the ALP-coupling complementarity mapping.

gaps.description: No machine-readable likelihood exists for the GW observables: the paper uses only power-law-integrated sensitivity comparisons, so neither the NANOGrav data preference nor future PTA/LISA non-observation can be evaluated statistically for this model's SGWB spectrum.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the model's FOPT SGWB spectrum into the public NANOGrav 15-yr free-spectrum likelihood (e.g. via PTArcade) and add LISA/ET signal-to-noise-based projected likelihoods for the future-reach statements.

route_step_status.reason: Two- and three-body B -> K + H1/X Xbar decay rates through the effective flavor vertex are closed-form analytic expressions given in the paper and need no dedicated code.

Generic relic solvers (micrOMEGAs/MadDM) can handle hidden-sector freeze-out with dark Higgs and dark photon final states, but the card lists no model implementation, so a FeynRules/CalcHEP model file must be built first.

The paper mass windows and published Belle II/KOTO bounds can be applied as hard cuts, but no public likelihood exists for a publication-grade recast (likelihood_available is no for all linked constraints).
The Higgs-mediated elastic DM-nucleon cross section is an analytic formula in the paper using the standard nucleon form factor f_n.
Published low-threshold direct-detection limit curves exist, but no ready likelihood for MeV-GeV masses is cited on the card and threshold systematics require detector-specific treatment.

gaps.description: No implementation of this gauged complex-scalar dark sector (X, dark Higgs H1, dark photon Zprime with Higgs mixing) exists in a public relic-density code; the paper uses analytic freeze-out estimates with x_f ~ 12-19 rather than a full Boltzmann solution over the X Xbar -> Zprime Zprime, H1 Zprime, H1 H1 channels.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Write a FeynRules model file for the X/H1/Zprime Lagrangian and run micrOMEGAs (or MadDM) to compute Omega_X h^2 across the m_X = 10 MeV-10 GeV window, including resonance and threshold effects near m_Zprime ~ 2 m_X.

gaps.description: No public likelihood exists for the Belle II B+ -> K+ + invisible measurement combined with KOTO and Higgs-invisible bounds in a form usable for this model's two-body (K+ H1) and three-body (K+ X Xbar) contributions; the card marks likelihood_available: no and recasting_needed: yes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a binned likelihood from the published Belle II q^2 spectrum for B+ -> K+ nu nubar, including the SM prediction B_SM = 4.97e-6, and add KOTO/B0 -> K0 invisible exclusions as auxiliary constraints so mixed two-body/three-body dark-sector signals can be fit consistently.

gaps.description: The direct-detection comparison for Higgs-mediated scattering of MeV-GeV scalar dark matter lacks a likelihood: standard tools are calibrated for heavier WIMPs, and low-threshold nuclear- and electron-recoil limits relevant near the 10 GeV upper edge and below are only available as published exclusion curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize current low-mass exclusion curves (e.g. sub-GeV to 10 GeV nuclear-recoil and Migdal/electron-recoil limits) and wrap them, or the corresponding DDCalc-style detector modules where available, into a reusable likelihood over (m_X, sigma_elastic).

route_step_status.reason: The paper gives EFT expressions for the enhanced P_zeta(k) under the sharp SR/USR/SR transition, but no public inflation-spectrum code handles Galileon (Horndeski c_i) mode functions, so the calculation must be re-implemented from the paper.

Press-Schechter with the w-dependent threshold delta_th = 3(1+w)/(5+3w) is a standard semi-analytic recipe, but it is restricted to the Gaussian linear-overdensity approximation and the card flags non-Gaussian corrections as unresolved with high extrapolation risk.

The scalar-induced GW spectrum follows standard analytic kernels computable from P_zeta(k), but the PTA comparison is only a band overlay because no PTA likelihood recast is wired in (likelihood_available: approximate).

gaps.description: No public code maps Covariantized Galileon coefficients c_i, sound speed c_s, and USR transition location to the enhanced curvature power spectrum P_zeta(k); standard Boltzmann/inflation pipelines (CLASS/CAMB, generic slow-roll solvers) do not implement Galileon SR/USR/SR mode evolution.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement a numerical Mukhanov-Sasaki-type mode solver for the Galileon EFT (effective c_s(tau) and z(tau) from the c_i) that reproduces the paper's sharp-transition benchmarks and outputs P_zeta(k) on the scales relevant for PTA and PBH formation.

gaps.description: The PBH abundance is computed only with a linear overdensity relation and Gaussian Press-Schechter thresholding; the nonlinear compaction-function and non-Gaussian (USR-induced) corrections, which can shift f_PBH by orders of magnitude, are not derived for this Galileon spectrum or its w-dependent thresholds.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Redo the abundance calculation with the nonlinear compaction function and threshold statistics (peaks-theory or compaction-based formalism) including the USR non-Gaussianity of zeta for each w in 0.16-1/3, and publish the corrected f_PBH(M) mapping for the paper benchmarks.

gaps.description: The claimed NANOGrav15/EPTA compatibility of the induced GW spectrum rests on a visual band comparison; no PTA likelihood evaluation of the model's Omega_GW(f) has been performed.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Feed the computed Omega_GW(f) into an existing public PTA analysis framework (e.g. the NANOGrav 15 yr free-spectrum posteriors via PTArcade-style recasting) to obtain posterior constraints on the Galileon amplitude, peak scale, and w.

gaps.description: The microlensing (EROS-2/MACHO) constraint on the near-solar and 10^4 solar-mass PBH benchmarks has not been recast for the model's actual mass function; the enrichment did not digitize an exclusion curve and the card marks recasting_needed: yes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Digitize the EROS-2 (and complementary OGLE/dynamical) f_PBH(M) exclusion curves and convolve them with the extended Galileon PBH mass function beta(M) to produce a proper f_PBH bound for each w benchmark.

route_step_status.reason: The authors have a working classical lattice solver (LATTICEEASY-style initialization), but it is not publicly released and the inhomogeneous runs are resolution-limited compared with dedicated axion-string simulations.
Redshifting field spectra to Omega_a h^2, B_0, and correlation length is a straightforward analytic transform given standard adiabatic scaling and plasma-conductivity assumptions.

Only a Planck relic-density target comparison is possible; no photon-mixing/X-ray or CMB spectral-distortion likelihood recast exists for the heavier-ALP spectra produced here (both linked constraints have likelihood_available: no).

gaps.description: The model-specific lattice code evolving the coupled ALP-photon-dark-photon system with the mixed (g_AX/2f) phi F Xtilde coupling is private; no public repository exists, so the relic-depletion and magnetogenesis results cannot be reproduced or scanned beyond the published benchmarks.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Release or re-implement the coupled axion-gauge lattice solver (e.g. as an extension of LATTICEEASY or CosmoLattice adding U(1) x U(1)_dark gauge fields with the three topological couplings), validated against the paper's f ~ 10^15 GeV homogeneous benchmark.

gaps.description: The post-inflationary inhomogeneous scenario (epsilon ~ 10^4-10^6, string/domain-wall initial conditions) is only qualitative because current lattice resolution cannot resolve the relevant spectra; relic abundance and B_0 windows may shift with proper string-network initial conditions.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run high-resolution lattice simulations with string-network initial conditions (adaptive-mesh or large static grids as in modern axion-string studies) coupled to the gauge sector, to quantify how initial inhomogeneity changes the depletion factor and magnetic spectrum.

gaps.description: No recast maps the predicted magnetic and dark-photon spectra of the heavier ALPs (m_phi ~ 10^-12-10^-8 eV, large g_X = g_AX couplings) onto the X-ray photon-ALP conversion and CMB spectral-distortion bounds, which were derived for late-time ultralight magnetogenesis with different spectra.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the constraint mapping for the paper's spectra: propagate the produced B and dark-photon backgrounds through photon-ALP-dark-photon mixing to compute X-ray conversion signals and mu/y distortions, then compare against COBE/FIRAS and X-ray survey limits as a reusable likelihood over (m_phi, f, g_A, g_AX).

route_step_status.reason: The mapping from FOPT parameters and dark asymmetry to (M_in, beta_PBH, T_n) uses paper-level Fermi-ball/false-vacuum collapse formulae; these are analytic but rely on a formation model whose efficiency is not calibrated by a public tool, and the FOPT thermodynamics itself would need a CosmoTransitions-style calculation for a specific potential.

Both the FOPT stochastic spectrum (standard sound-wave/bubble templates) and the PBH-density-fluctuation induced-GW spectrum are given by published analytic formulae reproducible from the paper and related literature.
The Delta N_eff/BBN extra-radiation check is a simple analytic integral of Omega_GW against the standard bound.
BBO/ET/CE/UDECIGO sensitivity curves are publicly available and the overlay is a direct data transform.
PBH lifetime, evaporation temperature, and the domination flag follow from standard analytic Hawking-evaporation and Friedmann relations.
The scalar dark-matter yield from Hawking emission is an analytic greybody-weighted formula in the paper, and public evaporation codes (BlackHawk-class) exist to refine it if needed.
Entropy dilution in the PBH-dominated regime is standard analytic early-matter-domination bookkeeping.
Comparing the diluted yield to the observed Omega_DM h^2 is a trivial validation step.
Only a free-streaming-length estimate against a cited Lyman-alpha bound is used; the nonthermal Hawking momentum distribution is not evolved through a transfer-function/flux-power likelihood.

gaps.description: The Lyman-alpha constraint on the warm, evaporation-produced scalar dark matter is applied only as a cited free-streaming-length cut; no pipeline maps the nonthermal Hawking emission spectrum (card notes distribution_function_available: no) to a linear transfer function and a Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihood for this M_in-M_DM plane.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Compute the redshifted phase-space distribution of the emitted scalars with a BlackHawk-class evaporation code (including the entropy-dilution history), feed it to CLASS as a non-cold relic to get T(k), and constrain with an existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulator/likelihood via the standard WDM-equivalent mapping.

gaps.description: The (M_in, beta_PBH) output of the FOPT Fermi-ball/false-vacuum collapse step rests on analytic formation-efficiency assumptions; no simulation-calibrated public tool computes the PBH mass and abundance from a given dark-sector FOPT potential, which propagates uncertainty into both the GW and relic routes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple a CosmoTransitions/PhaseTracer calculation of the dark-sector FOPT (nucleation rate, T_n, alpha_PT, beta_over_H) to a calibrated Fermi-ball collapse module, validated against published lattice/hydrodynamic studies of false-vacuum remnant collapse, and release it as a reusable (potential -> M_in, beta_PBH) tool.

route_step_status.reason: Parent-WIMP freezeout is solvable with standard relic machinery (micrOMEGAs-class solvers), but the card provides no UV-specific parent-sector implementation, and the coupled visible/dark two-sector freezeout with distinct temperatures is not covered by any public tool.
Mapping parent yields and CP asymmetry epsilon to baryon and dark-baryon asymmetries for out-of-equilibrium decays is standard analytic baryogenesis bookkeeping.
Computing T_prime/T from reheaton branching ratios and separate entropy conservation is a simple analytic calculation.
Delta N_eff follows analytically from T_prime/T and the dark relativistic species inventory, compared directly with Planck/BBN bounds.

Matching a chosen heavy mediator to low-energy operators is analytic, but the composite dark-neutron form factors/matrix elements needed to close the calculation are model dependent and not derived anywhere on the card.

Direct-detection and collider recast frameworks exist for specified simplified models, but no mediator benchmark, likelihood, or recast is provided (all linked constraints have likelihood_available: unknown and recasting_needed: yes).

gaps.description: No public solver implements the coupled two-sector cosmology of parallel WIMP baryogenesis: visible and dark parent freezeout at different sector temperatures, CP-violating decays, symmetric-relic annihilation in the dark QCD sector, and reheaton entropy injection must be tracked together to predict Omega_DM/Omega_b, and the paper only provides benchmark logic.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build a dedicated coupled Boltzmann code (or extend micrOMEGAs-style machinery with a two-temperature hidden-sector module) evolving parent yields, asymmetries, dark-sector temperature, and reheaton decay through confinement, validated against the paper's benchmark Omega_DM/Omega_b relation.

gaps.description: The dark-neutron nuclear matrix elements and form factors for scattering through Higgs/dark-Higgs, B-L, or heavy scalar mediators are not derived; without them the direct-detection cross section for the composite dark neutron cannot be computed beyond order-of-magnitude estimates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive dark-neutron sigma terms and form factors by rescaling QCD lattice/chiral-perturbation results to the dark confinement scale and detuned dark-quark Yukawas, for each candidate mediator operator, and publish them as inputs to the scattering calculation.

gaps.description: No direct-detection or collider likelihood/recast exists for any concrete mediator benchmark of this model: the mediator sector is left UV-realization dependent, so neutrino-floor comparisons and TeV-scale collider reach statements remain qualitative.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Define one or two simplified-model mediator benchmarks (Higgs-portal scalar and massive B-L vector), implement them in FeynRules, and recast with existing tools: DDCalc-style direct-detection likelihoods for nuclear recoils and LHC heavy-resonance/missing-energy searches via MadGraph plus CheckMATE/Contur.

gaps.description: The requirement that dark nucleosynthesis fail (so dark matter stays as individual dark neutrons rather than dark nuclei or atoms) is asserted from qualitative rate arguments; no dark-sector nuclear reaction network exists to verify it across the dark confinement scale, mass splittings, and dark-electron mass.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adapt a BBN reaction-network code (AlterBBN/PRIMAT-style) to the dark sector: compute dark deuteron binding and capture rates from rescaled nuclear EFT as functions of Lambda_QCD_prime and the p'-n' splitting, and map the parameter region where dark nucleosynthesis genuinely fails.

route_step_status.reason: Public multi-field inflation solvers (PyTransport/MultiModeCode class) exist, but the card names only a generic solver and no implementation of this scale-invariant scalaron plus hidden-scalar potential has been ingested.

Comparing derived n_s and r to public Planck/BICEP/Keck contours is a standard exercise with publicly released likelihood products, even though the card notes it is approximate without raw likelihood files.
The primary paper gives explicit analytic decay-width formulae valid in the stated mass hierarchy, so this is pen-and-paper math despite the generic tool label.
The coupled n_S and n_DM Boltzmann equations are written down in the paper and integrable with any standard ODE solver once the decay widths are supplied.

gaps.description: No public implementation of the classically scale-invariant multi-field inflaton dynamics (scalaron plus singlet S in the Jordan/Einstein frame) exists to compute the river-valley trajectory and its scalar/tensor perturbations for this specific potential.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's Jordan-frame potential and non-minimal couplings in an existing multi-field transport code such as PyTransport or MultiModeCode, verify the effective single-field river-valley reduction, and validate against the paper's r = 0.0017-0.0044 range for 50-60 e-foldings.

route_step_status.reason: The public author repository JovianNewPhysics reproduces the paper's geometric capture/absorption estimates, but it is documented only as figure-reproduction code with no stated inputs/outputs or validation for general parameter points.
Converting the captured population into a mediator/millicharged-particle flux is an analytic branching-and-lifetime calculation fully specified by the toy-model Lagrangian ingredients in the paper.
No Borexino event-time likelihood, Fermi-LAT Jupiter likelihood, or Jovian neutrino detector-response tool is publicly assembled, so detector-level statistical evaluation currently cannot be run.

gaps.description: No public time-series likelihood exists for the low-energy Borexino event rate, so the claimed 96 percent CL Jupiter-correlated modulation cannot be refit or tested against the captured-DM flux prediction with detector response and solar/detector systematics included.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Construct a binned timing likelihood from the published 2011-2021 Borexino low-energy rate data with a parameterized detector-response and background-modulation model, or obtain the collaboration's internal time-series likelihood, and interface it to the Jupiter-flux prediction.

gaps.description: The Fermi-LAT Jupiter gamma-ray analysis (arXiv:2104.02068) is not packaged as a reusable likelihood, and its long-lived-mediator limits must be recast to this model's Borexino-tuned mediator branching ratios before they constrain the 1-4 GeV scenario.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Rebuild the Jupiter gamma-ray analysis with public Fermi-LAT data and Fermitools, publish the flux upper limits as a tabulated likelihood, and map them onto this model's mediator decay-length and gamma-branching parameter space.

gaps.description: The benchmark spin-dependent cross section near 1e-24 cm^2 sits in the strongly interacting regime where naive rescaling of direct-detection and cosmic-ray-boosted limits fails; no public attenuation/saturation treatment covers a 1-4 GeV subcomponent with f_DM around 1e-4 at such large cross sections.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing Earth-shielding/attenuation code (verne or DaMaSCUS class) to spin-dependent scattering at subcomponent fractions and geometric-saturation cross sections, and re-derive the boosted-DM and underground-detector exclusion contours for this regime.

gaps.description: The proposed 236 MeV monoenergetic-neutrino test requires a neutrino detector near Jupiter that does not exist, so this observable has no data stream or likelihood on any current timescale.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Develop a near-Jupiter neutrino detector concept study with a simulated detector response, or recast the predicted line flux against existing large-volume terrestrial detectors (Super-K/JUNO class) pointing at Jupiter to obtain an interim sensitivity estimate.

route_step_status.reason: micrOMEGAs 5.0 with a LanHEP model implementation is the tool the authors actually used, and this four-parameter renormalizable WIMP sits squarely inside standard micrOMEGAs freeze-out assumptions.
The spin-independent cross section follows the scalar-mediated analytic formula given in the paper (also computable directly by micrOMEGAs), so the null tool_or_code reflects trivial analytics.

The composite likelihood can be approximately reconstructed from the Planck Omega h^2 = 0.12 Gaussian and public LZ limit curves (or DDCalc), but the authors' scan files and a full detector likelihood are not available.

gaps.description: The LanHEP/micrOMEGAs model files for this specific Z6 singlet Dirac model are not public, so reproducing the relic-density and cross-section pipeline requires reimplementing the model from the Lagrangian rather than running released inputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reimplement the Z6 Lagrangian in LanHEP or FeynRules, generate and publicly release the CalcHEP/micrOMEGAs model files, and validate by recovering the paper's viable 60 GeV to 6 TeV mass range and its LZ-compatible scan points.

route_step_status.reason: Slow-roll n_s, r, and A_s for nonminimally coupled quartic inflation in the metric formalism follow from standard analytic frame transformations and slow-roll formulae given in the paper.

The reheating-era fermion yield from perturbative inflaton decay is governed by standard Boltzmann yield equations written in the paper and integrable with any ODE solver, so the null tool_or_code is not a blocker.
Validation is a direct comparison of n_s, r, and Omega_chi h^2 against public Planck contours and the observed relic abundance, which is simple bookkeeping.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-production momentum distribution from inflaton decay kinematics with redshifting through the metric-formalism reheating history, feed it into CLASS as a non-cold relic to obtain the linear transfer function, and publish the resulting half-mode mass and effective thermal-WDM mass mapping across the viable y_chi-m_chi band for comparison with Lyman-alpha bounds.

route_step_status.reason: Slow-roll n_s, r, and A_s for nonminimally coupled quartic inflation in the Palatini formalism follow from standard analytic frame transformations and slow-roll formulae given in the paper.

Validation is a direct comparison of n_s, r, and Omega_chi h^2 against public Planck contours and the observed relic abundance, which is simple bookkeeping.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the decay-production momentum distribution from inflaton decay kinematics with redshifting through the Palatini quartic-oscillation reheating history, feed it into CLASS as a non-cold relic to obtain the linear transfer function, and publish the resulting half-mode mass and effective thermal-WDM mass mapping across the viable y_chi-m_chi band for comparison with Lyman-alpha bounds.

route_step_status.reason: The closed-wall abundance from post-inflationary string-wall statistics is a bespoke semi-analytic construction of the primary paper with no public code (associated_code unknown, tool_or_code null), and the wall-size/shape distribution requires string-wall network simulation input rather than simple pen-and-paper math.

PBH formation efficiency from aspherical wall collapse under Hubble expansion is a simulation step with no named tool; the paper uses in-house semi-analytic and numerical collapse inputs that are not packaged as a public code.

Public compilations of EROS/OGLE microlensing constraint curves and published survey efficiencies exist and can be recast, but the card records likelihood_available no and no packaged event-rate likelihood that handles the model's extended PBH mass function.

gaps.description: No public code computes the number density and size/shape statistics of self-enclosed N_DW=1 axion domain walls from post-inflationary string-wall network evolution (including the early-matter-domination option and the string density parameter whose uncertainty exponentially suppresses the PBH abundance), so the closed-wall abundance step cannot be run outside the authors' in-house calculation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Package a wall-counting module that takes percolation statistics from existing lattice string-wall network simulations (e.g. field-theoretic axion-string simulation outputs) and outputs the closed-wall size distribution as a function of f_a, N_DW, and the expansion history, calibrated against the primary paper's f_PBH(f_a) bands.

gaps.description: PBH formation efficiency from the collapse of aspherical self-enclosed axion domain walls is not covered by any public simulation suite; the fraction of walls that compactify inside their Schwarzschild radius instead of radiating away as axions controls f_PBH and is currently taken from rough semi-analytic collapse criteria.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a targeted campaign of numerical-relativity or field-theory collapse simulations of closed domain walls with varying asphericity and tension sigma_dw proportional to m_a(T) f_a^2, in both radiation-dominated and early-matter-dominated backgrounds, and fit a formation-efficiency function epsilon(shape, sigma_dw, H) usable in the abundance pipeline.

gaps.description: No machine-readable microlensing likelihood exists that applies EROS/OGLE efficiencies and Gaia DR4/Roman projections to the model's generated (non-monochromatic) PBH mass function; current comparisons use monochromatic or narrow-mass recasts of published exclusion curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build an event-rate likelihood that convolves the model PBH mass function with published OGLE/EROS survey efficiency curves and a standard Galactic model (extending public PBH-bound compilation codes to extended mass functions), and add Gaia DR4 and Roman projected sensitivities for forecasting.

gaps.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum has been derived for the specific wall network of this PBH calculation; the card only imports GW context from a related axion-wall paper with a different setup, so the GW observable cannot be evaluated for the same cosmology (same f_a, early matter domination) that sets the PBH abundance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the stochastic GW spectrum sourced by the same N_DW=1 string-wall network and closed-wall collapses used in the PBH abundance calculation, using standard domain-wall GW emission estimates parameterized by sigma_dw and the collapse-time distribution, then compare against PTA and interferometer sensitivity curves.

route_step_status.reason: The curvature-perturbation distribution from slow supercooled bubble nucleation is a bespoke semi-analytic calculation with tail fits to finite realizations (no tool_or_code, no public code named), and the card flags high extrapolation risk because PBH formation probes tails beyond the sampled range.
Critical-collapse scaling of the PBH mass distribution given a perturbation amplitude and horizon mass is a standard analytic formula that is straightforwardly evaluated without a dedicated code.

Public PBH constraint compilations (evaporation, microlensing, lensing, accretion curves) exist and are named as the required resource, but no packaged likelihood convolves them with this model's extended mass function (likelihood_available unknown, external likelihood required).
The bubble-collision GW component is a standard analytic power-law spectral fit in phase-transition parameters, which is simple analytic work covered by well-established published formulas.

Public scalar-induced GW integrators exist for Gaussian curvature spectra, but the secondary component here is sourced by the non-Gaussian FOPT false-vacuum perturbations, so existing tools need modification and no tool is named on the card.
PTA/LVK/LISA/ET sensitivity curves are publicly available but were not bundled, and no packaged stochastic-GW likelihood for the two-peak spectrum is identified (likelihood_available unknown).

gaps.description: The PBH abundance depends on the far tail of the density-contrast distribution generated by slow supercooled bubble nucleation, but the primary only fits tails from finite numbers of realizations; no simulation campaign or public code characterizes the false-vacuum-fraction perturbation statistics (including non-Gaussianity) at the rare-fluctuation level that sets f_PBH.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run large ensembles of bubble-nucleation realizations (extending the primary's improved nucleation-time treatment) to directly sample the density-contrast distribution to the PBH-forming tail as a function of beta/H_0 and T_reh, and release the resulting tail parameterization as a reusable curvature-spectrum/PDF module.

gaps.description: No machine-readable likelihood converts the model's extended PBH mass function into an exclusion in the (beta/H_0, T_reh) plane; the constraint step relies on overlaying public monochromatic PBH limit curves, which the card notes require recasting for extended mass functions and tails.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public PBH constraint compilation to an extended-mass-function recast tool that convolves the critical-collapse mass function with evaporation/BBN, gamma-ray, microlensing, lensing, and accretion limit curves and returns f_PBH exclusions per phase-transition parameter point.

gaps.description: The secondary scalar-induced GW component requires integrating induced-GW kernels over the non-Gaussian curvature spectrum generated by the slow transition; existing public induced-GW integrators assume Gaussian primordial spectra and there is no tool covering this model's source statistics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public scalar-induced GW code (e.g. a SIGWfast-class kernel integrator) to accept the FOPT-generated curvature spectrum and its non-Gaussian corrections as input, validated against the primary's secondary-peak amplitude fits.

gaps.description: No stochastic-GW likelihood is packaged for confronting the two-peak spectrum with NANOGrav/PTA data and LVK limits or for forecasting LISA/AEDGE/AION/ET reach; the route only has unbundled sensitivity curves and the card records no resolved likelihood.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wire the two-peak Omega_GW(f) prediction into existing public PTA analysis frameworks (NANOGrav free-spectrum posteriors / PTArcade-style wrappers) and standard power-law-integrated sensitivity curves for LVK/LISA/ET, returning SNR and exclusion regions in the (beta/H_0, T_reh) plane.

route_step_status.reason: The late-nucleating-patch PBH mass and abundance follow closed-form semi-analytic formulae ('FOPT PBH formulae') in T_reh, beta/H, and delta_c that are directly implementable from the primary paper without a dedicated code.

The magnetogenesis prediction uses MHD decay scaling laws that are analytic to apply but are calibrated only for maximally helical evolution, so the B_0 and lambda_0 outputs are unreliable outside that assumption and no simulation-backed tool covers general helicity.

The supercooled-FOPT bubble-collision GW spectrum is a standard published spectral template in T_reh and beta/H, and LISA/ET/CE/DECIGO sensitivity curves for the SNR comparison are publicly available.

gaps.description: The PBH abundance (tuned to f_PBH = 1) hinges on the collapse threshold delta_c for late-nucleating overdense patches during a supercooled FOPT, which the card flags as the dominant uncertainty; no simulation-calibrated value of delta_c exists for this vacuum-energy-dominated collapse scenario, only threshold choices carried over from standard radiation-era collapse.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Perform numerical-relativity simulations of the collapse of late-nucleating false-vacuum Hubble patches embedded in the reheated plasma to calibrate delta_c and the resulting mass relation as functions of beta/H and the supercooling strength, and publish the fit for use in the semi-analytic abundance formulae.

gaps.description: The present-day IGMF prediction (about 20 pG at 0.001-0.01 Mpc) assumes maximally helical MHD decay; no MHD simulation campaign covers the decay of FOPT-generated fields with partial or zero helicity for this scenario, so the magnetogenesis observable cannot be robustly evaluated across the helicity parameter the route itself lists as an input.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run magnetohydrodynamic decay simulations (e.g. with the public Pencil Code) initialized with the bubble-collision field spectra of this transition across a grid of fractional helicities, and fit B_0(lambda_0) evolution tracks to replace the maximally-helical scaling assumption.

gaps.description: Neither the asteroid-mass PBH window constraint nor the blazar IGMF lower bound has a machine-readable likelihood (both carded as likelihood_available no with recasting needed); the f_PBH = 1 viability check currently amounts to eyeballing published monochromatic window boundaries and blazar-cascade lower-bound curves.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Assemble a constraint module combining a public PBH bound compilation (evaporation, Voyager/CMB, HSC/OGLE microlensing curves, with a convolution option for the nearly-monochromatic mass function) and digitized blazar-cascade B_0-lambda_0 lower bounds, returning pass/fail and margins per (T_reh, beta/H, delta_c, helicity) point.

route_step_status.reason: Slow-roll expressions give n_s and r at CMB scales, but an accurate P_zeta(k) through the loop-corrected waterfall transition needs a numerical mode-by-mode perturbation solver (listed as a required code resource) that is not identified on the card and generic public inflation solvers do not ship this potential.

Standard semi-analytic machinery for f_PBH(M) (Press-Schechter/peaks with critical collapse) and scalar-induced GW kernel integrals exists publicly for Gaussian spectra, but the abundance is exponentially sensitive to threshold and peak-width choices and the card notes non-Gaussianity is not developed, so existing tools cover the step only approximately.

OGLE/Subaru-HSC microlensing curves and Planck accretion bounds are published (likelihood_available partial), but no extended-mass-function recast likelihood was run and the mapping from the model mass function to those analyses is not packaged.

gaps.description: No public inflationary perturbation solver implements the loop-corrected attractor hybrid potential with its dark-fermion contribution and waterfall transition, so the small-scale curvature peak P_zeta(k) that sets both f_PBH and Omega_GW can only be estimated analytically rather than computed mode-by-mode.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the loop-corrected hybrid potential (inflaton plus waterfall field with dark-fermion Yukawa corrections) in a public multi-field Mukhanov-Sasaki solver (e.g. a MultiModeCode/PyTransport-class code) and compute P_zeta(k) through the waterfall, validated against the primary's n_s about 0.964, r about 0.0087, and peak benchmarks.

gaps.description: Non-Gaussianity of the waterfall-enhanced perturbations is not developed in the paper, yet the PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to the tail of the density distribution and to the collapse threshold, so f_PBH(M) computed with Gaussian statistics carries an uncontrolled systematic.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the non-Gaussian statistics of the curvature perturbation through the waterfall transition (e.g. via the delta-N formalism or stochastic-inflation lattice methods applied to this potential) and propagate them into the PBH collapse fraction with compaction-function thresholds.

gaps.description: No packaged likelihood recasts the model's extended PBH mass function onto the OGLE 5-year and Subaru/HSC microlensing event-rate analyses and the Planck CMB accretion bounds; only monochromatic published exclusion curves are available, and all-DM claims require an extended-mass recast the card says was not rerun.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Build an extended-mass-function recast tool that convolves f_PBH(M) with published OGLE/HSC efficiency curves and Planck accretion constraint curves (extending a public PBH-bounds compilation), returning allowed benchmark regions directly in the model's potential-parameter space.

route_step_status.reason: Deriving the coupled background Klein-Gordon equations and energy-transfer terms for Q_phi = -Q_psi = beta phidot^2 psidot^2 is analytic work already done in the primary paper, so the null tool_or_code is not a gap.
The card records a public modified-CLASS implementation at a GitHub URL (has_associated_code yes) that solves the background and linear equations for this coupling.

MontePython/Cobaya-style samplers and the Planck/BAO/SN/LSS likelihoods are standard public tools that plug onto the existing modified CLASS; the inference has not been run, but the capability exists.

gaps.description: The matter-power observable extends to mildly nonlinear weak-lensing and galaxy-clustering scales, but the card records halo and subhalo mass-function effects as unknown with no simulation calibration, so no nonlinear prescription exists for the coupled SFDM-EDE matter power spectrum needed for S8-type comparisons.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the nonlinear response by running N-body simulations initialized with the modified-CLASS linear spectra and scale-dependent growth for representative (m_phi, beta, f_EDE) points, and fit a halofit/HMcode-style correction or emulator valid over the sampler's prior range.

gaps.description: The coupling Q = beta phidot^2 psidot^2 is imposed at the conservation-equation level without a microscopic action, and the card flags possible stability and prior pathologies of the perturbed energy-transfer terms outside the worked examples; no derived stability/viability conditions delimit the (m_phi, lambda_phi, beta) space over which the Boltzmann solution is trustworthy.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive the gauge-consistent perturbed energy-momentum transfer and its no-ghost/gradient-stability conditions for this coupling (following the interacting-dark-energy instability literature), encode the resulting viability bounds as hard priors in the MCMC, and add runtime stability checks to the public modified CLASS.

route_step_status.reason: The kinetic-misalignment axion abundance follows analytic relations between the PQ charge yield Y_theta, f_a, and m_a given in the primary and related KMM papers, which is straightforward pen-and-paper evaluation despite the null tool_or_code.

The freeze-in B-L transfer from the rotating PQ field through light right-handed neutrinos requires solving branch-specific Boltzmann/rate equations, and no public code implements lepto-axiogenesis transport with dynamical light RHNs (existing leptogenesis solvers such as ULYSSES do not include the PQ-rotation source).
Delta N_eff from saxion decays to axions and the thermalization/entropy boundaries are given as parametric analytic formulas in the primary paper, so the step is simple analytic work.

Comparing Y_B and Omega_a h^2 to their measured values is trivial, and public Planck-based Delta N_eff likelihoods exist, but no combined likelihood was run and the primary's baryon-yield and thermalization contours were not digitized (likelihood_available no/partial across constraints).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's chemical-equilibrium condition and repulsion terms in an open TOV solver (e.g. extend a CompOSE-compatible EoS pipeline) parameterized by (m_chi, m_phi, z_chi, z_n) over a family of nuclear equations of state, and validate against the paper's benchmark maximum-mass curves.

route_step_status.reason: Tree-level matching of vector-like quark masses and Yukawas onto the LEFT scalar-current Wilson coefficients is standard analytic EFT matching done in the paper.

route_step_status.reason: The flat-potential Q-ball mass-charge relation and the Q_B > (m_phi/m_n)^4 stability threshold are analytic order-of-magnitude formulas computable by hand.

Mapping condensate perturbations to a Q-ball charge distribution is done by rough instability-wavelength estimates with no tool, and the card itself flags the nonlinear completion of the fragmentation as future work.

The survival and BBN/CMB recast requires a dedicated thermal-erosion, evaporation, and energy-injection transport calculation that no identified tool provides (tool_or_code null, no likelihood identified).

gaps.description: No public simulation or calibrated semi-analytic pipeline converts an Affleck-Dine flat-direction condensate (given initial charge density and potential shape) into a Q-ball charge distribution; the paper relies on linear-instability estimates and identifies the nonlinear fragmentation as unsolved future work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run 3D lattice simulations of a complex scalar with MSSM flat-direction potentials (adapting a public lattice code such as CosmoLattice or GABE to conserved-charge initial conditions), scan initial charge density and potential flatness, and fit the resulting Q-ball charge distribution into a reusable semi-analytic emulator.

gaps.description: There is no implemented survival calculation combining surface fermionic evaporation, finite-temperature erosion, and charge leakage to evolve a Q-ball charge distribution from formation to today; the card notes these were not numerically recomputed and survival is asserted only at order-of-magnitude level.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Derive and code the Cohen-Coleman-Georgi-Manohar surface evaporation rate together with finite-temperature potential corrections and thermal charge erosion into a charge-distribution evolution solver taking the gap_1 output as input and returning the surviving relic abundance and evaporated charge Delta Q.

gaps.description: Existing BBN/CMB energy-injection codes assume spatially homogeneous injection, but the model's constraint hinges on emission being localized around rare macroscopic Q-balls; no tool treats inhomogeneous, source-localized energy injection during BBN and recombination, so the paper's localization argument cannot be tested quantitatively.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public injection code (ACROPOLIS-style BBN cascade treatment) with a diffusion-transport module for pointlike sources, parameterized by Q-ball number density, emission spectrum, and tau_Q, to produce homogenized effective limits or confirm the localized-injection escape.

route_step_status.reason: The thermal axion abundance for f_a around 1e6 GeV is a standard analytic hot-relic calculation from pion/nucleon scattering rates that the primary paper already performs and that can be reproduced with pen-and-paper plus published rate formulas.
A thermal eV-scale axion is a massive hot relic that CLASS/CAMB handle as an extra non-cold species and standard BBN codes (PArthENoPE, AlterBBN, PRIMAT) handle as extra relativistic energy density.

Published thermal-axion CMB/LSS bounds exist (likelihood_available is partial) but overlaying them on this model while separating standard from low-reheating histories requires a custom recast not provided by any packaged tool on the card.

gaps.description: No packaged likelihood exists for the hadronic-axion window: the stellar/solar/supernova constraint set (hadronic_axion_window) has likelihood_available 'no', and the modern thermal-axion cosmology bound is only 'partial', so the modern_bound_overlay recasting step cannot be run as a joint likelihood over (f_a, m_a, C_a) including the reheating-history dependence.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Wrap the published thermal-axion CMB/LSS posterior chains (Planck+LSS thermal axion analyses) and the stellar/solar/supernova exclusion curves into a MontePython/Cobaya likelihood module parameterized by (m_a, f_a, C_a, T_reheat), with a switch between standard and low-reheating thermalization histories.

gaps.description: The thermal_abundance step relies on the 1998 pion-nucleon scattering estimate, whose chiral-perturbation-theory rates are uncalibrated near the QCD crossover where an f_a around 1e6 GeV axion decouples, so Omega_a and rho_a/rho_nu at BBN carry uncontrolled systematic uncertainty.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Adopt modern smooth-interpolation axion-pion thermalization rates across the QCD crossover (post-2021 recalculations of the axion production rate) and tabulate n_a/s versus f_a for use in the BBN and structure steps, validating against the primary paper's 0.1-0.2 Omega_a benchmark.

route_step_status.reason: The 4x4 effective neutrino mass matrix follows analytically from the SO(10) texture given in the paper, so a null tool_or_code is fine for this pen-and-paper step.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Apply an existing sterile-neutrino quantum-kinetic solver (LASAGNA-type momentum-averaged or full-momentum code) to this model's mixing parameters with and without the lepton-asymmetry loophole, outputting Delta N_eff for the BBN codes and the cosmology likelihood.

route_step_status.reason: String-wall network simulations exist (the paper's own runs and successors) but only at v_a/m_a around 500 with no public code on the card, so the wall-decay spectrum and gamma at physical parameters rest on an uncertain extrapolation.
Combining gamma, m_a, and the network density into an order-of-magnitude Omega_a and velocity dispersion is the paper's analytic formula and is doable by hand.

Haloscope signal-shape models exist for standard halo distributions, but mapping the population-II broadened lineshape requires the local density fraction and velocity distribution of wall-decay axions, which no available calculation supplies.

gaps.description: No public high-dynamic-range simulation of the N=1 string-wall network reaches physically relevant v_a/m_a; the wall-decay Lorentz factor gamma (7 measured at v_a/m_a=500, about 60 extrapolated) and the radiated axion spectrum that set both the relic contribution and the population-II velocity dispersion are extrapolations with order-of-magnitude uncertainty.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Run modern adaptive-mesh or large-lattice field-theory simulations of the post-QCD N=1 string-wall network (in the style of recent AMR axion-string codes) to larger log(v_a/m_a), extracting the wall-decay axion energy spectrum and a fitted scaling law for gamma versus v_a/m_a.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations of minicluster formation seeded by the two-population initial phase space (cold population I plus high-dispersion population II) and follow tidal disruption in a Milky-Way potential to output the local smooth density fraction and velocity distribution of each population.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Extend a public haloscope lineshape likelihood to a two-component signal model (narrow population I plus broadened population II parameterized by its local fraction and dispersion) and recast existing cavity exclusion data with it.

route_step_status.reason: Splitting the 5 eV mass budget over two species and computing the free-streaming scale is simple pen-and-paper math.

The source-era CMB/galaxy data compilation and its model-probability machinery are not available as a runnable likelihood, and no modern recast has been performed (likelihood_available: no).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Run a small suite of neutrino-inclusive N-body simulations (e.g. Gadget-4 with linear-response or particle neutrinos) at the CHDM parameter point to calibrate the halo mass function and void statistics near 10 h^-1 Mpc, validating the claimed cluster-overproduction reduction of two versus one hot species.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Recast an existing Ly-alpha or Milky Way satellite-count likelihood in terms of a generalized transfer-function parameterization (e.g. alpha-beta-gamma fits) and map the low-reheat neutrino T(k) onto it, rather than through invalid thermal-WDM mass equivalents.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Couple the low-reheat neutrino thermalization solution to a modern BBN code (PRIMAT or PArthENoPE) with current D/H and He-4 measurements, and release the resulting T_RH-m_nu likelihood following the methodology of the Planck-era reheating-floor analyses.

route_step_status.reason: No tool computes the coupled singlet-sector thermal history (singlino decoupling, G -> s s, N_eff) with the required 10^4-10^5 entropy injection, and the entropy source itself is unspecified; the paper gives only rate estimates.
